**11.114.1 MEASURED: THE SECOND LINK SPRINGS BACK ON THE RULE'S OWN TARGET.** DR-113 rules that
`SIG-001` fires when an HDBaseT port is connected directly to a `net.ethernet` port that TERMINATES
the signal. So the target is, by construction, an Ethernet jack. The remedy's second link would be
the receiver's `HDMI OUT` into that same jack:

| End | Family | Connector |
|---|---|---|
| `V06:receiver` `hdmi.out` | `video.hdmi.2_0` | `conn.hdmi_a` |
| the switch port the user aimed at | `net.ethernet` | `conn.rj45` |

That pair fails `SIG-002` (the sink does not accept the family) and `CON-001` (the connectors do not
mate) together. **The remedy would refuse its own second cable**, which is not a corner case: it is
the only case `SIG-001` has.

**11.114.2 CANON IS NARROWER THAN THE DERIVED SENTENCE, AND CANON IS WHAT BINDS.** §280 says
*"`[ Insert HDBaseT receiver ]` therefore inserts a device, correctly"* and stops there. CR-015's
subject is the adapter/device split, *"does an installer pull two separate cables to it?"*, and the
answer for a TX/RX pair is yes, which is the whole of what that ruling decides. **The "both links"
clause is docs/05 prose**, priority-3 and derived, and it does not survive contact with the rule it
was written for.

**11.114.3 Ruled: the remedy mints the receiver, wires the HDBaseT run into it, and leaves the HDMI
end OPEN.** One undo step, one new device, one new link. The receiver's `hdmi.out` is connected to
nothing and that is the finished state of the remedy rather than a half-done one.

**AN OPEN END IS A THING THIS PRODUCT ALREADY MODELS**, which is why this is a narrowing rather than
an invention. AC-018 leaves a home run's far end open on purpose, `unlandedHomeRunIds` counts them,
the schematic status strip reports them, and `LNK-020` is *"a CHECKLIST, NOT A FAILURE"* over exactly
that state. The remedy therefore hands back a design in a state the product has a vocabulary for.

**AND IT IS WHAT THE TRADE WANTS.** An installer who drew a matrix output into a switch port did not
want a cable between the receiver and the switch; they wanted the HDBaseT run to reach a receiver
near the display. The remedy puts the receiver in the design and terminates the run on it. Where the
display is, is a fact about the job that the product does not have and must not invent.

*Rejected: wiring both links and letting the second one file a finding.* It follows §767 to the
letter and it is defensible under G2, *"a model that cannot draw a mistake cannot document reality."*
It is refused because G2 licenses the USER to draw a mistake; it does not license the PRODUCT to draw
one on their behalf and hand it back as a fix. A remedy that leaves a fresh error behind is the nag
`design-ux-schematic.md` contrasts a rule engine with, arriving one step later.

*Rejected: offering the remedy only where the second link is constructible.* `SIG-001`'s target is
an Ethernet port by definition, so this hides the button on every case the rule has. `#278`'s own
description is *"a remedy chip that only explains has not remedied"*, and a remedy that never
appears has explained.

**11.114.4 The docs/05 edit is owed and is listed in §12.** :767's clause becomes *"and wires the
run into it in one undo step"*. Nothing else in that paragraph moves: the adapter/device test, the
`mountMethod: notInRack`, the *"two or more `Link`s"* and the full symbol are all untouched and all
still true of a receiver, which will carry a second link the moment the user lands its HDMI end.

### §11.115 DR-116 · A rule is about the state, not about the gesture: landing a run end consults both tiers

**Question.** `#811`. Landing or moving a home run's loose end writes a `Link` endpoint, and
`buildBindEndpointCommand` asks almost nothing about it. Does binding adopt the connect gesture's
rule stack, or is occupancy genuinely a bind's only rule?

**11.115.1 MEASURED: SIX CHECKS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A RULE.** `buildBindEndpointCommand`
refuses when the link is absent, when it is not a home run (`structureOrigin == null`), when it has
no conductors, when that end is already landed, when `portConductorCount > 0`, and when the rack
label collides (CR-113). The candidate set the SURFACE offers is narrower still: `_armLandingFrom`
builds it from occupancy alone, and its own comment says so, *"a bind's only occupancy rule is
`TOP-003`."*

Of the six, four are gesture applicability, one is CR-113, and exactly one is a catalogue rule.
**`TOP-001` and `TOP-002` are unasked**, and no tier-2 rule is asked at all.

**11.115.2 THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE FLAGSHIP HAZARD ARRIVING THROUGH A SIDE DOOR.** Dragging an
HDBaseT run's loose end onto a switch port is `SIG-001` in every particular: the same two ports, the
same 100 W PoH, the same damaged switch. The connect gesture springs it back with a chip and the bind
gesture writes it silently, and nothing in the corpus ever decided that. It is an artefact of the
bind path predating both tiers.

**11.115.3 Ruled: a rule is a statement about the RESULTING STATE, not about the gesture that
produced it.** Both tiers govern the bind.

**TIER 1 COMPLETES.** `TOP-001` and `TOP-002` join the `TOP-003` already there. These are the rules
CR-017 calls states in which *"the model means nothing"*, and a meaningless document is not made
meaningful by the gesture that wrote it. The existing occupancy check stays exactly where it is and
keeps asking through `portConductorCount`, so `TOP-003` still lives in one place.

**TIER 2 SPRINGS BACK, WITH ITS CHIP AND ITS `[ Connect anyway ]`.** The six rules read a pair of
`ConnectTarget`s and neither of them cares which gesture assembled the pair.

**11.115.4 THE OVERRIDE IS WHY THIS IS SAFE FOR AS-FOUND WORK, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER TO THE
OBJECTION.** A home run was pulled weeks before anybody opened this sheet, so landing it is recording
a fact rather than proposing a design, and a product that REFUSED to record what the previous
installer did would fail G2 in the case G2 names: *"cannot import an as-found survey."*

CR-017 already resolves that tension and resolves it in this direction. Tier 2 does not refuse; **it
hesitates**, and the hesitation is the teaching moment. Somebody surveying an existing install lands
the run, is told the rule the last installer broke, presses `[ Connect anyway ]`, and now has a
document that both records reality and carries the finding. That is a better outcome than silence,
and silence is what ships today.

*Rejected: tier 1 only, on the ground that an existing cable is a fact rather than a proposal.* It is
the strongest objection and it fails on CR-017's own mechanism: the tier that would "argue with
reality" is the one built not to, and refusing to mention a hazard is not neutrality when the hazard
is a damaged switch. It also costs `SIG-001` on one of the two gestures that can create it, which
`seed_registries.dart` calls *"the highest-value validation in the product"*.

*Rejected: ruling that occupancy really is a bind's only rule.* It is the cheapest answer and it
leaves `TOP-001` and `TOP-002` unchecked on a gesture that writes an endpoint. That is not a matter
of taste: `TOP-001` is a conductor connecting a port to itself.

**11.115.5 The candidate set narrows with the command, and that is the half a surface must not
forget.** `_armLandingFrom` offers every free pin. Under this ruling a pin the command would refuse
at tier 1 must not be offered, on DR-011.5's standing rule that *"a pin the gesture OFFERS is never
then refused"* by tier 1: the claim M5-D split in two and whose tier-1 half survives intact. Tier-2
pins stay OFFERED and wear the amber ring, which is docs/05:476's *"they remain droppable"* reaching
the second gesture.

### §11.116 DR-117 · The lockup ships, arranging supplied art is not generating it, and the manual is a games manual

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-03.** Three clauses about the product's outward identity, ruled
together because they arrived together and because the second is the one a later reader will most
want to find.

**11.116.1 THE LOCKUP SHIPS AS IT STANDS, AND `#784`'s TWO OPEN QUESTIONS CLOSE WITH IT.** That item
landed *"landable and revisable, not final"* and left two review questions that would change the
path data: whether the rule matches `RACK` or runs the full width including Riley, and whether `PAL`
is flush left or optically centred under `RACK`.

**Both are settled as shipped**: the rule matches `RACK`, and `PAL` is flush left. The user has the
mark in front of a test group and it was well received, which is a better answer than either
question was going to get from argument. **A drawn mark that reads is not improved by re-deriving
its geometry**, and the two questions were asked by somebody who could not see it.

**RILEY'S PORTRAIT IS EXPECTED TO CHANGE AND THE LOCKUP IS NOT.** The two are separate paths for
reasons `brand.dart` already gives, and this ruling adds a third: they are on different clocks. Final
art replaces `_rileyD` and nothing else moves, because Riley's box, its 0.806:1 ratio, its cap-high
placement and its 268-unit clearance are all constants the letterforms never read.

**11.116.2 ARRANGING SUPPLIED ARTWORK IS NOT GENERATING IT, AND THIS REPOSITORY HAD NEVER SAID SO.**
The user's position is that composing supplied assets on a page is not AI-generated art. **Measured:
no ruling on the subject exists.** Canon, docs/10, the roadmap and the OKF bundle carry exactly one
`AI` clause, DR-089 §11.88's note on the *font licence's* §4.7, which is about supplying glyph data
to a model and is a different question entirely. So this is ruled rather than cited.

**The distinction is authorship of the marks, not the tooling that placed them.** Three cases, and
the line falls in the same place each time:

| Act | What it is |
|---|---|
| Tracing supplied raster art to outlines, as `#784` did at 98.6% pixel agreement | **Transcription.** Every curve descends from a mark the artist made |
| Composing a lockup: choosing a measure, a clearance, a fill rule, a baseline | **Layout.** The letterforms are cut from a licensed face and Riley is the artist's |
| Emitting a figure no hand drew, from a model, as the thing itself | **Generation**, and it is not how any mark in this repository was made |

**WHAT THAT ACTUALLY COMMITS THE PROJECT TO** is the part worth writing down, because the sentence
above is comfortable and the obligation is not: **every mark this product ships is traceable to a
human author, and the file that carries it says which.** `brand.dart` already does, for both halves.
A future asset that cannot make that claim does not ship, and the honest place to discover that is
before it is drawn rather than in a licence review.

**11.116.3 THE USER MANUAL IS A VINTAGE VIDEO-GAME MANUAL, AND THAT IS A REGISTER RATHER THAN A
JOKE.** No manual exists and none was scheduled: AC-058/D1 buys a glossary panel and M5-F3's
`[Why?]` viewer and stops there.

The register is chosen because it fits what this product is, not because it is charming. A games
manual of that era had to teach a system with **no network, no tooltips and no undo for the reader**,
so it explained the model first, listed the hazards plainly, and expected to be read once and
consulted after. That is a rack drawing's manual exactly. The **28-rule catalogue is a bestiary**, the
**device catalog is an item list**, the **keymap is a controls diagram**, and CR-021's *"a rule not
listed here does not exist"* is the promise a bestiary makes and a wiki does not.

**THE ONE THING THE REGISTER MAY NOT DO IS SOFTEN A SAFETY SENTENCE.** DR-079 demoted `CODE-001` and
`CODE-002` to warnings that ask a person to verify against a named article, and `SIG-001` exists
because 100 W of PoH damages a switch. **Those sentences are quoted into the manual verbatim or not
at all.** Riley may be beside them; Riley may not paraphrase them.

**11.116.4 THE MANUAL IS SCHEDULED INTO M9, BETA HARDENING, AND THE MILESTONE'S OWN CRITERION IS THE
ARGUMENT.** The user placed it at beta hardening and read that as M8; **beta hardening is M9** and M8
is release engineering (docs/12 §5.7, §5.8). The correction is worth making because M9's exit
criterion is a better case for the manual than the number was:

> Three integrators have each produced a sheet set they were willing to send to a client or a job
> site, and **none of the three needed to leave the app to fix something.**

**A manual is what that clause is measured against.** Its failure mode IS the criterion's failure
mode: an integrator who went looking elsewhere. Written earlier it would be guessing at what confuses
somebody; written for M9 it is read by the three people whose confusion the criterion counts, and
what they still had to ask is the revision.

**IT IS NOT A SCOPE AMENDMENT (§8.3), because nothing moves between release bands.** The manual is
new work inside a milestone that already exists, and RJ-017's *"documentation and onboarding"* line
under AC-058/D9 is where it lands rather than a v1 clause being added. **The mascot's three surfaces
stay at M8** where §10.12(f) put them: an app that draws Riley and a book that draws Riley are two
deliverables, and only the second is being scheduled here.

`docs/19-riley.md` carries the character reference this needs, including the pose catalogue the
manual's illustrations are drawn from.

### §11.117 DR-118 · The visor is a display, which buys the manual a narrator it did not have

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-03**, extending DR-117 §11.116.3. Riley's visor runs a range from
punctuation through kaomoji to a bluescreen, and the consequence is larger than a list of faces: it
is what makes the manual's chosen register actually writable.

**11.117.1 THE PROBLEM DR-117 LEFT BEHIND, WHICH THIS SOLVES.** §11.116.3 rules the manual a vintage
games manual and DR-117's companion document rules that **Riley does not speak in words there**.
Those two together are a constraint most characters could not survive. A wordless mascot whose only
vocabulary is posture and a domain glyph can *point at* things and can say almost nothing about
them; every page would need its body text to carry the whole load, and the illustrations would be
decoration on a technical document rather than a way of reading it.

**A display face removes that limit.** Riley can now react rather than only report, and a reaction
is what makes a manual read cover to cover instead of being consulted.

**11.117.2 Ruled: four registers, and the register is a statement about who is speaking.**

| Register | Examples | Who is speaking |
|---|---|---|
| **Product marks** | `—` for unknown, a domain glyph, a severity mark | **The product**, through Riley |
| **Punctuation** | `?` `!` `&` `!?` | **Riley**, minimally |
| **Grawlix** | `#$%&!` | **Riley**, with feeling |
| **Faces** | `>///<` `>_>` `^_^` `OwO` | **Riley**, fully |

**THE FIRST ROW IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING FROM THE OTHER THREE AND THE MANUAL MUST NOT BLUR
THEM.** A `?` on the visor is Riley being puzzled; a `—` on the visor is a `Finding` reporting that
nobody has supplied a value (G4/CR-114). **One is a joke and one is data**, and a page where a
reader cannot tell which they are looking at has made the product's most careful invariant into a
gag. Product marks are therefore reserved: they appear when Riley is speaking for the product and
never as decoration.

**11.117.3 TWO STATES THAT ARE THEIR OWN THING.**

**The BSOD is Riley failing, and that is not the same as the product not knowing.** The dash means
*nobody has told me*; the bluescreen means *I have fallen over*. The product distinguishes those and
so does the character. It is **manual-only and never on a page carrying domain glyphs** (user,
2026-09-03), which settles by placement a collision that would otherwise have needed a palette
answer: `video.digital` is `#0072B2` and a modern `#0078D7` bluescreen sits almost on top of it, so
a blue visor beside a legend could read as a domain marker. **Placement is the better fix**, because
the classic bluescreen is recognisable precisely by being that blue and greying it out would destroy
the reference this state exists to make.

**The loading face is the third member of that set**, and completing it is why it matters: `—` is
*nobody knows*, the bluescreen is *I have failed*, and loading is *not yet*. Three different answers
that a product which refuses to guess has to be able to give.

**11.117.4 WHAT IT OPENS, WHICH IS THE USER'S REASON FOR ASKING.**

- **Wordless sequential art.** A strip of panels carried by visor states alone can now teach a
  procedure. That is the device a manual of this era used most and the one a symbols-only character
  could not have sustained.
- **A failure-mode voice.** The manual can show the product's own limits honestly, in character,
  without a paragraph apologising for them.
- **Margin and furniture art that says something.** §7.2's page-as-a-building furniture was
  decorative; a visor gives a marginal Riley an opinion about the paragraph beside them.
- **A legible difference between the reference chapters and the teaching chapters.** Product marks
  dominate where the book is a bestiary; faces dominate where it is teaching.

**11.117.5 AND EXPRESSIVENESS IS A BUDGET DRAWN AGAINST THE CHARACTER'S AUTHORITY.** Riley is
*"the competent one ... not a mascot who mugs at the reader"*, and that is the spine every other
decision here hangs from. **A face on every page spends it.** The discipline is therefore stated
rather than left to taste: the wider the register, the rarer it should be, and the reference
chapters should be nearly all product marks.

**THE SAFETY RULE EXTENDS UNCHANGED AND GAINS A CLAUSE.** DR-117 §11.116.3 quotes `CODE-001`,
`CODE-002` and `SIG-001` verbatim and forbids Riley paraphrasing them. To that: **no grawlix and no
face on a page carrying one of those sentences.** Riley may be present, in a product-mark register
and a §4 posture. A bluescreen next to a warning about 100 W damaging a switch would be the book
laughing at the one thing it is most obliged to be straight about.

`docs/19-riley.md` §7.3 carries the vocabulary and the illustrator-facing form of all of this.

### §11.118 DR-119 · The stamp `#310` gates does not exist, so M5-I proves the stronger thing instead

**Ruled 2026-09-04, closing M5-I.** `#310` asks for proof that the
`ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION` stamp is the ONLY thing an error gates, *"via
`ExportSpec.issuedForConstruction`"*. **Measured: neither exists.**
`ExportSpec` appears nowhere in shipped code, no stamp is drawn, and
`ExportRequest` carries `documentJson`, `fontBytes`, `fileName` and
`issuedAt` and nothing else.

**11.118.1 THIS IS THE SECOND TIME A CLAUSE HAS DESCRIBED A FIELD THAT WAS
NEVER BUILT, AND THE PATTERN IS WORTH NAMING.** DR-117's companion work
found AC-058/D1 promising a viewer over `CompatibilityRuleDef.rationale`,
a type from `docs/research/design-data-model.md` that was never built;
M5-F3 had to author the field before it could build the viewer. This is
the same shape: canon §5's export section describes a design in the
present tense, and a chapter written from it reads as though the code
already had the field.

**Neither sentence was wrong about the DESIGN.** Both describe what the
product should do. What neither says is that it does not do it yet, and a
chapter derived from either prices as "wire up the existing thing" work
that is actually "build the thing". **A corpus sentence in the present
tense is a claim about the design, not about the tree**, and pricing a
task off one without reading the code is how both were mis-scoped.

**11.118.2 A VACUOUS ASSERTION IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE SUBSTITUTE.** The
tempting move is to write the test `#310` asks for and let it pass over a
stamp that is not there. It would be green forever and would mean
nothing, which is the exact failure this repository keeps finding in its
own suite: `status_marker_source_test.dart` records a gate that would have
counted zero offenders and passed, and `run_suite.ps1`'s own header
records green-over-nothing as the recurring shape.

**11.118.3 SO THE CLAUSE IS PROVED IN THE STRONGER FORM AVAILABLE TODAY:
NOTHING IS GATED, AND THE TYPE SYSTEM SAYS SO.** `ExportError` is a
sealed class with three arms, `ExportDocumentUnreadable`, `ExportNoRacks`
and `ExportFontMissing`, and **none of them is about a rule.** An
exhaustive `switch` over those arms in
`findings_never_block_export_test.dart` **fails to compile** if a fourth
appears, so whoever adds *"export refused because the project has
errors"* has to come to that file and argue with CR-022 rather than ship
past it.

A source scan is the second cue: `rackpal_export` never mentions
`evaluateDocument`, `kDrcRules`, `AckedFinding` or `blockExportOnErrors`.
**The exporter cannot gate on a finding it never asks for**, which is a
better guarantee than the one `#310` requested and is available now.

**11.118.4 WHAT M6 INHERITS.** When the stamp is built, the gating it
introduces is the FIRST gating the export path will have, and
`findings_never_block_export_test.dart` is where the tightening lands:
the exhaustive switch gains an arm, or the stamp's own predicate gains a
test that it is the only reader of a `Finding`. **M5's clause is
discharged either way**: "no rule prevents a PDF being written" is true
today and the test holds it true.

`#310` is therefore closed as delivered rather than parked, because what
it exists to protect is protected. The narrower assertion it names
becomes M6's, alongside the stamp it is about.

### §11.119 DR-120 · Vantage ships as `ctl.vantage`, and a seventh two-wire bus is the argument for the row rather than against it

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-04**, answering the half of `#692` the
census left open. Legrand's Vantage control system ships as a seeded
signal family. RJ-012 and DR-025 §11.24.3 govern.

**11.119.1 THE REASON IS THE USER'S AND IT IS BETTER THAN "IT IS
MISSING".** The argument given is that Vantage *"is a two wire bus and can
easily be confused for other two wire busses that may exist"*, and the
registry bears that out from the other side: **`ctl` already ships six**
in `ctl.rs485`, `ctl.dali`, `ctl.knx`, `ctl.cresnet`, `ctl.lutron_qs` and
`ctl.contact`.

So the crowding is not an objection to the row, it IS the row's case. A
Vantage run drawn as an unnamed two-wire cable is a run somebody lands on
the wrong controller, and the six neighbours are exactly what makes that
easy. **This is trade knowledge and it overturned the framing the census
was heading for**, which was "one of the two names already ships, so how
much of the rest is real?".

**11.119.2 A DECOMPOSITION GAP, NOT AN §8.3 AMENDMENT**, on `#692`'s own
test: *"filling out a vocabulary the roadmap already promises is a gap,
and adding a new class of signal is an amendment."* The `ctl` domain
exists, its hue and glyph are settled, and a control bus is the class of
thing it holds. Nothing moves between release bands and no scope list
changes.

**11.119.3 WHAT THE ROW ACTUALLY COST, because `#692` asked for that and
the answer is not "a row".** The (dash, weight) pair is **hand-authored
into four places** by DR-010's design: the Dart seed, `tools/pal1_check.py`,
`docs/catalog/seed-devices.md` §4.3/§4.4 and canon §6.2.5, with
`docs/01-domain.md` carrying a fifth, prose copy. The family COUNT was
written out at **twenty-three sites across twelve files**. The four
checked-in starters embed the registries and were regenerated.

**ONE OF THE TWENTY-FOUR WAS NOT A `55`.** `seed_registries_test.dart`
asserted `hasLength(54)` on a copy with one family removed, so a sweep
looking for the count missed it and the suite failed on a number that had
been correct. It is now `b.signalFamilies.length - 1`: **the property was
"one shorter", and writing that arithmetic out as a literal is what made
it a second copy.**

**11.119.4 THE CONNECTOR WAS INFERRED, WAS FLAGGED AS THE FIELD TO
CORRECT FIRST, AND WAS CORRECTED WITHIN THE DAY.** It shipped as
`conn.screw_terminal`, copied from `ctl.dali` on the reasoning that both
are polarity-flexible two-wire buses, and the seed's comment said in as
many words that it was the one value not taken from a stated fact.

**The user's correction: Vantage joins the bus with Wago or wire nut
connections.** So there is no connector at all. The conductors are
spliced, which is `power.ac_hardwired`'s situation exactly, and it takes
that family's connector: **`conn.hardwired`**.

`conn.unterminated` was the near miss and is wrong for a reason worth
keeping. It is what `structure.undetermined` and `structure.pathway` use,
and it describes a STATE, a cable end nobody has landed yet, rather than
a method. A wire-nutted Vantage drop is finished, not unterminated.

**`CON-001` was never at risk either way**, which is the only comfortable
part: an empty `matesWith` makes that rule SKIP (G4, `#255`), and neither
connector declares one. The cost of the wrong value was a lie in the
model rather than a false spring-back, which is the harder kind to
notice.

**11.119.5 THE DASH IS `9,3,1.5,3` AT 1.00×**, the free slot in this
domain's dash-dot run (DALI 5, RS-232 6, KNX 7, DMX 8, Cresnet 10). PAL-1
passes at 56 families over 400 in-band cross-domain pairs.
`vantage_family_test.dart` pins the property that matters rather than the
values: **no other `ctl` family renders identically**, checked pairwise,
because colour is per domain (CR-078) and on a greyscale print the dash
and weight are all a reader has.

**The rest of `#692` stays open.** This ruling adds the family the user
named and asked for; the gap LIST is still with the domain reviewer, and
whether anything else follows is M5-H2's to answer.

**11.119.6 F19, THE LOAD-CONTROLLING KEYPAD, AND WHY IT IS NOT A VANTAGE
DEVICE.** The user's second and third facts: Vantage keypads are typically
1-gang, and *"keypad voltage entirely depends on if it controls a load or
not. LV keypads do not, HV keypads are directly wired to loads."*

**The gang fact needed nothing.** Gang count lives on `Outlet`, not on the
device or the outlet template, and `outlet.keypad` already reasons that
the keypad fills the gang itself, which is why its 22/4 drop is a
euroblock at zero keystone cells. The fact confirms the model rather than
correcting it.

**THE VOLTAGE FACT IS A PORT SET, NOT A FIELD, AND NOT A BRAND.** What
makes a keypad high voltage is that line voltage arrives at it, which is
`F03`'s shape exactly: the motorised screen takes a trigger AND a
hardwired feed. So `F19` is the LOAD-CONTROLLING keypad and carries the
same three bus alternates `F13` does, because Lutron and Crestron build
both kinds too. A Vantage-specific device would have owed a Lutron and a
Crestron sibling immediately.

Supply only, no switched output (the user's call): the load is drawn as
its own run where a sheet needs it, which is what `F03` already does.
**No power figures**, because nobody has measured one and inventing a
nameplate for a device whose point is that it sits on a branch circuit
would put a fabricated number into `PWR-001`'s arithmetic (G4, AC-039's
neighbour).

**11.119.7 CR-061's NUMBER MOVES TO 49, AND ITS REASONING SURVIVES
INTACT.** That ruling states *"v1 ships 48 templates: 30 rack-side and 18
field-side"*, and its argument is that 48 *"sits mid-band in the confirmed
40-55"*. **Forty-nine is still mid-band**, so what CR-061 decided is
unchanged and only the integer moves. This is recorded in §12 rather than
edited in place.

**AND CR-061'S OTHER SENTENCE WAS ALREADY FALSE.** It says the count *"is
stated in exactly one place, `docs/catalog.md`, and no prose in any
document states a number."* Moving 48 to 49 touched **thirteen sites
across eleven files**, including four comments in `lib/`, six test
assertions, and canon itself twice. The single-source discipline the
ruling set was never held, which is why a one-device change is a
twenty-file diff. The count is not now consolidated: that would be its own
piece of work, and pretending otherwise by fixing three of thirteen is
worse than recording the state.

**11.119.8 THE ALTERNATES-AS-PORTS PATTERN HAS A STANDING COST, AND IT IS
NOW MEASURED.** Giving `F13` a third bus alternate moved the schematic
perf baseline from 2,371 symbol ops to 2,403. The arithmetic is exact:
the 300-link fixture holds sixteen keypads, and sixteen devices times two
ops for one more vector pin is the whole +32. Label ops did not move at
all, which is what says this is a port being drawn rather than the layout
shifting.

Every seeded keypad now draws all three buses whether the job uses one or
not, and a fourth alternate would cost another 32. **The alternative
exists and is not taken here**: P4's `TemplateRole` variants already model
"one device, several configurations" for `V06`. Whether the keypad should
become role variants rather than accumulate ports is a real question and
is left open rather than answered by drift.

### §11.120 DR-121 · P4 gains a second variant axis, because a keypad has one bus and the catalogue was saying it had three

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-04**, and it is an **§8.3 amendment**:
P4's table is a ruling about what a parametric variant may vary, and this
changes it. Nothing moves between release bands, so roadmap §2 is
untouched.

**11.120.1 THE CONFLICT, STATED BEFORE IT WAS ROUTED AROUND.** P4 lists
under *may not vary*: **"signal family of any port"** and **"connector
type"**. A keypad's bus changes both, `ctl.cresnet` on `conn.phoenix_4`
becoming `ctl.vantage` on `conn.hardwired`. The request was for
`TemplateRole` variants; that enum is closed and says why, since P4 uses
the role parameter *"exactly twice"* and both uses are extender halves.
Adding a bus to it would have made that sentence false and put a keypad's
wiring and an extender's direction on one axis.

**So the rule is amended rather than reinterpreted.** The alternative was
to add the axis quietly under a name P4 did not forbid, which is how a
ruling becomes decoration.

**11.120.2 THE ARGUMENT P4 COULD NOT HAVE MADE: THE CATALOGUE IS
GENERIC.** Every seeded template ships `manufacturer: 'Generic'` by
ruling, and `seed_catalog_test.dart` gates it. So `F13` is not a part
number, it is **"a keypad"**, and which bus it speaks is a wiring choice
on one archetype rather than a different product. P4's forbidden row is
right about the case it was written for, where the family IS the product:
a matrix that is HDMI or SDI is two products. It does not reach an
archetype whose family is a site decision.

**Scoped to the two keypads** (`F13`, `F19`), because that is where the
cost was measured. A third device registers in `busesFor` rather than
accumulating ports.

**11.120.3 WHAT THIS ENDED.** Before it, a keypad carried every bus it
might speak as a separate port. DR-120 §11.119.8 measured the drawing at
32 symbol ops per alternate, but **the model was worse than the drawing**:
a real keypad has one bus connection, and the catalogue said it had three.

**THE FIXTURE PROVED IT, BY FAILING.** Giving the keypad a single bus port
broke `schematic_fixture.dart` outright with *"KEY-1 ran out of ports"*,
because it had been wiring TWO home runs into each of sixteen keypads and
`claim` was handing the second one an alternate. That second cable was
never buildable. It existed because three ports existed.

The fixture now holds **thirty-two keypads with one bus cable each**,
still exactly 300 links. The symbol baseline went 2,403 to 2,515, and
**the old number was cheaper because the fixture was wrong**: a smaller
symbol layer bought by drawing a house that cannot be built is not a
saving.

**11.120.4 THE MACHINERY IS THE ROLE AXIS'S, WHICH IS THE POINT.**
`ControlBus`, `busVariantTemplateId`, `busesFor`, `resolveTemplateBus`
and `buildSeedBusVariants` mirror the role five exactly: the shipped bus
keeps the bare catalog id, derived bodies live outside
`buildSeedCatalog()`, and the variant id carries the axis so no `.rmpj`
gains a field (CR-117 untouched, AC-041's snapshot still resolves).

**The catalogue count does not move.** A variant is not a template, and
`buildSeedCatalog()` still returns 49.

**ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE ROLE AXIS, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.** V06's halves
are TRANSCRIBED because they are not a mechanical flip, seven ports
becoming six. The keypad bodies differ in exactly one port, so all six
come from one `_keypad` builder: computing them is what stops a Vantage
keypad drifting from a Cresnet one in a field nobody meant to change.

**11.120.5 THE PORT KEYS DID NOT MOVE**, and that was a constraint rather
than a preference. `F13` already shipped `cresnet` and `qs.link` as keys,
a document may hold either, and `connect_rules_test.dart`'s real-catalog
case resolves `portKey: 'cresnet'` on a seeded keypad. A tidier
`bus.link` would have moved bytes for nothing and broken that test to no
purpose.

### §11.121 DR-122 · A signal family may be CLONED, which answers RJ-012's objection instead of overruling it

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-05**, and it is an **§8.3 amendment**: v1
grows a surface RJ-012 refused, so roadmap §2.1 gains a paragraph and this
section records what moved. No milestone is renumbered and nothing leaves
v1.

**11.121.1 WHAT RJ-012 REFUSED, AND WHY THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT.** It rejected
*"a full registry authoring UI"* as *"a database admin tool wearing a
product's clothes"*, and gave signal families their own reason: *"a signal
family is not a thing a user should be inventing casually: it carries
direction defaults, topology, length limits, and rule applicability, and a
hand-rolled one produces silently wrong validation."*

**THAT OBJECTION IS TECHNICAL AND IT STANDS.** A family drives
`defaultDirection`, `defaultTopology`, `defaultConnector` and
`acceptedFamilies`, which are read by `TOP-003`, `DIR-001`, `SIG-002` and
`CON-001`. A person who picks the wrong topology does not get *missing*
validation. They get **confident wrong validation**, which is worse than the
gap they were working around, and worse in the specific way this product
sells itself against: `SIG-001` exists to stop somebody destroying a switch.

**11.121.2 SO NOTHING IS HAND-ROLLED: A NEW FAMILY IS A CLONE.** It is
derived from a shipped family and never authored from blank. The clone
inherits domain, direction, topology, connector and every field a rule
reads; the author renames it, sets a `shortTag`, and chooses a dash and a
weight. **What RJ-012 feared is not reachable, because there is no blank
form to reach it from.**

**MEASURED AGAINST THE CASE THAT PROVED THE NEED.** `ctl.vantage` (DR-120)
would have been *clone Cresnet, rename, change the connector to
`conn.hardwired`*. Three acts, every one of them a fact the user already
stated in a sentence, and not one of them a topology decision. **The
family the corpus was missing is exactly the family a clone expresses
well**, which is the evidence this shape is the right one rather than the
convenient one.

**11.121.3 WHAT IS STILL REFUSED.** RJ-012's other two limbs are untouched:
**no connector-type editor** and **no colour-scheme editor**. AC-011 is
untouched: **no user-authored validation rules**, because rules are Dart
functions keyed by `ruleId` and a UI for them would make the app an
interpreter for user input. A cloned family reaches existing rules through
existing data and adds no rule, so AC-040's cap of 28 is not approached.

**`refused_surfaces_test.dart` KEEPS ITS SIGNAL-FAMILY ARM UNTIL THE CHAPTER
THAT BUILDS THE EDITOR REMOVES IT**, and removing it is that chapter's
visible act. **A ruling that permits what the tree still refuses is the
correct state between an amendment and its build**: the gate is ahead of the
corpus rather than wrong, because nothing has been built. That file's own
header asks for exactly this, saying a later chapter *"cannot build one in
good faith without a test going red first"*.

**11.121.4 PAL-1 MOVES FROM CI INTO THE APP, FOR THIS CASE ONLY.** PAL-1 is
a gate over the **shipped** families' rendered greyscale values, and a
user-created family cannot be CI-gated because it does not exist when CI
runs. **The editor therefore runs PAL-1's own arithmetic live and refuses a
dash and weight that collide inside the domain.**

This requires PAL-1's rules to live in `rackpal_core` rather than only in
`tools/pal1_check.py`, with the gate and the editor reading one
implementation. **Two implementations of a legibility rule is how the
printed sheet and the CI check come to disagree**, which is the argument
CR-021 makes about the rule catalogue and M5-A made about the connector
mating matrix, applied a third time.

**CR-078 IS UNTOUCHED AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A PROMISE.** Colour lives
on the **domain**, never the family, and a clone inherits its parent's
domain. **So a clone cannot introduce a new hue even in principle.** What it
varies is dash and weight, which is precisely what AC-054 makes the
distinguishing channel for a type within a domain.

**11.121.5 DR-025'S REFUSAL SURVIVES, AS A CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN AN
EXEMPTION.** `@signal=` refuses an unknown value (§11.24.3) on the ground
that families are catalog-updated where media types are user-extensible.
**Clone-from-existing does not disturb it**: a family cannot be conjured
from a typed token, because a clone needs a parent that a person chose. So
the modifier still refuses, and RJ-009's *"an unmatched value creates a
media type"* still has no counterpart here. **The asymmetry that DR-025 was
built on is preserved by the shape of the surface rather than by a rule
saying so**, which is the more durable of the two.

**11.121.6 STORAGE IS BOTH, AND THE PROJECT COPY IS AUTHORITATIVE FOR THE
DRAWING.** A cloned family is written into `doc.registries.signalFamilies`
**and** onto the user's shelf. Neither replaces the other.

**THE USER'S OWN FRAMING IS THE PRECEDENT: RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 saves
custom scenery objects into the save file**, so a save opens on a machine
that never had them. That is AC-041 and DR-103's copy-on-place argument
arriving from outside this project, and it settles the direction: **the
document must never depend on a shelf**, or a drawing changes meaning when
it crosses machines, which docs/02's rejected-alternatives table names as
what embedded snapshots refuse. The shelf copy exists so the family follows
the person to the next job; the project copy exists so the file is
self-contained. **CR-117 needs nothing new**: `signalFamilies` is already a
serialized map with a round-trip arm.

**11.121.7 THE CLAIM THAT SURVIVES, RESTATED.** RJ-012 narrowed the
extensibility claim to *"media types and colours are user-extensible;
signal families and connector types are catalog-updated"*. It becomes:
**media types and colours are user-extensible, signal families are
user-extensible BY CLONE, and connector types remain catalog-updated.** The
claim is still narrowed and still true, which was RJ-012's actual
requirement, and §12.30 records the eight derived sites the old sentence
was written at.

### §11.122 DR-123 · An authored device reaches the shelf, and the project keeps its copy

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-05**, an **§8.3 amendment** and the
companion to DR-122. Nothing leaves v1 and no milestone is renumbered.

**11.122.1 THE CENSUS CAME FIRST, AND IT CUT THE SCOPE TO A THIRD OF THE
REQUEST.** The ask was that an authored device save to a master list, that
imported `.rmda` files join that list, and that export offer a choice of
devices. **Two of the three already ship**, from M4-N (§5.3.24 of docs/12):

| Asked for | State |
|---|---|
| Export offers a choice of devices | **Built.** `library_io_dialogs.dart` renders a `CheckboxListTile` per template, everything ticked when it opens so *pack the lot* stays one click |
| An imported library joins the list | **Built.** `loadLibraryShelf` reads EVERY library on the shelf, and `#242` made the palette list them all at once with source chips and a per-library filter |
| An authored device joins the list | **MISSING, and this ruling is that gap** |

**This is why the census precedes the pricing.** A ruling written from the
request would have re-specified two shipped subsystems, and the derived
document would then have described a rebuild nobody did. §1's caveat on
every decomposition names the same hazard and this is the fourth time it
has paid.

**11.122.2 THE GAP, STATED AS A MEASUREMENT.**
`SaveTemplateToProjectCommand` writes into `RackDocument.templates` and
nowhere else. A device authored in the builder therefore **lives in that
project only** until somebody deliberately exports an `.rmda`.

**So requirement 2, *"author the long tail once and use it everywhere"*, is
satisfied for devices that arrive by IMPORT and not for devices the user
CREATES**, which is backwards, and is the sentence
`device_builder_actions.dart` has been apologising for since M4-D. M4-N
closed the import half and read as though it had closed both.

**11.122.3 SAVE WRITES BOTH, AND THE PROJECT COPY IS AUTHORITATIVE FOR THE
DRAWING.** The project keeps its embedded snapshot exactly as AC-041 and
DR-103 already require. The shelf gains a copy so the device follows the
person to the next job. **Neither replaces the other.**

**THE USER'S PRECEDENT IS RollerCoaster Tycoon 2**, whose save file carries
the custom scenery objects it uses, so a save opens on a machine that never
had them. That is copy-on-place arriving from outside this project, and it
decides the direction: **the document must never resolve a device out of a
shelf**, which docs/02's rejected-alternatives table names as *"a live
library reference"* and prices as *"drawings that change silently across
machines"*. DR-103 §11.102 is untouched, `templateRef{templateId, version,
contentHash}` is untouched, and no `.rmpj` changes shape.

**ONLY AUTHORED DEVICES**, which is the user's own boundary: *"custom
devices (beyond the archetypes)"*. The 50 seeded templates ship with the
application and need no shelf copy. A fork of a seeded template **is**
authored, carries `derivedFrom`, and goes to both.

**11.122.4 THE SHELF WRITE IS NOT A COMMAND, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING A
READER WILL NOT EXPECT.** AC-014 makes the command stack the single
mutation gate **for the document**, and the shelf is not the document: it
is a directory under the data root, shared by every project this person
opens. A shelf write therefore does not enter the `UndoStack`.

**SO UNDOING THE SAVE DOES NOT UN-SHELVE THE DEVICE**, and that asymmetry
is deliberate rather than an oversight. `Ctrl+Z` is scoped to the drawing a
person is looking at, and reaching out of it to delete from a personal
library is a surprise in the more damaging direction: **an undo that
silently removes an asset from a library the user has been building across
jobs is the loss they will not forgive** (DR-015 §11.15.4 makes the same
argument about `.rmdev`). Withdrawing a device from the shelf is its own
act in the library surface.

**AND A SHELF FAILURE IS A NOTICE, NEVER A REFUSAL.** The project save
happens FIRST and completes on its own terms; the shelf copy follows and
may fail on a session with no data root, an absent directory or an
unwritable one. All three are states `loadLibraryShelf` already answers as
an empty shelf without throwing, and the same posture holds for the write:
**a person must never lose an authored device because a library directory
was unavailable.**

**11.122.5 PROVENANCE IS KEPT, SO ONE LIST IS A VIEW AND NOT A
FLATTENING.** The user's answer was one master list **with** provenance.
The palette keeps badging every row by source, and an authored device lands
in a library that is the person's own rather than in an unattributed pool.
**Discarding the source chips would make *"where did this device come
from"* unanswerable at exactly the moment it matters**, because DR-101's
`templateIdFor` derives an id from the display name identically on every
machine, so two libraries holding an `HDMI Matrix 16x16` **collide by
construction**. DR-103 §11.102.3's three cases decide that collision with
no prompt and apply to the shelf write unchanged: the key is free, the key
holds an identical body, or the key holds a different body and a fresh id
is minted at v1.

**11.122.6 WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** It does not make the shelf a sync
target, does not add a second format, does not touch `.rmdx` or `.rmda`,
and does not give a library a version chain. It is one write, in one
caller, plus the surface that names where the write went.

### §11.123 DR-124 · An IR emitter output carries two conductors, and the catalogue had no way to say so

**Found by the user on 2026-09-05, during the M5-H2 domain review**, and
fixed the same day. **Not an §8.3 amendment**: no scope moves, roadmap §2
is untouched, and the number below was already the design's.

**11.123.1 THE TRADE FACT.** A dual-head IR flasher is **one 3.5 mm plug
with two heads**: SnapOne ships the Episode `IRF-2`, and Control4's
Composer Pro models it directly by allowing more than one connection on a
single port. **Three or more is not a bigger flasher**; it needs a second
port or an IR expansion block, which is its own physical device with its
own ports. **So `2` is a physical bound and not a cap somebody chose.**

A splitter needs no exemption, because a splitter *is* a device and gets
modelled as one. The dual-head flasher is the case that is genuinely one
connection carrying two heads.

**11.123.2 THE DESIGN DOCUMENT WAS RIGHT AND HAD BEEN SINCE M0.**
`docs/catalog/seed-devices.md` declares `"maxConnections": 2` on
`ir.out.1`. Somebody knew this at the start.

**THE CODE COULD NOT EXPRESS IT.** `catalog_ports.dart`'s `p()`, which
every seeded port is built through, **had no `maxConnections` parameter at
all**, so all 727 seed ports took `PortDef`'s default of `1` **by
construction rather than by anybody's choice**. `effectiveMaxConnections`
widens a default `1` only on a `busNode` pin, and an IR output is
`PortDirection.source`, so nothing rescued it downstream.

**`TOP-003` IS TIER 1, WHICH IS WHY THIS MATTERED.** docs/02 §5's tier
table gives T1's escape as *"None. There is nothing to escape to."* So the
second head of a legal, shipping, commonplace device was refused at the
gesture on **every IR output in the catalogue**, with no
`[ Connect anyway ]`. **The product could not draw a system it ships a
catalog for.**

**11.123.3 THE RULE IS NOT AT FAULT AND IS NOT CHANGED.** `TOP-003` reads
`effectiveMaxConnections` and honours a declared value above one. The
catalogue was what could not speak. `p()` gains the parameter, the **seven
`ctl.ir_emitter` source ports** across `catalog_control.dart` and
`catalog_video.dart` declare `2`, and nothing about the rule, the tier or
the evaluator moves.

`catalog_field.dart`'s `pigtail` is deliberately **not** among the seven:
it is `ctl.ir_receiver` carried on a `source` pin, which is a receiver's
return leg to the controller rather than a flasher jack.

**11.123.4 THE THIRD INSTANCE OF DR-119'S PATTERN, AND THE WORST OF THE
THREE.** `connect_target.dart` argued its own design from the missing
number, in the present tense:

> `2` on an IR emitter output (docs/catalog/seed-devices.md's `ir.out.1`)
> is a real, authored bound and this must not widen it to infinity.

**It was authored nowhere in code.** After
`CompatibilityRuleDef.rationale` (M5-F3) and
`ExportSpec.issuedForConstruction` (M5-I), this is the third time a
present-tense corpus sentence has been read as a statement about the tree.
**It is the worst of the three because the document was RIGHT**: the other
two described things nobody had decided to build, and this one described a
decision that was made and then silently lost between a design document
and a builder signature, with a tier-1 rule enforcing the loss.

**11.123.5 THE AC-051 PAIR COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT, AND THAT IS THE
GENERALISABLE PART.** `TOP-003`'s known-bad and near-miss both build a
**synthetic** port and pass the bound in explicitly, as
`connectPair(avrMax: 4)`. Both halves passed, forever, while the shipped
catalogue refused a legal connection.

**A rule exercised only against ports the test itself authored is a rule
tested against its own assumptions.** That is the house rule about
asserting the artifact rather than the mechanism, arriving from a new
direction: the fixtures were not wrong about `TOP-003`, they were wrong
about *what `TOP-003` runs on*.

`connect_rules_test.dart` now carries two cases over the real catalogue: a
census that every IR emitter output declares `2`, guarded against vacuity
by requiring the census to find some; and a behavioural case where a second
head lands on a seeded `V01` and a third is refused naming `2 of 2`.
**Whether every tier-1 rule owes a shipped-catalogue case is a real
question and is left open rather than answered by this ruling**, because it
is a gate change and belongs to whoever prices it.

**11.123.6 WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT M5-H.** The domain review had not
finished, and had already produced a defect that sixteen green gates,
3,946 core tests and a 56-fixture AC-051 corpus could not see. **That is
the clause's whole argument, paid before the clause closed**, and it is the
second time this project has been corrected by trade knowledge it could not
derive: DR-120's Vantage census was the first.

### §11.124 DR-125 · The M5-H2 review's twelve findings, and the four that were not what they looked like

**Returned by the user on 2026-09-05**, mid-review, as one batch. Every
finding was censused against the tree before it was priced, and **four of
the twelve turned out to be something other than what the ticket said**,
which is the same rate §1's decomposition caveat has been recording all
milestone.

**11.124.1 THE DISPOSITIONS.**

| # | Finding | What it turned out to be |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `DIR-001` and eARC | **Already correct, and the fact CONFIRMS the model.** Exactly two seeded ports declare a return channel and they are a matched pair: a TV's `hdmi.1` is `sink` + `ARC`, a soundbar's `hdmi.out.main` is **`source`** + `eARC`. That is the reviewer's own point, that an eARC port is a source in the HDMI spec, already in the catalogue. Directions are opposite so `DIR-001` never fires, and an explicit eARC exception exists for the same-direction case |
| 3 | `DIR-003` and IR | **A real defect, held for a decision** (§11.124.3) |
| 8 | `NET-001` and PoE draw | **The model was already right and the sentence was not.** `_ceilingFor` prefers a stated `watts` and falls back to the IEEE class ceiling, which is the conservative direction and the only defensible one for a PSE. But **no seeded PD states any watts**, so every figure is a ceiling, and the message presented it as a draw. Now named as an estimate |
| 9 | `RCK-003`'s band | **Architectural, not a threshold** (§11.124.2) |
| 10 | `RCK-012` / `RCK-013` wording | Accepted as stated. Both sentences now say *"may require adjustment of the rack ears"* |
| 6 | `LEN-001` / `LEN-002` usage | **Not a defect: a usage expectation, recorded as one.** The reviewer predicts these stay quiet until plan-view run estimation exists, because a residential run near 100 m is uncommon and the case that reaches it is a second building, where the trade answer is fibre or a wireless bridge |
| 1, 4, 7 | Offer an adapter / a power strip | **One feature, three-quarters built** (§11.124.4) |
| 5 | `ELE-006` and speaker taps | `maxTapWatts` exists on the model; a tap SELECTOR and CV-to-Low-Z switching do not. A real modelling gap, unpriced |
| 11 | `PLC-001` and cabinet head ends | Expressible as `OffRackPlacement` with a `mountNote`, but crude, and the reviewer's point is that it is the COMMON case rather than an edge. Unpriced |
| 12 | `CODE-002` surfacing | Accepted; unpriced. A code-adjacent finding wants more than a row in a panel |

**11.124.2 `RCK-003`'S BANDS NEVER REACHED A USER, AND NOBODY HAD
CHECKED.** The reviewer asked for the advisory to move from 85% to 60%,
with a reason from the job: a 42U rack at 85% of a 1,000 lb rating is
around 850 lb, already enough for the casters to mark a floor, so a notice
that arrives then arrives after the fourth amplifier was specified rather
than before it.

**Measured while implementing it, every `RCK-003` finding surfaces as
`warning` in every band, and always has.** `evaluateDocument` builds its
`Finding` with `severity: resolved`, where `resolved` is
`projectSeverity(ruleId, settings)`, and **the predicate's own severity is
discarded**. The `advisory` that `ruleRck003` has set since M5-E has never
been seen by anybody.

| docs/02 §5.3 | *"warning (advisory at 85%)"*, since M0 |
| The predicate | Implements two severities |
| The evaluator | Flattens both to the catalogue default |
| The AC-051 pair | Asserts WHICH RULE fires, never how loudly |

**THE FLATTENING IS DELIBERATE AND WAS RIGHT ONCE.** M5-E records
`LEN-001` proposing its own `advisory` on a good argument, and the
evaluator overwriting it because *"that argument is not in the
catalogue"*: a predicate choosing a second severity is inventing a rule
(CR-021). **`RCK-003` is the opposite case**, where the catalogue row
itself authorises the band, and the evaluator has no way to tell the two
apart.

**Ruled: the catalogue authorises the band.** `RuleMeta` gains an explicit
banded-severity declaration and `evaluateDocument` honours a predicate's
severity **only** for a rule whose row declares one. `LEN-001` stays
overwritten because its row declares a single severity; `RCK-003` is
obeyed because its row will declare three. **CR-021 is preserved exactly**:
the catalogue still decides what a rule may say, and a predicate still
cannot invent it.

The bands are **advisory at 60%, warning at 85%, error over capacity**.
The `error` band blocks nothing (CR-022/G3); what it buys is that a loaded
rack stops reading as a note somebody scrolls past.

**THAT WORK IS NOT IN THIS COMMIT**, deliberately. It needs a `RuleMeta`
field, an evaluator change and a docs/02 row, and landing it beside three
unrelated sentence fixes would make one commit that cannot be reverted in
parts.

**11.124.3 `DIR-003` KEYS ON THE ONE FACT THAT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE.**
Its catalogue summary says *"`PortDef.pinoutVariant` exists solely to
detect it"*. The predicate matches **families only**, and `pinoutVariant`
is read by no rule anywhere in the tree.

The catalogue itself is unambiguous, and censused it separates the two
cases three ways:

| Emitter jack | `ctl.ir_emitter` · `source` · `conn.3_5mm_ts` · `mono-tip-sleeve` |
| Receiver jack | `ctl.ir_receiver` · `sink` · `conn.3_5mm_trs` · `xantech-stereo` |
| Receiver pigtail | `ctl.ir_receiver` · **`source`** · `xantech-stereo` |

**So the data to discriminate exists and the rule ignores all of it.** The
reviewer's fact is that an IR receiver *"can be either"* a window or a
jack and *"some devices feature both"*, which means family-matching fires
an `error` spring-back on a connection that is correct and everyday.
**Held for a decision on which pairings are legal**, because that is a
trade question and not a code one.

**11.124.4 THE ADAPTER PROMPT IS ONE FEATURE AND IT IS MOSTLY BUILT.**
`SIG-002`, `CON-001` and `PWR-003` all asked for the same thing: offer to
create the part that fixes it, and wire it in. `insert_receiver.dart`
already does exactly that for `SIG-001`, in three commands under one undo
entry through `TxnScope`.

**Its own header already names the interaction**, which is why this is a
generalisation rather than an invention: the `SIG-001` remedy leaves its
second link open because the receiver's HDMI end *"fails `SIG-002` and
`CON-001` together"*. Unpriced, and it wants a ruling of its own.

**11.124.5 THE REVIEW'S VALUE, MEASURED.** Before this batch the review
had already produced DR-124. This batch adds a defect nobody had checked
in `RCK-003`, a rule keyed on the wrong field in `DIR-003`, and a message
that presented a ceiling as a measurement in `NET-001`. **Three of those
four are the same shape**: a document stating a behaviour, code doing
something else, and a test suite that asserted around the gap rather than
through it. **The AC-051 corpus is complete at 28/28 and saw none of
them**, because a pair proves a rule fires, not that it fires correctly.

### §11.125 DR-126 · `DIR-003` was never keyed on the wrong field: the catalogue was calling two signals by one name

**DR-125 §11.124.3 held this for a decision and framed it wrongly**, in
terms this ruling has to correct before it can answer. That paragraph says
the predicate *"matches families only"* and that *"the data to discriminate
exists and the rule ignores all of it"*, over a three-row census of the
emitter jack, the receiver jack and the receiver pigtail.

**The census was a row short, and the missing row is the whole case.**

| Port | Family | Dir | Connector | Pinout | Bank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C02.emitter.N` | `ctl.ir_emitter` | source | `conn.3_5mm_ts` | `mono-tip-sleeve` | `emitterOut` |
| `C02.ir.rx.N` | `ctl.ir_receiver` | sink | `conn.3_5mm_trs` | `xantech-stereo` | `rxIn` |
| **`V01.ir.in`, and ten more like it** | **`ctl.ir_receiver`** | **sink** | **`conn.3_5mm_trs`** | **`xantech-stereo`** | `control` |

Rows two and three are **identical on every field any rule reads**. Row two
is the hazard and row three is a matrix, an AVR, a cable box or a TV: the
thing an emitter head is put on, which is what an IR system is for. So no
re-keying of the predicate could have separated them, `pinoutVariant`
least of all, and the fix DR-125 imagined was unavailable.

**11.125.1 THE MECHANISM WAS WRITTEN DOWN IN THE REGISTRY THE WHOLE TIME.**
`seed_registries.dart` states it beside the two family definitions:

> receivers are tip = signal, ring = GND, sleeve = +12 V; emitters are tip
> = IR in, sleeve = GND. Plugging an emitter into a receiver jack destroys
> the emitter and can damage the supply.

*The ring and sleeve in that quotation are reversed: a receiver jack is ring +12 V, sleeve GND
(DR-221 §11.220.3, §12.45). The quotation keeps the words the registry had.*

**A two-conductor TS plug entering a three-conductor jack bridges ring to
sleeve.** That is the damage, and it happens because the jack SUPPLIES
+12 V, not because the device at the other end is called a receiver. So
the discriminating fact is **whether the jack is powered**, and the
catalogue had no way to say it because it filed powered and unpowered
sinks under one family.

**11.125.2 RULED: the passive device input is its own family.**
`ctl.ir_direct` ships, and eleven port sites move to it. `ctl.ir_receiver`
keeps its id and narrows to what it always meant, **the powered
receiver-eye circuit**: a block's RX inputs, a block's `IR IN`, and the eye
pigtail that draws the supply.

**THE PREDICATE DOES NOT CHANGE, AND THAT IS THE POINT.**
`_irEmitterIntoReceiver` asks for one `ctl.ir_emitter` and one
`ctl.ir_receiver` and is correct as written. It fired on the everyday case
because the everyday case was wearing the hazard's family name. **A rule
reported as keyed on the wrong field turned out to be a rule reading a
field that lied**, which is a different defect with a different fix, and
DR-125 would have had us edit the one thing here that was already right.

**11.125.3 THE BLOCK'S `IR IN` IS POWERED, ON A TRADE ANSWER.** Censused,
`C02.ir.in.processor` was the only port whose side was not obvious. The
answer is that it depends on the unit: an RTI head end carries +12 V and
the IR signal on a four-wire Phoenix bus, while others take a supply from
an adapter and present a 3.5 mm input that will accept either a receiver
eye or an emitter lead directly. **None is self-powered**, because an
emitter output has only enough current for two diodes, which is DR-124's
`maxConnections: 2` arriving from the other direction.

**Assume powered.** The seeded `C02` therefore files `ir.in.processor`
with the RX jacks. This is deliberately the conservative side of a fact
that varies by model: the rule springs the wire back and always offers
`[ Connect anyway ]` (CR-017), so a false hesitation on a block that
tolerates a direct emitter lead costs one click, and the opposite error
costs an emitter and possibly a supply.

**11.125.4 THE SPLIT EXPOSED A SECOND DEFECT IN THE ELEVEN.** They declare
`xantech-stereo`, the powered pinout, on jacks this ruling has just
established are not powered, and `conn.3_5mm_trs` on jacks an emitter's TS
plug goes straight into. Both are corrected with the re-family:
`ctl.ir_direct` defaults to `conn.3_5mm_ts` and `mono-tip-sleeve`, so an
emitter output and a device input agree on family, connector and pinout,
and the direct-connect cable is the same object at both ends.

**11.125.5 THE ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED, AND ITS BEST ARGUMENT.**
The eleven could have been re-familied to `ctl.ir_emitter` with
`dir: sink`, adding no family at all. The predicate would then be correct
for the same reason, PAL-1 would face no thirteenth `ctl` pattern, and the
argument is strong: `SignalFamilyDef` answers *"what IS this signal"*, and
an emitter output and a device input carry one signal, so a second family
for the far end of one cable is the mirror of the error being fixed.

**It was rejected on the legend.** A family's `displayName` prints on
T0.01 and in the inspector, and `IR emitter (flasher)` on a television's
`IR IN` row is a device name on a port that is not that device. Renaming
the family to cover both ends would leave the id `ctl.ir_emitter`
describing half of what it holds, and an id is in the file format
(CR-117), so it cannot be renamed without a migration. **Two names that
are each right beat one name that is right at one end.**

**11.125.6 PAL-1's OWN HISTORY IS THE REASON THIS IS MEASURED AND NOT
ASSERTED.** `tools/pal1_check.py` records that PAL-1 was called *"verified
clear"* three times over a palette holding fourteen collisions, **the two
IR families among them**. The thirteenth `ctl` pattern is therefore chosen
by running the gate, not by reading the table it checks.

**11.125.7 SILENCING `DIR-003` WOULD HAVE BOUGHT A DIFFERENT SENTENCE AND
NOTHING ELSE**, and this was found by the first run of this ruling's own
test rather than by reading the code. With the eleven re-familied, the
everyday emitter-into-a-television connection still sprang back, now
carrying `SIG-002: does not accept ctl.ir_emitter`.

`acceptsFamily` is `signalFamily == family || acceptedFamilies.contains
(family)`, and **`catalog_ports.dart`'s `p()` had no parameter for the
second limb**, so all 727 seeded ports carried an empty list BY
CONSTRUCTION rather than by anybody's choice. `SIG-002` therefore refuses
every cross-family pairing in the shipped catalogue, and nobody noticed
because almost every seeded connection is same-family. **DR-126 created
the first one that is not, on purpose.**

**THIS IS THE SECOND FIELD IN TWO DAYS FOUND UNAUTHORABLE BY
CONSTRUCTION**, after DR-124's `maxConnections`, in the same builder, on
the same evidence: a rule firing on a connection that is correct. The
shape is now three for three this milestone, counting `RCK-003`'s
discarded severity (DR-125 §11.124.2): **a field the model has, the
documents describe, and no producer ever writes.** A census of `p()`'s
parameters against `PortDef`'s fields is owed and is not done here.

`p()` gains `accepts`, and the eleven declare `ctl.ir_emitter`.

**11.125.8 THE COUNTS, SO NOBODY RECONCILES TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT WERE
NEVER THE SAME ONE.** Eleven DECLARATION SITES were edited; eighteen
PORTS ship, because the eight-zone matrix amplifier declares
`zone.$zone.ir` inside a loop. Six ports stay on `ctl.ir_receiver`.

**One of the eighteen is on `V06:receiver`, a ROLE VARIANT**, which lives
in `buildSeedRoleVariants()` and not in `buildSeedCatalog()`. A sweep over
the base catalogue alone sees seventeen and misses it in silence, which
matters more than the arithmetic: `insert_receiver.dart` places that exact
template as the `SIG-001` remedy, so **it is the one IR port in the
catalogue the product creates on a user's behalf**. `ir_family_split_test
.dart` reads both builders for that reason.

**11.125.9 PAL-1 AND THE PALETTE COPIES.** The pattern is `1.5,9` at
0.75x: the emitter's own dot at three times the gap, so the two read as
siblings on T0.01 and are unmistakable at 300 dpi. **3,928 candidates were
run through `tools/pal1_check.py` in full and 1,209 survived**, so the
choice among them was a design one made after the gate rather than
against it. Near misses like `2,3` and `1.5,4` also pass and were rejected
by eye: half a point of dot or gap does not read on paper.

**A PATTERN THAT TILES TO ANOTHER ONE IS A COLLISION THE GATE CANNOT
SEE.** Its within-domain limb compares the exact `(dash, weight)` tuple,
so `1.5,3,1.5,3` passes against `ctl.ir_emitter`'s `1.5,3` while rendering
as the identical line. It was excluded by hand, and the search excluded
every repetition with it. **That is a gap in `pal1_check.py`, recorded
here rather than fixed**, because closing it is a change to the authority
and belongs in its own commit.

The family lands in all four copies of the palette (the Dart seed,
`pal1_check.py`, `seed-devices.md` §4.4 and docs/01 §6.6) and all three
palette gates pass at 57 families over 415 in-band cross-domain pairs.

### §11.126 DR-127 · The M5-H2 review's unpriced findings enter M5, which is an amendment and not a disposition

**A §8.3 AMENDMENT, in its own commit, with its own ruling ID**, because
that is what §8.3 requires of a scope change and because four of DR-125's
dispositions were *"unpriced"* rather than refused. Unpriced is not a
state a milestone can close over: it means somebody agreed the finding was
real and said nothing about who builds it.

**Settled by the user 2026-09-05**, on the reasoning *"might as well
finish them out while they're fresh"* and that M5's buildable work was
done.

**11.126.1 THE FOUR BODIES, AND WHERE THEY GO.**

| Board | What | From |
|---|---|---|
| `#837` M5-J | The remedy prompt generalises: `SIG-002`, `CON-001` and `PWR-003` each offer to create the part that fixes them and wire it in | DR-125 §11.124.4 |
| `#838` M5-K | `ELE-006`: a tap selector for constant-voltage speakers, and CV-to-Low-Z switching | DR-125 §11.124.1 finding 5 |
| `#839` M5-L | `PLC-001`: a cabinet head end, which the reviewer says is the COMMON residential case rather than an edge | DR-125 finding 11 |
| `#840` M5-M | `CODE-002`: a code-adjacent finding wants more than a row in a panel | DR-125 finding 12 |

**11.126.2 A FIFTH ARRIVED WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN**, and it is
DR-126's, not the reviewer's. `#842` M5-N holds the fields with no
producer, and `#841` its one chapter: **census `p()`'s parameters against
`PortDef`'s fields.** Three such fields turned up in one milestone
(`maxConnections` at DR-124, `acceptedFamilies` at DR-126, `RuleMeta`'s
severity one layer up at DR-125), **two of them because a user's review
made a rule fire on a connection that is correct**. The third was found
the same way. Nobody has looked for the fourth, and the census is the only
one of the five items here that could have been scheduled before the
review rather than after it.

**11.126.3 WHAT THIS AMENDMENT DOES NOT DO.** It adds no rule. The
catalogue stays at 28, CR-021 and AC-040 are untouched, and M5-H1's pack
told the reviewer in writing that *"whether there should be MORE checks"*
was not being asked. **Every item here changes what an EXISTING rule
offers or how it reads**, which is the difference between answering the
review and reopening the rule set.

**11.126.4 THE COST NOTE, RECORDED BECAUSE THE REASONING FOR THE
AMENDMENT RESTS ON IT.** The decision was taken on the ground that M5's
buildable work was finished and the project is ahead of the roadmap's
pricing (§7, `M`, 4-6 weeks). **That was measured before 2026-09-05's
findings and is no longer quite true**: DR-126 alone added a signal
family, a builder parameter and a test file, and this ruling adds five
items to the board.

**The estimate is not amended, because an estimate is not scope and
changing it here would confuse the two.** What is recorded is that M5-H2
has produced buildable work at a rate no decomposition predicted, being
four rulings in two days, so **M5's remaining cost should be re-measured
before M6 opens rather than after**, and §8.9 makes that a live question
rather than a tidy one: M6 opens only over a predecessor whose clauses are
discharged or parked.

**11.126.5 THE SIGN-OFF IS NOT BLOCKED ON ANY OF THIS.** `#305` and `#306`
close on the REVIEW, which is a human act, and these five are its
consequences. **A milestone clause is discharged by evidence, not by an
empty backlog** (§8.1), so nothing here reopens M5-H, and an item still
open when M5 closes is re-parented rather than left under a closed Epic
(DR-097).

### §11.127 DR-128 · The remedy prompt, and the fourth field in one milestone whose only writer is the decoder

**Board `#837` (M5-J), authorised by DR-127 §11.126.** Settled by the user
2026-09-05, in three answers.

**11.127.1 DR-125 CALLED THIS *"ONE FEATURE, THREE-QUARTERS BUILT"*. IT IS
NOT.** That reading came from `insert_receiver.dart` existing and doing
the same shape of thing for `SIG-001`. Censused before pricing:

**`InlineAdapter` is modelled, round-trips through the codec, and is read
by `_adapterSatisfies` to clear `CON-001` and `SIG-002`. Its only writer
in the entire tree is `_decodeInlineAdapter`.** No command builds one, no
widget offers one, and `schematic_canvas_screen.dart` twice reasons
carefully about how *"an `InlineAdapter` already declared on it"* clears
those rules, a sentence whose subject cannot come into existence.

So `CON-001`'s catalogue summary, *"Satisfied by data: declaring the
adapter clears it"*, **describes an action no user can take**. The rule
tells somebody to do a thing, and the product has no way to do it.

**THE FOURTH IN ONE MILESTONE**, after `maxConnections` (DR-124),
`acceptedFamilies` (DR-126) and `RuleMeta`'s discarded severity
(DR-125). It is the first of the four where the missing writer makes a
SHIPPED RULE'S OWN PROMISE unkeepable rather than merely leaving a
default in place, and it strengthens `#841`'s census from a tidy-up into
the thing that should have run first.

**11.127.2 `CON-001` DECLARES AN ADAPTER, AND CR-015 ALREADY CHOSE THE
SHAPE.** CR-015 splits adapters on a mechanical test, *"does an installer
pull two separate cables to it?"*: no makes it an `InlineAdapter` value on
the Link, yes makes it a real `DeviceInstance`. `CON-001` is *"the plug
does not fit the jack"*, which is the barrel, the gender changer, the
null-modem shell. **Value object.**

`[ Declare an adapter ]` writes one with **both connectors prefilled from
the two pins that just failed**, an optional model, and
`satisfiesRuleIds: ['CON-001']`. The model is optional deliberately: an
adapter with no model reaches the BOM as an unspecified line, which is
worse than a specified one and better than a remedy nobody uses because
it demanded typing mid-gesture. G4's frame applies, an absent model is
unknown and prints as unknown, rather than being invented.

**11.127.3 `SIG-002` INSERTS A DEVICE, ON THE SAME TEST READ THE OTHER
WAY.** *"The sink does not accept the source's family"* is answered by
electronics, not by a plug shape: HDMI to composite, SDI to HDMI, a
balun. An installer pulls two cables to every one of those, so CR-015
makes them devices, exactly as it says of the `SIG-001` remedy.

**11.127.4 THE CONVERTER IS MINTED, NOT SHIPPED, AND THE CATALOGUE DOES
NOT GROW.** Censused: the catalogue holds no generic converter. It holds
the HDBaseT extender pair and a presentation scaler, and nothing else
that converts.

A seeded `Signal Converter` archetype was rejected: **a converter's ports
cannot be right in general**, because the families it bridges vary per
use, so it would ship with unknown-family ports or a P4 variant axis, and
that is a great deal of machinery for a box whose entire purpose is to be
specific. A palette filtered to devices bridging the two families was
rejected on measurement: **that filter returns almost nothing today**, and
an empty picker behind a remedy button is worse than no button.

**So the remedy AUTHORS the device from the two pins it was invoked on**:
one input port carrying the source's family and connector, one output
port carrying the sink's, `mountMethod: notInRack`, named for what it
bridges. DR-123's authored-device path and `insert_receiver.dart`'s
`TxnScope` are both built and are what this uses. **CR-061's count of 49
does not move**, and the device is correct for its case by construction
rather than generic.

**IT STATES NO WATTAGE AND NO MODEL**, which is G4 rather than an
oversight, and is the precedent DR-120's `F19` set: a shipped row that
cannot cite a source states nothing rather than guessing. The BOM line is
uncosted and says so.

**11.127.5 `PWR-003` IS A TIER-3 FINDING AND HAD NO SURFACE AT ALL.**
DR-125 §11.124.4 grouped it with the other two as one feature. It is not
one feature: `SpringBackRemedy` lives on a CHIP, `PWR-003` is a row in the
issues panel, and **`Finding` has no remedy field**. The three could not
have shared a mechanism because two of them had one and the third had
nowhere to put it.

**Ruled: `Finding` gains an optional remedy**, the issues panel renders it
as a button, and `PWR-003`'s inserts `P01`, the 24-outlet 0U vertical PDU
that already ships. **Built once, here, because `CODE-002` (`#840`) wants
the same surface**, and a second bespoke path is how one mechanism becomes
three: §5.3.20 records three unreachable models in one issue arriving
exactly that way.

The field is optional and absent by default, so CR-117's round trip is
unaffected for every finding that has no remedy: **unknown serializes as
an absent key** (G4/CR-114), and a finding is computed rather than stored
in any case (docs/02 §4.8).

**11.127.8 THE `PWR-003` REMEDY WAS DECIDED WRONG FIRST, AND THE TRADE
CORRECTED IT.** This ruling's own §11.127.5 says the remedy inserts `P01`,
the 24-outlet 0U vertical PDU. **The option that produced that answer was
written by an agent listing what the catalogue happened to hold**, and the
user returned the fact it was missing:

> a small bank of PoE injectors or Sonos Ports connected to a simple power
> strip and then plugged into a PDU outlet to allow for remote resetting
> (Via BlueBOLT or OvrC, e.g.) and automation/power sequencing

and, separately, that *"these small power strips are commonly just set on
a shelf in the rack"*.

**THE MODEL ALREADY EXPRESSED IT AND THE CATALOGUE DID NOT.** All three
seeded templates that provide outlets are `outletsConsumed: 1` with
`outletsProvided: N`, which is exactly a strip: one outlet in, six out, so
`PWR-003`'s arithmetic closes the shortfall by five. **What is missing is
the row**, and it is the fifth thing in one milestone that a rule asks a
person to do and the product cannot express.

`P02`, a shelf-mounted 6-outlet passive strip, ships. **CR-061's count
moves from 49 to 50** on DR-120's precedent for `F19` (§12.28), and 50 is
still mid-band in CR-061's confirmed 40 to 55, so the ruling decided a
band and this moves within it. **Six outlets is the user's figure and it cites a
real product**: *"6 outlets is standard on the most basic Wattbox power
strip, which is easily the most common my company installs."* That is
AC-052 satisfied in the form the rule actually wants, a number with a
source rather than a number with a rationale.

**THE ROW STAYS GENERIC, AND THE CITATION DOES NOT.** §10.9 keeps the
shipped catalogue to archetypes, so `P02` is a `Rack Power Strip` and not
a WattBox; the brand is recorded as WHERE THE SIX CAME FROM, in the
template's source note and here, which is the same split `sources.md`
already uses. The strip states no wattage of its own, being passive.

**11.127.9 AND THE REMEDY ASKS RATHER THAN GUESSING WHEN THE RACK IS
EMPTY.** Ruled: if the rack already has anything providing outlets, the
button inserts the strip, because that is the everyday fix and it needs no
0U channel. **If nothing in the rack provides an outlet, the remedy
returns a CHOICE rather than picking**, and the panel asks whether to add
a strip or a PDU.

The rule already knows which case it is, having summed `outletsProvided`
to decide the rack was short, so the branch costs nothing to evaluate. The
reason for asking rather than deciding is that the two answers are
different jobs: a strip in a rack with no distribution reaches a wall
outlet and is a legal drawing, a PDU is the beginning of a power plan, and
**a remedy that silently picks the second has made a design decision on
somebody's behalf.**

**11.127.7 THE REMEDY'S OWN TEST FOUND THREE GHOST IDS IN THE AC-051
CORPUS.** `spring_back_scenarios.dart` named `conn.xlr3_f`,
`video.hdmi` and `audio.analog_bal`; the shipped ids are `conn.xlr3`,
`video.hdmi.2_0` and `audio.line_bal`. Every case passed on the ghosts,
because the predicates that read them compare ids directly and a fixture
family only has to DIFFER from the other end rather than exist.

**`CON-001` is where it mattered.** That rule reads the registry, and
`_connectorsDoNotMate` skips entirely when the FROM connector is unknown
(the G4 branch, `#255`). So a ghost exercises the real limb or the
unknown limb **depending on which end it lands on**. Here it landed on the
TO end, so the known-bad fired, and what it was actually asserting is that
HDMI does not mate with a typo, which is true of every typo.

Found because DR-128's own first draft invented `conn.xlr3_m` and was
caught by its own *"this is not vacuous"* test. **That test existed only
because the house rule says to assert the artifact**: a remedy test
checking `inlineAdapters.length == 1` would have passed on a rule that
never fired. `spring_back_rules_test.dart` now censuses both id kinds
against the seeded registries.

**This is the second time in two days that DR-125 §11.124.5's sentence has
proved too kind.** It says the AC-051 corpus *"saw none of them, because a
pair proves a rule fires, not that it fires correctly"*. The corpus also
could not see that three of its own fixtures named entities the product
does not ship.

**11.127.10 THE SHELF MODEL IS PARKED AS A MAYBE, NOT AMENDED.** Building
`PWR-003`'s remedy required putting a device on a shelf, which nothing in
the product could do, and the user returned five trade facts about what a
shelf really holds: **1/12th granularity is right; a Roku is under 1U so
two stack, and 0.5U heights are necessary; a shallow device leaves room at
the back where the power strip goes; a modem sits sideways or upright
depending on the install; and Penn Elecom and Marantz make shelves for
specific gear.**

**AC-043 sorts them, and the sort is the whole reason no amendment was
needed here.** That ruling KEEPS *"auto-pack left to right;
`ShelfPlacement.order` decides sequence"* and defers *"free lateral
positioning, `Alt`-drag, the third focus level entered with `Enter`, and
per-host depth-overhang warnings"*, saying **"only the UI defers"**. So
fact 3 is cut by name, facts 1 and 4 sit against the same cut, and **fact
2 is neither cut nor built**: AC-043 never mentions height, and there is
no body height in `Len` anywhere on `TemplateBody`. The half that shipped
is the half AC-043 keeps.

**Ruled by the user, in their own words:**

> As much as I don't want to both A: go back on AC-043's decision and B:
> don't want to increase scope for v1, this may be a necessary fix before
> v1. File it as a "maybe" under M8/M9; I'll see how the team reacts to
> the version you're building now.

`#844` sits under **M9, Beta hardening**, rather than M8: the trigger
named is how a team reacts to a build, which is what beta hardening is
