total order and is not a new opinion: the rack leads because `PLN-003` makes its absence cost every
length on the plan, so the row that matters most is the row nobody has to scroll to. **One
comparator, one place, changed in a line** when the user says otherwise.

**11.141.7 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the strip's appearance, height, or whether it collapses.
Not whether a rack row is drawn differently from a device row, which §11.139.6 reserved and which
remains reserved. Not `PLN-002` and `PLN-003`, which stay separate advisories with separate remedies
(§11.139.5): **the strip is a surface, not a rule**, and it may show what two rules report without
collapsing them into one.

### §11.142 DR-143 · The floorplan importer had no caller, so the Plan view had nothing to open

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-08**, at `PLAN-E/5`'s census, before a line of the shell was
written. `PLAN-E/5` was scheduled as the chapter that makes three chapters' work reachable
(DR-141 §11.140.7, then four at DR-142). **The census found a fifth surface, and it sits upstream of
all of them.**

**11.142.1 NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT CAN PUT A FLOORPLAN IN A PROJECT.** `PLAN-D` built the import
sequence, the format allowlist, the byte and pixel caps, the PDF page lifter and the page picker,
with tests for each. Censused by call site rather than by name, in `lib/` only:

| Built by `PLAN-D` | Call sites outside its own file |
|---|---|
| `pickAndImportFloorplan` | **0** |
| `importFloorplanFrom` | **0** |
| `importFloorplanBytes` | **0** |
| `readPdfPages` | **0** |
| `importLiftedPdfPage` | **0** |
| `ImportedFloorplan` | **0** |
| `PdfPagePickerDialog` | **0** (exported from the barrel, imported by nothing) |

So `AddPlanUnderlayCommand` has no producer. **The four starters contain no `underlays` key**, and
`PlanCanvasScreen.underlay` is a required non-null parameter. Mounting the Plan tab on this tree
would have mounted a view that can never hold anything, which is DR-091's own rule arriving from the
one direction that ruling did not anticipate: not a tab onto an unbuilt view, but a **fully built
view onto content the product cannot create**.

**11.142.2 THE PRODUCER IS TWO PIECES, NOT ONE, AND THE SECOND IS QUIETER.**
`DocumentSession._members` is the map of container members that rides from open to save, and it is
written in exactly one place: `adopt`, wholesale, when a different document replaces this one.
**There is no way to add a member to an open session.** A menu item calling the importer would
therefore have had somewhere to get the bytes and nowhere to put them, and a save would have written
a `PlanUnderlay` naming a member the container does not contain.

**11.142.3 WHY THE REACHABILITY GATE DID NOT SEE IT, WHICH IS TWO BLIND SPOTS AND NOT ONE.**
`actions_have_callers_test.dart` exists for exactly this defect and had just caught it again at
`PLAN-E/3`. It scans **function-typed fields on `*Actions` records** in **`packages/rackpal_ui/lib`**.
`plan_import_actions.dart` holds **free functions** in **`apps/rackpal/lib`**. It fails both
predicates, so the gate was never going to fire, and the file's name ending in `_actions.dart` makes
that easy to miss at a glance.

> **A gate's scope is part of its claim.** Reading "actions have callers" as "reachable code has
> callers" is how a green board coexists with a feature nothing can start. The gate is not wrong and
> is not weakened here; what is recorded is that **its name is broader than its scan**, and
> `PLAN-E/5` is where that cost showed up.

**11.142.4 RULED: THE PRODUCER LANDS IN `PLAN-E/5`, AND THE COMMAND LIVES IN THE `File` MENU.** Both
settled by the user against the alternatives.

The producer **folds into `PLAN-E/5`** rather than becoming its own chapter or reopening `PLAN-D`.
`PLAN-E/5` is already the reachability chapter and its brief says so in terms; the ordering is forced
regardless, because DR-091 wants a tab to open onto something that can exist. Reopening `PLAN-D`
would move a closed epic's mark under §8.9 for a defect that is cheaper to pay forward. **This is not
a §8.3 scope amendment**: nothing is added to roadmap §2, and the work was always inside *"Import:
PNG and JPEG, a PDF page LIFTED at import with a page picker"*. What moved is only which chapter
carries it.

**`File ▸ Import floorplan…`**, beside `Import Template` and `Import Library`, which are already
there. `plan_import_actions.dart`'s own header says `Plan ▸ Import floorplan…` and **there is no
`Plan` menu**: the shell has exactly one `MenuBar` with one `SubmenuButton`. A second top-level menu
holding one item was rejected as premature, and the header's line is a `PLAN-D` assumption that this
ruling supersedes rather than a decision anybody made.

**11.142.5 THE `Ctrl+n` MAPPING IS NOT RENUMBERED HERE, AND THIS SUBSECTION EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST
READING SAID IT WAS.** `app_shell.dart` says the mapping is deferred *"until Plan lands"* in one
paraphrase, and that paraphrase is wrong. **DR-091 §11.90.4 defers it past M6**: *"the view set is
not final until M6. Plan lands before M6 (DR-029) and Rear Panel in v1.1"*, and *"the mapping is
settled after M6, when there is nothing left to insert."*

So the Plan view **gets a tab and no accelerator**, joining Locations, Device Manager and Structured
Wiring, which have none either. `Ctrl+3` stays reserved and unbound for CR-071's Rear Panel.
Renumbering here would be the second relearning §11.90.4 spends its argument avoiding.

**11.142.6 `Esc` IS THE FOURTH ROW OF AN EXISTING PATTERN AND NOT A NEW DECISION.** `rackCancel`,
`schematicCancel` and `dialogDismiss` are three `KeyBindingId`s, three scopes, one trigger and one
label, with `KeymapConflictKind.meaningDrift` failing if the labels diverge. `planCancel` in a new
`KeyScope.plan` is that pattern continued: it dismisses the arm mode and clears the selection, which
is what the other three mean.

**11.142.7 THE MEMBER IS ADDED OUTSIDE THE UNDO STACK, AND THE MODEL ALREADY RULED THAT.** Importing
writes bytes into the session's members and runs `AddPlanUnderlayCommand`; undoing removes the
underlay and **leaves the member**. That asymmetry is not an oversight discovered here:
`RemovePlanUnderlayCommand`'s own doc states it, because *"the member is cheap, the bytes are the
architect's, and deleting them on an undo would make a redo unable to find them."*

**11.142.8 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the Plan view's own layout beyond docs/15 §6's three
regions plus `PLAN-E/4`'s strip. Not what the underlay list looks like or whether it is orderable.
Not the empty state's wording. Not whether `actions_have_callers_test.dart` should widen its scan,
which is a real question this ruling deliberately leaves open rather than answering inside a chapter
about a floorplan.

### §11.143 DR-144 · A calibration carries its unit, and the number it reports back is not a length

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-08**, at `PLAN-F`'s decomposition, before a line of the chapter was
written. `PLAN-F` is three chapters over one sentence of docs/15 §5, *"two picked points and one
typed distance"*, and the census found the same defect the last two chapters found, one field over,
plus a hole in the chapter split that only shows from outside any one of the three.

**11.143.1 `PlanScale`'s WHOLE DERIVATION API HAS NO CALLER, WHICH IS DR-143's SHAPE AGAIN.**
`PLAN-C/2` built the calibration model with the rounding rule argued out in its own header, and
`PLAN-C/5` serialized it. Censused by call site, in `lib/` only, excluding the file that declares
them:

| Built by `PLAN-C` | Call sites in `lib/` |
|---|---|
| `PlanScale.nanometresPerPixel` | **0** |
| `PlanScale.pixelSpan` | **0** |
| `PlanScale.isUsable` | **0** |
| `PlanScale.lengthBetween` | **0** |
| `PlanScale.lengthAlong` | **0** |
| `PlanUnderlay.isCalibrated` | **0** |

Every one is reached only from tests. **There is also no writer**: `plan_commands.dart` ships five
command classes covering six acts, and not one of them sets a scale, so `PlanUnderlay.scale` is null
in every document this product can produce. This is the third instance in three chapters (DR-140's
rack with no pinning gesture, DR-143's importer with no menu item) and it is recorded because the
pattern is now the expected finding rather than a surprise: **`PLAN-C` built a model, and a model is
not a reachable field.**

**11.143.2 SO `PLAN-F/2`'s "N LENGTHS" HAS NOTHING TO COUNT, AND THAT IS THE HOLE.** `#634`'s brief
requires that *"a recalibrate that changes N lengths should say N, on the same G4 principle that
makes every rollup report its unknown count"*. **At `PLAN-F` there are no derived lengths at all.**
`planLowerBound` is not a `ScheduleLengthSource` value, nothing derives one, and docs/15 §6's own
pin-drag row already carries the note that its recompute clause is forward-dated to `PLAN-G`. A
report counting schedule rows would therefore print `0` on every calibration in the product, which is
worse than silence: it is a G4 report whose number is an artifact of what has not been built yet.

**11.143.3 RULED: THE COUNT IS OF MEASURABLE PINS, AND IT PRODUCES NO `Len`.** The report names how
many pins on this plan a length could now be derived for, and when none can, it names the reason:

> Calibrated Level 1. 12 pins can now be measured from the rack.

> Calibrated Level 1. No rack is pinned on this plan, so no length derives yet.

Three properties make this the honest version rather than a placeholder. It is **computable today**,
from the scale's usability and whether any rack stands on this underlay. It is **the set `PLAN-G`
will turn into rows**, so the number does not change meaning when the tier arrives. And the second
sentence is **actionable in the view it appears in**: the unpinned strip is along the bottom of the
same screen and the rack is its first row (DR-140 §11.139), so a person told no rack is pinned is
told it eight inches from the control that fixes it.

**IT MUST NOT PRODUCE A LENGTH, AND THAT BOUNDARY IS THE POINT OF THIS CLAUSE.** A derivation that
returned a `Len` per pin would be `planLowerBound` shipped early under another name, without the
rank, the `>=` prefix, the italic, the rollup exclusion or `LEN-001`'s reading, which are five
decisions DR-037 §11.36.4 already took and `PLAN-G` already owns. **Which rack is the datum is
likewise not decided here**: the count asks only whether a datum exists, and a document with two
pinned racks is counted the same as a document with one. §4.1 says *"rack pin to device pin"* and
does not say which rack when there are several; that question belongs to the chapter that derives the
number, not to the one that counts what is derivable.

**11.143.4 RULED: `Calibrate…` LIVES ON THE UNDERLAY ROW.** The user's call against a canvas toolbar
and a canvas context menu. docs/15 §6 gives the view three regions and says *"there is no fourth
region"*, so a toolbar would be new chrome over a layout ruled eight days ago; and this product has
no context menu on any canvas, so a right-click affordance would be discoverable by nobody who had
not been told. **A calibration is a property of an underlay**, the left rail is the list of
underlays, and a row that already carries a name and a room can carry a state line and an action.

The row therefore reads its state, and **the state line is present in both directions**: `Not
calibrated` is a fact worth printing and not an absence worth hiding (§11.143.6 below). The action
reads `Calibrate…` on an uncalibrated plan and `Recalibrate…` on a calibrated one, which is
`SetPlanPinCommand`'s two-labels-one-command rule applied to an affordance instead of an undo entry:
the word names the act the person is about to perform.

**11.143.5 RULED: A TYPED DISTANCE CARRIES ITS UNIT, AND A BARE NUMBER IS REFUSED BY NAME.** The
user's call against two boxes for feet and inches, and against a number field with a unit picker.

**A bare `36` is 36 inches or 36 feet and the two differ by a factor of twelve**, applied to every
length the plan will ever yield. This is G4 in the place it is cheapest to break and most expensive
to have broken: a guessed unit does not degrade a number, it produces a confident number that is
wrong by an order of magnitude, on a drawing an installer will trust. So the parser accepts
`36"`, `36in`, `3'`, `3ft`, `3' 6"`, `3ft 6in`, `3' 6-1/2"`, `2.4m`, `2400mm` and `240cm`, and
refuses a bare number with a sentence naming both readings rather than picking one.

**AND IT DIVERGES FROM `parseLengthCell` DELIBERATELY, WHICH IS WHY THE DIVERGENCE IS RULED RATHER
THAN LEFT TO A READER.** `derived/structure_table.dart`'s length-cell parser reads a bare number as
**whole feet** and refuses everything else, including `62 ft 3`. Two parsers in one product
disagreeing about what a bare number means is exactly the kind of near-duplicate this corpus keeps
finding, so the difference is stated: **that column is whole feet of cable, ordered and cut in whole
feet, and its refusal keeps the stored value equal to the displayed one**; this field is a distance
on somebody else's drawing whose whole purpose is that its magnitude is not known in advance. The
two are not candidates for harmonisation, and a later pass that unified them would silently give
calibration a default unit.

**THE PROJECT'S `displayUnits` SHAPES THE REFUSAL AND NOT THE GRAMMAR.** An explicitly united value
is unambiguous whichever system the project is set to, so `2.4m` is accepted on an imperial project
rather than refused for being metric; what `displayUnits` decides is which pair of readings the
refusal sentence names, and which example the field's hint shows. CR-001 is untouched: the parse
lands in `Len` nanometres and no floating-point millimetre is stored anywhere.

**11.143.6 THE PICK IS A MODE, ON DR-141's PRECEDENT, AND `Esc` GROWS A THIRD RUNG.** The user's
call: `Calibrate…` puts a chip on the canvas, the first click sets one end, a line follows the
pointer, the second click opens the distance dialog. The alternatives were a modal that opens first
and asks the user to click the canvas behind it, and an inline field at the second point.

**IT REUSES `PlanPinArmController`'s SHAPE AND NOT ITS INSTANCE.** Both are canvas modes with a chip
and an `Esc` exit, and there the resemblance stops: the arm mode outlives each pin by design
(DR-141 §11.140.2) and a calibration pick is **consumed by its own second click**, because there is
exactly one distance being described. A mode that stayed armed after a calibration would be offering
to calibrate the same plan again, immediately, which is not a workflow anybody has.

`Esc`'s rungs on this canvas become three, in this order: **the calibration pick, then the arm mode,
then the selection.** The pick goes first for the reason the arm mode goes before the selection
in §11.140: it is the most recently and most deliberately entered state, and it is the thing on
screen saying so. The binding does not change; `planCancel` gains a third thing to mean, and its
`isActionEnabled` gate gains a third clause, which is the same `_PlanGatedAction` that already
refuses the key when there is nothing to cancel.

**A REFUSED PICK IS NOT AN ERROR.** Two clicks in the same place span no distance, and
`PlanScale.nanometresPerPixel` already answers null for that case rather than throwing, on the model
header's own reasoning. The dialog refuses to commit and says why; the pick stays live so the second
point can be moved rather than the whole mode restarted.

**11.143.7 THE CHAPTER SPLIT INSIDE `PLAN-F` MOVES, BECAUSE `PLAN-F/1` CANNOT LAND WITHOUT A
WRITER.** `#633` is the pick and the typed distance and `#634` is *"recalibration is a document
command"*, read as though the command belonged to the second. It does not: a dialog that parses a
distance and has nowhere to put it is the no-caller defect of §11.143.1 pointed the other way, and it
could not be gated green, because `actions_have_callers_test.dart` and this repo's own standard both
refuse a surface with no writer behind it.

So **`PLAN-F/1` carries the parser, `SetPlanScaleCommand`, the row affordance, the pick mode and the
dialog**, which is one reachable gesture end to end. **`PLAN-F/2` carries what a recalibration does
to everything else**: the epoch mask tested against a listener rather than against itself, and the
count of §11.143.3 with the sentence that reports it. **`PLAN-F/3` carries uncalibrated as a
first-class fact**: the row's state line, and the proof in both directions that placement and
calibration do not block each other. **This is not a §8.3 amendment.** Nothing enters or leaves
roadmap §2, no chapter is added or removed, and the three briefs keep their subjects; what moves is
which chapter carries the writer, on DR-143 §11.142.4's precedent for the same kind of move.

**11.143.8 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not `PLN-001`'s wording, its severity or its band, which are
`PLAN-I`'s and which this chapter only supplies the state for. Not whether a calibration can be
**cleared** back to unknown: undo covers the mis-calibration a person notices immediately, docs/15
§5 does not ask for a clear, and a `ClearPlanScaleCommand` built on nobody's request would be a
sixth command for a gesture no surface offers. Not the scale bar, which is `PLAN-H/4`'s and which
that chapter rules is **drawn and never printed as a ratio**, so nothing here prints one. Not which
rack is the datum when two are pinned on one plan (§11.143.3). And not whether the underlay row
should show anything else about the calibration, such as when it was taken or by whom;
`EntityMeta` carries that and no surface asks for it.

---

### §11.144 DR-145 · The second real plan set is all vector, so DR-138's trigger has fired and the deferral survives it

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-08**, after the file was put through the shipped importer rather than
read. DR-138 §11.137 deferred pdfium *"until a PDF needs it"* and stated the cost of the lifter in
terms: *"a vector PDF falls through to a refusal and reinstates the manual step DR-029 bought out."*
**A PDF now needs it.** This ruling records the measurement, keeps the deferral, and names where it
is re-examined so a fired trigger and an unexplained wait do not sit side by side in the record.

**11.144.1 WHAT THE FILE IS, MEASURED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED.** A three-page residential plan set,
supplied by the user and **kept out of the repository** on DR-137 §11.136.6's precedent. Read by
regex over the raw bytes, which is the method §5.9.5.1 wrote down so that any figure here can be
re-derived from somebody else's plan set:

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Producer | `pdfplot16.hdi`, from **AutoCAD 2022** |
| Pages | **3**, `/MediaBox [0 0 1224 792]`, ANSI B (17 x 11 in) landscape |
| `/XObject` occurrences | **0** |
| `/Image`, `/DCTDecode` | **0** |
| `/Font` occurrences | **39** |
| Cross-reference | classic table; no `/ObjStm`, no `/XRef` stream |
| Size | 1,169,090 bytes |

**11.144.2 THE IMPORTER REFUSES IT, AND THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT FOR THE RIGHT REASON.** All three
pages come back `PdfPageNotLiftableError ... draws no image`, and `readPdfPages` turns that into the
document-level sentence a person sees:

> this PDF has 3 pages and none of them can be used as an underlay (PLAN-D/3, DR-138). The first page
> draws no image. Export the page you want as PNG or JPEG for now.

**A REFUSAL CAN BE RIGHT FOR THE WRONG REASON AND THIS ONE IS NOT.** `draws no image` sits in
`liftPage` **after** the MediaBox, the malformed-box and the Resources checks, so reaching it proves
the parser resolved a real AutoCAD classic xref, walked its page tree, read a usable `/MediaBox` and
resolved each page's resource dictionary before finding no image to lift. Had the parse failed the
error would have been `PdfCompressedCrossReferenceError`, `declares no usable MediaBox` or
`has no resources`, and it was none of them. **This is the first time the lifter's front end has run
on a real vector PDF**; before today it had seen synthetic fixtures and one raster-flattened set.

**AND THE SYNTHETIC CASE PREDICTED IT EXACTLY.** `pdf_page_lift_test.dart`'s
*"no XObject at all is refused"* asserts the same string the real file produced. That is worth
recording because the corpus carries the opposite experience as a practice: a parser whose synthetic
cases all passed and which refused every page of the first real file it saw. Here the fixtures and
the real input agree, and saying so is what makes the practice a rule of thumb rather than a law.

**11.144.3 THE TWO REAL SETS SIT AT OPPOSITE ENDS, WHICH NEITHER ALONE COULD SHOW.** This project has
now been given two plan sets by the trade rather than by a test:

| | 2026-09-07 (DR-137 §11.136) | 2026-09-08 (this ruling) |
|---|---|---|
| Sheets | 18, ARCH D (36 x 24 in) | 3, ANSI B (17 x 11 in) |
| Content | **every page one full-page JPEG**, zero fonts, zero vector | **zero images**, 39 fonts, all vector |
| Origin | an office flattening a drawing at 60 dpi | a plot straight out of AutoCAD |
| The importer | lifts it, losslessly | **refuses every page** |

**docs/12 §5.9.5.3 wrote the sentence this confirms** a day before the file arrived: *"A vector PDF
breaks it."* The lifter was shipped knowing that. What is new is not the mechanism but the
**population**: the ordinary path forks, both forks are ordinary, and the import covers one.

**11.144.4 DR-029 IS NOT WRONG AND ITS PURCHASE IS HALF-DELIVERED, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE.**
DR-029 bought PDF import at a costed two to three weeks because *"architects send PDFs and a manual
conversion step would sit on the ordinary path rather than the exceptional one."* That premise holds
exactly: PDFs are the ordinary input, and for a raster-flattened set the manual step is gone. For a
CAD plot it is back. **The honest statement is that half the ordinary path is bought**, and the half
that is not is the one a drawing office produces without doing anything to it, since a plot from CAD
is vector by construction and flattening is an extra act somebody chose.

**ONE FILE IS ONE SAMPLE AND THE CLASS IS NOT.** The corpus has been wrong twice by generalising from
a single run (the CI duration note, in both directions), so the claim is deliberately narrow: nothing
here says how the two classes are distributed across the trade. What it says is that both classes are
real, both have now been seen, and a mechanism covering one of them cannot be described as covering
*"PDF import"* without qualification.

**11.144.5 RULED: THE DEFERRAL STANDS, AND IT IS RE-EXAMINED AT `PLAN-H`.** The user's call against
opening the rasteriser as scope now and against closing the question in favour of the manual step.

**Not now**, because a vendored pdfium plus a direct FFI binding is the largest single piece left in
this epic and would displace `PLAN-F` and `PLAN-G`, which are the chapters that make a plan yield a
length at all. A plan that locates a drop is useful uncalibrated (§1); a rasteriser that arrives
before the length model buys a prettier picture of the same missing number.

**Not never**, because the trigger has fired and a deferral with a fired trigger and no review date is
how a debt stops being visible. **`PLAN-H` is the review point** and the reason is structural rather
than a guess at a date: `T1.01` is the first thing in this product that needs an underlay *rendered*
rather than *stored*, so the chapter that builds it is the first one whose own work is blocked by the
absence rather than merely inconvenienced by it.

**The route is unchanged and is not `pdfrx`.** DR-138 §11.137 refused that package twice over, and
docs/03's row is kept rather than deleted so the choice is not re-derived. When the review happens the
candidate is a direct FFI binding over a **vendored** pdfium, which is what CR-100 requires.

**11.144.6 RULED: THE FIXTURE IS A SYNTHETIC TWIN AND THE FILE STAYS OUT OF THE REPOSITORY.**
DR-137 §11.136.6 kept the first set out because it carries a sealed engineer's licence number and
DR-036 would publish every commit ever made. **This file is kept out for a plainer reason**: it is the
user's reference material and nothing about the finding needs the bytes. What the regression needs is
the *signature*, so the fixture is built to match it (a classic xref, three pages, an ANSI B
`/MediaBox`, fonts and paths in the content stream, and no `/XObject`), and the measurements above are
written out so anybody with their own CAD plot can re-derive them.

**11.144.7 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the resolution a rasterisation would use when one exists;
DR-137 §11.136.4's *"never above the source's own effective resolution"* is a rule for a raster source
and a vector source has no such ceiling, which is a question `PLAN-H` inherits along with the
rasteriser. Not whether the page picker should show a grid of refused pages rather than a single
sentence when **every** page is refused; the current behaviour is deliberate and this file did not
test the mixed case, because it has none. Not whether a pure-Dart renderer for the subset a CAD plot
emits is worth considering, which is named here only so that it is on the record as *not* costed.

### §11.145 DR-146 · An uncalibrated plan states what it costs, and the count is one population in both directions

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-08**, at `PLAN-F/3`'s census, before a line of the chapter was
written. `PLAN-F/3` is the last of DR-144 §11.143.7's three chapters and its brief has three clauses;
the census found one already discharged, one true but proven only by accident, and one hole of the
shape this epic has now found four times.

**11.145.1 CLAUSE ONE IS BUILT, AND IT IS THE ONE THE BRIEF LEADS WITH.** `#635` opens with
*"`scale == null` means UNCALIBRATED. It does not mean 1:1 and it never acquires a guessed value."*
Censused by site rather than read:

| Where a default could enter | What is there |
|---|---|
| `PlanUnderlay.scale` | `PlanScale?`, documented *"null does not mean 1:1 and it never acquires a guessed value"* |
| `PlanUnderlay.isCalibrated` | `scale?.isUsable ?? false`, so a stored scale that cannot yield a factor reads as uncalibrated |
| `_encodePlanUnderlay` | `putIfNotNull`, so an uncalibrated plan writes **no `scale` key** (G4, CR-114) |
| `_decodePlanUnderlay` | `json['scale'] == null ? null : …`, and never a fallback |
| `SetPlanScaleCommand.scale` | non-nullable, so no gesture can write "unknown" over a scale |
| `planMeasurabilityOf` | gates on `isCalibrated`, so an unusable scale counts nothing |

**No site substitutes anything**, and `plan_serialization_test.dart` already asserts the absent key
and the null read-back. **So the clause the brief leads with was discharged by `PLAN-C/5` and
`PLAN-F/1`**, and this chapter neither re-implements nor re-litigates it.

**11.145.2 CLAUSE TWO IS TRUE AND IS PROVEN BY ACCIDENT, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS PROVEN.** The brief
asks that *"pins place, and no length derives, and neither fact is blocked by the other."* Nothing in
`lib/` gates a pin on a scale: `plan_canvas_screen.dart`, `unpinned_strip.dart` and
`unpinned_carriers.dart` mention calibration only for the pick mode that shares their canvas. The
direction holds.

**AND NOT ONE TEST IN THE SUITE SAYS SO.** Every plan fixture in `rackpal_ui` is built without a
`PlanScale`, so every pin gesture the suite runs is already a pin on an uncalibrated plan, and the
property passes because the fixture's default happens to be the interesting case. The mirror
direction, **a pin placed on a plan that IS calibrated**, is exercised nowhere: `PlanScale` appears in
no UI plan test outside `plan_calibrate_test.dart`. A property that is only ever satisfied by a
default is a property nobody would notice losing, which is this repository's own standard applied to
a fact rather than to a number.

**11.145.3 CLAUSE THREE IS A HOLE, AND IT IS THE FOURTH OF ITS SHAPE IN FOUR CHAPTERS.** The brief
ends *"`PLN-001` reports the state as an advisory rather than blocking anything. `PLAN-I` builds it;
this task is the model and derived behaviour it reports on."* The state exists per underlay; what
does not exist is any reader of the number it would report. `PlanMeasurability.pinnedCarrierCount`
was built at `PLAN-F/2` with a doc comment naming its own intended caller, *"on an uncalibrated plan
with forty pins the first is 0 and the second is 40, and a surface that had only the first would
report a fully pinned plan as empty"*, and it has **zero call sites in `lib/`**. The surface it
describes is the underlay row, and that row prints a bare `Not calibrated`: **a plan carrying
thirty-nine stranded pins reads exactly like a plan with none.** DR-140, DR-143 and DR-144 each found
a modelled thing nothing could reach; this one is a *count* nothing reads, which is the same defect
with a smaller radius.

**11.145.4 RULED: THE UNCALIBRATED ROW NAMES WHAT IS STRANDED.** The user's call, against three
alternatives that were put with it.

> Not calibrated · 39 pins carry no measurable position

The words are **docs/15 §9's own `PLN-001` sentence**, chosen so that the row and the advisory
`PLAN-I` will build say the same thing rather than two things about one state. G4 is the reason the
line exists at all: a rollup reports its unknown count rather than presenting a flattering total, and
an uncalibrated plan's unknown count is every drop standing on it. `Calibrated · 12 measurable`
already tells a person what a calibration bought; this is the same sentence before the purchase.

**A PLAN WITH NOTHING STRANDED SAYS ONLY `Not calibrated`.** The count is the cost, and a plan with
no drops on it has not incurred one; `Not calibrated · 0 pins carry no measurable position` is the
`Calibrated · 0 measurable` that DR-144 §11.143.3 already refused, one state earlier.

**11.145.5 RULED: ONE POPULATION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH DECIDES WHICH FIELD SURVIVES.** The
alternative put to the user was to count every pin on the plan, the rack included, which is both what
`pinnedCarrierCount` holds and what a person counts on screen. It was refused for a reason visible
only across the two states: thirty-nine stranded pins would become `Calibrated · 39 measurable` under
one reading and forty would become thirty-nine under the other, **and a number that drops by one at
the moment of a calibration reads as a pin lost to it.** The rack is the datum in both directions
(DR-144 §11.143.3) and belongs in neither count.

**SO `pinnedCarrierCount` IS REPLACED RATHER THAN RETAINED.** `subjectPinCount` is what the row wants:
the pins a length could be derived FOR, counted whether or not one currently can be. `PLAN-F/2`
anticipated this row and guessed its population one chapter before it was ruled, which is the
ordinary hazard of building a field for a surface that does not exist yet; keeping the unread one
beside the read one would leave the next census to find it again.

**AND `measurableCount` BECOMES A DERIVED GETTER, WHICH IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN TIDY.** It was
stored as `calibrated && hasRack ? others : 0` beside the two booleans that decide it, so three
fields could disagree and a constructor could be handed a count that its own flags forbid. With the
subject count stored, the gate is written once and the disagreement is unspellable. `blockedBy`
already worked this way and is the precedent.

**11.145.6 RULED: THE SENTENCE LIVES IN `rackpal_core`, BESIDE THE DERIVATION.** DR-144 §11.143.3
made the row and the snack bar one function each so the two could not drift; the same argument
crosses a package here, and the package boundary is the reason it must be settled rather than left.
`PLN-001` is a validation rule and `rackpal_core/src/validation/` is where rules live; the underlay
row is `rackpal_ui`. A sentence written in the UI would have to be **copied** into core when
`PLAN-I` arrives, and a copied sentence is a sentence that will disagree with its original the first
time somebody edits one of them. So the phrase is core's, next to the count it reports, and the row
composes it. **The plural is hand-written**, on `PLAN-F/2`'s own finding: `1 pins` is the `0 pathways`
status bar this repository has already shipped once.

**11.145.7 RULED: THE PROOF IS A GESTURE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT A MODEL CALL.** A test that runs
`SetPlanPinCommand` against an uncalibrated document proves the command, and the command was never
where a gate would be added. **A gate would be added on a surface**, as a disabled strip row, a
refused drop or a `Calibrate first` chip, and every one of those is invisible to a test that talks to
the document. So both directions are asserted through the shipped gestures: a carrier dragged out of
the strip onto an uncalibrated plan lands a pin, and a plan carrying pins takes a calibration through
the pick and the dialog without disturbing one of them.

**11.145.8 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not `PLN-001`'s severity, its band or its behaviour as an
advisory, which stay `PLAN-I`'s under DR-144 §11.143.8; this chapter supplies the state and the
sentence and files no finding. **Not a document-level rollup over every underlay**, which `PLAN-I`
can assemble by iterating the per-underlay derivation it already has: building one now, for a rule
that does not exist, would be committing this epic's own recurring defect on purpose. Not whether a
calibrated row should also name its subject total, which would put a second number on a line the user
has just settled. And not the reading a **stored but unusable** scale produces, where the state line
says `Not calibrated` while the action still says `Recalibrate…`: the first is DR-144 §11.143.4's
rule that an unusable scale is not a calibration, the second is `SetPlanScaleCommand`'s rule that
replacing a stored value is a recalibration whatever the value was worth, both are deliberate, and
the combination is reachable only from a file this product cannot write.

### §11.146 DR-147 · The bound measures from the run's own rack, and the two rollups it must not enter are two

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-08**, at `PLAN-G`'s census, before a line of the chapter was
written. `PLAN-G` is four Chapters (`#636`–`#639`) decomposed on 2026-08-10, and the census found
that two of the four briefs describe a tree that has since changed underneath them.

**11.146.1 THE CENSUS, WHICH FOUND THREE THINGS AND NONE WAS IN A TICKET.**

| Found | Where | What the brief assumed |
|---|---|---|
| `LEN-001` and `LEN-002` **already ship** | `validation/rules_cable.dart`, M5 | `#639`: *"M5 owns the rules; this task owns the input and the seam. Do not build the rules here."* Written before M5 built them |
| The rules **do not read the tier ladder at all** | `knownLengthOf` is `terminatedLength ?? cutLength` | §4.1's *"`LEN-001` and `LEN-002` read the bound regardless of which tier printed"* describes a ladder those two functions have never consumed |
| There are **two footage rollups** and the booby trap guards one | `cable_footage.dart`'s `_isQuantity` versus `schedule.dart`'s `_footageOf` | `#638` names *"the footage rollup"*. `_footageOf` sums `row.length` with no source check and builds `ScheduleView.footage` and `ScheduleGroup.footage`, which is §3.8's `Σ 11 runs · 601 ft · 3 estimated` footer |

**THE BOOBY TRAP WORKED AND ITS SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN ITS REPUTATION.** `cable_footage.dart:309`'s
`_isQuantity` is an exhaustive switch with no default arm and its header says why: *"the day it is
added this file stops compiling and somebody decides, rather than a bound silently joining a
purchase."* It does stop the build, and it is the one gate of its kind in this tree. **It guards the
takeoff and it does not guard the sheet footer**, because `_footageOf` reads a `Len?` and never asks
where the number came from. A gate's scope is part of its claim, and this one's claim was read one
rollup too wide by its own ticket.

**11.146.2 RULED: THE DATUM IS THE RUN'S OWN RACK.** DR-144 §11.143.3 left *"which rack is the datum
when two are pinned on one plan"* to this chapter, and it is the question with the most ways to be
quietly wrong. The user's call, against two alternatives put with it:

> The bound is the straight line from the pin on **the rack this link lands in** to the pin on this
> run's subject. When that rack carries no pin, **no bound derives**, even when another rack is
> pinned on the same underlay.

The two refused alternatives were *the nearest pinned rack* and *the first pinned rack in document
order*. Both yield a bound more often and both yield a **wrong** one on any job with a head end and a
satellite rack, which is the ordinary shape of the work this product is for. A distance to a rack the
cable does not go to is not a weaker bound, it is a different building's number wearing a
measurement's authority, and it is the G4 failure §4's opening paragraph forbids in the one place
where the reader cannot see it happening.

**AND IT MAKES THE RACK-TO-RACK RUN FALL OUT RATHER THAN BE EXCLUDED.** Exactly one end of a link may
be in a rack for a bound to exist. A jumper has both ends in one rack and a sub-feed has them in two;
neither has a field end, so neither has a subject, and the rule that finds the datum is the same rule
that refuses those two. `plan_measurability.dart` already holds the other half of this: *"racks are
the datum and not the subject"*, so a pinned rack is counted in neither population.

**11.146.3 RULED: THE BOUND IS EXCLUDED FROM BOTH ROLLUPS AND COUNTED IN BOTH.** DR-020 §11.19.2(2)
says a bound *"never enters the footage rollup as a quantity"*, and the finding is that the sentence
reads on any rollup called footage. The user's call:

> The bound enters neither `Σ`. Both rollups grow a bound count beside the estimated count they
> already carry.

`Σ 11 runs · 601 ft · 3 estimated · 2 bound`. Summing a floor with ten totals produces a number that
is neither a floor nor a total, and the alternative put with it, *summed like an estimate*, would have
given the sheet footer and the materials page two different answers for one document with nothing on
either saying why. The third alternative, *excluded silently*, was refused for the reason
`Rollup.unknownCount` exists at all: a `Σ` that shrinks as more of the job gets planned, with no
count beside it explaining the shrinkage, is the flattering half.

**A BOUND ROW IS STILL AN UNKNOWN TO THE TAKEOFF, AND THAT IS NOT A DEMOTION.** In
`cable_footage.dart` a bound row lands in `footage.unknownCount` exactly as a lengthless row does,
because the question that rollup answers is *how much cable to order* and a floor answers it not at
all. `boundCount` sits beside it and says how much of that ignorance has a floor under it, which is
strictly more than the reader had before. `runCount` and `unknownLengthCount` are unchanged, so no
existing number moves.

**11.146.4 RULED: A FLOOR AND A GUESS ARE TWO CLAIMS AND GET TWO FLAGS.** `lengthIsEstimated` is the
italic flag and `ScheduleView.estimatedCount` is what §3.8's footer prints. The user's call:

> `lengthIsEstimated` stays **false** for a bound. A new `lengthIsBound` carries the `≥` and the
> exclusion. The renderer italicises on either.

A footer reading `5 estimated` on a document holding three guesses and two measured floors is wrong
about the one thing that footer exists to say, which is what the total rests on. The prefix is not
decoration and is not optional: *italic only* was refused because it makes a floor indistinguishable
in print from a room estimate, which is the confusion DR-020 was written to prevent.

**THE `≥` GOES IN `ScheduleEntry.lengthCell` AND NOT IN `scheduleLengthCell`.** The shared speller is
read by `pathway_table.dart`'s nominal length and by three `structure_table.dart` columns, none of
which can hold a bound, and one of those columns is parsed back by `parseLengthCell`. A prefix in the
shared function would put a character into cells that must round-trip and into cells that cannot
mean it.

**11.146.5 RULED: THE RULES READ THE FLOOR, AND ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT PROVES SOMETHING.** `#639`
says *"do not build the rules here"* and that sentence has expired. The user's call:

> An unmeasured run whose plan floor **already exceeds** the limit becomes a proven violation with its
> own message. A floor **under** the limit still emits *"length unknown, cannot verify"*.

That is DR-020 §11.19.2(2)'s asymmetry as executable code: *"a plan can prove a length violation and
can never prove compliance"*, because if the floor is already over the limit no route rescues it, and
if the floor is under it every route may still exceed it. The refused alternative was to feed the
bound into `knownLengthOf`, which reads `terminatedLength ?? cutLength` and is documented as *"the
length this run is known to be"*: a floor admitted there would pass a run under the limit, turning
the one statement a plan may honestly make into the one it may not.

**AND THIS TESTS DR-125's PREDICTION RATHER THAN CITING IT.** `rules_cable.dart`'s header records the
M5-H2 domain review's forecast that both rules *"will rarely fire before the plan view's run
estimation exists"*, and that the **unmeasured** limb would do nearly all the work until then. This
is the chapter that gives the other limb an input on a document nobody has measured.

**11.146.6 RULED BY CONSTRUCTION: A MISSING `riseAllowance` COSTS THE BOUND NOTHING IT IS ENTITLED
TO.** docs/15 §4.1 gives the bound as the straight line *"plus the location's `riseAllowance` if one
is set"*, and `Location.riseAllowance` is null on every location this product has ever written. A
null contributes zero, and **the result is still a true lower bound**, because dropping a
non-negative term from a floor leaves a floor. It is therefore not a G4 substitution and must not be
"improved" into one: this paragraph exists so that the next reader who notices the omission
understands it was priced. The allowance is read from **the subject carrier's own location**, the
outlet's or the off-rack device's, rather than from the schedule row's room fallback chain, because
the rise is a fact about where the device is and the row's chain can land on the far end's room.

**11.146.7 RULED: DR-050's "NO NEW TIER" IS SCOPED TO ROOM GEOMETRY, AND THE TIER STANDS.** Found by
reading this chapter's brief against canon rather than against the tree, one commit after the tier had
already been added on DR-037's authority. **§11.49.2 says, in terms, *"THEREFORE NO NEW TIER, AND THIS
IS THE RULING. `ScheduleLengthSource` gains nothing"*, and it is dated 2026-08-12**: two days after
DR-037 §11.36.4 ruled the rank and two days after `PLAN-G` was decomposed into a Story whose title is
*"`planLowerBound`, the fifth tier"*. Neither ruling lists the other in §12. A reader meeting those
words alone would stop, and one did.

The user's call is that **DR-050 answers the question it was asked**, which was whether a figure
derived from room vertices earns a tier of its own. It does not; it fills
`Location.estimatedRunLengthFromRack`. It does not reach the pin-to-pin floor, and three things in
DR-050's own text say so:

- **§11.49.4 preserves `planLowerBound` by name**, *"remains forbidden from the rollup"*. A ruling
  cannot forbid from a rollup a value it has just abolished.
- **§11.49.1's table lists it as *"not built"*, not as abolished**, in a table whose whole purpose is
  to separate the three sources that sum from the one that does not.
- **§11.49.2's reason does not reach it.** The objection is that *"a fourth tier would buy a
  provenance distinction"* between figures that all sum, and that wire is a consumable quoted with
  margin. A floor is not a provenance distinction: it is excluded from every `Σ`, prefixed `≥` and
  ranked below the estimate it can never replace. **The distinction it buys is behavioural**, and
  §11.146.3 is the behaviour.

**§11.49.5's two items are still owed and are still nobody's.** *"The geometry-to-estimate derivation
and the computed-versus-typed marker"* have zero implementation in this tree: no `Location` ceiling
height, no proposed-versus-typed flag, and no vertex gesture. They are not `PLAN-G`'s and this ruling
does not adopt them; they are recorded here because the census that found the collision also found
that the ruling on the other side of it is entirely unbuilt, which is why nothing in the tree had
made the two disagree out loud.

**11.146.8 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not a bound between two underlays. A carrier holds exactly one
`PlanPin` (DR-142 §11.141), so a rack pinned on `Level 1` can never be the datum for a drop pinned on
`Level 2`, and a two-storey job yields bounds only on the rack's floor. That is the honest answer and
`PlanMeasurability` already reports it per underlay as `noRackPinned`; a cross-plan bound would need a
vertical distance between floors that no floorplan carries. Not `PLN-003`'s severity or band, which
stay `PLAN-I`'s. Not the as-built tally (§4.2), which DR-020 already put outside this feature. And not
whether the Pull Sheet's footer prints the bound count, which is `PLAN-H`'s sheet and not this
chapter's derivation.

### §11.147 DR-148 · The rasteriser is deferred a second time, and the debt is wired into the exit criterion rather than into a review date

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-09**, at `PLAN-H`'s census. DR-145 §11.144.5 named `PLAN-H` as the
review point for a vendored pdfium, on the ground that a *"deferral with a fired trigger and no review
date is how a debt stops being visible."* This is that review.

**11.147.1 DR-145's STRUCTURAL REASON DOES NOT SURVIVE THE CENSUS, AND THE REVIEW STILL STOOD.**
§11.144.5 chose `PLAN-H` because *"`T1.01` is the first thing in this product that needs an underlay
**rendered** rather than **stored**, so the chapter that builds it is the first one whose own work is
blocked by the absence rather than merely inconvenienced by it."*

**`T1.01` is not blocked.** `PlanUnderlay.format` is `png | jpeg` by construction and has been since
`PLAN-C`; a PDF page is **lifted to one of those at import** (DR-138) and the member written to the
container is a raster. So the thing `T1.01` renders is a stored PNG or JPEG, which
`DiagramCanvas.drawImage` and `PdfImage` have both done since `PLAN-A`. **The rasteriser is an IMPORT
gap and not a RENDER gap**, and it belongs beside the importer rather than beside the sheet.

The review was held anyway, because a scheduled review that is skipped on the grounds that its stated
reason was wrong is a deferral with no review date by another route. What changed is the answer's
shape rather than its timing.

**11.147.2 RULED: THE DEFERRAL STANDS A SECOND TIME, AND THE SECOND TIME IS SAID OUT LOUD.** Nothing
displaces `PLAN-H`, `PLAN-I` or `PLAN-J`. The route is unchanged and is still not `pdfrx` (DR-138
§11.137): a direct FFI binding over a **vendored** pdfium, per CR-100.

**This is the second deferral of the same debt and the record says so**, because two deferrals with
one trigger between them is the shape a permanent omission takes when nobody counts.

**11.147.3 RULED: THE NEW TRIGGER IS THE EXIT CRITERION, NOT A DATE AND NOT A CHAPTER.** `PLAN-J`'s
drill is bound to **the CAD plot**, the three-page all-vector set of DR-145, rather than to whichever
of the two real sets happens to import.

**The epic therefore cannot close until the rasteriser exists.** That is the user's call and it is a
stronger instrument than a review point: a review can be held and deferred again, and an exit
criterion cannot be met by deciding to meet it later.

**AND IT ADDS NO SCOPE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING TWICE.** The exit criterion already says *"an
architect's floorplan PDF is imported **without leaving the app**"* (DR-037 §11.36.1, roadmap §4). A
plot from CAD **is** an architect's floorplan PDF, it is the form a drawing office produces without
doing anything to it, and this product refuses it. **The criterion has been unmeetable on that input
since the day it was written**, and nobody had noticed because the only set anybody had tried was the
JPEG one. So this is not an §8.3 amendment: it is the criterion read against an input it always
covered.

**11.147.4 RULED: THE DRILL'S OWN RISK IS RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED.** Put to the
user with the deferral: `PLAN-J` run on the JPEG set would **pass**, the exit criterion would read as
discharged, and half of the real PDF inputs this product has met would remain unimportable. A green
drill would have been evidence about callouts and legibility that a later reader would take as
evidence about import coverage.

Binding the drill to the harder input removes that reading rather than annotating it. **DR-145
§11.144.4's *"half the ordinary path is bought"* stops being a note and becomes a gate.**

**11.147.5 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the resolution a rasterisation uses, which DR-145
§11.144.7 already left open and which is still owed by whoever builds it: DR-137 §11.136.4's *"never
above the source's own effective resolution"* is a rule for a raster source and a vector source has no
such ceiling. Not the page picker's behaviour when every page is refused, likewise still DR-145's.
Not `PLAN-H`'s own content, which is unaffected in every chapter. And **not a licence or vendoring
question**: CR-100 governs the mechanism and DR-036's census covers what is in the tree today, so a
vendored pdfium reopens that census when it lands and not before.

---

### §11.148 DR-149 · The plan sheet's place in the set, how light it prints, and the export path that could not reach an underlay

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-09**, at `PLAN-H/1`'s census. Two presentation calls the corpus had
deliberately left open, and one finding that is upstream of every chapter in `PLAN-H`.

**11.148.1 THE EXPORT PATH STRUCTURALLY CANNOT REACH AN UNDERLAY, AND NO TICKET SAYS SO.**
`ExportRequest` carries `documentJson`, `fontBytes`, `fileName` and `issuedAt`. The underlay bytes
live in `DocumentSession.members`, written by `adopt` and read by the Plan editor;
`export_controller.dart` builds the request and **never passes them**. So:

| Piece | State before `PLAN-H` |
|---|---|
| `DiagramCanvas.drawImage`, `ImageRef` | built at `PLAN-A` |
| `PdfDiagramCanvas.drawImage` | built at `PLAN-A`, emits the `cm`/`Do` pair |
| `PdfImageResolver` | a **typedef with zero production call sites**; only `pdf_canvas_image_test.dart` supplies one |
| `ExportRequest.members` | **does not exist** |

**This is `PLAN-E/1`'s finding one package over.** That chapter found `FlutterImageResolver` had no
implementation and wrote `plan_image_cache.dart`, whose header says *"a typedef with no
implementation is a seam, not a feature"*. The export backend has been in exactly that state since
`PLAN-A` and nothing noticed, because no sheet asked for an image. **`T1.01` is the first caller**,
and the screen's solution is the model rather than a design question: load once, resolve
synchronously, because a paint callback cannot await and a decode per frame is tens of megabytes.

**11.148.2 AND THE SECOND BOOBY TRAP FIRES HERE, THOUGH NOBODY LEFT IT ON PURPOSE.**
`build_document.dart`'s `switch (sheet.role)` is exhaustive with no default and assigns a
definitely-assigned `final DiagramScene scene`, so **adding a fourth `SheetRole` stops the export
package compiling**. `PLAN-G/1` met the same shape in `cable_footage.dart`, where the arm was left
open *on purpose* and its header said so. This one is a consequence of definite assignment rather
than a decision, and the effect is identical and equally welcome: the slot cannot be added without a
sheet behind it.

**It also forces the chapter's shape.** `#640` reads as though the enum value could land alone; it
cannot, and a `case` that drew a frame over white paper would be the *"title block over white
paper"* docs/15 §7 already names as indistinguishable from a plan with no drops on it. So the slot,
the resolver, the screening and the sheet land together, and what `#641` keeps is the **evidence**:
the emitted bytes carry no `/SMask` and no `/ExtGState`.

**11.148.3 RULED: `T1.01` SITS AFTER `T0.02` AND BEFORE THE ELEVATIONS.** Cover, Symbol Legend,
Exceptions, **plans**, rack elevations, interconnect, schedules, details.

**The order was a choice and not a consequence**, which is why it was put to the user: docs/08 §2.2's
table is *not* numeric, `T5.01` sitting last at `n+5` after `T6.30`. The ground is the job rather than
the number: **a reader orients in the building before they open a rack**, which is the order the work
is walked, and it agrees with the NCS convention that puts `T1` plans ahead of `T2` elevations.

*Last, beside `T5.01`* was refused, though it has a real argument (both are `AUTO`, and a set whose
page count moves in the middle is harder to collate). *Immediately before the Pull Sheet* was refused
too, and it is the closest call: it couples the locator to the deliverable it serves. The set is
ordered by drawing type and not by errand, and `T6.10`'s callouts already carry the cross-reference.

**11.148.4 RULED: THE UNDERLAY PRINTS AT 25%, AND THE NUMBER IS CONFIRMED BY A LASER RATHER THAN BY
THIS RULING.** One named constant in the export backend, so changing it is a one-line edit and never a
re-import (docs/15 §7's own reason for putting the pass here rather than at import).

**25% and not 18%**, which is the legend chip's tint, because a chip is a swatch behind a single rule
and an architect's floorplan is line art whose walls, doors and dimension strings must survive the
pass. **25% and not 40%**, because the callout has to win: AC-054 requires every callout legible over
the screened underlay, and PAL-1's own exclusion block records this as *"the only new legibility
question this palette has met"*.

**THE HONEST HALF IS THAT NO NUMBER CHOSEN HERE IS EVIDENCE.** AC-054 sets the standard as a print on
a real greyscale laser at ANSI B, `PLAN-J`'s drill is where that happens, and this ruling names it as
the confirmation point. A screening value argued from a monitor is a stated
cost wearing a measurement's clothes.
Moving it after the drill is a one-line change and is **expected rather than a defect**.

**11.148.5 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the callout pill's own geometry or colour, which is
`PLAN-H/3`'s and which CR-078 already constrains to the signal **domain**. Not the leader-line rule.
Not the scale bar (`PLAN-H/4`) or the per-plan device schedule (`PLAN-H/5`). Not whether a project
with several underlays orders its plan sheets by `PlanUnderlay.order` or by location name: `order` is
a `FracIndex` the user controls and every other per-entity sheet in this product sorts on it, so it is
taken rather than decided. And not the resolution question DR-145 §11.144.7 left open, which belongs
to whoever builds the rasteriser.

### §11.149 DR-150 · A pin has no domain, so a callout has no colour, and the screening turns PAL-1's open obligation into arithmetic

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-09**, at `PLAN-H/3`'s census. `#642` is one of the two `PLAN-H`
briefs that describe a tree which has moved since 2026-08-10, and the movement is recorded in the
tree itself.

**11.149.1 THE BRIEF'S COLOUR RULE CANNOT BE APPLIED, AND THE FILE THAT SAYS SO IS ONE CHAPTER
YOUNGER THAN THE BRIEF.** `#642` reads *"callouts carry the device designator and reuse the
schematic's tag-pill geometry and the signal domain's colour (CR-078: colour lives on the DOMAIN,
never the family)."*

**A pin carries no domain.** It hangs on one of docs/15 §3.4's three carriers and none of them
resolves one:

| Carrier | What it knows about signal |
|---|---|
| `Rack` | nothing. It is the datum, not a signal path |
| `Outlet` | `designation`, `tia570Grade`, a `service` string on its gangs. **No `SignalFamilyId`, no `SignalDomainId`** |
| `OffRackPlacement`'s device | ports across several domains. A television is video **and** network |

`plan_scene.dart` wrote this down at `PLAN-E/2`, one chapter after `#642` was filed: the marker's
kind *"is deliberately NOT a colour decision here: CR-078 puts colour on the signal domain, and a pin
carries no domain."* The brief asked for a colour from a fact the model does not hold.

**AND THE DELIVERABLE IS GREYSCALE ANYWAY.** AC-054 sets the standard as a print on a real greyscale
laser, and DR-037 §11.36.1's drill hands a person that print. A hue chosen here reaches the person the
sheet is for as a grey.

**11.149.2 RULED: ONE UNIFORM CALLOUT, OPAQUE, BLACK.** A white-filled stadium with a black hairline
outline and black text, masking whatever is beneath it.

**A KNOCK-OUT IS NOT A CONTRAST DECISION, WHICH §11.149.4 MAKES CLEAR.** Black text on the darkest
sample the screening can leave is 11.5:1, so luminance was never the problem. **Dense line work is,**
and it fails by pattern rather than by contrast: a dimension string crossing a designator is
unreadable at any ratio. Masking is what a callout bubble is for in drafting, and it makes legibility
unconditional rather than a function of what the architect drew at that spot.

Carrier kind stays distinguished by the **marker shape** `plan_scene.dart` already draws, which is
where DR-140's rack-is-not-a-device distinction already lives. The two refused alternatives were a
tint by carrier kind, which buys on a colour printer what the marker already carries and buys nothing
on the only printer the criterion names; and porting the schematic's translucent pill verbatim, which
is right on the uniform paper the schematic has and puts a wash over walls here.

**11.149.3 RULED: THE CALLOUT PRINTS THE CARRIER'S OWN DESIGNATOR.** `RK-1`, `WP-1`, `TV-1`.

The exit criterion says *"a callout for every pinned drop, each printing the designator its Pull
Sheet row prints"*, and a pinned outlet can have **several** Pull Sheet rows: a row is a `Link` and a
drop can carry three cables. **The cable designator is therefore not a function of a pin**, and
choosing it would put three overlapping callouts on one dot. The carrier's designator is one string
per pin, it appears on every Pull Sheet row for that drop, and it names the wall rather than the
cable, which is what somebody standing in the room is looking for.

*Both, stacked* was refused on the sheet rather than on the principle: it doubles every pill's height,
and on a 60-drop rough-in at ANSI B that is the difference between a plan and a field of boxes.

**11.149.4 RULED BY ARITHMETIC: THE SCREENING DISCHARGES PAL-1's OPEN OBLIGATION, AND THE CHECK IS
MECHANICAL.** `tools/pal1_check.py`'s own exclusion block has carried
`CALLOUT_OVER_UNDERLAY_IS_CHECKED_AT = 'PLAN-H/3'` since `PLAN-A/5`, recording that the underlay's
exclusion from PAL-1 does **not** cover *"the requirement that callout glyphs remain separable against
a non-white background ... the first background in the corpus."*

**It is decidable because the screening is a constant.** The darkest sample 25% ink can leave is
`255 - ⌊255 × 250 / 1000⌋ = 192`, and black on 192 is **11.54:1**, past WCAG AAA. The break-even for
4.5:1 is **550 per-mille**, so DR-149's 250 carries a 2.2× margin and even the 40% the user refused
would have passed at 7.37:1.

**THE CHECK IS COMPUTED FROM THE CONSTANT AND NEVER FROM A COPY OF IT.** `pal1_check.py` parses
`kUnderlayInkRetained` out of `plan_image.dart`, on `registry_parity.py`'s precedent for a Python gate
reading Dart source. A second copy of a moving number is a liability, and this corpus has swept that
mistake five times. Raising the screening past 550 fails the gate rather than degrading a sheet
quietly.

**canon §14.1's LESSON IS WHY IT IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT AN EYE.** PAL-1 shipped collisions three times
because *"the rule was checked by inspection"* and read at the domain level rather than over rendered
values. The same discipline applied here means the obligation is discharged by a number the gate can
recompute, not by looking at a proof.

**11.149.5 RULED: A RING OF CANDIDATE OFFSETS, THEN A LEADER.** docs/15 §7: *"a leader line is drawn
only when the pill cannot sit within its own pin's clearance."* The placement takes the preferred
offset, walks a fixed ring of alternatives when that box overlaps one already placed, and draws a
leader when the chosen spot is past the clearance radius.

**IT IS A HEURISTIC AND THE RECORD SAYS SO**, rather than a layout solver. It is deterministic because
`planPinsFor` already orders pins totally by entity id, which was built for the display-list
comparison and pays a second time here.

**AND A CALLOUT IS NEVER DROPPED.** When the ring is exhausted the pill is placed at its preferred
offset anyway, overlapping, with a leader. **An absent callout is a drop the stranger cannot find and
an overlapping one is a drop they can read twice**, which is G4's asymmetry: the sheet reports what it
could not place cleanly rather than silently printing fewer callouts than there are pins.

**11.149.6 THE PILL IS BUILT IN CORE, AND THE BRIEF'S "REUSE" WAS NOT AVAILABLE.** `#642` says to
reuse the schematic's tag-pill geometry. `_PillSizer` is **private to
`rackpal_ui/src/canvas/schematic/wire_trace.dart`**, and `rackpal_export` may never import
`rackpal_ui` (docs/03 §7.1). The bundle has recorded this since 2026-07-28 as *"a violation in
waiting"* that leaves M6's interconnect sheets unbuildable until the file moves.

**This chapter does not move it.** `wire_trace.dart` is the drawn-wire staircase plus its pill, it is
M6's blocker rather than this sheet's, and moving a thousand-line file to borrow ninety of them would
put an unrelated migration inside a chapter about callouts. What is taken is the **reasoning**, which
is what a shared rule actually is: near-edge anchoring rather than centring, height from the type size
rather than from font metrics so screen and paper agree, and a stadium radius. Each is cited where it
is used.

**11.149.7 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE.** Not the leader's own arrowhead or terminal, which the drawing
does without. Not a north arrow, which has no field on `PlanUnderlay` to read. Not the per-plan device
schedule (`PLAN-H/5`) or the scale bar (`PLAN-H/4`). Not whether `wire_trace.dart` moves to core,
which stays M6's and stays recorded. And not the callout's type size as a final figure: it is a
starting value like `kPlanMarkerRadiusFraction`, and `PLAN-J`'s print drill is where a size read at
arm's length is settled.
