`Esc` has never worked on this surface either**: `planCancel` shipped at `PLAN-E/5` as the scope's
only binding, is green in its own cases, and could not fire. Fixed here, because §11.161.1's key
would have been dead on arrival for the same reason.

**AND NO POINTER GESTURE REACHES THE PLAN TAB AT THE APP MOUNTING**, measured by the first
app-level test ever to open it: a tap does not select a pin, a drag does not move one, and a drag on
the rail's grip does not reorder. All three work in `rackpal_ui`'s own suites, and
`signposting_test.dart` taps the RACK canvas in the same harness, so it is specific to this tab.
**Whether that is the product or the test harness is NOT settled here and is not guessed at.** Board
`#882` carries the evidence and the one-minute check that tells them apart. This ruling's two
gestures are proved at the widget level; the app-level proof is owed and is named as owed.

**11.161.7 Scope.** **No scope change.** Both commands are `PLAN-C` work that shipped without a
caller; this rules how they are reached, inside scope the Plan view already owns. Board `#878` cites
it, and `#872`'s exemption list loses both rows.

---

### 11.162 DR-163 · A 0U channel is added, removed and occupied from the inspector

**The question.** AC-044 rules that in v1 *"a 0U occupant is created and edited from the inspector
(channel, start U, span) and renders as a plain bar; there is simply no drag gesture."* **The
inspector half was never built.** `zero_u_commands.dart` holds three commands with real reverts,
three plan functions with real refusals, and `occupantsOfZeroUChannel`, whose own doc says it is
*"Public because the inspector needs to say 'AMP-1 is in this channel' before offering to delete
it"*. Nothing in `lib/` constructed two of the three commands or called any of the three planners.

`#875` made the third reachable by wiring PWR-003's remedy, which mints a channel so a 0U PDU has
somewhere to sit. `add_outlets.dart` quotes AC-044 while doing it and says why it is not the same
thing: *"this is not a person: it is a remedy the person asked for by name."* So a channel could
appear in a rack and nobody could add one deliberately, move the PDU inside it, or take it away.

**11.162.1 RULED: THE RACK INSPECTOR OWNS BOTH, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THAT WAS A CORRECTION.**
Settled by the user on 2026-09-13, twice.

A channel is a rail on a rack and belongs to the rack's panel, which was never in doubt. The
occupant's channel and start U were ruled onto the DEVICE inspector first, because that is where
AC-044 puts them (*"created and edited from the inspector (channel, start U, span)"*) and where every
other device property is edited. **It was built there and it could not be reached.**

**A 0U OCCUPANT CANNOT BE SELECTED.** `draw/scene/scene_builder.dart` reads
`if (placement is! RailPlacement) continue;`, so a 0U device is never in the elevation's scene, never
hit-tested and never selectable. AC-044's other half, *"renders as a plain bar"*, was never built
either, which is what makes the first half unreachable: **the ruling's two clauses depend on each
other and only one of them shipped.**

So a section on the device inspector would have been a surface nothing could open, which is the exact
defect `#872` exists to catch, in the ticket closing `#872`'s last two rows. The fields moved under
their channel in the rack panel, which `Ctrl+Alt+U` reaches with nothing selected. **The alternative
was building the bar first**, and it was refused as a separate body of work rather than as a bad idea:
it is scene geometry, a hit-test and selection for a placement the scene builder drops on one line,
and it is owed whether or not these fields exist.

**RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY RE-AIMED.** The first answer was given against a premise that turned
out to be false, and a ruling that silently ended up somewhere else would leave the next reader
believing the device inspector had been considered and rejected on its merits.

**AND THE FIELDS HAVE SINCE MOVED BACK, BY DR-167 §11.166 (2026-09-13).** `#883` drew the bar and
made a 0U device selectable, so the obstacle this clause reasons from is gone. Everything above
stands as the record of why they were ever anywhere else; where they ARE is the device inspector,
which is where AC-044 put them all along.

**11.162.2 RULED: ADDING A CHANNEL TAKES ITS BOUNDS UP FRONT**, in a form of side, start U, end U and
an optional name, rather than a one-click default the person then corrects.

**THE REASON IS A CONSTRAINT AND NOT A PREFERENCE: THERE IS NO COMMAND THAT EDITS A CHANNEL'S
BOUNDS.** `zero_u_commands.dart` has add and remove and nothing else, so a channel whose extent is
wrong is replaced rather than corrected. A one-click full-height default would therefore be a claim
about the rack that somebody who wanted U 1 to U 12 has to delete and retype, and
`add_outlets.dart`'s own comment promised an editability that has never existed (*"an ordinary one
they can edit or remove afterwards"*), which is now corrected to say what is true.

**A FOURTH COMMAND WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED HERE.** `SetZeroUChannelBoundsCommand` would remove the
constraint rather than design around it, and it carries a question this ruling does not want to
answer in passing: a channel shrinking under an occupant has to re-run `PLC-003` for every device in
it, which is `planSetZeroUPosition`'s job pointed backwards. It is a legitimate later chapter.

**11.162.3 THE PLANNERS ARE THE VALIDATION, AND THE SURFACE ADDS NONE.** `planAddZeroUChannel`
already refuses a duplicate id, an inverted span and a span that does not fit the rack, each with a
sentence naming the rack and the numbers. `planRemoveZeroUChannel` refuses while occupied and names
the occupant. `planSetZeroUPosition` re-runs `evaluatePlacement` and returns `PLC-003`'s own message.
A second copy of any of those checks in a widget is how the dialog and the edit come to disagree,
which is DR-013 §11.13.2's rule arriving at a different surface.

**11.162.4 AND THE ONE CHANNEL THE PRODUCT COULD MAKE WAS OUT BY ONE.** Found on the way.
`add_outlets.dart` wrote `startU: 0, endU: heightU - 1` and cited **CR-025** for it; CR-025 rules
*"1-based, bottom origin, `ruIndex` in [1, heightU]"* and calls itself the contradiction that *"will
actually hurt"*. Every starter, every other test, `placement_rules.dart`'s inclusive length and
`rack_shrink.dart`'s normalisation of *"an inverted or sub-1 channel"* all disagreed with it, and
`planAddZeroUChannel` would have refused it outright.

**THE SHARP PART IS THAT THE GUARD EXISTED AND THE PRODUCER BYPASSED IT.** The remedy builds
`AddZeroUChannelCommand` directly, so the planner's `startU < 1` check never ran on the only path
that ships. **A validated planner beside an unvalidated producer protects the callers it does not
have**, and `#876` is what gave it one. Fixed, with the test that had pinned the defect as intended
behaviour corrected in the same commit.

**11.162.5 WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** It does not build AC-044's deferred half: no gutter rendering, no
drag-into-gutter, no resize handles, no `G` toggle and no overlap warnings, all of which that ruling
sends to v1.1. It does not let a person CREATE a 0U occupant from nothing either: placing a device
into a channel is `catalog_placement.dart`'s, and AC-044's *"created"* is satisfied by the palette
placing a 0U-capable device, not by a control in this panel.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-13, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN.** The
palette cannot place a 0U-capable device. `catalog_placement.dart`, the file this clause defers to,
refuses one with *"P01 is a 0U occupant: it mounts in a vertical channel, not rail holes. **Add it
from the rack inspector** (AC-044)."* **So this panel deferred to the palette and the palette defers
to this panel**, and between the two of them nothing in the product could put a device in a channel
at all. DR-164 §11.163 rules the control, and the sentence above stands as written because what it
got wrong is the point.

**AND IT DOES NOT BUILD THE PLAIN BAR, WHICH IS STILL OWED.** AC-044 puts that in v1 and
§11.162.1 is why it matters: a 0U occupant is invisible in the elevation and unselectable, so the
only place it can be seen or edited is the rack inspector's list. Board `#883` carries it, with the
one line in `scene_builder.dart` that drops it.

**11.162.6 Scope.** **No scope change.** AC-044 already scopes the inspector surface to v1 and this
builds the part of it that was owed. Board `#876` cites it, and `#872`'s exemption list loses its
last two rows.

### 11.163 DR-164 · A device is put into a 0U channel from the channel's own row

**The question.** `#876` built the rack inspector's 0U list and this is the hole underneath it:
**nothing in the product can put a device in a channel.** Reported by the user on 2026-09-13 as
*"the rack inspector list doesn't actually show a 0U device at all"*, which is true of every project
a person made and always was.

**MEASURED.** `buildPlaceFromCatalogCommand` takes a `ZeroUTarget? zeroU`, and the branch behind it
is complete: it builds the `ZeroUPlacement`, runs `evaluatePlacement` and returns `PLC-003`'s
refusal by name. **`ZeroUTarget` has one definition, one mention in an `add_outlets.dart` comment
and zero call sites.** The only reachable writer of a `ZeroUPlacement` in the product is
`planSetZeroUPosition`, which MOVES one that already exists. The three starters that do show a PDU
get it from `tool/starters/authoring.dart` writing the placement directly, bypassing every command.

**11.163.1 THE GAP WAS RECORDED, AND RECORDED AS HANDLED.** §11.162.5 says placing into a channel
*"is `catalog_placement.dart`'s"* and that AC-044's *"created"* is *"satisfied by the palette"*. The
file it names is where the falsehood is visible: the palette's 0U row is refused there with *"Add it
from the rack inspector (AC-044)."* **Each surface deferred to the other.** A deferral reads as a
decision and not as a gap, so `#876` shipped a list, a remove that refuses while occupied, and a
move between channels, over a set that nothing could ever add to.

**11.163.2 RULED: AN `Add device…` CONTROL ON THE CHANNEL'S OWN ROW.** Settled by the user on
2026-09-13, against dragging from the palette onto the rendered bar. The bar does not exist
(`#883`), so the drag would put the only producer behind the one clause AC-044 has already left
unbuilt, which is §11.162.1's trap a second time and in the same feature. The control is reachable
today, it makes the refusal sentence above TRUE for the first time, and it makes this ruling's own
title true rather than needing it walked back.

**11.163.3 THE OCCUPANT LANDS AT THE CHANNEL START**, and is moved afterwards with `#876`'s row.
Not "the first free offset": **a 0U occupant has no extent anywhere in the format**, which
`zero_u_commands.dart` records as a known model gap and the seed catalog's one 0U device confirms
with `frontU: 0, rearU: 0`. With no extent there is no overlap, so "free" has no meaning and an
offset search would be arithmetic dressed as a rule. `PLC-003` still checks the offset lands inside
the channel, which is the check that exists.

**11.163.4 AND THE NEW OCCUPANT IS NOT SELECTED**, which every other placement in this product does.
`_finalizeCatalogPlacement` does two things in one breath: it requests CANVAS FOCUS and it makes the
placed device the sole selection (docs/04 §3.1 step 6). Pairing those here would leave the keyboard
aimed at the canvas with **a device the elevation never draws** selected, and the next `Delete` or
arrow key would act on something nobody can see. `Delete` is the sharp one: `_deleteSelection`
removes an unwired device with **no confirmation at all**, by design, because `confirmDeviceRemoval`
only builds a dialog when something would be cascaded. So the rack panel keeps the keyboard, the new
row appears under its channel, and this is `#883` shaping a decision rather than blocking one: it
reverses when the bar lands.

**THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS CLAUSE GAVE THE WRONG REASON AND A MUTATION CAUGHT IT.** It said selecting
would swap the inspector from the rack panel to a device panel. **It would not.** `_inspectorTarget`
is moved by canvas GESTURES and never by `_selection.apply`, so the rack panel stays either way; the
case asserting it stayed passed with the mutation applied, which is how the error surfaced. **A test
that cannot fail is not evidence**, and that one was defending a mechanism rather than an artifact.
What it defends now is the artifact: after a placement, `Delete` does not destroy what was just
placed.

**11.163.5 THE PICKER READS THE DOCUMENT**, not the seed catalog, on DR-077 §11.76.1: a 0U template
authored in the Device Builder is in the document and in no catalog. One 0U template ships (`P01`,
`catalog_power.dart`), so most projects list one row, and a project with none says so rather than
opening an empty dialog.

**11.163.6 Scope.** **No scope change.** AC-044's *"created and edited from the inspector"* is v1
scope, and this is the half of it `#876` deferred to a path that refuses. Board `#884` cites it.

### 11.164 DR-165 · The device palette is the shell's, so the Plan view can place a device

**The question.** docs/15 §6's gesture table opens with *"Drag from the device palette or staging bin
onto the plan: places the device and sets its pin in one command."* **The command half is built**
(`buildPlaceOnPlanCommand`, which carries the pin on the placement so one undo restores both) and
**the gesture half is built** (`PlanCanvasScreenState.armPaletteDrag`, public, whose own comment says
*"the host that owns a palette hands the armed pointer down, and `PLAN-E/5` wires the real one"*).

**MEASURED: `armPaletteDrag` has three call sites and all three are tests.** `DevicePalettePanel`
has exactly one mount in the tree, inside `RackCanvasScreen`, so when the Plan tab is open the
palette is not on screen at all. `PLAN-E/5` shipped the tab and the layout and did not bring it.

**What it costs today.** A field device can only be born in the Rack tab. Its palette row **refuses
to drag** there, deliberately, because docs/04 §3.1 is *"drag from palette to RAILS"* and a
`notInRack` body has no rails to snap to; so it is created by double-click, lands as an
`OffRackPlacement`, and is **invisible in the view that created it**. It reappears only after a tab
change, in the Plan view's unpinned strip. Three surfaces and a tab change for *"put a camera in the
living room"*.

**11.164.1 RULED: THE PALETTE IS HOISTED, AND `RackCanvasScreen` STOPS OWNING ONE.** Settled by the
user on 2026-09-13, against a second mount in the Plan view's own layout. docs/15 §6 says there is
*"no fourth region and no plan-specific palette; the device palette is the device palette"*, and two
instances of one widget is the sentence obeyed in the letter and broken in the spirit: the search
query would not survive a tab change, and *"the palette"* would have two code paths for the rest of
the product's life.

**A `PaletteHost` OWNS WHAT IS IN THE COLUMN**: the row list and its memo, the search field's
controller, and the `/` handler. It wraps the whole tab view, so there is one search query and one
memo rather than one per tab. **It lays nothing out** (§11.164.5), and the COLUMN itself is placed
by each view that wants one, in that view's own layout: the Rack tab and the Plan tab, and no other.
The Structure editor places outlets and plates from surfaces of its own, and a device palette there
would be a control that cannot act on anything in view, which is docs/04 §3.4's rule about a control
that silently does nothing.

**11.164.2 THE HOST HANDS OVER A RESOLVED ROW, NOT A KEY**, and that removes a defect rather than
only some duplication. A `rowKey` is `source/id@version` and a template id is not (DR-102
§11.101.4), and the two are different strings that both read as *"which template"*.
`PlanCanvasScreenState._placeFromPalette` took a `rowKey` and passed it straight to
`buildPlaceOnPlanCommand` as a **`catalogId`**, which would have resolved nothing for any real row;
its three tests pass a bare id, so the parameter was never given the value its own name promised.
**Handing over the `PlaceableTemplate` makes the wrong call unrepresentable**, and it leaves the row
list with one owner instead of two.

**11.164.3 THE SEARCH FIELD'S FOCUS NODE IS OWNED BY THE COMMON ANCESTOR**, which is the shell. The
insertion caret's activation reads `_canvasFocus.hasFocus || _paletteSearchFocus.hasFocus`, because
arming a placement from the search box is a placement gesture and the caret must stay lit across the
hand-off. That is the CANVAS's rule about its own caret, so the canvas keeps it and reads a node it
was handed. The alternative, a notifier reporting focus upward and a second copy of the rule in the
host, is two things that can disagree about one fact.

**THIS CLAUSE FIRST SAID THE HOST OWNS IT AND LENDS IT DOWN, AND THAT CANNOT WORK.** The shell
builds the tab bodies during its own `build`, before `PaletteHostState` exists, so a node created in
the host is not there to lend and the canvas spends its first frame reading null. Two widgets need
the node and neither is the other's parent, so its owner is the one above both. The same argument
already governs the drag-row notifier, which the palette reads while it builds and the canvas writes
from a drag that starts after.

**11.164.4 AND `/` REACHES THE PALETTE FROM BOTH VIEWS.** `focusPaletteSearch` is `KeyScope.rack`
today and gains `KeyScope.plan`, since a palette a person can see and cannot reach from the keyboard
is half a surface. Same binding, same intent, one more scope.

**11.164.5 AND THE COLUMN IS PLACED BY THE VIEW, NOT BESIDE THE TAB VIEW.** Found by a test, and the
mechanism is worth keeping. The first build drew the column as a sibling of the shell's `TabBarView`
with a `showColumn` flag, which is the obvious shape and the wrong one: **a `TabBarView` is a
`PageView`, and a `PageView` positions by PIXEL OFFSET**, `index * viewportWidth`. Hiding a 280px
column widens the viewport by 280, so an offset animated for the old width lands between pages.
Tapping `Schematic` from the Rack tab showed `Structured Wiring`, one page short, every time.

Two smaller versions of the same mistake were passed through on the way, and both are the kind that
a suite catches and a person does not. A conditional child in a `Row` shifts its siblings, because
multi-child elements are matched BY POSITION: `if (showColumn) ...[column, divider]` moved the canvas
from slot 2 to slot 0 and destroyed every tab's `State`. And an `InheritedWidget` carrying a `State`
OBJECT must notify on every rebuild, since comparing `state != old.state` asks "was this widget
replaced" and never "did anything change": with that comparison a template saved while the canvas
was open never reached the palette.

**So the host provides and the view places.** The page width never moves, and *which views have a
palette* becomes a fact about those views rather than a flag passed down from above.

**11.164.6 Scope.** **No scope change, on DR-143's precedent.** The gesture is in docs/15 §6's own
table and has been since the chapter brief; this is an unbuilt clause reaching its producer, exactly
as the floorplan importer did. Board `#885` cites it.


### 11.165 DR-166 · A 0U occupant has a span, and it draws as a bar on its rail

**The question.** AC-044 keeps two things in v1: a 0U occupant is *"created and edited from the
inspector (channel, start U, span)"* and *"renders as a plain bar"*. `#876` built two of those three
fields and `#883` is the bar. **Neither could be finished, for one reason: the model has no extent
for a 0U occupant.**

**MEASURED.** `ZeroUPlacement` carries `channelId`, `offsetFromChannelStart` and `orientation`.
`TemplateBody` carries `bodyDepth`, `chassisWidth` and `frontU`/`rearU`, both **0** for a 0U body,
and no physical length at all. `PLC-003` treats the occupant as a POINT: it checks the offset lies
within `[0, channelLength]` and asks nothing about what comes after it.
`zero_u_commands.dart` recorded the gap in its own header the day those commands were written, and
said closing it *"is a ruling and not a code review"*. This is that ruling.

**11.165.1 RULED: `ZeroUPlacement` GAINS A SPAN ALONG THE CHANNEL.** Settled by the user on
2026-09-13, against two alternatives that both invent a length the file does not hold. Running the
bar *"from its start U to the end of its channel"* is honest only while one occupant is in a
channel, and `#884`'s `Add device…` puts every occupant at offset 0, so two in one channel would
draw two identical bars. Spanning *the whole channel* is simpler still and makes `#876`'s **Start U**
field change nothing visible, which is docs/04 §3.4's silently-does-nothing defect arriving through
the back door.

**A `Len` and not a count of U**, on `offsetFromChannelStart`'s precedent and CR-001's: the field
beside it is a `Len`, the channel's own length is computed as one, and a vertical PDU is not a whole
number of rack units long. The inspector edits it in U because the channel's bounds and the start
are in U, and the two existing converters already do that arithmetic in one place.

**11.165.2 ABSENT IS UNKNOWN, WHICH IS G4 AND NOT A DEFAULT.** Every document that exists today has
no span, so this is the common case rather than an edge. An occupant with no span **draws as a
one-U stub carrying G4's unknown marker**, not as a bar whose length nothing in the file supports:
the drawing says *"this device is here and its length is not recorded"*, which is exactly what G4
asks of a rollup and had never been asked of a rendering. It serializes as an **absent key**, never
an explicit null (CR-114). The four starters are regenerated with real spans, so the only documents
left in that state are ones made before this shipped.

**11.165.3 `PLC-003` IS WIDENED, NOT JOINED BY A SECOND RULE.** Its rationale already reads *"A
device in a channel this rack does not have, or past the end of one, has nothing to screw into"*,
and an occupant whose TAIL hangs off the end is that sentence exactly. A second, unnumbered refusal
sitting beside a numbered rule about the same physical fact is the drift CR-021 exists to stop, and
this file has already paid for it once, when `PLC-001` was transcribed by hand into a planner and
had to be given its rule id back. The summary becomes *"the occupant lies within the channel"* and
the widened predicate gets its own AC-051 pair.

**11.165.4 THE BAR SITS ON THE RAIL**, which is where a 0U PDU is screwed in. Each rail is ≈7.9
diagram units wide at zoom 1, derived from the real EIA-19 flange of 15.875 mm rather than from a
figure in a spec, and `ZeroUChannelSide` already names front/rear × left/right, which is precisely
the two rails of the face being drawn. **No new width and no layout change**, so every elevation and
every printed sheet keeps its geometry, and v1.1's 16 px gutters can still be added outside the
panel when that half lands.

**11.165.5 WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUILD.** AC-044's deferred half stays deferred and this ruling does
not quietly take a bite of it: no 16 px gutters, no **rotated** bar rendering, no drag-into-gutter,
no resize handles, no `G` toggle and no channel-overlap warnings. `ZeroUOrientation` is still
written and still unread; the bar runs ALONG its channel whichever value it holds, and the rotation
that value exists for is v1.1's.

**11.165.6 AND §11.162.1's REASON IS NOW SPENT.** The occupant's channel and start U were moved to
the rack panel because a 0U device **could not be selected**. It can now, so the reason on the
record no longer holds and the placement went back to the user as a live question rather than being
inherited.

**ANSWERED THE SAME DAY BY DR-167 §11.166**: they move to the device inspector. This clause said
they would stay, which was true for as long as it took to ask.

**11.165.7 Scope.** **No scope change for the bar or the inspector field**, both of which AC-044 puts
in v1 in as many words. **The MODEL FIELD is new and is ruled here**: it is CR-117's byte surface, it
is additive, and `Placement.unknown` carries it unharmed through a reader that does not know it.
Board `#883` cites it.

### 11.166 DR-167 · The 0U occupant's fields move to the device inspector

**The question.** AC-044 puts a 0U occupant's *"channel, start U, span"* on the inspector, and every
other device property is edited on the DEVICE inspector. §11.162.1 put these three on the RACK panel
and said exactly why: **a 0U device could not be selected**, because `scene_builder.dart` dropped
every non-rail placement, so the device panel could never open on one. §11.165.6 recorded that
`#883` removed that reason and that the fields stayed put on a fresh decision rather than an
inherited one.

**11.166.1 RULED: THEY MOVE.** Settled by the user on 2026-09-13, once the bar existed and the
device could be clicked. Both earlier clauses are corrected in place rather than left to read as
current, because a reader who finds a placement argued from an obstacle that is gone will re-derive
the wrong conclusion from it.

**11.166.2 THE CHANNELS STAY ON THE RACK PANEL, and that is not a compromise.** A channel is a rail
on a rack: adding one, removing one, and the occupant count that makes a Remove about to refuse say
so first are all facts about the RACK. What moved is the occupant's own channel, start U and span,
which are facts about the DEVICE. **Nothing is editable in two places**, which is the point of
moving them rather than copying them, and a case pins that the rack panel still NAMES what is in a
channel while no longer editing it.

**11.166.3 Scope.** **No scope change.** AC-044 puts these fields on the inspector in v1 and always
did; this is the surface arriving where that ruling pointed. Board `#887` cites it.

### 11.167 DR-168 · The Location and Plan views are one view, called Site

**The question.** Two tabs do adjacent halves of one job: `Locations` holds the project's location
tree, and `Plan` holds floorplan underlays, the room outlines drawn on them, and the pins. The user
asked for them merged, and `plan_editor_screen.dart` has carried a note since `PLAN-E/5` saying a
merge *"IS POSSIBLE BEFORE v1"* and was deliberately not designed for in that chapter.

**11.167.1 THE MERGE IS HALF-DONE ALREADY, AND docs/15 §6 SAYS SO.** That section's layout paragraph
reads: *"Left is the underlay list and the location tree, read-only with the same 'edit in
`Project ▸ Locations…`' affordance the Structure editor uses (CR-112)."* **The tree has been in the
Plan view's rail since the chapter brief.** What the design withheld was EDITING it there, and the
affordance it named instead **points at a menu the application does not have**: there is no `Project`
menu, Locations was promoted to a tab by DR-091 §11.90, and three on-screen strings still send people
to look for it (`#888`). The room list in that rail today was added on the user's own call on
2026-09-11, on the reasoning that *"the thing you are working through is listed where you work"*.

**11.167.2 RULED: ONE VIEW, CALLED `Site`, AT POSITION 1.** Settled by the user on 2026-09-13. The
name is neither half's: a site HAS rooms, and some of those rooms are drawn on a floorplan. It
survives a project that never imports a plan, which is the state CR-112 exists to protect, and it
does not read as though one of the two views won.

**POSITION 1 IS `Locations`' PLACE, and the job order is otherwise untouched.** §11.90.3's sequence
is *"survey the site, decide what equipment exists, mount it, pull cable to it, interconnect it, mark
where it physically sits, hand over the paperwork"*, and the surveying end is where a merged view
belongs: the rooms are the first thing anybody enters and the last thing a plan gets drawn onto.

**11.167.3 §11.90.3's TABLE GOES FROM SEVEN ROWS TO SIX, and §11.90.4 is what permits it.** That
clause refuses to freeze the strip, in terms: *"the view set is not final until M6."* It is written
about Plan arriving and Rear Panel arriving in v1.1, and it reads the same way for two views
becoming one. **The order is not re-argued and no other view moves.**

**11.167.4 THE RAIL IS THE TREE, AND THE UNDERLAY LIST APPEARS WHEN THERE IS AN UNDERLAY.** A project
with no floorplan is an ordinary project, not an empty view with an import button, which is CR-112 and
docs/04 §7.5 read as a layout requirement rather than a data one: *"a project with racks and no
Structure device must still be able to say which room a rack is in."*

**11.167.5 THE TREE CREATES A ROOM; AN OUTLINE IS AN ATTRIBUTE OF ONE.** Drawing-creates-a-room was
put to the user and refused. **One producer**, and the reason is CR-047: an arbitrary-depth tree makes
a new room answer *which parent, which kind, where in the order*, and a drag on a floorplan has
nowhere to ask. The tree stays the source of truth for a project that has no plan at all, and the
merge buys adjacency and a shared selection rather than a second way to make a room.

**11.167.6 WHAT IS NOT AMENDED.** **CR-112 stands**: the tree is not owned by the Structure editor or
the rack editor, and it still is not. **CR-047 stands**: one arbitrary-depth tree of which every other
surface is a view. **docs/15 §6's "no fourth region" stands** and is restated for a view that holds a
tree, an underlay list, a plan and the standard inspector; the rail is one region whose contents
depend on the document, not two regions.

**11.167.7 AND `showLocationsPanel` IS DELETED RATHER THAN PORTED.** It has **no caller in `lib/` and
none in any test**: it is the modal route CR-112's ellipsis promised, superseded when DR-091 promoted
Locations to a tab, and left behind. Seventh instance of the no-producer shape after DR-143, `#674`,
`PLAN-E/5`, `LEN-A/3`, `#870` and `#885`.

**11.167.8 Scope.** **No scope change.** Both jobs stay in v1 and neither loses a clause; what changes
is how many tabs they are behind, which §11.90.4 already declined to fix before M6. Board `#889`
cites it, and its five Chapters carry the work.

### 11.168 DR-169 · A plan mark is sized in screen points, coloured by domain, and says which one it is

**The question.** Three complaints in one message from the user, 2026-09-13, after drawing rooms in
the product: *"the pin size on the room view is massive, and there's no way to differentiate objects
currently."* The third, a room outline refusing to draw over a pinned item, is `#895` and is a defect
under §11.49.10 rather than a decision.

**11.168.1 MEASURED FIRST, BECAUSE "MASSIVE" IS A NUMBER.** `kPlanMarkerRadiusFraction` is 1/110 of
the underlay's longer side and is expressed in SCENE units, which are image pixels. On a 3300-unit
architectural sheet that is a 30-unit radius, so a **60-point mark** at 1:1, and the hit box is the
same square. **And the plan canvas never fits to its window**: `ViewportController.new` with no
`fitToContent`, where the rack editor and the schematic both call it. So a plan opens at 100%
anchored to its top-left corner, showing about a quarter of an architectural sheet with marks at
their largest. Both facts were measured on 2026-09-13, not inferred.

**11.168.2 RULED: THE MARK IS A CONSTANT SIZE IN SCREEN POINTS.** Settled by the user. A marker is a
fixed number of points at every zoom, which is what `_withinCloseRadius` already does for the
outline's close radius and what its own comment argues for: *"ten points of pointer travel at every
zoom, which is what a person aims with."* Zooming in shows more PLAN rather than a bigger dot, and
the hit target stops depending on how far in somebody happens to be. **The proportional rule is
retired, not re-tuned**: shrinking the fraction keeps the property that caused the complaint, since
at 400% the mark and its hit box would still be four times what they are at 100%.
`kPlanMarkerRadiusFraction`'s own note called itself *"a starting value, not a ruling"* and named the
user as the decider; this is that decision.

**AND THE SEAM FOR IT ALREADY EXISTS WITH NO PRODUCER.** `buildPlanScene` takes a `double?
markerRadius` that overrides the fraction, and **no caller anywhere passes it**: not the three in the
canvas, not the sheet. Eighth instance of the no-producer shape after the seven §11.167.7 lists. So
each caller computes the radius from ITS OWN scale, the canvas from the viewport and the sheet from
its page mapping, and a mark is a constant size on screen and a constant size on paper without the
scene builder learning what a zoom is.

**ONE PLACE COMPUTES IT PER SURFACE, NOT THREE.** The canvas builds the scene in three methods (the
hit test, the marquee's catch and the paint). A radius computed separately in each is a hit box that
can disagree with the mark drawn, which is invisible on screen and is exactly the defect class
`#895` just cost: there the drawn mark and the clickable area were the same square and the tie was
still wrong. This clause is a rule and not an implementation note, because a disagreement here
cannot be seen.

**11.168.3 RULED: THE PLAN FITS ON OPEN, AND GAINS A FIT CONTROL.** Also the user's. Each plan opens
fitted to the window with the rack editor's own margin, and a Fit affordance returns to it. The
per-plan viewport is still remembered, so this is what an UNVISITED plan does rather than a reset of
one somebody has already positioned.

**11.168.4 RULED: COLOUR ENCODES THE CARRIER'S PRIMARY SIGNAL DOMAIN.** The user's answer to telling
marks apart, and it is CR-078's rule rather than a new one: colour lives on the DOMAIN. The eight
seeded domains carry the hues already.

**11.168.5 AND THE DOMAIN IS AUTHORED, BECAUSE THE CENSUS SAYS IT CANNOT BE DERIVED.** Measured over
the 51 seeded templates: **13 have ports in exactly one domain**. Excluding `pwr`, `ctl` and `str`,
which sit on almost everything, it rises to 26 and **nine templates then have no domain at all**,
including a control keypad whose only ports are the ones excluded. A television reads as
`(video.digital, audio.analog, net)`. **A set of port domains does not answer what a device IS**, and
G4 forbids estimating it. So `TemplateBody` gains a **nullable `primaryDomain`**, absent meaning
unknown and drawing a neutral mark, the Device Builder gains a picker, and the 51 seeded templates
are authored. The `category` string was considered and refused: its nine values include `Sources`,
which covers both audio and video sources, so the mapping would lie.

**11.168.6 THE MARK CARRIES THE DOMAIN'S GLYPH, AND THAT IS WHAT SURVIVES THE PRINT.** Also ruled by
the user, against colour alone. `plan_sheet.dart` SPLICES `buildPlanScene`, so every mark on screen
is a mark on `T1.01`, and the Installer preset exports greyscale. **§14 records that the eight hues
collide in greyscale by design**, three of them inside one luminance band, and PAL-3 resolves that
for a LINE with dash and weight. **A filled dot has neither.** The glyph channel already exists
(`family_glyph.dart`, and §6.2.2's verdict table cites glyphs), so the mark carries it and the sheet
stays legible without a second rule and without the screen and the print showing different things.

**11.168.7 THE DESIGNATOR IS A HOVER.** The user's, over a label drawn beside every mark: sixty drops
in one room is sixty labels, and the plan is somebody else's drawing to begin with. Colour answers
*what kind of thing is this* at a glance; hover answers *which one* on demand.

**11.168.8 THE RACK MARK IS UNCHANGED.** A rack has no signal domain: it is the datum every length on
the plan is measured from (`PLN-003`), which is why it is a square with a cross rather than one more
dot. It stays black and uncoloured, so it reads as a different KIND of thing rather than a ninth
domain. **The user has an asset in hand for it by launch**, which this clause does not pre-empt.

**11.168.9 Scope.** **No scope change.** Every clause is the appearance or the reachability of a
surface already in v1, plus one nullable model field that writes a key only when present, so
`kSchemaVersion` does not move on DR-026's own precedent. Board `#896` cites this ruling and its
chapters carry the work.

**11.168.10 A PRINTED MARK IS THE ROUND END OF THE CALLOUT PILL BESIDE IT.**

*Added 2026-09-14, on `#904`. Settled by the user, answering that chapter's question by pointing at
the callout pills it named as the obvious thing to read a printed mark against.*

§11.168.2 ruled that each surface computes the radius from its own scale, *"the canvas from the
viewport and the sheet from its page mapping"*, and said nothing about how big a mark is on PAPER.
The canvas half shipped at `#897` and was corrected at `#903`. The sheet passed no radius and kept
the retired fraction, and **measured on ANSI B landscape before anything moved** it printed at 6.87
points on a 2000x1500 plan, 5.15 on 1500x2000 and 10.20 on a 4000x1000 panorama, because the fit
binds on the tighter axis while the fraction read the longer one.

**RULED: a mark on `T1.01` is the size of the round end of its callout pill**, a stadium whose ends
have a radius of half its height. A sheet then carries one size of round thing where it would have
carried two nearly-equal ones for a reader to reconcile, and the mark reads as the same family of
object as the designator it is labelled with.

**THE CLAUSE RULES A RELATION, NOT A NUMBER.** The pill's type size is itself a starting value that
`PLAN-J`'s print will settle (DR-150 §11.149.7), so the radius is derived from the pill and moves
with it; a figure written here would be a second copy of a moving number. **Nor is it the screen's
point size.** A canvas mark is aimed at with a pointer and a printed one is read at arm's length,
and a screen figure borrowed for paper would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes.

**IT DOES NOT RULE THE MARK'S LINE WEIGHT.** The outline is still in scene units and rides the fit,
measured on the same sheets at 2.52 and 4.41 points for an outlet and a device on a 600x450 scan and
at **0.50 and 0.50** on a 6600x5100 one, where both reach the print floor and a device prints exactly
like a drop. That is a separate appearance question and is `#905`. No scope change, on §11.168.9's
reasoning.

**11.168.11 A MARK'S LINE WEIGHT IS THE DRAFTING WEIGHT, CONSTANT ON EVERY SURFACE.**

*Added 2026-09-14, on `#905`. Settled by the user, choosing among three weights drawn side by side at
the same enlargement.*

§11.168.10 ruled the printed radius and said in terms that it did not rule the line weight, which
was still a stroke of 2 scene units riding the fit on paper and the zoom on screen. **Both halves
were measured before anything moved.** On paper, off the rendered ops: 2.52 and 4.41 points for a
drop and a device on a 600x450 scan, and **0.50 and 0.50** on a 6600x5100 one, where both reach the
print floor and a device prints exactly like a drop. On screen, through `TestRecordingCanvas`: a drop
at 0.5, 2 and 8 pixels at 25%, 100% and 400%, and at 400% a 14-pixel device ring covering the fill
and the glyph of a mark 7 pixels in radius.

**RULED: a drop is outlined at the product's base line and a device is ringed at twice it, at every
zoom and on every scan.** On paper that is `kSignalBaseWeightPt` and docs/05 §5's own `2.00x` row,
so a mark prints at the weight of the cables around it. On screen it is one and two logical pixels,
which land on the grid and draw crisp. A ratio of two clears PAL-1's 1.4 with room.

**THE CORNER IS WHY THE RING HAS A CEILING.** A square glyph fills its box of 1.15 radii, so its
corners reach 0.813 of the radius, and a ring whose inner edge crosses that point runs black into
black. Network carries the square. The ceiling is therefore about 37% of the radius, which the
drafting weights clear on both surfaces. Of the two alternatives shown, **matching the pill's
hairline** (0.5 and 0.875 points) cleared it but put a drop exactly on the print floor and a device
0.375 points from it, and **freezing today's look at 100%** (2 and 3.5 pixels) ran the ring into the
square's corners on both surfaces. That ring already crossed them at 100% before this clause.

**THE WEIGHT IS NOT DIVIDED BY A SCALE, AND THE CANVAS IS TOLD ITS ZOOM.** A mark's strokes are
emitted with `scaleWithGeometry: false`, CR-082's own spelling of "constant on the surface", so each
backend divides by its own scale. The plan canvas zooms in a transform layer above its cached
picture, which `FlutterDiagramCanvas`'s stack cannot see, so it now takes that layer's scale as
`outerScale`. Without it a one-pixel line at 400% would have been floored back to two. **No scope
change**, on §11.168.9's reasoning.

**What this does not rule.** The exact point size of the mark ON SCREEN (on paper it is
§11.168.10's), the glyph inventory per domain, and the rack asset, all of which are appearance and
are the user's as they arrive. Whether an OUTLET's
domain is authored or read from its member links, which is a different question from a template's
and is `#896`'s first chapter to answer with a measurement. And the callout treatment docs/15 §7
schedules for `PLAN-H`, which this touches but does not close.

> **THE FIRST OF THOSE ARRIVED ON 2026-09-17 AND BROUGHT §11.168.2 WITH IT.** The user asked for a
> bigger mark that also grows with the plan once you zoom past a threshold, which is **DR-183
> §11.182** and is listed at §12.36. It raises the point size from 7 to 11 and **partly reverses
> §11.168.2's "retired, not re-tuned"**: the proportional rule returns above a crossover, floored
> below it. Everything else in §11.168 stands, including §11.168.2's other half, that one place
> computes the radius per surface and the drawn mark and the hit box are the same figure.

### 11.169 DR-170 · Editor chrome is drawn at its authored screen width at every zoom, and a canvas is told the zoom its layer applies

**The question.** Found while building `#905` and measured at `#906`, 2026-09-14. The plan, rack and
schematic canvases push the viewport as a `pushTransform` layer above a cached picture, so a pan
re-projects a texture, and `FlutterDiagramCanvas` starts its own transform stack at identity every
paint. Its stroke rules therefore read scale 1 at every zoom. `#905` told the plan canvas its zoom;
the other two were measured before anything here was ruled.

**11.169.1 MEASURED FIRST.** Through `TestRecordingCanvas`, as each stroke's recorded width times the
transforms it was painted under, on the real render objects:

| Chrome | Authored | Rack at open, 3.02x | Rack at 12.1x | Schematic at 4x |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Selection outline | 2 px | 6.0 px | 24.2 px | n/a |
| Hover ring | 1.5 px | 4.5 px | 18.1 px | n/a |
| Port chip | 1 px | 3.0 px | 12.1 px | n/a |
| Caret, source, candidate and selection rings | 2 px | n/a | n/a | 8 px |
| Connect band | 1.5 px | n/a | n/a | 6 px |

The port chip and the connect overlay mark their strokes `scaleWithGeometry: false`, CR-082's *"UI
chrome, selection halos and hit slop do not"* scale, **and the layer defeated the flag**: the overlay's
own comment says the flag *"handles the STROKE WIDTH"*, and it did not. `RenderDeviceBox`'s hover,
focus and selection rings are raw `Paint` strokes that no flag ever reached. The grid painter and the
editing overlay painter already divide by `viewport.scale`, and are correct.

**11.169.2 RULED: CHROME IS DRAWN AT ITS AUTHORED SCREEN WIDTH, AT EVERY ZOOM.** Settled by the user.
Selection and focus at 2 pixels, hover 1.5, the port chip 1, the connect rings 2 and the band 1.5, on
the rack and the schematic alike. docs/04 §3.5 already says *"a 2 px outline per member"* and CR-082
already says chrome does not scale, so this makes the product agree with both. **It is visibly thinner
when a rack first opens**, because the rack opens fitted at about 3x and its chrome was three times its
authored width there. Freezing that opening look instead was offered and refused: it contradicts
docs/04, and the schematic opens at a different zoom, so the two canvases would not have matched.

**11.169.3 RULED: A LINE NEVER PAINTS THINNER THAN HALF A PHYSICAL PIXEL.** Also the user's. Telling a
canvas its zoom moves `FlutterDiagramCanvas`'s 0.5 floor from scene units to physical pixels for
strokes that DO scale, so zoomed out, a 0.7-unit wire at 30% goes from 0.21 pixels to 0.5. That is what
CR-082's floor already means on paper, and what the plan canvas has done since `#905`. Keeping
zoomed-out hairlines was offered and refused, because it needs one canvas to treat one zoom two ways,
for the width and for the floor, which is a rule the PDF backend does not have.

**11.169.4 ONE SCALE PER CANVAS, PASSED WHERE ITS LAYER IS PUSHED.** A canvas that zooms in a layer
tells the `FlutterDiagramCanvas` it replays through, and anything it paints as a child reads the same
scale at paint time rather than a copy held somewhere that repaints on a different schedule.

**11.169.5 Scope.** **No scope change.** Appearance of surfaces already in v1; no model field, no file
format, no printed output. Board `#906` cites this ruling.

**11.169.6 THE RUBBER BAND IS SOLID, AND ITS COLOUR WAS NEVER OPEN.**

*Added 2026-09-14, on `#907`. Settled by the user.*

Until `#907` the paragraph below said that the rubber band's colour, weight and dash were an open gap,
because docs/05 §7.5 gives them to the source domain. **That was wrong, and it was written without
reading DR-114.** §11.113.2 had already ruled the band cursor chrome, naming *"the caret ring, the
source ring, the rubber band"* among the marks that keep theme roles, so a cursor reads in both
brightnesses and against the theme its owner chose. Its width is §11.169.2's. **docs/05 §7.5 item 5 was
the stale sentence**, and it is corrected to match both rulings.

**RULED: the band is SOLID**, the one channel neither ruling had reached. A dashed band on this canvas
already means something: a right-to-left marquee draws dashed to select what it intersects (CR-102's
solid and dashed distinction), so a dashed rubber band would borrow a selection's look in the middle of
a wiring gesture. The band still previews what the user will get where that matters, which is the
PATH: it routes through the same `orthogonalTrace` a committed wire does (DR-072 §11.72.2).

**What this does not rule.** Any chrome width other than those measured above.
