### 11.170 DR-171 · Outlet counts are derived, never stored: provided from outlet ports, consumed from the cords drawn and from inlet ports where none is

**The question.** Board `#558` (96-K) was ruled by the user on 2026-08-03 and marked RULED on the board
that day, and **the ruling never reached this document.** docs/06 §3.3 has said since M0 that
`outletsProvided` and `outletsConsumed` are read-only and counted from ports; the code read two
authored `PowerProfile` integers instead, and the rack chip strip, `PWR-003` and its remedy all summed
them. The board ruling decided what the two counts mean and left two things open: what becomes of the
stored fields, and what a rack reads before anyone has drawn a cord. Both were put to the user on
2026-09-14, after the measurement below.

**11.170.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-14 over the tree at `d4479d8`:

- **The 51 seed templates.** `outletsProvided` is stated on 35 and agrees with the template's
  outlet-role `power.*` ports on all 35; the 16 that state nothing have no outlet port. `outletsConsumed`
  is stated on 35 and agrees with the inlet-role ports on 29. **The six that disagree are the six the
  board item named in 2026-08** (`F09`, `F11`, `F12`, `F16`, `V06`, `V07`), each stating 0 against one
  inlet port, and four of the six also carry a PoE powered-device port.
- **The four starters.** Five racks, 27 links, and **not one conductor lands on a power inlet.** Their
  chips read `outlets 5/16`, `12/40`, `11/40`, `3/16` and `23/74` from the authored figures.
- **`LinkClass.powerCord` is never derived.** The board ruling pointed at it as the data already
  present, and `linkClassOf` answers only `jumper` or `fieldCable`: a cord from an amplifier to a PDU in
  the same rack is a jumper. Filed as `#908`. So the test for a power connection cannot be the link's
  class; **it is a conductor landing on an inlet-role power port**, which says what it is by being one.

**11.170.2 RULED 2026-08-03, RECORDED HERE: CAPACITY FROM THE HARDWARE, USAGE FROM THE GRAPH.**
`outletsProvided` is a count of the device's `power.*` ports whose `PortPowerSpec.role` is `outlet`: a
24-outlet PDU provides 24 whether or not any are used. `outletsConsumed` is usage, counted from the
power connections that land on its inlets. The principle the user gave, which generalises past power:
**the port list is a complete description of the hardware, not a statement of what is in use.** A
PoE-fed camera still has its barrel jack; it simply is not fed through it, so counting inlet ports as
usage over-counts exactly that case.

**11.170.3 RULED 2026-09-14: THE STORED FIELDS ARE DELETED, AND OLDER FILES DROP THEIR KEYS ON READ.**
`PowerProfile.outletsProvided` and `outletsConsumed` are removed from the model. A stored count beside a
derived one is a trap for the next reader, and six shipped templates already disagreed with their own
ports. The project format advances to `schemaVersion` 6 and the device template and device archive
formats to 3; each migration strips both keys from every template body. `minReaderVersion` does not
move, because a reader that knew the keys meets their absence as unknown and loses nothing.

**THE CONTENT HASH IS RECOMPUTED ONLY WHERE IT ATTESTED THE OLD BYTES.** Stripping a key changes a
body's canonical bytes and therefore its `contentHash`. DR-134's `.rmdx` step recomputed the hash
unconditionally, and said the cost out loud: a recomputed hash cannot attest to what the exporter wrote.
These steps first check the stored hash against the body as stored, and re-hash only when it matched;
a mismatch or a placeholder is carried unchanged, so a body edited outside the product still reports
as edited after the migration. A device's `TemplateRef.contentHash` that equalled its snapshot's old
hash moves with it.

**11.170.4 RULED 2026-09-14: CORDS WHERE THEY ARE DRAWN, INLET PORTS WHERE THEY ARE NOT, AND THE SPLIT IS
SAID.** Per device, in order:

1. If any inlet-role power port has a conductor landing on it, the device consumes that many outlets.
2. Otherwise, if a PoE powered-device port has a conductor landing on it, it consumes none: its power
   arrives over the data run. This covers `F09`, `F11`, `F12`, `V07` and the `V06` receiver's PoH input.
3. Otherwise it consumes one outlet per inlet-role power port, and it is **counted from its ports**, a
   separate figure every surface that shows the total also states.
4. A template that does not resolve is unknown for both counts (G4), and so is one that resolves
   with no ports at all (§11.170.8).

**The trade fact that made it per device.** Asked how often power cords are drawn, the user answered:
for PDU-fed gear, where sequencing or remote reboot matters, and not for everything. A rack therefore
mixes drawn and undrawn cords as a matter of course, so the rule reads each device's own evidence and
never switches a whole rack from one mode to the other. A redundant-supply switch with one cord drawn
counts one, by clause 1, because the drawing says one.

Offered and refused: **cords only, the rest unknown**, the board ruling read literally, under which every
starter rack reads `outlets 0/N` and `PWR-003` cannot fire until a person draws cords most people never
draw; and **both figures on the chip**, the widest chip on a strip that already scales itself down,
while `PWR-003` would still have had to pick one.

**11.170.5 WHY CLAUSE 3 IS NOT AN ESTIMATE IN G4's SENSE.** The inlet is a hardware fact, stated on the
template. What clause 3 assumes is that it will be fed from an outlet, and that assumption is **stated
beside the number**, never blended into it, which is the shape `ScheduleView.estimatedCount` already
has for lengths. G4 forbids a figure that pretends to be measured, and this one says what it is.

**11.170.6 `PWR-003` AND ITS REMEDY READ THE SAME FIGURES AS THE CHIP.** One resolution serves the chip
strip, the rule and the remedy's branch, so the button can never answer a different question from the
finding it sits on. The remedy's six-outlet strip is placed with its cord undrawn, so it provides six
and consumes one by clause 3, and the net gain of five that §11.127.8 states is unchanged.

**11.170.7 Scope.** **No scope change.** A stored model field is removed and three file formats advance
to drop it; every surface it reached already existed. Board `#558` cites this ruling.

**11.170.8 AN EMPTY PORT LIST IS UNKNOWN, NOT A MEASURED ZERO.**

*Added 2026-09-14, while building `#558`.*

§11.170.2 reads the port list as a complete description of the hardware, and that presupposes somebody
described it. AC-049 lets a template be saved with three fields and no ports, so an empty list cannot
tell a blank panel from an amplifier nobody has entered yet, and reading it as `outlets 0/0` is the
confident chip `derived/totals.dart` was rewritten to stop. **A template with ports and no power port is
a real zero**: its ports were described, and none of them takes power. The three passive templates
(`X01`, `X02`, `X03`) carry no ports and were already counted unknown, and they stay unknown.

**11.170.9 RULED 2026-09-14: THE CHIP SAYS THE SPLIT ON HOVER, AND ONLY THERE.** Settled by the user.
The outlets chip reads `outlets 24/74`, and hovering adds *"21 devices have no cord drawn and are
counted from their power inlets"*. The superscript keeps its one meaning on every chip, a device missing
from the total (docs/04 §5), and a device counted from its inlets is in the total. Offered and refused:
**a tilde**, `outlets ~24/74`, which on a drawing where only PDU-fed cords are drawn nearly every rack
would wear for good; and **dimming the consumed figure**, a colour-only signal that CR-078 argues
against and greyscale erases. `PWR-003`'s sentence carries the same clause.

**What this does not rule.** The power-cord classifier (`#908`), and whether a device may declare that
an inlet is deliberately unused.

---

### 11.171 DR-172 · The undo depth is a per-machine preference from 50 to 1000, applied at once, and a full history says so once per document

**The question.** Canon §10.12(a) was answered on 2026-08-03: keep 200, and make it a setting. Board
`#560` found the cap enforced and unreachable. `UndoStack.maxEntries` was a constructor default that
neither `DocumentController` nor `TemplateEditSession` ever passed, and the oldest entry dropped
silently, against AC-058 D5's *"the undo cap at 200 gains a status-bar signal instead of silently
dropping the oldest entry"*. The answer also left open where the setting lives and how a person edits
it, and the app had no surface for a setting that belongs to the machine: File > Project settings
(`#805`) edits what travels in the file.

**11.171.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over the tree at `4e57b7b`:

- Both undo stacks were built with no argument, so nothing anywhere could set the cap.
- `DocumentSession`'s status line never clears itself. An edit repaints it, and a message stays until
  another replaces it.
- docs/03 §11.1 sets 200 undo entries as the scale target, with no hard cap and no memory figure.
- No settings surface for this machine existed anywhere in the app.

**11.171.2 RULED: A PER-MACHINE PREFERENCE, EDITED IN EDIT > PREFERENCES.** Settled by the user. The
depth is a property of this machine's memory budget, not of the design, so it lives in `prefs.json`
beside the coach marks and the favourites, never travels with a file, and never enters CR-117's byte
surface. It is edited in a new Edit > Preferences dialog, the app's first surface for this machine's
settings; File > Project settings keeps what travels in the file.

**11.171.3 RULED: A WHOLE NUMBER FROM 50 TO 1000**, defaulting to 200. The ceiling keeps the setting
within reach of docs/03's measured target, since nothing budgets memory past it, and the floor keeps a
slip of the keyboard from leaving a handful of steps. Offered and refused: **preset choices**, under
which a depth of 300 cannot be expressed, and **any whole number**, which is memory nothing has
budgeted. A value outside the range in a hand-edited `prefs.json` reads as absent, not clamped.

**11.171.4 RULED: A NEW DEPTH TAKES EFFECT IMMEDIATELY**, on the open document and on an open Device
Builder window. Lowering it drops the oldest steps at once and the status line says how many went;
raising it keeps more from then on. Offered and refused: **taking effect at the next document opened**,
under which lowering it to free memory does nothing until a reopen.

**11.171.5 RULED: A FULL HISTORY SAYS SO ONCE PER DOCUMENT.** The first time a step drops, the status
line reads *"Undo history is full at N steps. Each new edit now drops the oldest."* Once, because the
line never clears itself: said on every dropped step, it would own the line from then on, "Saved."
included. A resize that drops steps is that document's notice. Offered and refused: **a notice on every
dropped step**, and **a menu hint as well**, which would change a label the keymap and tests read.

**11.171.6 RULED: ONE SETTING CAPS BOTH STACKS.** The Device Builder's history takes the same depth as
the document's, so a person who chose a depth gets it everywhere they undo. Offered and refused: **the
builder keeping a fixed 200**.

**11.171.7 DECIDED BUILDING IT, NOT ASKED.**

- **The field commits on Enter or Close, never on clicking away.** The project dialog's number rows
  commit when focus leaves them, which is harmless for a sheet number and wrong here: the depth takes
  effect at once and lowering it drops history, so typing "60" on the way to "600" and clicking
  elsewhere would lose steps nobody meant to lose. Escape and a click outside the dialog discard what
  was typed.
- **A resize goes through the controller, not the stack.** Dropping the entry the save point sits on
  changes `editsSinceSave`, which the window title and the close prompt read, so the controller rings
  its change notifier when anything went.
- **The first document is built at the chosen depth**, by loading the preferences before it rather than
  resizing a moment later.

**11.171.8 Scope.** **A scope addition under roadmap §8.3**: the app's first surface for this machine's
settings, holding one setting. §10.12(a) asked for the setting, and no ruling had placed a surface for
it. Board `#560` cites this ruling.

**What this does not rule.** A full-history notice inside the Device Builder, which has no status line;
a keyboard shortcut for Preferences; and any second preference.

### 11.172 DR-173 · A matrix's de-embedded zone audio is a stereo pair per zone, on two balanced 3-pin blocks

**The question.** Board `#112` (96-E), deferred by DR-014 §11.14.7 beside `#111`. V01 (8×8) and V03
(16×16) modelled each zone's de-embedded audio as one mono balanced 3-pin block, and
`docs/catalog/seed-devices.md` specified exactly that (*"8x EURO3-OUT"*). A matrix de-embeds a zone in
stereo, so the model could not say that a zone's left and right are two conductors of one feed, and the
connect gesture had no pair to land.

**11.172.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `b4d02c6`:

- V01 declares 8 zone outputs and V03 16, each `conn.euroblock_3` on `audio.line_bal` in an `audOut`
  bank.
- V02 (4×4) de-embeds to S/PDIF coax, which carries both channels on one connector, so one port per
  output is already right.
- V05, the presentation switcher, already models a stereo balanced output as ONE port on
  `conn.euroblock_5`, with no set.
- No starter materialises a port on a matrix zone output. The 300-link performance fixture wires eight
  of V03's zone outputs to two amplifiers.

**11.172.2 RULED 2026-09-15: AN L/R PAIR PER ZONE, ON TWO BALANCED 3-PIN BLOCKS.** Settled by the user.
Each zone is a `stereoPair` set of `AUD OUT n L` and `AUD OUT n R`: one drag lands both as a single
two-conductor cable, and dragging one half to a different device splits the set (DR-014). V01 goes from
8 zone ports to 16, and V03 from 16 to 32. Offered and refused: **one 5-pin block per zone**, V05's
shape, under which a zone's two channels can never land on different devices and the pair stays
invisible inside one port.

**11.172.3 THE TRADE FACT THAT BOUNDS IT.** The user's answer was an L/R pair per zone, with a
qualification: some amplifiers and matrices list their channels 1 to 16 or 1 to 32 without
distinguishing left from right, and the more capable of those can split a zone into individual
channels. The user's own examples: the Triad TS-AMS8 and TS-AMS16 cannot split zones, and the ELAN
(Nice) EL-IPD-MTX-8CH can. **An HDMI matrix de-embeds a stereo zone, which is the Triad case**, and that
is what the seeded V01 and V03 are. A device of the ELAN kind is authored as numbered mono channels,
which the Device Builder already expresses; nothing in the model has to know which kind a template is.

**11.172.4 DECIDED BUILDING IT: THE PAIRS ARE NUMBERED WITHOUT PADDING.** V03's video banks read
`HDMI OUT 01`, and its zone pairs read `AUD OUT 1 L`. The label grammar (docs/06 §4.2) cannot write a
counter that is both zero-padded and grouped: `{n@2:2}` is a parse error by design, because roadmap §2's
M4 Risks names generalising that grammar as the milestone's scope hazard. A padded pair would be a label
the Device Builder cannot reproduce. docs/06 §4.2's own worked example, `ZONE {n@2} {L,R}`, is unpadded,
and so is every pair the catalogue specification seeds.

**11.172.5 Scope.** **No scope change**: a catalogue data correction and the specification it follows.
Board `#112` cites this ruling.

**What this does not rule.** The set bracket that tells a pair on one cable from one that has been split
(`#111`); V02's S/PDIF outputs, which stay one port each; the seeded amplifiers, whose zone sets are
unchanged; and the set gesture's missing tier-2 check (`#909`), which DR-116 §11.115.3 already rules on
and which this ruling puts two more templates in reach of.

### 11.173 DR-174 · A set on one cable draws one pennant on a bracket, and a split set draws a pennant per pin

**The question.** Board `#111` (96-D). The user ruled it on the board on 2026-08-01, and the ruling never
reached canon. The board item's title is *"draw a set bracket only when the whole set is one cable"*,
and its description reads *"one pennant on a bracket spanning the set pins"*. DR-014 §11.14.7 then
deferred it with a new obligation: a drag can now lift one member out of a set's cable, so the bracket
must tell a set that is one cable from one that has been split.

**11.173.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `3ca1328`:

- **No set bracket exists.** The net-label layer labels a link by `Link.conductors.first` alone. So a
  stereo pair on one cable draws its pennant on the first conductor's pin, and the other pin carries
  no mark at all.
- **The seeded catalogue has 70 atomic sets, every one two adjacent pins in one bank.** 46 sit on a
  symbol's right edge and 24 on its left; none sits on a top or bottom edge, and none mixes directions.
  52 of the 70 are in banks over `kBankCollapseThreshold`, where a collapsed bank draws no individual
  pin.
- **The pennant fits the pair.** It is 13.5 units tall against a pin pitch of 2 gu, which is 14.173
  units, so a pennant centred between two adjacent pins stays inside those two rows.

**11.173.2 RULED 2026-08-01, RECORDED NOW: A BRACKET ONLY WHEN THE WHOLE SET IS ONE CABLE.** Settled by
the user on the board. An atomic set draws a bracket across its pins when every member has a conductor
end on one and the same link. **The test reads the document, not the drawing**, because the drawing
labels only a link's first conductor and would report an intact pair's second pin as unconnected. Two
other states follow from the ruling as written:

- **A split set** (DR-014), whose members are on two or more cables, draws no bracket. Each wired
  member draws its own pennant, as today.
- **A partly wired set**, where some members have no cable, draws no bracket either.

**11.173.3 RULED 2026-09-15: THE ONE PENNANT IS CENTRED ON THE BRACKET.** Settled by the user. Its
leader leaves the bracket's midpoint, so the flag names the cable and not its first conductor. Offered
and refused: the pennant on the first member's pin with the bracket beside it, which changes least but
still reads as belonging to that pin.

**11.173.4 RULED 2026-09-15: THE BRACKET TAKES THE CABLE'S SIGNAL COLOUR.** Settled by the user. It is
drawn in the leader's own hue and stroke (CR-078), so it reads as part of the cable's label. It adds no
colour, dash or weight that the leader does not already use, which leaves PAL-1's inputs unchanged.
Offered and refused: a neutral grey bracket, which reads as symbol structure and adds a second line
style beside every coloured leader.

**11.173.5 Scope.** **No scope change**: a presentation rule inside the schematic's net labels, with no
model or file-format change. docs/05 §11.5 is amended to match. Board `#111` cites this ruling.

**What this does not rule.** A set on a top or bottom edge, where pennants run in lanes and no seeded set
sits; a set inside a collapsed bank, which draws no pin to bracket; the drawn-wire render mode; and the
gesture that drags an unwired member onto a wired one (DR-014 §11.14.7), which needs its own ruling if
this work shows it is wanted.

### 11.174 DR-175 · The registry parity gate holds the seed to the specification's family table for the descriptive fields

**The question.** Board `#81`, filed on 2026-07-28 from the DR-010 agent's mutation M13.
`tools/registry_parity.py` checks the Dart seed against `tools/pal1_check.py` on hue, dash and weight,
and its own record calls it *"deliberately blind"* to a family's display name, short tag, default
connector, default direction, default topology and glyph, because that authority carries none of them.
Those fields were pinned only by the starter and fixture goldens, and a golden failure says to
regenerate the asset, which is how a typo ships.

**11.174.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `e9c7200`:

- `docs/catalog/seed-devices.md` §4.4 tabulates every seeded family: 57 rows against the seed's 57
  `_family` calls, with columns for display name, default connector, direction, topology, tag and
  glyph.
- **The table and the seed already agree** on every id in both directions, every tag and every
  display name. Nine names differ only by markdown bold, and one connector cell is `—`, stating
  nothing (`structure.pathway`).
- **The Dir and Topo cells are prose around a leading symbol or word**, such as *"→ (+ARC ↔)"* and
  *"BUS, topology-free"*. The leading one names the seed's value on every row: `→` src, `←` snk, `↔`
  and `⤳` bi, `passive` pas; `P2P` p2p, `STAR` star, `MD` and `BUS` md.
- **The seed stores no glyph per family** (DR-010 §11.10.3). The table's Glyph column is the domain's
  glyph in its native or transported form.
- The four starters and five core fixtures carry all 57 families' descriptive fields, which is why
  their goldens were the only thing a change there moved.

**11.174.2 RULED 2026-09-15: THE GATE COMPARES THE SEED WITH §4.4 FOR THE DESCRIPTIVE FIELDS.** Settled
by the user. `registry_parity.py` reads the §4.4 table and fails when the seed and the table disagree
on a family's display name, default connector or tag, compared exactly once markdown emphasis and code
marks are removed, or on its direction or topology, read from the cell's leading symbol or word. The
id sets must match in both directions, so a table the gate cannot read fails rather than passing. A
typo now has to be made in both the specification and the code to get through, and the failure names
both files instead of a starter. Offered and refused:

- **A committed snapshot of the descriptive fields** with its own failure message: a new copy of 285
  values that can still be regenerated past.
- **Rewording the golden failures only**: no gate, and it relies on the message being read.
- **Keeping the gate blind** and closing `#81`: the laundering path its own record describes stays
  open.

**11.174.3 THE GATE DOES NOT SAY WHICH FILE IS WRONG.** For the numeric half `pal1_check.py` is the
authority and the seed yields to it. For the descriptive half neither file is: a disagreement is fixed
in whichever of the two is wrong, in one commit, and never by regenerating a starter.

**11.174.4 Scope.** **No scope change**: a CI gate's coverage. Board `#81` cites this ruling.

**What this does not rule.** The glyph, which the seed does not store per family; the numeric half,
which stays with `pal1_check.py`; the `SignalFamilyDef` fields §4.4 does not tabulate, such as typical
media and run lengths; and the starter golden's own failure wording.

### 11.175 DR-176 · Your rack presets are saved from a rack, kept per machine, and sit beside seeded presets you can hide

**The question.** Board `#561`. DR-016 was ruled inside §10.12(c) on 2026-08-03: *"the starting racks
become EDITABLE PRESETS the user tailors to their own inventory"*, a scope addition under §8.3 with a
milestone cell of M1. It named no surface, no store and no rule for the seeded presets, and nothing
was built.

**11.175.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `e9c7200`:

- `buildRackPresets()` seeds eleven archetypes, and `rack_presets_test.dart` pins exactly those eleven,
  their ids, their heights, depths in whole inches and capacities in whole kilograms, as docs/04 §4's
  named list.
- **Two places build the preset map, not one.** The rack canvas builds it for the rack inspector's
  Preset dropdown and its new-rack dialog. The app shell builds its own for the same new-rack dialog,
  opened from a project that has no rack yet. Applying a preset is one undo step either way. A draft of
  this ruling said one map fed every surface; reading the callers found the second.
- **A rack never records its preset** (no `presetRef`), so a user's presets cannot reach a project file.
  The inspector's dropdown shows whichever preset a rack's values match, derived and never stored, and
  "Custom" when none does.
- The app already keeps per-machine state beside the executable when portable, through one data-root
  seam: `prefs.json`, recents, and a `libraries` folder of device archives.

**11.175.2 RULED 2026-09-15: A PRESET IS SAVED FROM A RACK.** Settled by the user. The rack inspector
gains **Save as preset...**, which captures the selected rack's height, form factor, width class, rail
type, usable depth, weight capacity and swing-frame settings under a name. Your presets appear in the
Preset dropdown in their own group below the seeded ones, and in the new-rack dialog. They are renamed
and deleted in a list under Edit > Preferences. Offered and refused: a Preferences editor with a form
for every field, which types in by hand what a real rack already holds; and both surfaces, which is
twice the building for the same result.

**11.175.3 RULED 2026-09-15: THEY ARE KEPT PER MACHINE, IN THEIR OWN FILE.** Settled by the user.
`rack_presets.json` sits beside `prefs.json` under the data root, so it follows a portable install and
never travels in a project. Offered and refused: inside `prefs.json`, which mixes authored content with
settings; and a library file, which would need a second kind of library in a loader that reads only
device archives.

**11.175.4 RULED 2026-09-15: SEEDED PRESETS CAN BE HIDDEN, NOT EDITED.** Settled by the user. The
eleven archetypes stay as shipped. You can hide the ones you never stock, and show them again; the
hidden set is kept in the same file. To vary a seeded preset, save a rack that started from it under
your own name. Offered and refused: seeded presets always shown, which cannot trim the list to an
inventory; and editing them in place, which needs an override layer and a reset action over a list
the tests pin.

**11.175.5 Scope.** **No new scope**: DR-016 already added it under §8.3. This ruling settles its
surface, store and rules. Board `#561` cites DR-016 and this ruling.

**What this does not rule.** Sharing presets between machines or people; a preset carried into a
project file; editing a preset's values after it is saved, beyond its name; and the milestone
bookkeeping for a scope addition whose cell still reads M1.

### 11.176 DR-177 · A passthrough pair stays one front port to one rear port, and N04 stays unpaired

**The question.** Board `#557`. DR-087 §11.86.4 ruled that the seeded 24-fibre LIU, `N04`, ships
unpaired, and left one thing open in terms: *"Whether `PassthroughPairDef` should ever become 1:N is
not ruled here and is not M4's question."*

**11.176.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `d75508e`:

- Of the **51** seeded templates, two are passthroughs. `N03`, the 24-port patch panel, has 24 front
  ports, 24 rear ports and 24 pairs. `N04` has 12 `conn.lc_duplex` front adapters, 24 rear splices
  and no pairs. **`N04` is the only template whose two faces differ in count.**
- `passthrough_commands_test.dart` pins `N04` unpaired, and its 36 ports carry the unpaired notice at
  notice severity, which docs/06 §4.6 makes a load warning rather than an error.
- Pair by order, run over `N04` anyway, pairs twelve ports and reports the twelve rear ports it left
  over (`PairByOrderResult.leftOverRear`).

**11.176.2 RULED 2026-09-15: NO ONE-TO-MANY PAIR.** Settled by the user. `PassthroughPairDef` keeps one
`frontKey` and one `rearKey`. `N04` stays unpaired, and its notice stays the honest report of a device
the model cannot express. **The cost is the reason**: a one-to-many pair is a codec change, a migration
and a new Termination Schedule column, for one seeded device. Offered and refused: parking the question
under the v1.1 community catalog (`#592`), where a contributed fibre cassette fanning one trunk out to
several ports would first need it; and keeping `#557` open as that question.

**What this does not rule.** A template a user authors with unequal faces gets the same unpaired notice
and the same leftover count, and nothing new is built for it. A real device that needs a fan-out is a
new question with its own evidence.

### 11.177 DR-178 · A test that asserts a time runs in its own gate step, one test at a time

**The question.** Board `#843`. On 2026-09-05 a docs-only commit failed the core suite on
`schematic_perf_test.dart`'s text-bound case: 20.877 ms against a 16.67 ms frame, where the same test
run alone took 6.355 ms. The file asserts deterministic operation counts and stopwatch readings side
by side, and only the second can fail for a reason outside the change under test.

**11.177.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `d75508e`:

- **The service has run 184 builds since 2026-09-05**: 174 succeeded, 8 were cancelled and 2 failed.
  Both failures were the machine and not this test: build 195 a torn workspace, build 207 an agent that
  stopped responding.
- **Run alone today**, the 300-link case takes 5.032 ms, the text-bound case 4.434 ms and a wires-only
  edit 0.485 ms, against a 16.67 ms frame. The twelve-pod cold build takes 67.874 ms against its 400 ms
  ratchet.
- **Two test files carry the `perf` tag**, `schematic_perf_test.dart` in core and
  `paint_budget_test.dart` in ui, and **only the first asserts a time**: five `lessThan` checks, three
  against a fixed number (the frame, in two places, and the ratchet) and two comparing one timing with
  another. `paint_budget_test.dart` starts a stopwatch but asserts only cache counts.
- **The tag filters nothing.** `run_suite.ps1` runs every test in a package, so a timed case shares the
  machine with the rest of its own suite.

**11.177.2 RULED 2026-09-15: A TEST THAT ASSERTS A TIME RUNS IN ITS OWN GATE STEP.** Settled by the
user. Every assertion on a stopwatch reading leaves the package suites and runs in one gate step of its
own, one test at a time, in `run_local.ps1` and in the pipeline alike. Everything that asserts a count,
a digest or a shape stays in its suite, so M2-C's operation-count record and the determinism checks
keep running beside everything else. **The budgets do not move**: §11.75.4 still binds an edit to one
frame and keeps the cold build's ratchet. Offered and refused: closing `#843` on the evidence above;
re-timing once before failing; and timing a reference workload in the same process and asserting the
ratio, which survives any machine and is the most work. Widening the budget was refused by the ticket
itself.

**What this does not rule.** It does not protect the timed step from another program loading the same
machine, which a self-hosted agent shares: it removes competition with the test's own suite, and that
is all. It changes no budget's value.

### 11.178 DR-179 · The file extensions are `.rppj`, `.rpdx` and `.rpda`, and every extension a build has written still opens

**The question.** Board `#782`. DR-096 §11.95.3 deferred re-cutting the `rm`-prefixed extensions to
match RackPal, with M8 as the trigger, and did not rule the letters.

**11.178.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `d75508e`:

- **The ticket and §11.95.3 name the wrong set.** Both name `.rmdev` and `.rmlib`, which DR-015 had
  already renamed. The extensions the app writes are `.rmpj` (project), `.rmdx` (device template) and
  `.rmda` (device library), in 424, 88 and 103 places across code and tests.
- **No file stores its own extension.** The four starter projects, the only files in the tree carrying
  any of these extensions, contain none of the three strings, and the `.rmda` codec names `.rmdx` only
  in comments. So CR-117's byte round-trip is not in play: this is a rename, not a migration.
- **The deadline is earlier than M8.** MSIX-7 (`#171`, under the Store alpha epic `#100`) registers
  these three extensions in the package manifest, and the Store alpha puts a package in the team's
  hands.
- **The old project extension that still opens is the wrong one.** DR-015 §11.15.2 kept `.rackmate`,
  which every build before `dc22ddc` wrote, opening and saving in place. The product rename (`#781`,
  `0e2c5bb`) rewrote that constant to `.rackpal`, in the code and in §11.15.2's own text. No build ever
  wrote `.rackpal`, so a project saved before 2026-08-02 no longer appears in the Open dialog, and a
  Save would give it a second name. It is the class §11.95.8 names, prose asserting a fact about the
  old name, and it survived that section's restoration.
- Web searches found no existing format using `.rppj`, `.rpdx` or `.rpda`; the nearest are REAPER's
  `.rpp` and Axure's `.rpprj`.

**11.178.2 RULED 2026-09-15: `.rppj`, `.rpdx` AND `.rpda`, NOW.** Settled by the user. The project,
device template and device library extensions become `.rppj`, `.rpdx` and `.rpda`, keeping the letters
after the prefix so DR-015's family stays recognisable. It lands as its own change, before MSIX-7
writes a manifest, rather than at M8.

**11.178.3 RULED 2026-09-15: EVERY EXTENSION A BUILD HAS WRITTEN STILL OPENS.** A project opens as
`.rppj`, `.rmpj` or `.rackmate`; a device template as `.rpdx` or `.rmdx`; a device library as `.rpda` or
`.rmda`, in the libraries folder as well as through a dialog. Save keeps the name a file was opened
with, which is §11.15.2's rule unchanged. `.rackpal` comes off the list, because nothing ever wrote it.
§11.15.2's text is restored to `.rackmate` in the same commit as this ruling. Offered and refused:
renaming at the M8 trigger, which costs the same plus every file saved in the meantime; and keeping
`rm`.

**What this does not rule.** File-type registration, its icons and whether the portable build
registers anything, all of which stay MSIX-7's. The file format, the schema version and every byte
inside a file are untouched.

### 11.179 DR-180 · A project states its wiring standard, and a cable may override it

**The question.** Board `#80`, from M2-B: four fields docs/08 §3 names that the model did not have.
Three have since been settled, `SignalFamilyDef.shortTag` by DR-010 §11.10.3, `Pathway.designator` by
DR-026 §11.25.1 and `Outlet.nominalRunLength` by §11.25.2. The fourth is T568A or T568B.

**11.179.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `d75508e`:

- **Nothing in the model states a wiring standard.** `TerminationType` is keystone, punchdown, F barrel,
  euroblock, unterminated, field connector, binding post and RJ45 plug. The schedule's `TERM` cell
  prints the termination type and the port designator, and the Structure view's `FIELD TERM` and
  `RACK TERM` cells print the termination type alone.
- **The corpus asks for it in three places and overloads a field for it in a fourth.** docs/08 §3.3's
  examples print `T568B` in both termination columns; docs/08 §3's sheet list turns `T5.01` Plate, Panel
  & Pinout Details on for a *"non-default T568A"*; and `schedule.dart` has said since 2026-07-28 that a
  `Link.wiringStandard` is owed. docs/02 and `byte_roundtrip_test.dart` store `"colorCode": "T568B"` on a
  `Conductor`, whose field is the pair colour.
- `ProjectSettings` already holds project-wide defaults of the same kind: display units, sheet
  numbering, designator formats and the default network media.
- `T5.01` is not built; only comments in `sheet_def.dart` name it.
- The seed's four-pair twisted-pair media are `media.cat5e`, `media.cat6`, `media.cat6_futp` and
  `media.cat6a_futp`, and its only RJ45 connector is `conn.rj45`.

**11.179.2 RULED 2026-09-15: THE PROJECT STATES A STANDARD, AND A CABLE MAY OVERRIDE IT.** Settled by
the user. `ProjectSettings` gains a wiring standard, T568A or T568B, and a `Link` gains an optional
override with the same two values. A cable's standard is its override, else the project's, else
unknown. **Unset is unknown, never T568B** (G4, CR-114): both keys are absent when unset, and nothing
prints a standard nobody stated. One entry per job replaces one per drop. Offered and refused: a field
per cable with no project value; one per end, beside `FIELD TERM` and `RACK TERM`, which could show an
accidental crossover at twice the entry; and not modelling it.

**11.179.3 IT IS SHOWN ONLY WHERE IT CAN BE TRUE.** A wiring standard is a fact about a four-pair cable
on an RJ45, so a cable shows, edits and prints one only when its media is a four-pair twisted-pair type
or one of its ends is an RJ45 port or plug. A coax or speaker run never prints one, whatever the
project says.

**11.179.4 WHERE IT PRINTS.** The termination cells print a known standard beside the termination type,
as docs/08 §3.3's examples already do. **A cable whose standard differs from the project's is what turns
`T5.01` on**, which is docs/08 §3's *"non-default T568A"* stated against the project instead of against
an assumed default. `T5.01` itself stays M6's.

**What this does not rule.** A crossover cable, T568A at one end and T568B at the other, which the
refused one-per-end option could have expressed. `Conductor.colorCode` keeps its meaning, the pair
colour, and the docs/02 example that stores `T568B` there is a derived edit owed with the build.

### 11.180 DR-181 · A signal family may override its domain's glyph

**The question.** Board `#82`: six disagreements the registry seed hit. The one with teeth was that
`audio.analog` and `pwr` each have three glyphs and `SignalDomainDef` has two slots, so
`audio.speaker_cv` and `power.bonding` draw the wrong shape.

**11.180.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15 over `d75508e`:

- **Twenty-six of the 57 seeded families draw the wrong shape, not two.** `docs/catalog/seed-devices.md`
  §4.4 gives every family a glyph, and §4.3 gives each domain a native glyph and one or two more.
  `signal_style.dart` draws only the domain's native glyph, so every family whose §4.4 glyph is another
  of its domain's shapes is drawn with the native one: 2 in digital video, 4 in analog video, 2 in analog
  audio, 4 in digital audio, 4 in network, 7 in control, 2 in power and 1 in structure. The renderer
  already flags every family whose shape it cannot verify (`SchematicScene.underGlyphedFamilyIds`),
  a wider set that includes all 26, rather than hiding them.
- **DR-010 §11.10.3 added exactly three render fields** to `SignalFamilyDef`, `shortTag`, `dashOverride`
  and a weight override, and §11.10.4 kept the rest of the corpus shape out. §4.1's entity table lists
  an optional `glyphOverride` all the same.
- **A document carries its own copy of the registries.** Every starter embeds all 57 families, and the
  seed is copied in only when a document is created (`blank_document.dart`) and when the starters are
  generated (`authoring.dart`).
- Of the other disagreements, the empty aliases are resolved (DR-060). Four need no ruling: docs/02
  §6.2's worked JSON still shows one-letter tag prefixes where docs/08 §3.5 and the seed use `VID`, `NET`
  and the rest; `structure.pathway`'s connector (`conn.unterminated`) and topology (`p2p`) are declared
  in code and in no document; `topologyFree` (AC-030) is not on the class; and the logical-flow
  direction of `video.avoip`, `audio.dante` and `audio.aes67` is recorded as bidirectional.

**11.180.2 RULED 2026-09-15: A FAMILY MAY OVERRIDE ITS DOMAIN'S GLYPH.** Settled by the user.
`SignalFamilyDef` gains an optional `glyphOverride`, absent when unset, and a family draws its override
when it has one and its domain's native glyph otherwise. The seed sets it on every family whose §4.4
glyph differs from its domain's native glyph, the 26 above, so `audio.speaker_cv` draws ○ and
`power.bonding` draws ⏚. The glyph geometry gains the two shapes no domain slot holds, ○ and ⏚, and
`registry_parity.py` compares the glyph column as it compares the others (DR-175). **The reason is the
greyscale print**: shape is one of the channels that survives it (docs/05 §6.1), and a constant-voltage
speaker line is not interchangeable with a low-impedance one. Offered and refused: ruling the glyph a
domain property and letting dash, weight and tag separate the families; and deciding it with signal
family authoring (DR-122, `#816`).

**What this does not rule.** Refreshing a saved project's registries from the seed. The override is an
additive key, so `kSchemaVersion` does not move and an older file still loads unchanged (CR-117); new
projects and the regenerated starters get the overrides, and a project saved before this keeps drawing
its domain's shape and keeps reporting the families it cannot verify, as with every earlier registry
addition. Nor the logical-flow direction, which stays owed a field.

### 11.181 DR-182 · The roadmap keeps its sizes and retires its week total

**The question.** Board `#796`, with `#797`, `#798` and `#799`. docs/09 §6 prices ten milestones at 44
to 67 weeks and names only DR-001, DR-005 and DR-015 as absorbed. On 2026-08-30 the user chose to leave
it alone and file the gap.

**11.181.1 MEASURED FIRST**, on 2026-09-15:

- **M0 to M5 are closed.** §6 priced them at 29 to 44 weeks cumulative, and they took about 7.3 weeks,
  from 2026-07-18 to M5's close on 2026-09-07: four to six times faster than estimates written for a
  human team.
- **The v1 saga holds 20 epics**, where `#796` counted seventeen on 2026-08-30; signal family authoring
  (`#816`) and authored devices reaching the shelf (`#817`) were created on 2026-09-05. §6 has rows for
  ten.
- **The Plan view has a size and no row.** docs/09 §4 sizes it `L`, §6 does not count it, and 13 of its
  14 board children are Done.
- **Nine epics have no size anywhere**: macOS (`#55`, 2 of 15 children Done), the Store alpha (`#100`,
  1 of 8), project history (`#655`, 0 of 5), NET-A (`#681`, 0 of 4), EXP-A (`#686`) and DOC-A (`#688`),
  neither yet decomposed, cross-cutting debt (`#786`, 37 of 52), and `#816` (0 of 3) and `#817` (0 of
  1).
- docs/09 §4's M4 heading reads `M` where §6 reads `L` (`#799`).

**11.181.2 RULED 2026-09-15: THE SIZES STAY AND THE WEEK TOTAL RETIRES.** Settled by the user. §6 gives
every v1 epic a size, `S`, `M` or `L`, including the Plan view and the nine that have none, each sized
from its stories with the evidence named. A closed milestone shows its actual duration beside its
estimate. **The week total is withdrawn rather than re-estimated**, with a sentence saying why: relative
sizes still order the work, and the weeks described a team that is not the one building it. The M4
heading is corrected in the same change, and §6's two levers are re-read against the withdrawn total
there. Offered and refused: a full re-cost in weeks with a new total; marking the gap and keeping 44 to
67 with a caveat; and leaving docs/09 as it is.

**11.181.3 Scope.** **No scope changes.** This amends how roadmap §6 states cost, under §8.3, and moves
no epic between Sagas.

**What this does not rule.** A release date, any milestone's scope, and the size letters themselves,
which the docs change assigns from evidence.

### 11.182 DR-183 · A plan mark sticks at a floor size and grows with the plan above a crossover

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-17, with a screenshot: *"we need to increase the site view pin
size a bit; I feel like it should 'stick' at a certain size below a certain zoom level ... zooming out
it stays physically this size, zooming in it should grow relatively in size to the room plan
underlay."*

**11.182.0 MEASURED FIRST, AND THE SCREENSHOT WAS NOT.** `plan_canvas_screen.dart` computed
`kPlanMarkerRadiusPt / viewport.scale`, which is a **7-point radius on screen at every zoom from 5% to
3200%**, by construction rather than by measurement. That is §11.168.2, whose own words were *"the
proportional rule is retired, not re-tuned"*. **The screenshot yields no number and this says so**: it
is a crop at an unknown zoom of a plan of unknown pixel dimensions, so nothing in it converts into
points, and a figure read off it would have been a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. The two
numbers below came from the user instead, against four discs drawn at actual size and a chart of size
against zoom, which is §11.168.11's own method.

**11.182.1 RULED: THE RADIUS IS THE LARGER OF A SCREEN FLOOR AND A FRACTION OF THE PLAN.** Settled by
the user. A canvas mark is `max(11 points / scale, (1/200) x planSize)` in scene units, so:

- **At or below the crossover** the first term wins and the mark is a **constant 11 points on screen**.
  This is §11.168.2's rule and §11.168.2's reason, kept: a mark is aimed at with a pointer, which is
  what `kOutlineCloseRadiusPt` says for the close test in its own words, and a mark that shrank with
  the plan would be sub-point on a fitted architectural sheet.
- **Above it** the second wins and the mark is a **fixed piece of the drawing**, covering the same
  floor however far in somebody goes. This is the rule §11.168.2 retired, returning bounded.

**The floor was 7 and is 11.** Chosen by the user from 9, 11 and 14 drawn at actual size, and that is
where the clause ends: §11.168's closing clause makes the point size appearance and theirs, so **no
reason is attributed to them here**.

**THE MEASURABLE CONSEQUENCES ARE TWO, AND THE SECOND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The domain's
glyph fills a box of `kPlanGlyphSideFactor` radii, so it grows from **8.05 points across to 12.65**.
And a device's ring is a constant 2 logical pixels (§11.168.11), so as a fraction of the radius it
**falls from 28.6% to 18.2%**, moving further clear of the roughly 37% ceiling §11.168.11 sets to keep
a ring out of the corners of Network's square glyph. A bigger mark could have crowded that ceiling; it
does the opposite, because the ring does not grow with it.

**THE FRACTION AT 1/100 WAS OFFERED AND DECLINED**, and the reason belongs in the record: that is within
rounding of the retired `kPlanMarkerRadiusFraction`'s 1/110, so at four times the fitted zoom a mark
would reach four times the floor, which is the size reported as *"massive"* in the first place. 1/300
was the third and barely grows before somebody is inside a single room.

**11.182.2 THE PLAN'S SIZE IS THE GEOMETRIC MEAN OF ITS TWO SIDES, NOT ITS LONGER ONE.** An
implementation clause and not an appearance one, because §11.168.10 already MEASURED what the longer
side does with a fraction of exactly this shape, on paper: **6.87 points on a 2000x1500 plan, 5.15 on
1500x2000 and 10.20 on a 4000x1000 panorama**, because a fit binds on the tighter axis while the
fraction reads the longer one. A corridor scanned in one strip is a real plan and would have taken a
mark twice the size of the same room drawn square. `sqrt(w x h)` has no such cliff and agrees with the
longer side on a square scan by construction. On a 3300x2550 sheet the anchored radius is **14.5 scene
units** and the crossover falls at a zoom of **0.76**.

**AGAINST THE FITTED ZOOM IT IS A RANGE AND NOT A FIGURE**, because the fit depends on the window:
**2.3x fit in a 1920-point canvas and 3.4x in an 1100-point one**, over `fitToContent`'s own 0.9
margin. This clause first said *"about 2.7 times the fitted zoom"*, which is one window's answer
wearing the shape of a constant. **What a window cannot change is the effect of the anchor itself**:
on this scan the geometric mean is 2901 against a longer side of 3300, so choosing it moves the
crossover **1.14x further in**, wherever that crossover happens to sit.

**11.182.3 IT SUPERSEDES §11.168.2 IN PART, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A TWELFTH CLAUSE.**
§11.168.10 and §11.168.11 each ADDED a clause to DR-169 and neither contradicted one. This changes what
§11.168.2 decided, so it takes an ID and appears in §12. **What survives untouched is that clause's
other half**: one place computes the radius per surface, and the drawn mark and the hit box are the
same figure at every zoom. DR-183 changes the SIZE and never the agreement, and `#903` is the record of
what happens when the agreement breaks.

**11.182.4 Scope.** **No scope change**, on §11.168.9's reasoning: this is the appearance and the
reachability of a mark that already exists.

**What this does not rule.** The PRINTED mark, which is §11.168.10's round end of the callout pill: a
sheet is read at arm's length and has no zoom to cross a threshold with, so that constant is unaffected
and that is a decision rather than an oversight. The mark's line weight, which is §11.168.11's drafting
weight and stays constant on the surface. Colour, the glyph inventory, and the rack asset.

### 11.183 DR-184 · A floorplan turns in quarter turns, saved on the plan

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-18, on board `#911`: *"the floorplan view, for example,
doesn't allow the rotation of floorplans."*

**11.183.0 MEASURED FIRST, AND THE DEFECT WAS LARGER THAN THE REPORT.** `PlanUnderlay` carries no
orientation of any kind (`model/plan.dart`), and `buildPlanScene` maps one image pixel to one scene
unit with no transform between them, so a plan drawn sideways by its architect stays sideways on
screen and on `T1.01`. **The second finding is a defect and not a missing feature.** The PDF lifter
carries `/Rotate` down the page tree with `/MediaBox` and `/Resources` (`pdf_page_lift.dart`,
`_inherited`) and then **never reads it**: `LiftedPdfPage` has no field that could hold it, and the
page picker previews the lifted bytes as they stand. pdfium applies `/Rotate` before it renders
(`pdfium_document.dart`). So a page stored portrait with `/Rotate 90`, which is how scanners and some
plotters write a landscape sheet, **imports upright when it is rendered and sideways when it is
lifted**, and lifting is the path the importer prefers.

**11.183.1 RULED: QUARTER TURNS, SAVED ON THE PLAN.** Settled by the user. `PlanUnderlay` gains
`rotationQuarterTurns`, an integer from 0 to 3, **clockwise** as the plan is seen. The screen and the
printed sheet both follow it, because they replay one display list (CR-086) and a turn that only the
screen knew about would be a screen and a sheet that disagree about which way is up.
`SheetItem.rotationQuarterTurns` (docs/02 §2.11, *"0..3, no float angles"*) is the precedent for the
name, the range and the integer. **Two options were declined**, and the prices belong in the record:

- **A free angle.** It resamples the architect's line work on screen and on paper, which DR-137 rules
  is what a floorplan IS; it leaves empty triangles in the corners of the sheet and shrinks the fit to
  make room for them; and every pin would round-trip through trigonometry.
- **A view-only turn.** Not saved, so the sheet prints unturned and the next session opens unturned:
  the screen and the paper would disagree, which is the failure CR-086 exists to make unspellable.

**11.183.2 A STORED COORDINATE NEVER TURNS.** An implementation clause. Pins, the calibration's two
points and every room outline stay in the image's own pixel space (docs/15 §3.3), and the turn is a
map applied where a pixel meets the scene. For a quarter turn that map is **exact on integers**, so a
turn moves nothing, rounds nothing and can be undone by turning back. What follows from it is the
cheapest possible failure: **a build that does not know the field drops it and shows the plan
unturned, with every pin still on its drop.** The loss is an orientation and never a drawing, which is
`PlanSourcePage`'s standard for an ordinary additive optional field, so `kPlanMinReaderVersion` does
not move.

**11.183.3 THE FILE OMITS AN UNTURNED PLAN.** Absent means 0, so no document in existence changes a
byte on its next save, on the reasoning that keeps an empty `underlays` map out of the file. A
present value must be 0 to 3 and anything else is refused at the boundary, on `pageIndex`'s precedent
in `PlanSourcePage`: nothing is normalised modulo four, because a 5 in a file is somebody's mistake
and not a turn.

**11.183.4 RULED: THE BUTTONS LIVE ON THE OPEN PLAN'S ROW, AND THE KEYS ARE ACROBAT'S.** Settled by the
user. Two icon buttons, turn left and turn right, sit beside `Calibrate…` and `Remove…` on the open
plan's row in the rail, which is the host DR-144 §11.143.4 ruled for a property of a plan. The keys are
`Ctrl+Shift+Plus` (clockwise) and `Ctrl+Shift+Minus` (anticlockwise) while the plan canvas has focus.

**THE FIRST QUESTION OFFERED A HOST THAT DOES NOT EXIST**, and that is recorded because the user chose
it. It named *"the Plan editor's toolbar"*; there is none, and docs/15 §6 rules three regions and
*"no fourth region"*. The slip was caught before any widget was written, and the host was asked again
as its own question. The keys were chosen in the same first question and stand.

**11.183.5 RULED: THE VIEW TURNS ABOUT THE CANVAS CENTRE AND KEEPS ITS ZOOM.** Settled by the user. The
spot under the middle of the canvas is still under the middle after the turn, so somebody zoomed into
one room is still looking at that room. Re-fitting on every turn was declined: it would throw that
person back out to the whole sheet. `Fit` remains one click away.

**11.183.6 A LIFTED PAGE TAKES ITS TURN FROM `/Rotate`.** An implementation clause, not a user
decision: it is §11.183.0's defect, and §11.183.1's field is what makes the fix lossless. The lifted
bytes stay byte for byte what the PDF embeds (DR-138 §11.137.3); the page's `/Rotate` becomes the new
plan's `rotationQuarterTurns`, and the picker's preview is turned to match, so the tile, the canvas
and the sheet show the page the way a PDF viewer does. A `/Rotate` that is not a multiple of 90
**refuses the lift with that reason**, on this lifter's own rule that a wrongful refusal costs one
export while a wrongful acceptance costs a drawing, and the page is then offered to the renderer like
any other. A rendered page arrives at 0, because pdfium has already turned it.

**11.183.7 Scope.** **No scope change.** The Plan view is v1 (DR-029), and this is which way up an
existing picture is drawn.

**What this does not rule.** A north arrow, which docs/15 §8 already records as having no field to
read and which a turn does not supply. Mirroring, which no architect's sheet needs. A free angle,
declined above rather than deferred.

### 11.184 DR-185 · A floorplan page can be renamed and says which floor it shows, and an import asks

**The question.** Found on 2026-09-18 while measuring DR-184, and put to the user on board `#912`:
a plan's name and the floor it shows had no way in.

**11.184.0 MEASURED FIRST.** Two facts, both a modelled field with no writer:

- **The name is the file's, forever.** `FloorplanIo.import` names every page
  `basenameWithoutExtension(path)`, and no command renames a `PlanUnderlay`. Three pages lifted from
  one PDF are three rows reading the same words.
- **`PlanUnderlay.locationId` is never written.** The import signatures accept it and the one caller
  in `lib/` passes nothing, so every plan in every project has no floor. The rail's room line
  (`_UnderlayRow.room`) can never print, and DR-142 §11.141 rules that a plan with no location lists
  **every** unpinned carrier in the project, so on a three-storey house each floor's strip shows the
  whole building.

**11.184.1 RULED: AN `Edit plan…` DIALOG ON THE OPEN PLAN'S ROW.** Settled by the user. A button
beside `Calibrate…` opens a dialog with two fields, **Name** and **Shows**, where Shows lists the
Site tree in its own order with a "no floor" choice for a site plan. Both fields commit as **one undo
entry**. Declined: editing inline on the row, where double-click-to-rename is invisible and a
dropdown in a 240-pixel rail truncates a floor's name; and the right-hand inspector, which docs/15 §6
gives to the selected room and where a plan's property would vanish the moment a room was clicked.

**11.184.2 RULED: AN IMPORT PROPOSES BOTH AND ASKS.** Settled by the user. The name defaults to the
file's, with the page appended when the PDF has more than one; Shows defaults to the location
selected in the Site tree, or none. The same dialog then opens pre-filled, so `Enter` accepts. What it
asks is part of the import: **the import and its details are one undo entry**, and dismissing the
dialog keeps the proposal rather than abandoning a page somebody has just picked. Declined: the same
defaults applied silently, which would still leave most plans floorless, since hardly anybody selects
a floor before importing; and today's behaviour.

**11.184.3 A PLAN IS THE TENTH LOCATION CARRIER.** An implementation clause, and the consequence of
giving `locationId` a writer. DR-021 §11.20 censused **nine fields across seven entities** that point
at a location, and `PlanUnderlay.locationId` was not among them because no document could hold one
set. The day it can, deleting a floor would leave its plans pointing at nothing, so deleting a
location now clears every plan that shows it, on exactly the terms of the other nine: cleared to null,
counted in the dialog as an item that loses its room, and put back by the same undo. Listed at §12.37.

**11.184.4 Scope.** **No scope change.** Both fields are in the model since `PLAN-C` (docs/15 §3.1);
this is their writer.

**What this does not rule.** Renaming a page from the printed sheet's title block, which reads the
name and gains nothing by being written from there. Replacing a plan's picture with a revised drawing
while keeping its pins, which is a different feature with its own geometry question.

### 11.185 DR-186 · `Ctrl+L` locks a rack device's position, and pins a schematic symbol where it stands

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-18, on board `#913`: CR-034 ships three lock flags in v1 and
docs/04 §8 binds `Ctrl+L` to *"lock / unlock (position here, route in the schematic)"*, and none of it
could be reached.

**11.185.0 MEASURED FIRST.** docs/12 §3.3 has said since M1 *"Locks: half-built ... no `Ctrl+L`, no way
to set `Placement.locked`"*, and it is still true: the field has no writer but the decoder, and
**compaction is its only reader**. Dragging, nudging and the width command all move a locked device,
and so does a rack shrink trimmed from the bottom. On the schematic, CR-068 and docs/05 §10 rule that
auto-layout never moves a pinned symbol and that `Ctrl+L` sets `SheetItem.pinned`. The layout **reads**
pins (`schematic_scene.dart`, `_pinnedPositions`), and nothing writes one; **nor does any document hold
the schematic `Sheet` a pin lives on**, though CR-073 says exactly one is created per project.

**11.185.1 RULED: A LOCK REFUSES MOVING AND A SHRINK THAT WOULD MOVE IT, AND NOTHING ELSE.** Settled by
the user. A locked device refuses a drag, a nudge, a width or face change and compaction (which already
honoured it); **Trim from bottom** is refused while a locked device would have to shift, and says which.
A top trim moves nobody and stays available, so every option in the shrink dialog is still lossless.
**A lock does not refuse a delete**: the ruling is *"lock position"*, and a lock that has to be undone
before a delete tends to be left off, which defeats it. Pushing by others was offered and not chosen.
**That option described docs/04 §3.3's Alt-drop push as existing, and it does not**: no gesture in
this build pushes one device with another, so the question it asked has no surface yet.

**11.185.2 RULED: `Ctrl+L`, A CHECKBOX, AND A PADLOCK.** Settled by the user. `Ctrl+L` toggles the
selection: if anything selected is unlocked it locks them all, and otherwise it unlocks them all. The
device inspector carries a `Locked` checkbox, and a locked device carries a 🔒 badge. **The badge is
editing chrome and does not print**, on the selection outline's reasoning: an elevation sheet is a
deliverable, and a lock is a fact about somebody's editing session rather than about the rack.

**11.185.3 RULED: THE SCHEMATIC'S `Ctrl+L` PINS A SYMBOL WHERE IT STANDS, NOW.** Settled by the user,
against a first description of the option as doing *"nothing visible"* until symbols could be moved.
**That description was wrong** and is recorded because the user chose past it: the layout already
honours pins, so a symbol pinned at the position the layout gave it stays there when devices are added.
The same toggle rule as §11.185.2, and the same label on both surfaces, because arbitration requires one
chord to carry one meaning and docs/05 already calls both *"lock"*. A pinned symbol carries a 📌 badge,
screen chrome as the padlock is.

**11.185.4 THE ONE SCHEMATIC SHEET IS CREATED BY THE FIRST PIN.** An implementation clause. CR-073's
single schematic `Sheet` had no producer, so the first pin creates it and every later pin finds it;
nothing creates a second. It is created empty of every filter, and its number and title are read by
nothing, since the export partitions the schematic by domain at export time.

**11.185.5 Scope.** **No scope change.** CR-034's three flags and CR-068's pin are v1; this is their
writer and the refusals they already implied.

**What this does not rule.** Dragging or nudging a schematic symbol, which is the soft-glue task and has
its own questions. `DeviceInstance.designatorLocked` and `Link.designatorLocked`, the other two CR-034
flags, which belong to renumbering and are untouched.

### 11.186 DR-187 · The schematic holds its layout, and a symbol drags, nudges and pins

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-18: *"the schematic view needs a 'soft glue' option for
devices; it's getting annoying to see devices get auto placed and shift positions significantly. It
should preserve the relative location of devices, just expanding the canvas slightly. This also comes
with the ability to nudge them on the schematic view."*

**11.186.0 MEASURED FIRST, AND ONE OF THE THREE CHANGED THE PLAN.** Probed on
`schematic_scene_test.dart`'s fixture:

- **Adding two devices re-flows the sheet and moves the symbols already on it.** That is the report,
  reproduced.
- **Pinning a symbol where it already stands moves nothing**, and pinning it 24 by 8 grid units away
  **moves all five of its neighbours**, because a fixed node stops relaxing and the rest re-flows
  around it. So a stored position is a strong instrument: it holds one symbol and disturbs the others.
- **WITH EVERY EXISTING SYMBOL FIXED, A NEWLY ADDED DEVICE LANDS EXACTLY ON TOP OF ONE OF THEM.**
  `MID-1` arrived at the identical position as `SNK-2`, a real overlap. **Freezing the sheet works and
  placing the newcomer does not come free**, which is the half of this feature an unmeasured plan
  would have discovered at the end.

**11.186.1 RULED: THE SHEET KEEPS ITS LAYOUT, AND THE POSITIONS ARE IN THE FILE.** Settled by the
user, from three shapes. Once a sheet has been laid out, every symbol keeps its place; a new device is
placed in free space and the sheet grows; nothing else moves until `Tidy sheet` is pressed. **This
overrules DR-011.4's third clause** (§12.38), which rejected *"pinning every symbol on first layout"*
on the ground that it *"would write a `SheetItem` per device into every document and grow the CR-117
byte surface to carry UI state"*. That cost is real and is now paid deliberately: the alternative
offered was a session-only freeze, and it was declined because *"reopening the project re-flows the
sheet, so the layout you arranged is gone the next morning."*

**11.186.2 RULED: THE FIRST EDIT THAT WOULD RE-FLOW IS WHAT RECORDS THE POSITIONS.** Settled by the
user. **Opening or viewing the Schematic writes nothing**, so looking at a project never marks it
changed. When an edit arrives that would re-flow the sheet, the positions every symbol had BEFORE that
edit are recorded, and only the new symbol is placed. Writing at save time was declined because it
would mutate the document outside a command (docs/03 §5.6), and writing on first layout because it
would prompt *"save changes?"* on a project nobody edited.

**11.186.2.1 THIS CLAUSE SAID *"ITS OWN UNDO ENTRY"* AND THAT WAS WRONG, MEASURED.** The sentence was
written here by the author of the option, not by the user, and the first build of it was refuted by two
tests older than the ruling. `schematic_remedy_test.dart` and `schematic_remedy_dr128_test.dart` assert
*"ONE undo takes back the device AND the cable"* and *"one undo takes back the converter and both
cables"*, which is the Edit menu's standing promise; a freeze pushed as a second entry broke both.
**The behaviour it produced is the one the ruling exists to abolish**: the first `Ctrl+Z` after any edit
took back the ARRANGEMENT and left the edit, so the sheet visibly scrambled and the device stayed
deleted, and undoing one delete took two presses. **RULED INSTEAD: the freeze is a CHILD of the edit's
own undo entry.** One undo reverts both and lands on exactly the document that existed before either,
which re-flows to the layout that was frozen, so the arrangement is right either way. The entry is
still named by the edit, because `_commit` names a transaction after its FIRST child (DR-156
§11.155.2). The mechanism is `DocumentController.addConsequence`, a hook that runs at the tail of a
transaction that changed something, with the entry still open; an epoch listener cannot do this,
because by the time an epoch bumps the entry is sealed.

**11.186.3 RULED: A STORED POSITION IS HONOURED WHETHER OR NOT IT IS PINNED, AND PINNED MEANS `Tidy`
LEAVES IT ALONE.** An implementation clause of §11.186.1, and it reverses a rule rather than adding
one: `schematic_scene.dart` ignores an unpinned `SheetItem.position` today, because *"honouring it
would freeze the first layout the document ever received and make every recompute a no-op"*. **That
freeze is now the point.** The distinction the two states carry is what `Tidy sheet` does with them:
it re-flows an unpinned symbol and clears its stored position, and never touches a pinned one
(CR-068).

**11.186.4 RULED: A DRAG OR A NUDGE MOVES A SYMBOL AND PINS IT, AND THE ARROWS NUDGE WHEN NO CONNECT
IS IN FLIGHT.** Settled by the user. The pin half is CR-068 and docs/05 §10 as already written: *"any
manual move sets `SheetItem.pinned = true`"*. The keys are the arrows, which the schematic scope binds
to the connect-mode pin caret: one chord, two modes the canvas can tell apart, and **the keymap row is
relabelled to say both** so the generated table does not promise one of them. `Alt`+arrows was declined
because docs/04 gives that chord to the rack's swap, and one chord meaning two unrelated things across
canvases is what the arbitration fails on.

**11.186.5 A NEW SYMBOL TAKES A FREE SLOT.** An implementation clause, and §11.186.0's third
measurement is why it is a clause at all: the layout places a new node among fixed ones without
avoiding them. The new symbol takes the first free slot in the layer the graph gives it, and the sheet
grows to hold it, which is the user's *"expanding the canvas slightly"*.

**11.186.6 Scope.** **No scope change.** docs/05 §10 already rules *"first layout is automatic; any
manual move pins; a single Tidy sheet lays out all unpinned symbols"*, and none of it was built. This
is that paragraph, plus the persistence DR-011.4 had refused.

**11.186.7 RULED: `Tidy sheet` SITS ON THE DOMAIN FILTER BAR NOW AND MOVES TO THE CONTEXT MENU WHEN
THE DRAG LANDS.** Settled by the user on 2026-09-22, in those terms, over the two hosts §11.186.6
left open. **The bar is the schematic's only existing chrome**, so the way out of the freeze ships in
the same change as the freeze rather than waiting on a surface nobody has built; docs/05 §5 already
lists `Tidy sheet` on the empty-space context menu, so that is where it belongs once `#918`'s drag
gives that menu its other reasons to exist. **The button is the only DOCUMENT EDIT on a bar of view
toggles**, which is a real objection and is answered in the widget rather than argued away: it is
separated from `All`/`None`, it is DISABLED when nothing would re-flow, and it asks first, with the
count, per docs/05 §10's *"behind a plain confirm"*. A move to the context menu is then a move and
not a redesign, because the count and the confirm travel with it.

**11.186.8 RULED: A DRAG SHOWS A GHOST OUTLINE, AND THE SHEET LANDS ON RELEASE.** Settled by the
user on 2026-09-22 over three preview shapes, **priced first**. One frame is 16.7 ms. Measured on
`schematic_perf_test.dart`'s two fixtures, best of five:

| Path | 300 links, 110 devices | 3,600 links, 1,320 devices |
|---|---|---|
| Wires re-routed, symbol tier reused | 0.72 ms | **8.8 ms** |
| Layout reused, wires re-routed | — | **36.3 ms** |
| Cold scene build | 7.7 ms | **76.9 ms** |

**Live re-routing is affordable on a house and not on a campus**, and a twelve-pod job is exactly
the sheet somebody needs to drag symbols around on, so the expensive case is the one that matters.
A dashed rectangle follows the cursor, the symbol and its cables do not move, and the whole sheet
lands at once on release. It costs one overlay op per frame at any size, which is the same budget
CR-102's marquee band already runs on.

**WHAT THIS COSTS IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED**: the wires are not seen until the drop, so a
symbol dropped into a tangle looks fine until it is released. One `Ctrl+Z` is the way out, and the
alternative was a preview that stutters on the sheets most in need of tidying.

**11.186.9 RULED: `Ctrl+Shift+U` UNPINS, AND IT SHIPS WITH THE DRAG.** Settled by the user, moving
this out of §11.186.6's not-ruled list rather than amending roadmap §2: docs/05 §10 already rules
*"any manual move pins; `Ctrl+Shift+U` unpins"*, so this is existing scope changing chapters and not
new scope. **The reason it cannot wait is that the drag creates the need.** Every symbol a person
ever nudges is pinned from then on, and `Tidy sheet` spares a pinned symbol by design (§11.186.3,
CR-068), so without an unpin the act of tidying a sheet by hand is what permanently removes it from
the reach of `Tidy sheet`. The command is the unpin half of `SetSymbolPinnedCommand`, which exists
and is tested; what was missing is the chord docs/05 names. `Ctrl+L` remains the toggle (DR-186
§11.185.3) and is not replaced: a toggle answers *"pin this"* and an explicit unpin answers
*"give this back to the layout"*, which is the question somebody has after a drag.

**11.186.10 CORRECTED: THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE CARET, NOT *"A CONNECT IN FLIGHT"*.** §11.186.4 gave
the arrows a second job on the words *"the arrows nudge when no connect is in flight"*, and building
it found that reading cannot work. **The arrows are also how a pin is REACHED before anything is
armed** (docs/05 §7's *"arrow to a candidate port"*, and `schematic_keyboard_connect_test.dart`'s
route in its own name: *"arrows reach a pin, W arms it, Enter commits"*), so *"no wire in flight"* is
true for half of the connect route itself. Sixteen tests said so on the first build.

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-22 from four shapes: A CARET ON SCREEN IS THE MODE.** With a caret
the arrows move it, exactly as before; `Esc` hands them back. With no caret and a symbol selected
they nudge it one grid unit and pin it (CR-068). With no caret and nothing selected they seed a
caret, which is the old behaviour and keeps the key from being the silent no-op docs/04 §3.4 forbids.
**The route to a caret is still one key**: `W` seeds a caret and arms from it in a single press, and
always did, so nothing was taken away. `Alt`+arrows was declined a second time for §11.186.4's
reason, and the other three modifiers are spoken for on this canvas.

**A RUN OF PRESSES IS ONE UNDO ENTRY**, through a `mergeKey` on the move keyed by the set of symbols.
Five presses costing five `Ctrl+Z` would make the feature worse than not having it. A pin and an
unpin never merge, which is not an oversight: those are decisions rather than adjustments, and two in
a row are two things somebody meant.

**THE RELABELLING §11.186.4 REQUIRED IS HALF WHAT IT SOUNDS LIKE, AND A GATE IS WHY.** The ↑/↓ rows
already carried *"Caret up · nudge the selection up"*, a union shared with the RACK's caret rows,
against a note saying the sheet nudged nothing; that note was false the moment this shipped and is
replaced. **`Arrow Right` ALONE keeps a caret-only label and carries the nudge in its note**, because it is
shared with the Device Builder's `quickAddComplete` and `meaningDrift` refused the pair the instant
that row gained a schematic-only clause. **THIS CLAUSE SAID `←/→` UNTIL 2026-09-23 AND THE CODE
NEVER MATCHED IT**: `Arrow Left` is shared with nothing, carries the union label, and always did.
The sweeping version was written because an edit script aborted between its two replacements and the
result was not re-read, which is the same shape as every other stale count this corpus keeps
finding. Three rows carry the union and one cannot. The gate was right: a keyboard-only user
cannot see a scope boundary, so **a shared label may state only what is true in EVERY scope that
shares the chord**, and a label promising a nudge that the builder does not perform is worse than a
note somebody has to open.

**What this does not rule.** Multi-select drag. The v1.1 route constraints, untouched.

### 11.187 DR-188 · RackPal is CAD-lite, and DXF interchange opens v1.3

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-23, on reading docs/21's claim that the product *"is not a
CAD package"*: *"I think we're selling ourselves a bit short by not calling it a CAD package;
Granted it is representative of reality rather than strictly adhering to it, so I think CAD-Lite is
a reasonable (even if made up) term to call the product."*

**11.187.1 RULED: THE PRODUCT IS CAD-LITE.** Settled by the user, whose reason is recorded in their
own words because it is trade knowledge rather than a product opinion: *"It's also nearly impossible
in this industry to draw precise technical drawings that won't get altered and/or ignored by the
installers for one reason or another. TV's get shifted because of furniture, wiring gets re-routed
or a box gets moved because an electrician took the space first, etc. It'd be unbelievably tedious
to document all of those changes, so the trade-off in precision is negligeable to the workflow."*

The precision is therefore spent where it survives contact with a site and withheld where it does
not: **calibrated floorplans, exact elevations (RU is discrete and a device fits or it does not),
and cable footage**; representative everywhere else, which is symbol positions, routing paths and
plan pin placement.

**11.187.2 THE DESCRIPTION THIS REPLACES WAS THE AUTHOR'S AND WAS NEVER MEASURED.** docs/21 §21.1
said *"it is not a CAD package"*, written to manage a tester's expectations downward and checked
against nothing. It undersold a tool that calibrates plans to real-world scale, draws exact
elevations and resolves cable footage through four ranked sources. Recorded because this ruling
family has now produced four clauses that were the author's sentences rather than the user's
choices, and three of them were refuted by their own build.

**11.187.3 RULED: v1.3 IS CREATED AS A RELEASE BAND, AND DXF INTERCHANGE OPENS IT.** A §8.3
amendment, and the first band added since the roadmap was written. roadmap §2 carried four bands
(v1, v1.1, v1.2, v2) and the board's Sagas mirror them; **v1.3 did not exist and is created here**,
between v1.2 and v2, because §2.4 rules v2 to be *"the next product decision, not the next
release"* and an interchange export is neither a fast follow nor a new product.

**11.187.4 RULED: DXF, NOT DWG.** Settled by the user from three shapes. DXF is Autodesk's
documented interchange format and every CAD tool opens it; docs/08 §9 estimates it at ~400 lines of
new geometry mapping, which is plausible because `DiagramCanvas` is an abstract interface with two
production backends already (`bounds_canvas`, `pdf_canvas`) and this is a third, exactly as CR-086
intends. **Native DWG was declined on a licence collision rather than on cost**: the open writer is
GPL-3.0, which the licence ruling accommodates, but the commercial route (Open Design Alliance) is
a paid membership and is GPL-incompatible, so native DWG would put the feature in conflict with
this project's own licence. **This overrules docs/08 §9's `not planned`** (§12.39).

**11.187.5 RULED: THE DEVICE LOCATION PLAN IS IN. RACK ELEVATIONS ARE NOT YET RULED, AND THE
BLOCKER IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE.** The plan is the drawing another trade actually wants and the
only sheet whose geometry is already in real-world units. The user raised elevations as *"a
maybe"*, for a reason recorded in their terms: *"We've encountered situations too many times where
a cabinet was too small for a pull-out rack, or a closet was shaved down to make space for a mini
bar and the rack no longer fit."*

They expected this to need *"a future schema of the rack templates"* carrying physical dimensions.
**MEASURED: that schema exists.** `Rack` declares `overallWidth`, `overallDepth`, `overallHeight`,
`ownWeight`, `hasFrontDoor`, `hasRearDoor`, `frontDoorClearance` and `rearDoorClearance`, and they
serialize. **Five of the six appear only in `rack.dart` and `json_codec.dart`: no writer, no
reader.** Only `ownWeight` is read, by the rack inspector. So the cabinetmaker deliverable is
blocked on somewhere to type the numbers, not on a model change, and that is a smaller and
independently useful piece of work than the export it gates. **This is the fourth instance of the
`Placement.locked` shape** (§11.185.0): a field with no writer is a rule nobody is following.

**11.187.6 Scope.** **A scope change**, per §8.3, carried in its own commit. Creates roadmap §2.4
for v1.3 and renumbers §2.4 to §2.7.

**What this does not rule.** Whether rack elevations join the DXF export, which waits on
§11.187.5's writer. Whether the product should CHECK a rack against a room's dimensions rather than
only draw it, which is the thing that would have caught the shaved closet before anybody built it.
DWG, permanently or otherwise. What layer names, units and block structure the DXF uses.
