### 11.188 DR-189 · The licence is AGPLv3-or-later, and a vendor's door is the CC0 catalog

**The question.** From the user, 2026-09-23: *"I want to switch the intended license to be AGPLv3; I
remember there being a reason that this ended up being a potential problem, but APGLv3 allows for
exceptions to be carved for specific use cases, which I feel we can use to work around those
problems."*

**11.188.1 RULED: THE APPLICATION CODE IS AGPLv3-OR-LATER.** Settled by the user. **This reverses
DR-036 §11.35.1 clause 2** (§12.40). Every other clause of DR-036 stands unchanged: the project is
public, the community catalog is CC0, contributions arrive under a DCO sign-off, and nothing is
priced.

**11.188.2 THE OBJECTION THE QUESTION REMEMBERS IS NOT RECORDED, AND WAS SEARCHED FOR RATHER THAN
ASSUMED.** `AGPL` and `Affero` appear nowhere in the tracked tree, in `docs/`, in `.okf/`, or in any
commit message on any branch. **Two recorded facts are adjacent and are the likely memory**: `pdf`
being Apache-2.0 closes **GPLv2** permanently and not v3 (§11.35.2), and §11.35.4's **output
exception**, which is a real problem solved by exactly the mechanism the question proposes. No
AGPL-specific objection was ever raised in this project, so none is overruled here.

**11.188.3 THE DEPENDENCY CENSUS STILL HOLDS AND NEEDS NO RE-RUN.** §11.35.2 measured the tree at
`pdf` 3.13.0: one Apache-2.0, four MIT, the rest BSD-3-Clause, zero copyleft. **Apache-2.0 is
one-way compatible into AGPLv3 on the same terms that admitted it to GPLv3**, so the tree is clean
for this licence exactly as it was for the last one.

**11.188.4 WHAT AGPL CHANGES TODAY IS NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** AGPLv3 §13 obliges offering
source to users who interact with the program **over a network**. RackPal is a Windows desktop
application with no server, no accounts and no telemetry, so §13 is currently inert. **The value is
prospective**: it forecloses a hosted RackPal built on this code without released modifications,
in advance of anyone wanting one. A licence chosen after that becomes attractive is chosen too
late.

**11.188.5 THE OUTPUT EXCEPTION CARRIES OVER UNCHANGED IN MECHANISM, AND IS STILL UNWRITTEN.**
AGPLv3 incorporates GPLv3 §7's additional permissions, so §11.35.4's exception grants identically:
a document produced by RackPal is the user's own work and is not a derivative of RackPal, embedded
template snapshots and exported sheets included. **MEASURED: this repository contains no `LICENSE`
file, and README line 168 still calls the licence TBD and *"under consideration"*.** §11.35.4
requires the exception to be *"stated in `LICENSE` and in the README, not inferred, because an
exception nobody can find is not one"*, so that clause has been undischarged since 2026-08-10. **The
outstanding work is not this switch. It is that the project has never been licensed at all.**

**11.188.6 THE EXCEPTION TEXT IS NOT DRAFTED HERE AND NOT BY THIS AUTHOR.** §11.35.4's own
precedent is the GCC Runtime Library Exception, drafted by the FSF's counsel. An additional
permission that does not say what its author believes is worse than none, and this is the one
deliverable in the project where approximately right is not a category that exists. **Ruled: the
`LICENSE` file and its exception go to a qualified reviewer before any public push**, and M8's
AC-058/D7 licence deliverable is where that lands.

**11.188.7 THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED.** AGPL is prohibited outright by some
organisations' open-source policies. For an integrator's laptop this is very unlikely to bite; **it
bites if a manufacturer or distributor ever wants to contribute code or embed the product**, which
is a narrower door than GPLv3 leaves open. Recorded so the trade is visible rather than found
later.

**11.188.8 RULED: A VENDOR'S DOOR IS THE CC0 CATALOG, AND THE SEED BOUNDARY IS A LICENCE
BOUNDARY.** The user asked whether the planned community template repository needs an exception
carved from AGPL, and offered *"this may be as simple as just making the device template repository
CC0"*, wanting manufacturer maintenance to be *"frictionless"*.

**It needs no exception, and §11.35.1 clause 3 is why**: the catalog is already CC0 and was never
under the code licence, for §11.35.3's reason, which is this question's own concern reaching one
step further than it expected. **What this clause adds is the boundary.** The seeded catalog is
Dart source in `rackpal_core/lib/src/catalog/` and is therefore AGPL as code; the community catalog
is data and is CC0. **Vendor and manufacturer contributions arrive in the CC0 catalog and never as
source**, because CC0 imposes no conditions and so flows into AGPL freely, while the reverse would
put a vendor's product data under copyleft, which is the friction the question exists to remove.
Promotion from community to seed is legitimate and one-way.

**11.188.9 PROVENANCE NEEDS NO RULING, AND THE MODEL ALREADY HOLDS THE LINE.** The user raised
vendor provenance and then declined it themselves, on the ground that verification *"introduces a
lot of potential network operations that I'd like to avoid"*. **Measured: `TemplateProvenance` is
already a sealed class answering *"where a placeable template came from, as far as THIS build can
tell"*, and `ProjectProvenance` already states the discipline in terms: the name says which SHELF
and not which author.** A manufacturer library is therefore another shelf, `LibraryProvenance`
carries its id and name, and the badge-versus-filter split (DR-033's handle-and-id split applied
one level down) already handles two libraries claiming one name. **No network operation is
required, because the trust is established on acquisition rather than at runtime**, and that limit
is stated rather than papered over: a badge means a library file said so. Signed archives are the
next rung if one is ever wanted, and verification of a signature is also local; the cost there is
key distribution, which is administrative rather than technical.

**Scope.** **No scope change.** Licensing is not roadmap §2 feature scope. This reverses one clause
of DR-036 and adds a boundary the catalog already implied.

**What this does not rule.** The licence text itself. Whether a hosted RackPal is ever built. The
catalog's CC0 status, which stands under §11.35.3 untouched. Signed archives.

---

### 11.189 DR-190 · Close in the Device Builder asks before it discards

**The question.** Found writing docs/21 (`#924`): the Device Builder's `Close` returns to the
browser by unmounting the builder, and the builder's `TemplateEditSession` is an in-memory copy, so
**a dirty draft is destroyed without a word**. The shell's own comment above `onDone` called a
discard-and-return route *"a gap rather than a decision"*; `Close` was that route, unguarded. Put
to the user on 2026-09-23 with three options and prices.

**11.189.1 RULED: CLOSE ON A DIRTY DRAFT SHOWS SAVE / DON'T SAVE / CANCEL.** Settled by the user,
choosing the recommended option. The reasoning below is the author's as offered; the user accepted
it and added none of their own. **It is the prompt the application already shows when a project is
closed** (`UnsavedChangesDialog`, docs/03 §9.5), with its four rules unchanged: `Save` is the
default and holds focus, `Esc` is Cancel, nothing on the keyboard reaches `Don't Save`, and a click
outside is not an answer. A clean draft closes with no prompt.

**11.189.2 `SAVE` OBEYS THE SAVE BUTTON'S OWN RULE.** A draft missing a name, a prefix or a height
cannot be saved (AC-049), so `Save` from the prompt on such a draft saves nothing, closes nothing,
and says why in the builder's refusal band. The person is left where they were, with the reason in
front of them.

**11.189.3 DR-099 §11.98.4 IS NOT CONTRADICTED.** That clause refuses, rather than prompts, when
door 2 would REPLACE one dirty draft with another template, because the dialog offering to discard
is dismissed by reflex on the way to something else. `Close` is not on the way to anything: leaving
IS the act, so the standard three-button question is the honest one and a refusal would leave no
way to abandon a draft at all.

**Scope.** No scope change: this makes an existing control do what docs/03 §9.5 already requires of
closing anything dirty.

---

### 11.190 DR-191 · A room's plan estimate follows its inputs, and says why when it cannot

**The question.** Found writing docs/21 (`#924`): `roomEstimateFor` is called only when an outline
is closed or reshaped, and returns null unless the plan is calibrated, a run to the room lands in a
rack, and that rack is pinned on the outline's own underlay. **The natural order (import,
calibrate, outline, then place and land) computes nothing, and supplying the missing input later
never fills the field.** Put to the user on 2026-09-23 with three options and prices.

**11.190.1 RULED: THE PLAN-DERIVED FIGURE IS REFRESHED BY EVERY EDIT THAT CHANGES IT.** Settled by
the user, choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without
addition. After every transaction, each room whose figure the plan may fill (DR-050 §11.49.3:
empty, or the plan's own earlier figure) is re-derived, and a changed answer is written **inside
the same undo entry** through `DocumentController.addConsequence` (DR-187 §11.186.2's mechanism).
Pinning the rack, calibrating, landing a run or moving a corner therefore updates the figure, and
one `Ctrl+Z` takes back the edit and its consequence together.

**11.190.2 A FIGURE THE PLAN CAN NO LONGER DERIVE IS CLEARED, NOT KEPT.** When a room's plan figure
stops deriving (the rack is unpinned, the outline cleared, the calibration removed) and the stored
figure is the plan's own, it is cleared. A computed number whose inputs are gone is a guess, and
G4 does not let a guess stand as a measurement. **A figure a person typed is never touched in either
direction**, which §11.49.3 already rules and this keeps.

**11.190.3 THE HOOK IS INSTALLED BY THE CONTROLLER, NOT BY A VIEW.** DR-187's freeze is registered
by the Schematic view and therefore does nothing until that view has been opened, which docs/21
§21.8 has to warn about. A fact about the document must not depend on which tab somebody visited,
so this consequence is installed when the `DocumentController` is constructed, on every route that
builds one.

**11.190.4 A BLANK FIGURE NAMES WHAT IS MISSING.** The room's helper line, which says where a
figure came from, now also says why there is none: no outline, plan not calibrated, no run to this
room lands in a rack, or the rack is not pinned on this plan. **The multi-floor case gets its own
sentence**, because it is the one a person cannot fix by doing the next thing: a head end on the
basement page cannot measure to a room outlined on Level 1, and the answer there is to type it. The
same line loses its `AC-024` citation, which was a ruling ID shown to a user.

**Scope.** No scope change: DR-050 bought the figure and this makes it arrive.

**11.191.2 NO ROW IS INFLATED, AND THERE IS NO GRAND TOTAL WITH WASTE.** The factor is applied to

**11.191.3 THE HELP LINE IS CORRECTED TO SAY WHERE IT APPLIES**, the Schedule's takeoff, rather

### 11.192 DR-193 · The validation keys work from every view and go where the fix is

**The question.** Found writing docs/21 (`#924`): `F7`, `F8` and `Shift+F8` sit in
`KeyScope.global`, and only the Rack view's `Actions` handle them, so on four views of six they do
nothing while the keymap and the generated reference say otherwise. Many findings are about cables
and floorplans, which are not fixed on the Rack view. Put to the user on 2026-09-23 with three
options and prices.

**11.192.1 RULED: THE SHELL HANDLES THE THREE KEYS, AND `F8` SWITCHES TO THE VIEW THAT CAN FIX THE
FINDING.** Settled by the user, choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's,
accepted without addition. The destination is decided by what the finding points at:

| The finding points at | `F8` goes to | And |
|---|---|---|
| A device in a rack | Rack | switches to its rack, selects it |
| A device not in a rack | Schematic | selects its symbol, or says it has none |
| A rack | Rack | switches to it, opens its settings |
| A cable | Schematic | selects the cable, or says it has no drawn end on the sheet |
| A floorplan | Site | opens that plan |
| Anything else (a net, a circuit) | Rack | and says the finding has no single item to show |

**11.192.2 ONE CURSOR, IN THE ENGINE'S ORDER.** The walk is over `evaluateDocument`'s findings in
its own deterministic order, wraps at both ends, and names what it selected on the status channel.
`F7` re-checks from any view and says the counts.

**11.192.3 THE DRAWER STAYS ON THE RACK VIEW.** Moving it into the shell under every view was the
more complete option and was not chosen. docs/04 §1's layout stands.

### 11.193 DR-194 · A local diagnostic log ships now, because builds are already in the wild

**The question.** Found by the full-tree review (`#97`). A release build reports nothing anywhere.
`main.dart`'s fatal handler routes every uncaught error to `FlutterError.presentError`, which its own
comment calls a no-op in release, so a throw in the awaits before `runApp` is still a black window
and no message. `storage_log.dart` carries a complete §12.4-safe structured log, typed so that a
fact may be an `int`, a `bool` or an `Enum` and never a `String`, and **nothing in `lib/` installs
its sink**. §9.9 schedules *"crash reporting local-first and opt-in remote"* for M8. Pre-release
builds are with testers now, so every crash they hit reaches the author as a description rather
than as evidence. Put to the user on 2026-09-23 with three priced options.

**11.193.1 RULED: THE LOCAL HALF OF §9.9'S CRASH REPORTING IS PULLED FORWARD.** Settled by the user,
choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. It lands
under Epic `#786`, not under a milestone, and it moves no milestone's clause.

**11.193.2 WHAT THE SLICE IS, AND NOTHING MORE.**

1. **A local log file in the data root**, capped in size and rotated, never uploaded. It receives
   the storage layer's structured events through the existing sink, and every fatal error.
2. **A fatal error is recorded as its TYPE and its stack frames, never its message.** The message is
   where a path, a client name or a site address ends up (§12.4, CR-096); the frames name the code,
   not the user's files. The type-and-frames form is a floor, not a design for M8's reporter.
3. **A dialog when startup fails**, so the case the header of `main.dart` calls a black window says
   that the app could not start and where its log is.
4. **`Help ▸ Open diagnostics folder…`** beside `About`, because a log nobody can find is a log
   nobody sends.

**11.193.3 WHAT STAYS AT M8.** The opt-in remote half, symbol archival, CR-096's redaction policy
reconciled as a whole, and **§9.9's exit clause**: *"a deliberately induced crash produces a local
report containing no project content"* is still M8's to demonstrate. This slice is the mechanism it
will be demonstrated on, not the demonstration.

**Scope.** An amendment of timing under §8.3, recorded in §12.41. No scope enters or leaves v1.

### 11.194 DR-195 · The seed catalogue's explicit values stay explicit, and the ratchet is cleared around them

**The question.** Of the analyzer's 233 infos, 161 were `avoid_redundant_argument_values` and 49
`cascade_invocations`. `#98` recorded clearing them as a user decision in M2 and it was never taken.
The full-tree review (`#97`) counted where the 161 live: **116 are in the nine seed catalogue files**,
and they are values such as `requiresClearanceAboveU: 0` and `dir: PortDirection.bidirectional`.
Put to the user on 2026-09-23 with three priced options.

**11.194.1 RULED: THE CATALOGUE KEEPS ITS EXPLICIT VALUES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS SWEPT.** Settled by the
user, choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition.
Each seed catalogue file carries a file-wide `ignore` for that one lint, with its reason written
beside it. Every other occurrence of both lints is fixed, and the pin is re-measured in the same
change. docs/11 §7's lint configuration is unchanged.

**11.194.2 WHY A VALUE EQUAL TO THE DEFAULT IS NOT REDUNDANT HERE.** Under CR-114 an explicit `0`
means *measured zero*, and a catalogue entry is a record of what a device IS. An argument that
happens to equal today's constructor default is a fact that coincides with it; deleting it hands the
fact to the constructor, and a later change to that default would then rewrite every device that
had said it silently. The lint is right about code and wrong about data.

**11.194.3 CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHAPTER: FIXTURES ARE DATA TOO, AND THE CORPUS HAD ALREADY SAID
SO.** The options were priced on "~45 redundant arguments outside the catalogue", offered as
sweepable. Applying the sweep (`#936`) and then reading the ratchet's own history found `#246`
(DR-107), which **kept** sixty explicit `mountMethod: MountMethod.rackEars` sites, *"catalog and
fixture"*, because that default had moved once and *"a template that had gone silent on the question
would have changed meaning without a diff"*. That is §11.194.2's argument, made a month earlier and
missed when this question was priced. Every one of the 45 builds a `TemplateBody` or a rack in a
test fixture. **So the fixture files that carry them take the same documented file-wide ignore as
the catalogue, and their values stay written.** One site in `lib/` (`shake_animation.dart`) passes a
named constant that equals the default, and keeps it with a line `ignore` for the same reason.
`cascade_invocations` is swept as ruled. The outcome the user chose is unchanged: the pin drops to
the 23 infos worth reading, and only the route to it differs.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.195 DR-196 · The two canvas screens are not split before M7 (`#98`'s verdict)

**The question.** `#98` was conditional on the full-tree review (`#97`) calling for it, and named four
candidates. The review measured them: `rack_canvas_screen.dart` is 6,092 lines, 2,775 of code and

of code; `schematic_canvas_screen.dart` is 5,784, 2,715 of code, one `State` of 4,872 lines and 102
members. The methods are not bloated; the classes are. Put to the user on 2026-09-23 with three
priced options.

**11.195.1 RULED: `#98` CLOSES WITH ONE MOVE MADE AND THREE DECLINED.** Settled by the user, choosing
the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition.

| Candidate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `wire_trace.dart` to `rackpal_core` | **Moved** (`#931`), the one item `#98` called not a judgement call |
| `rack_canvas_screen.dart` | **Not split now.** Revisited at M7 |
| `schematic_canvas_screen.dart` | **Not split now.** Revisited at M7 |
| `json_codec.dart` | **Not touched.** Under CR-117's byte gate, and nothing asks |

### 11.196 DR-197 · A CSV import offers one new cable type per id, and lists every spelling

**The question.** Found by the full-tree review (`#97`) and probed on the real import path. A sheet
that spells one cable two ways that differ only in case or punctuation (`Plenum Speaker 14/4` and
`plenum-speaker 14-4`) put **two** boxes in the import dialog's *"will create"* list and made **one**
type: both spellings derive the same id, and since `#935` the second add refuses rather than
overwriting the first. Re-importing the sheet was probed and is idempotent. Put to the user on
2026-09-23 with three priced options.

**11.196.1 RULED: ONE ROW PER ID, CARRYING EVERY SPELLING.** Settled by the user, choosing the
recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. New spellings whose
derived ids collide are one entry in the list, named by the first spelling in sheet order and
listing the others. The type it creates takes that first spelling as its name and **every** spelling
as an alias. Unticking the row declines all of its spellings together.

**11.196.2 WHY.** The dialog is a promise about what the import will do, and a list with more boxes
than the import makes types is a small lie told at the one moment somebody is checking. Spellings
that derive the same id differ only in case and punctuation, which is how one cable gets written
twice, not how two cables get told apart.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.197 DR-198 · A file another program has locked is named as locked when it will not open

**The question.** Found by `#947`'s tests of `DocumentStore.open`, the first to make a read fail
after the file was found. A read refused with a sharing violation (Windows errno 32: OneDrive or
Dropbox syncing the file, antivirus, a second RackPal) classified as `OpenUnexpected`, and the user
read *"Something went wrong that RackPal does not have a specific explanation for."* Save has had
its own answer for the same condition all along (`SaveLocked`: three silent retries, then Retry,
Save As or Cancel). Put to the user on 2026-09-25 with four priced options: name it with OK only;
name it with a Try again button; retry silently three times first, then name it; leave it.

**11.197.1 RULED: NAMED, WITH OK ONLY.** Settled by the user, choosing the recommended option; the
reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. A read refused as locked reports its own
error, `OpenLocked`, not `OpenUnexpected`. The dialog says the file is in use by another program,
names the usual holders (OneDrive, Dropbox, antivirus, a second copy of RackPal), says to wait or
close it there and then open it again, and says nothing was changed on disk. Its one action is OK.
The recents entry is kept: only `OpenNotFound` evicts.

**11.197.2 WHY.** The generic sentence is true and useless: it names no cause, so it suggests no
remedy, and the remedy here is simple and the user's to perform. Re-opening from File > Recent is
already one action, so a Try again button would add the open sequence's first retry path for about
one click saved. Silent retries were declined with it: they delay the report of a lock that is not
going to clear.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.198 DR-199 · An import refusal's title names the cause, not "that is not a device library"

**The question.** Found by `#947`'s route tests of the device library and template imports. Every
refusal carried the same title, *"That is not a device library"* (or *"…template"*), including
the two cases where the file is one: over the size cap, and written by a newer RackPal, whose
detail line says so directly under a title denying it. Put to the user on 2026-09-25 with three
priced options: a title by cause; one neutral title for every refusal; leave it.

**11.198.1 RULED: THE TITLE NAMES THE CAUSE.** Settled by the user, choosing the recommended option;
the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. For a device library, and in the same
words for a device template:

| Cause | Title |
|---|---|
| Not that kind of file, or a zip archive | *That is not a device library* |
| Written by a newer RackPal | *This library needs a newer RackPal* |
| Over the size cap, or nested past the limit | *That library is too large to import* |
| Anything else that does not decode | *That library could not be read* |

The detail lines are unchanged. Too-deeply-nested shares the size title because the detail already
treats the two as one limit, and a sentence of its own for a file only a broken or hostile writer
produces is not worth the reader's time; that call is the author's.

**11.198.2 WHY.** The title is read first and is often the only thing read. *Not a library* sends a
person looking for a different file when theirs is fine and merely large, or merely new.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.199 DR-200 · A path too long for Windows is named when a file will not open

**The question.** Found by `#947`'s read of the storage layer, and the same shape as DR-198. On
open, `StorageFailure.pathTooLong` fell through to `OpenUnexpected`, so a project in a deep OneDrive
or SharePoint folder read *"Something went wrong that RackPal does not have a specific explanation
for."* Save has named the condition all along (`SavePathTooLong`, stating both numbers). Dart adds
no long-path prefix on Windows, so the case is reachable, not theoretical. Put to the user on
2026-09-26 with three priced options: name it with both numbers, OK only; name it without numbers;
leave it.

**11.199.1 RULED: NAMED, WITH BOTH NUMBERS, OK ONLY.** Settled by the user, choosing the recommended
option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. A read refused because the path
is too long reports `OpenPathTooLong`, whose dialog says the path is too long for Windows, gives its
length and the limit, says to move it to a shorter folder or shorten the folder names and open it
again, and says nothing was changed on disk. OK is its only action; the recents entry is kept.

**11.199.2 A CORRECTION TO THE QUESTION AS PUT.** The option's example said Windows allows *260*.
The limit used is `kWindowsMaxPath`, **259**, the same constant `SavePathTooLong` states, so open and
save give the same number for the same folder. The example was the author's slip, not the user's
choice.

**11.199.3 WHY.** The remedy is the user's to perform, and *"too long"* without a number cannot
tell them how much shorter it has to be, which is the argument save's own message was written on.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.200 DR-201 · The collision policy leaves Project Settings, because it governs nothing

**The question.** Found by `#945`'s triage of the declarations nothing calls:
`resolveDesignatorCollision`, the only reader of `ProjectSettings.collisionPolicy`, had no caller.
The setting was an editable row in Project Settings (append a letter, append a number, or refuse)
and changed nothing. New designators come from `_lowestUnused`, so an allocated one cannot collide
by construction, and a typed device designator that is already taken is not checked against the
setting (it is allowed, and validation flags the duplicate). Put to the user on 2026-09-29 with
three priced options: remove the row; wire the policy to every surface a designator is typed into,
under a ruling of its own; leave it and file it.

**11.200.1 RULED: THE ROW IS REMOVED; THE STORED VALUE IS KEPT.** Settled by the user, choosing the
recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. Project Settings no
longer offers the collision policy. `ProjectSettings.collisionPolicy` stays in the model and on the
wire, read and written exactly as before, so every existing project saves back byte for byte
(CR-117) and nothing migrates. `resolveDesignatorCollision`, which nothing called, is deleted with
its tests; the enum stays because the stored field is typed by it.

**11.200.2 WHY.** A control that changes nothing teaches the person using it that the settings
cannot be trusted, which costs every other row in the dialog. And the question it asks is moot for
allocation, the only place a designator is computed.

**11.200.3 WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE.** What a typed duplicate designator should do is unchanged:
allowed at entry, flagged by validation. Wiring a policy to typed entry was the second option, and
it was not chosen; if it is wanted later it is a ruling of its own, and the stored field is still
there for it.

**Scope.** No scope change.

### 11.201 DR-202 · Save replaces a version nothing is placed from, and the change class speaks only for placed devices

**The question.** Reported by the user on 2026-09-29 (`#950`) as two defects in the Device Builder.
First: *"when hitting Save, it will save a new version rather than saving the edits to the original
template, if it's the first time a template is opened. Once the template is closed and re-opened,
save functions as normal."* Second: *"'Breaking' is a bit confusing, especially if it is a brand new
template."*

**The first was a regression of §11.76.3, and not a new question.** §11.76.3 was fixed while the
builder was a dialog, which built its wiring once per opening; `#778` (2026-08-26) made it a view,
and from then the shell called `buildDeviceBuilderActions` inside `build`. The closure it returns is the only record of the id a new
template's first Save mints; a save changes the document, the document change rebuilds the shell,
and the rebuilt closure's id was null again. So the second Save on a new template minted `tpl.foo_2`
beside `tpl.foo`, exactly the defect §11.76.3 was written to remove. Reopening worked because door 2
supplies the id from the shell. **The §11.76.3 tests passed throughout**, because each held one
closure still and called it twice; the app never held it still. The shell now builds the wiring once
per authoring session, and `builder_save_route_test.dart` presses the real button.

**Fixing that exposed the ruling question.** With the id kept, every Save forks `version + 1`, so a
template saved thirty times while it is built carries thirty full snapshots in the `.rppj`. And the
change class measured the draft against the body the window opened with, which for a new template is
a blank: typing a height read `Breaking`. Put to the user with priced options for both.

**11.201.1 RULED: SAVE REPLACES THE NEWEST VERSION WHILE NO DEVICE IS PLACED FROM IT.** Settled by
the user, choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition.
CR-050's fork exists so a device placed from v1 keeps resolving to v1, and the only holder of a
`TemplateRef` is a `DeviceInstance`. When none references the newest version a fork protects nobody,
so `planTemplateSave` replaces that version in place, and forks from the first Save after something
is placed from it. **A seeded id's `@1` is never replaced**, placed or not: it is the shipped body
§11.157.3 calls identical in every project, so editing it forks `@2`, and later saves replace `@2`.
Undo restores the replaced snapshot as the same object, so the save stays one bounded document edit.

**11.201.2 RULED: THE CHANGE CLASS IS SHOWN ONLY WHEN DEVICES ARE PLACED, WITH THE COUNT.** Settled
by the user, choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without
addition. The class answers what an edit means for devices already placed, so it is measured
against the **newest version any device stands on** and reads `Breaking · 4 placed`, with the
version named in the tooltip. A template nothing is placed from shows no chip, however large the
edit. **The baseline was offered to the user as "your last Save"** and is refined here to the placed
version: under §11.201.1 the last Save of a template with placements is either that placed version
or an unplaced version above it, and only the placed one is what the devices resolve to.

**11.201.3 WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE.** No placed device is ever migrated by a Save; that was true
before and is unchanged, and the change class stays an advisory label (CR-050). A device placed from
the palette while the builder is open turns the next Save into a fork, which is the rule working
rather than an edge case.

**Scope.** No scope change. §11.76.3's fork clause is narrowed (§12.42); its id clause stands.

---

### 11.202 DR-203 · Size and mounting is asked once, on Identity, and what follows from it is derived

**The question.** Reported by the user on 2026-09-29 (`#951`): *"The layout of the template builder
is a bit confusing, and data has to be entered multiple times in some situations."* Three
situations were put to the user and all three confirmed; the user asked for the rest of the form to
be checked and for a mockup before any code.

| Situation | Why it happened |
|---|---|
| **A 2U device's height was typed twice and `Occupies` corrected by hand** | front RU was on Identity, rear RU and `Occupies` on Physical, and §11.156.5 only ever filled a blank side |
| **`0U mount` did not light Save** until `Occupies` also said 0U | the Save rule read the side, and nothing derived it from the mount |
| **`Half rack` left the span at 12** | width class and `nominalSpanTwelfths` were two independent inputs |

The check found three more. **The Passthrough switch was on Physical** while the pairing it enables
is on Ports, and `Pair front to rear` was hidden until it was flipped. **A hosted template could not
be saved at all** (the seeded AVR is one), and **neither could docs/06 §3.2's own rear lacing bar**
`{front: 0, rear: 1}`, because the Save rule read the front height alone. And a census of the seeded
catalog found **21 of its 25 rack-ear devices take the same RU front and rear**, while the rear
height defaulted to 0.

**11.202.1 RULED: ONE `Size and mounting` BLOCK ON IDENTITY.** Settled by the user from a mockup,
choosing the recommended option; the reasoning is the author's, accepted without addition. How it
mounts, front and rear RU, and width sit together on Identity, because the height is one of AC-049's
three required facts and a required fact on the fourth section is one a person meets only when
Save refuses. Physical keeps depth, chassis width, weight, load, clearances, thermal class and
`Container`.

**11.202.2 `Occupies` AND THE SPAN ARE DERIVED, NOT ASKED.** `derivedOccupancy` writes them on every
edit to the mount, a height or the width, inside that edit's own undo entry: the side from the
heights (both, front, rear, or none), and the span from the class (12, 6, 4, 3), typed only for
`Custom width`. `Occupies` is shown as a reading. **§11.156.5's "only ever fills a blank" is
replaced** (§12.43): that clause is exactly why a second height left the side wrong. Editing
anything else does not re-derive, so a hand-written body that disagrees stays as written until
somebody touches its occupancy. **Every seeded template already satisfies the derivation**, and a
test sweeps the shipped catalog to keep it so.

**11.202.3 THE REAR HEIGHT FOLLOWS THE FRONT UNTIL IT IS TYPED.** True while the two agree as
opened, which a new template's `0 / 0` does; false from the first keystroke in the rear box. A
front-only device costs one `0`, against a second height on the common case.

**11.202.4 RULED ON TRADE KNOWLEDGE: SIDE-MOUNTED AND IN-FURNITURE GEAR TAKE NO RACK UNITS.** Asked
rather than guessed, and answered by the user. Rack ears, a shelf and a rear rail take rack units;
a 0U mount, a hosted card, side-mounted gear, gear in furniture and gear not in a rack take none, and
show no height or width at all. Choosing one zeroes the heights, because `{frontU: 2, side: none}`
is the body DR-157 refuses to place.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-30 (`#952`): "a shelf" was the author's error, and it was never asked.** The
user's answer covered side-mounted and in-furniture gear only; `shelf` was put in the rack-units
list by the author. `MountMethod.shelf` means the device **sits on** a shelf, and the U it sits in
is the shelf's: the seeded P04 power strip carries it with the comment *"NO RAIL HOLES AND NO U OF
ITS OWN, WHICH IS THE SHELF'S JOB"*, and docs/04 §6.1 says a shelf's hosts *"consume zero additional
RU"*. So only rack ears and a rear rail take rack units, and `On a shelf` joins the mounts that ask
no height. The builder had been demanding a height of a strip lying on a shelf and refusing to save
it without one. The shelf itself is a rack-ears device and is unaffected.

**11.202.5 SAVE'S THIRD FACT, STATED ONCE.** `hasMeantOccupancy`: a rack mount means its occupancy
with a height, front **or** rear; every other mount means a zero by being chosen, the reading DR-107
§11.106.2 already made of `notInRack`. **This is not a fourth required fact**: it is AC-049's third,
with the spellings §11.106.2 left out admitted. The user chose to fix the hosted case here rather
than file it.

**11.202.6 RULED: PASSTHROUGH IS A TOGGLE ON THE PORTS TOOLBAR.** Settled by the user, choosing the
recommended option. It sits beside `Pair front to rear`, where a person is standing when they need
it, and is not offered for a field device, as before.

**11.202.7 WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE.** The model and the file: every field is where it was, and
nothing migrates (CR-117). Which sections exist (§11.106.2's `Panel` rule is unchanged).

**Scope.** No scope change: the same fields, asked in fewer places.

### 11.203 DR-204 · A device can be set on a shelf, and it is drawn there

**The question.** Reported by the user on 2026-09-30 (`#953`): *"In the rack editor, it doesn't seem
to be possible to place devices on a shelf."* AC-043 kept shelves in v1 with **auto-pack left to
right**, and docs/04 §6.1 draws the interaction. Censused before anything was offered:

| Found | Where |
|---|---|
| **No gesture creates a `ShelfPlacement`.** `buildPlaceOnShelfCommand` exists (DR-128) and its only caller is the `Add outlets` remedy | `shelf_placement.dart` |
| **A device that IS on a shelf is never drawn.** `_visibleDevices` skips every non-rail placement; the Home Theatre starter's two shelf components have been invisible since M1, counted only by the load gutter's `undrawnCount` | `scene_builder.dart` |
| **Deleting a shelf strands its hosts**, pointing at a device that no longer exists. Unreachable only while nothing can be put on a shelf | the delete path reads no `ShelfPlacement` |
| **No shelf width is known.** `chassisWidth` is non-nullable, defaults to 432 mm, is always written, and no shelf or hosted seed sets it | `template.dart` |

The last row corrects a question already put: the author first offered "an unrecorded width gets a
hollow slot" on the premise that widths came from `chassisWidth`, and the user chose it. The premise
was false, and the question was put again with that said.

**11.203.1 RULED: DRAG ONTO A SHELF, AND AN INSPECTOR PICKER, BOTH.** Settled by the user, choosing
over the recommended drag alone. A palette drag onto a shelf's tray sets the device on it at the
nearest gap; selecting a shelf offers `Put a device on this shelf…`, AC-044's shape for 0U
occupants and the keyboard's route.

**11.203.2 RULED ON TRADE KNOWLEDGE: ANY DEVICE MAY SIT ON A SHELF.** The author recommended a rule
keyed on mount method; the user explained why it is wrong: *"it depends heavily on the
amplifier/AVR. Some AVR's have rack mount kits available, but those are both A: a separate product
and B: sized to fit a specific or a small range of AVR's. Sometimes those kits aren't even
available."* So the template gets no vote. **A rack-ear device set on a shelf is allowed and the
status line says so**, which catches a mis-drop without blocking a real one (the user's choice of
the two offered).

**11.203.3 RULED: A SHELF WIDTH IS ITS OWN OPTIONAL FIELD.** Settled by the user, choosing the
recommended option. `TemplateBody.shelfWidth` (`shelfWidthNm`), a `Len?`, blank meaning unknown and
serialised as an absent key (G4, CR-114). Additive; nothing migrates. The builder shows it in `Size
and mounting` for shelf and hosted mounts and on Physical for everything else. **A known width draws
at true scale; an unknown one draws as a hollow fixed slot reading `width unknown`**, the 0U bar's
treatment of an unknown length (§11.165.2). `chassisWidth` is not reused: it is the rack panel's
connector-flow width, and its 432 mm default would draw every unmeasured host a full shelf wide as
though measured.

**11.203.4 HOSTS ARE DRAWN AND SELECTABLE.** Inside the shelf's block, packed left to right by
`ShelfPlacement.order`, below a header naming the shelf and above its tray. They join the scene's
hits and layouts as a 0U bar does (§11.165.1), which is what makes them selectable and inspectable.

**11.203.5 RULED: DRAGGING A HOST.** Along its own shelf, it reorders. Onto another shelf, it moves
there, keeping its id, ports and links (the recommended option). **Anywhere else, it is deleted**,
the user's own instruction, with the status line saying `Removed STB-1. Ctrl+Z to undo`.

**11.203.6 RULED: DELETING A SHELF ASKS.** docs/04 §6.1 item 7: `SHF-1 hosts 3 devices. [Delete all
4] [Move hosts to Staging Bin] [Cancel]`, defaulting to the bin. Recommended by the author as data
safety and chosen by the user.

**11.203.7 RULED: THE SHELF SAYS WHAT IT CARRIES.** docs/04 §6.1 item 4: the header shows the load
against `containerWeightCapacity`, over capacity marked and **never blocked**, because an integrator
may be documenting an existing over-spec install. Unknown masses are counted (G4): `≥ 12.4/22 lb (1
unknown)`.

**11.203.8 WHAT STAYS DEFERRED.** AC-043's cuts are untouched: free lateral positioning
(`lateralOffset` stays null), `Alt`-drag, the third focus level, and depth-overhang warnings. `#844`
stays parked: sub-1U heights, stacking, orientation and purpose-made shelves. **Lateral overflow**
(docs/04 §6.1 item 5) is refused on a drop only when every width involved is known, and otherwise
said rather than refused, because an unknown cannot be added up.

**11.203.9 RULED: WHERE A DRAGGED HOST CAN LAND, WITH THE BIN BUILT.** Settled by the user on
2026-09-30, building `#958`, on the recommended option. §11.203.5 said *"anywhere else, it is
deleted"*, and DR-205 then ruled that a release off the rack keeps the device's wiring in the bin;
the two are reconciled, and the rails case neither named is added:

| Release | Result |
|---|---|
| its own shelf | reorder |
| another shelf | move there |
| free rails, and the device has a rack height | move onto the rails |
| off the rack | Staging Bin, wiring kept (DR-205) |
| anywhere else on the rack | removed, `Removed STB-1. Ctrl+Z to undo` |

The rails case is the AVR one from §11.203.2: a rack-mountable device first set on a shelf and
mounted after all. The removal is announced on the drag ghost before the release, and the status
line names the cables that go with it.

**11.203.10 RULED: A LOADED SHELF IS LABELLED IN ITS HEADER, AND ITS HOSTS' CHIPS WAIT.** Settled by
the user on 2026-09-30 from a screenshot of a loaded 2U shelf (`#968`), both on the recommended
option. The shelf's own name and type lines were drawn under its hosts and showed straight through a
hollow, width-unknown one, and each host's CR-105 port chip, 11 units tall on a host about 26 tall,
sat on its label.

- **A shelf carrying devices draws its top line only**: designator, U badge, and between them its
  load (§11.203.7), in the header band reserved for it. The name and type lines are dropped while
  it hosts anything and stay in the inspector; an empty shelf draws as any device does. It prints
  the same on the PDF, which rules out the tooltip-only option: paper has no hover. An off-rack
  margin label was the third option, and was not chosen.
- **A shelf host's port chip shows on hover or selection**, not at rest. Rail devices keep the
  always-on chip. The chip is pressable exactly when it can be seen: a mouse always hovers before it
  presses, and a touch or pen press on an unselected host does not fire a chip nobody could see.

**Scope.** No scope change: AC-043's v1 half, built.

### 11.204 DR-205 · The Staging Bin ships: a strip under the canvas, four ways in and two ways out

**The question.** Building DR-204's shelf deletion (§11.203.6) needed its default, *"Move hosts to
Staging Bin"*, and **the bin does not exist**. `StagedPlacement` has round-tripped since M0 with no
command that produces one, nothing that lists one and no way back; Shrink Rack shows its bin option
disabled for exactly that reason. The author had offered the default without checking, the same
error §11.203 records about shelf widths, found within the hour. Put to the user with three options
and prices; **the user chose to build the bin**.

**IT IS NOT A SCOPE AMENDMENT, AND IT WAS FIRST DESCRIBED AS ONE.** CR-032 already rules that the
Staging Bin *is* `StagedPlacement`, and that *"It ships in v1 with the return affordance"*. Like shelves, it
was ruled, specified in docs/04 §1, §3.1 and §4.1, and never built. This ruling settles its shape.

**11.204.1 RULED: A STRIP UNDER THE RACK CANVAS, SHOWN ONLY WHILE SOMETHING IS IN IT.** docs/04
§1's own sketch, the recommended option. Each staged device is a chip; a click selects it exactly as
a click on the rack would, and the inspector shows it. The bin is a query (CR-032): nothing stores a
list.

**11.204.2 RULED: FOUR WAYS IN, EVERY ONE KEEPING THE DEVICE.** Chosen by the user, all four
offered: deleting a shelf (its default, §11.203.6), **a release off the rack** (a palette drag
creates the device there, docs/04 §3.1; an existing device dragged off keeps its id, ports and
links, the user's own addition: *"should also keep wiring"*), the **`U`** key on the selection
(docs/04 §8), and Shrink Rack's option 2 (docs/04 §4.1), no longer disabled. A device keeps its
wiring in the bin because a stage replaces its placement and touches nothing else
(`ReplacePlacementCommand`).

**11.204.3 RULED: TWO WAYS OUT.** The recommended option. A **return chip** puts a device back where
it was, *"once space exists"* (CR-032): `Return to RK-1 U21` for a rack position, or `Return to
SHF-1` for a shelf, which needed one additive field, `StagedPlacement.lastHostDeviceId`. Where a
return is not possible the chip says why. And **dragging** a chip onto a rack or a shelf places it
anywhere. CR-032 draws the chip with a `↩`, and the glyph-coverage gate refused it: the product
font has no bold `↩`, so the chip carries CR-032's words without the arrow.

**11.204.3a `U` IS THE RACK'S FIRST BARE LETTER, AND CANON ALLOWS IT.** §1.10 principle (c) says a
bare letter *"must not collide between views that share the canvas"*. The arbitration test had
asserted something stricter, that the rack binds no bare letter at all, which described the registry
rather than the ruling. The schematic binds no bare `U` (its unpin is `Ctrl+Shift+U`), so the test now
asserts the ruling, and a real collision is still caught by `arbitrate()`.

**11.204.4 A CONSEQUENCE STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED.** docs/04 §3.1 sends ANY release off the
rack to the bin, so a palette drag that wanders down the palette and is let go there now creates a
device. It is undoable and the status line says so; `Esc` is the way to cancel a drag.

**11.204.5 WHAT STAYS DEFERRED.** `RCK-014`, the advisory naming a non-empty bin, stays v1.2
(CR-021). Paste and duplicate overflow to the bin (docs/04 §8) are not built here.

**11.204.6 RULED: SHRINK RACK TAKES THE BIN AS docs/04 §4.1 WROTE IT.** Settled by the user on
2026-09-30, building `#967`, both times on the recommended option.

- **Rule 2 as written.** Option 1 is preselected when compaction fits everyone; otherwise option 2,
  *"Move the N above to the Staging Bin"*, is. So Enter gives the height that was typed, and the
  devices that do not fit wait in the bin with their wiring, one Ctrl+Z away. The dialog had
  preselected option 3 (*"Keep rack at N U"*) only because the bin did not exist. Option 3 is
  preselected now only when a casualty is **locked**, since a locked device does not move (DR-186
  §11.185.1) and staging is a move; option 2 is then shown disabled, naming the locked devices.
- **Option 1's partial form takes the spec's label**, *"2 of 3 fit, 1 goes to Staging Bin"*: it
  compacts, stages the leftovers and reaches the requested height. It stops taller, as before, only
  when a leftover is locked. On a bottom trim the compaction's downward shift is re-sized to the
  requested height (`CompactionRescue.binMoves`), because the shift already planned was sized to the
  taller fallback.
- Staging runs **first** in the one transaction, before any displacement and the height change: it
  frees the U the casualties held, and a staged device can no longer be moved.

**Scope.** No scope change: CR-032's v1 bin, built.

### 11.205 DR-206 · The schedules say what a run's lifecycle is: grouped on the Pull Sheet, a suffix on T6.11

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-30, resolving `#576`.** `ScheduleEntry.lifecycleStatus` was
populated in `schedule.dart` and read by nothing, so four of the five states printed identically to
`new` on both schedule presets: an installer handed the Pull Sheet could pull a cable that is already
in the wall, or one marked for demolition.

**11.205.1 THE PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS PART OF THE RULING.** `#576` said a
status column would be an unruled scope change to a specified sheet. docs/08 §3.4 had already
specified one: an optional `LIFECYCLE` column, 44 pt, switched on by *"any `lifecycleStatus !=
new`"*, with its width taken from `CONDUCTOR / NOTES` and then `MEDIA` and an ANSI B promotion when
the columns overflow. Nothing of §3.4 is built. What the spec had not priced is T6.11: its thirteen
columns already sum to exactly its 690 pt (DR-055), so that column promotes every retrofit job's
Termination Schedule to 11×17. The options were put with that cost on them.

**11.205.2 RULED: THE PULL SHEET GROUPS BY LIFECYCLE.** The user's choice, over docs/08 §3.4's one
list with a column and over a pull-only list with a count of the rest. Rows are split into
sections, each with its own header and row count, in this order: **TO PULL** (`new` and
`designIntent`, the two a crew pulls), **EXISTING** (verify only), **TO REMOVE** (`removed`) and
**FUTURE** (`future`). An empty section is not drawn. Nothing is hidden, and a crew working down
the page reaches everything it has to pull before anything it must not. The Pull Sheet is on
screen only (DR-155), so this costs no printed width.

**11.205.3 RULED: T6.11 CARRIES IT AS A SUFFIX ON `CABLE ID`.** The recommended option, over §3.4's
column (which promotes the sheet to ANSI B) and over a column off by default (which leaves the
state invisible on paper, the defect this ruling answers). `W042 EX` · `W043 RM` · `W044 FUT` ·
`W045 DI`; **`new` carries no suffix**, being what the sheet is for. A one-line key prints in the
sheet header whenever any suffix appears on the sheet, and not otherwise. It costs no width: the
56 pt mono `CABLE ID` column holds a designator and three letters. **This is a recorded deviation
from docs/08 §3.4** for T6.11, and docs/08 is edited to match; §3.4's `LIFECYCLE` column stays
available to sheets with the room for it.

**11.205.4 WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE.** Devices' lifecycle is unaffected: the elevation and the
equipment list already express it (`#576`'s own finding). Rough-in state and DRC issues keep their
own vocabularies and headers (CR-065). T6.11 is not yet built (`#693`); the suffix is specified
here and lands with that sheet.

**Scope.** No scope change: CR-064's lifecycle states, expressed where docs/08 left them silent.

### 11.206 DR-207 · The legend's cable-type key: the ten named types always, then what the set uses

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-30, building M6-B (`#316`), on the recommended option.** docs/08
§5.4 asks for *"one row per named cable type"* with *"all ten types the brief names ... individually
identifiable"*, and its connector table says *"every glyph used in the set"*; it never said whether a
project's legend prints the ten regardless or only what that project uses.

**11.206.1 THE PRICE THAT DECIDED IT.** Three of the four starters carry no cables at all, and the
fourth uses four families. A legend of only what is used prints an empty cable key on three of them,
and hands AC-054's physical test (all ten identifiable on a greyscale photocopy) a sheet that does
not contain the ten. A legend of every shipped family does not fit one ANSI B sheet beside the five
other blocks.

**11.206.2 RULED: THE TEN, THEN WHAT THE SET USES.** Requirement 4's ten named types are always
printed, one row each, as canon §6.6 draws them: a type with several families (HDMI's three
weights, RG6's three carried families) shows them together on its row. After them, one row for each
other family some cable in the set carries. So the key a crew learns is the same on every project,
it is the exact sheet AC-054 verifies, and a project's own extras still appear.

**Scope.** No scope change: docs/08 §5.4's block 1, made definite.

### 11.207 DR-208 · The legend explains what the set prints; its notes ship seeded

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-30, building M6-B3 and M6-B4 (`#319`, `#320`), both on the
recommended option.**

**11.207.1 RULED: THE SYMBOL TABLE AND CONVENTION KEY EXPLAIN WHAT THE SET PRINTS.** docs/08 §5.4
lists net-label stubs, home-run and local tag pills, junction dots, `— OPEN —` ends and the revision
cloud and triangle, and no sheet in the set prints any of them yet: they arrive with the
interconnect sheets (M6-D) and the sheet furniture (M6-G). T0.01 explains what a reader can find in
the PDF they hold: the device marks the set's devices carry, the plan's rack, drop and device
markers when the set has a plan, lifecycle borders, hatched passives, the RU span label and the load
gutter. Each later convention joins the key in the same change that first prints it. It is DR-207's
reasoning and B1's rule applied to the other blocks: the legend never documents a rendering the
sheets do not have.

**11.207.2 RULED: ABBREVIATIONS AND GENERAL NOTES SHIP SEEDED, AND EDITING IS ITS OWN CHAPTER.**
§5.4 calls block 6 *"editable, seeded"*. This pass prints the seeded block from one constant; a
project field for it, its codec entry and an editor are a separate Chapter, since the edit surface is
a UI decision in its own right.

**Scope.** No scope change: docs/08 §5.4's blocks 2 to 6, made definite.

### 11.208 DR-209 · The front matter gets a Sheet set dialog, and the legend's notes are its first section

**Settled by the user on 2026-09-30, building M6-B6 (`#969`), on the recommended option both
times.** DR-208 §11.207.2 left the edit surface for T0.01's abbreviations and general notes as a UI
decision of its own.

**11.208.1 THE FACT THAT PRICED IT.** Nothing in any `lib/` writes `ProjectInfo`: the title block
every sheet prints carries a project name, client, drawn-by and checked-by that the format encodes
and no surface lets anybody type. That is M6-A1's to fix, and it means the front matter will need an
editor whichever way this Chapter went. The existing Project settings dialog is a single scroll of
modelling defaults.

**11.208.2 RULED: A `Sheet set…` DIALOG ON THE FILE MENU, BESIDE `Export PDF…`.** It holds what
the set's front matter prints. This Chapter builds it with one section, the legend's abbreviations
and general notes; M6-A1's title block and cover fields join it rather than Project settings. The
option not taken was a section at the foot of Project settings, cheaper by about one dialog.

**11.208.3 RULED: ROWS WITH ADD AND REMOVE, NOT A TEXT BOX.** One row per abbreviation, with an
abbreviation field and a meaning field, and one row per note, each with a delete control, plus an
add control per list. Nothing is parsed, so there is no malformed line to explain. The option not
taken was one free-text box per list with `NTS = not to scale` lines.

**11.208.4 THE DATA, WHICH FOLLOWS FROM G4 AND CR-117 RATHER THAN BEING CHOSEN.** Two fields on
`ProjectInfo`, since docs/01 names abbreviations and general notes as front matter beside the cover
and the symbol key: `legendAbbreviations` and `legendNotes`. **Absent means seeded**: an unedited
project writes no key and prints the seed, so a file does not freeze today's seed into itself. A
list, including an empty one, is what the author wrote and prints exactly. `Restore defaults`
returns both to absent. A row left entirely blank is not saved. The signal-domain tag prefixes stay
derived from the project's registries, printed after the author's abbreviations, and are not
editable here. Every edit is one undo step on the document stack.

**Scope.** No scope change: DR-208 §11.207.2's Chapter, made definite.

### 11.209 DR-210 · The cover puts its index on the right, and the title block becomes editable

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-A1 (`#312`), on the recommended option four
times.** docs/08 §2.2 lists what `T0.00` carries and never placed it; the title block's eleven
`ProjectInfo` fields had no writer anywhere; `approvedBy` was in the format and printed on no sheet.

**11.209.1 RULED: THE DRAWING INDEX IS A FULL-HEIGHT RIGHT-HAND COLUMN.** The project block and
the scope paragraph take the left of the cover, the rack summary strip runs along its foot, and the
title and revision blocks sit bottom-right as on every sheet. **What priced it is the index**, the
one block that grows: a set at AC-050's 40-sheet warning needs about forty rows, which a
full-height column holds and a band across the lower half (the centred title page, not taken) does
not without a continuation page.

**11.209.2 RULED: THE EDITOR GROUPS THE FIELDS AS THE SET PRINTS THEM.** `File ▸ Sheet set…`
(DR-209) gains a Title block section in four groups (Project, Client and site, Integrator,
Sign-off) and a Cover section holding the scope paragraph, above the Legend section. A field
commits when it is left, as the legend rows do, and each commit is one undo step. The option not
taken was one flat list of seventeen boxes.

**11.209.3 RULED: `approvedBy` PRINTS ON THE COVER.** The cover's sign-off line reads drawn,
checked and approved. Approval is a statement about the whole set, and the per-sheet title block
is a fixed 115 pt that would lose a row. The option not taken was to leave the field out of the
editor until a sheet printed it.

**11.209.4 RULED: A CLEARED PROJECT NAME IS REFUSED, WITH A REASON.** The field keeps its last
value and says that a project needs a name because it heads every sheet. It is the one required
`ProjectInfo` field, and the Recent Files label. The option not taken was a silent fallback to
`Untitled Project`, which lets a client PDF go out under that title with nobody choosing it.

**11.209.5 THE DATA, WHICH FOLLOWS FROM G4 RATHER THAN BEING CHOSEN.** One new field,
`ProjectInfo.scopeNarrative`, absent when nobody has written one; an absent scope prints no SCOPE
heading, under docs/08 §5.2's *"empty optional lines collapse"*. Every optional field cleared to
blank is stored absent rather than as an empty string, so a cleared field and a never-set one are
the same fact on the wire.

**Scope.** No scope change: docs/08 §2.2's row 1, made definite.

### 11.210 DR-211 · The cover's rack strip, and passives leave the equipment list

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-A2 (`#313`).** docs/08 §2.2 gives the strip's
columns as designator, `heightU`, device count, populated RU, total mass and total draw, each with
an unknown count, and leaves open which draw, which face, which devices and what happens when racks
outnumber the space. Two answers reached further than the strip and are ruled here as well.

**11.210.1 RULED: POWER IS VA AND BTU/HR.** Apparent power for circuit sizing (CR-056) and heat
from typical watts (AC-039), the two figures each elevation's load gutter already prints, so the
cover agrees with T2.xx to the digit. The option not taken was VA alone.

**11.210.2 RULED: POPULATED RU IS SHOWN PER FACE**, `F 31 · R 19`, as `computeRackRollups` counts
it (docs/04 §5). The option not taken was the front face alone.

**11.210.3 RULED, IN THE USER'S WORDS: "Leave out passives from an equipment list, but note them on
the BOM."** The cover's device count is active equipment. Passive is **the catalog's whole `Passive
& Mechanical` category** (blanks, vent panels, shelves, lacing bars, cable management), chosen over
excluding shelves and over adding patch panels. **The ruling reaches T6.30**, the user's choice over
applying it to the cover alone: the equipment table drops passive rows and the materials section,
which AC-055 makes the set's BOM, lists them by type. That is M6-F6 (`#970`), so the cover's count
and T6.30's rows agree again.

**11.210.4 RULED: A STRIP TOO LONG IS CAPPED AND SAYS SO.** The racks that fit print in rack order,
then one row naming how many more and which elevations hold them, and the export carries a notice.
The option not taken was shrinking the text, which falls under the 6 pt floor past about 25 racks.

**11.210.5 RULED: THE SEED CATALOG STATES A PASSIVE'S POWER AS ZERO.** Measured on the four
starters before the strip was built: Whole House's power read `≥ 2490 VA (10 unknown)`, and five of
the ten were vent panels, a blank and a shelf whose `PowerProfile` the catalog left empty. A blank
panel drawing nothing is a measured zero, which G4 permits. The seed's passive entries state 0 W
and 0 VA and the starters regenerate; a project already saved keeps its own template snapshots until
they are refreshed. The options not taken were a rollup rule skipping passives, which infers a zero
from a category, and leaving the counts as they were.

**Scope.** No v1 scope change: docs/08 §2.2's rows 1 and 7, made definite. M6-F6 is a new Chapter
inside M6-F's existing T6.30 scope.

### 11.211 DR-212 · The drawing index: both numbers, flat, ranges collapsed, sub-columns on overflow

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-A3 (`#314`), on the recommended option four
times.** docs/08 §2.2 rules only that the index is generated after the sheet list resolves. The
column DR-210 reserved holds about forty rows; Whole House's set is six sheets today and about
nineteen when M6 is complete, and a ten-rack job reaches about thirty-seven, so overflow was priced
as a real case.

**11.211.1 RULED: EACH ROW CARRIES BOTH NUMBERS**, the set position and the NCS id, `4  T2.01`,
because every title block prints both (`SHEET 4 OF 6` and `SHEET NO. T2.01`) and a reader may hold
either. The option not taken followed the Sheet numbering setting.

**11.211.2 RULED: FLAT, IN SET ORDER.** The NCS ids group the rows by series already, and a band
header is a row the column cannot spend on a sheet. The option not taken banded by series.

**11.211.3 RULED: A MULTI-PAGE SCHEDULE IS ONE ROW**, `6–8  T6.30–T6.32  EQUIPMENT LIST AND
MATERIALS (3 pages)`: consecutive pages of one schedule collapse, and nothing else does. The option
not taken listed every page.

**11.211.4 RULED: OVERFLOW FLOWS INTO SUB-COLUMNS**, two then three, with titles fitted to the
narrower width. A set that three cannot hold still exports, with a notice naming the sheets the
index omits. The options not taken were shrinking the type below the 6 pt floor and a continuation
index sheet, which would make the set's sheet count depend on the index's own size.

**Scope.** No scope change: docs/08 §2.2's row 1, made definite.

### 11.212 DR-213 · T6.30's subtotals stay whole-rack, and the materials are one list

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-F6 (`#970`), on the recommended option both
times.** DR-211 §11.210.3 moved passives off T6.30's equipment rows and into its materials section.
Two consequences were left open, and building the move found both.

**11.212.1 RULED: A RACK'S SUBTOTAL IS THE WHOLE RACK, AND SAYS SO.** Weight and VA still count the
passives, so the subtotal equals the cover's rack strip and the elevation's load gutter, which a
test has held equal to `computeRackRollups` since M1. The line names what it includes:
`26 DEVICES + 5 PASSIVES (SEE MATERIALS)`. The rows above it then sum to less than it, and the line
is why. The option not taken summed the rows alone, giving one rack two weights in one set.

**11.212.2 RULED: THE MATERIALS ARE ONE LIST AT THE END.** A `MATERIALS` section after the last
rack band: one row per item and lifecycle status, the total quantity, the manufacturer and model,
and a `WHERE` column with the split by rack (`RK-1 × 3, RK-2 × 1`). M6-F's cable and hardware
rollups join this section. The option not taken put a passives block under each rack.

**11.212.3 THE EXIT CRITERION'S BIJECTION, RESTATED RATHER THAN DROPPED.** T6.30 has carried "every
device in exactly one row" since M1. It becomes: every device is exactly one equipment row or exactly
one unit of one materials row, so nothing in the document is missing from the sheet or counted
twice, and the starter test asserts that form.

**Scope.** No scope change: DR-211 §11.210.3, made definite.

### 11.213 DR-214 · T0.02 leads with the project-wide exceptions, then errors first, and keeps every signed reason

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-C (`#322`), on the recommended option four times.**
docs/08 §2.2 rules what `T0.02` carries (every open finding with rule, severity and locus; every
acknowledgement with reason, author and date; emitted even when empty) and not its order. Measured
first on the starters: Whole House opens with 39 findings, 15 of them errors, and messages run to
about 140 characters; the other three carry two to five warnings; no starter holds an
acknowledgement or a rule override.

**11.213.1 RULED: PROJECT-WIDE EXCEPTIONS COME FIRST**, in their own section: every
`ProjectSettings.ruleOverrides` entry (the rule, its catalogue severity and what it is in this
project) and every project-wide `"*"` mute, each with its mandatory reason, author and date. A
reviewer meets a silenced rule before reading a list it no longer contributes to. The option not
taken put them last.

**11.213.2 RULED: OPEN FINDINGS ARE BANDED BY SEVERITY, ERRORS FIRST**, each row carrying severity,
rule, locus and message; the locus is its own column so a reader in a rack room can find the thing
(`#323`). Within a band the order is `evaluateDocument`'s, which `groupFindings` already refuses to
re-sort. The option not taken banded by location.

**11.213.3 RULED: ACKNOWLEDGED FINDINGS ARE THEIR OWN SECTION**, after the open ones, adding reason,
author and date. The option not taken marked them inline.

**11.213.4 RULED: AN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT THAT OUTLIVED ITS FINDING STILL PRINTS**, at the end of the
acknowledged section, marked `NO LONGER OCCURS`: docs/08 says *every* `AckedFinding`, and a signed
reason that silently left the deliverable cannot be told from one deleted to hide it. The option not
taken printed live acknowledgements only.

**11.213.5 DECIDED WITHOUT A QUESTION, AND SAID SO.** A set too long for one sheet continues on
`T0.03`, `T0.04` and on, as `T6.30` continues to `T6.31`; the set resolves the page count before
anything renders, as the equipment list's does. An empty section says so in words, and an empty
sheet says that the checks ran and when (`#325`): *"No open exceptions"* is a claim, and the sheet
states the basis for it. Every join goes through `acknowledgementFor` and the findings
`evaluateDocument` returns, as DR-111 §11.110.3 binds.

**Scope.** No scope change: docs/08 §2.2's row 3, made definite.

### 11.214 DR-215 · Zones on drawing sheets only, from the lower right; revision entries and clouds park on project history

### 11.215 DR-216 · Export for construction is its own command, the stamp is on every sheet, and the logo sits top-right

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-G5 (`#346`) and M6-G6 (`#590`), on the recommended
option three times.** CR-022 settles the stamp's logic, `ExportSpec.issuedForConstruction`, with
open errors suppressing the stamp and never the bytes; DR-030 settles the logo's nature (optional,
full opacity, fit-inside, a member like an underlay's, import limits). Neither placed anything.

**11.215.1 RULED: `File ▸ Export for construction…` BESIDE `Export PDF…`.** It requests the stamp
for one export and remembers nothing. With zero open errors every sheet is stamped; otherwise the
set still exports, unstamped, and the status line says why and points at `T0.02`. M6-I's export
dialog takes this over as an option when it exists. The options not taken were a saved project
setting, which would stamp later exports by default, and waiting for M6-I, which would leave G5
undemonstrable.

**11.215.2 RULED: THE STAMP IS ON EVERY SHEET, DIRECTLY ABOVE THE REVISION BLOCK**, the same width,
reading `ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION` and the issue date, because sheets travel separately on a site and a
loose sheet must say what it is. The option not taken was the cover only. **Decided without a
question and recorded as such:** an ANSI A sheet has no revision block (§5.2's compact strip), so
there the stamp is a full-width band directly above the strip. A stamped export lays out every sheet
with the stamp's height reserved, in the dry run, so pagination and `SHEET i OF n` see it.

**11.215.3 RULED: THE LOGO SITS AT THE TOP RIGHT OF THE TITLE BLOCK'S IDENTITY BAND**, in a box
about 100 by 45 pt, fitted inside with its aspect kept, the project, client and address lines
keeping their left alignment in what remains. The firm's text line stays (DR-030 §11.29.1). It is
set in `File ▸ Sheet set…`'s Title block section, beside the fields it sits with. The option not taken
was a box outside the title block, which takes drawing space on every sheet.

**11.215.4 THE REVISION BLOCK'S `issued` FLAG PARKS WITH G3.** CR-022 has open errors withhold the
stamp and the revision block's issued flag; `RevisionEntry` carries no such flag and its writer is
parked on HIST/3 (`#658`) by DR-215 §11.214.3. The flag joins it there. The stamp alone is G5.

**Scope.** No scope change: CR-022 and DR-030, made definite.

### 11.216 DR-217 · The logo imports from PNG, JPEG, PDF or SVG, is stored as a raster, and is previewed where it is set

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-01, building M6-G6 (`#590`).** DR-030 §11.29.5 owes *"a format
allowlist"* and names none; DR-216 §11.215.3 places the logo and its control. Two questions were put.

**11.216.1 RULED: PNG, JPEG, PDF AND SVG**, the user's choice over the recommended PNG, JPEG and PDF,
with *"might as well if we're doing it."* The SVG price offered was two to three days, on the premise
that a decoder and a rasteriser had to be added. **That premise was wrong and is corrected here**:
the `pdf` package, already a dependency, draws SVG as PDF vectors, and the vendored pdfium (DR-153)
already rasterises PDF. An SVG therefore becomes a one-page PDF and takes the PDF route, with no new
dependency.

**11.216.2 STORED AS A RASTER, PNG OR JPEG, so `ProjectLogo` mirrors `PlanUnderlay`** exactly as
§11.29.5 asks and `rackpal_core` still needs no decoder. **Decided without a question and recorded as
such:**
- **A PNG or JPEG is stored verbatim** (§11.29.5, *"Stored bytes go in verbatim"*), flattened over
  white only when it carries alpha, which is the underlay's rule for docs/08 row 9's reason.
- **A PDF or SVG is rendered once, at import**, to a PNG that fits inside the logo box at 600 dpi:
  834 by 375 px, aspect kept. The box is fixed, so the raster can be no sharper on paper than that.
  A PDF gives its first page; a logo has no page picker. The source file is not kept: a different
  box is a re-import, not a re-render.
- **Caps**: the image cap every import carries (M4-M4), and 4 MB for SVG text, which is parsed
  before anything bounds it. The SVG parser follows only embedded `data:` images and expands no DTD
  entity; nothing in it touches a file or the network.

**11.216.3 RULED: A THUMBNAIL WITH REPLACE AND REMOVE.** The Title block section shows the logo at
the box's aspect, as it will print, with its pixel size, `Replace logo…` and `Remove logo`; with none
set, `Choose logo…`. The option not taken was the file name alone, which leaves the first sight of a
badly flattened logo to a printed sheet. **The preview matters more for SVG than anywhere**: the
`pdf` package's SVG support is partial (no filters, no CSS stylesheets), and the thumbnail is where
a logo it cannot draw is seen before it is issued.

**11.216.4 RULED: A CELL SPANNING THE TITLE BLOCK'S UPPER BAND, refining DR-216 §11.215.3 on a
measurement.** §11.215.3 placed the logo at the top right of the identity band, about 100 by 45 pt.
**That band is 26 to 49 pt tall**, by how many lines a sheet prints, so the box does not fit in it on
every sheet. Two placements were put. The one taken is a ruled cell at the right of the whole upper
band (the identity and sheet-title lines, 65 pt), with the logo fitted into 100 by 45 pt and centred
in it, **the same size on every sheet**. Every upper line then has 280 pt rather than 388; the widest
line on any starter is 222 pt (Whole House's project line). With no logo the block is unchanged. The
option not taken was the identity lines alone, which prints the logo at a different size on
different sheets of one set.

**11.216.5 RULED: THE COMPACT STRIP PRINTS NO LOGO.** ANSI A sheets (today `T6.30`) use §5.2's 43 pt
strip, which is already full: Whole House truncates its second row without a logo. The firm's text
line stays, and it is the carrier DR-030 §11.29.1 kept because it survives a photocopy. The options
not taken were growing the strip, about one schedule row per page, and squeezing a cell into it,
which truncates that text line further.

**11.216.6 THE PDF EMBEDS A LOGO NO LARGER THAN ITS BOX AT 600 DPI.** **Decided without a question
and recorded as such**, on a measurement made while building it. The PDF backend has no path that
embeds a PNG or JPEG as it is (docs/08's raster note): it decodes to raw RGB and deflates. Measured on
Small Office, a flat 3000 px logo added 23 KB to the export and a photographic 3000 px JPEG added
**14.8 MB**. The member stays verbatim (§11.216.2); the export's copy of a full-value image is fitted
inside 834 by 375 px, averaged, never enlarged, as the floorplan's screening already lives in the
backend rather than the member. Remeasured after the change: 5 KB and 742 KB, the second pure noise,
which no compressor shrinks. A floorplan is never resized: it prints at sheet size.

**Scope.** No scope change: DR-030 §11.29.5's allowlist, made definite.
