### 11.218 DR-219 · T6.30's rollups are sections with their own headers; the outlet map lists assignments; an acknowledged support still prints

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-02, on the recommended option three times, building M6-F (`#335`).**
docs/08 §2.2 and AC-024, AC-026 and AC-028 put four rollups on `T6.30` beside the equipment table:
cable footage by media with a waste factor, the hardware implied by rules, jumpers and power cords by
media, length and colour, and the PDU outlet map. None says how they sit on a sheet whose table has
one thirteen-column header.

**11.218.1 RULED: EACH ROLLUP IS ITS OWN SECTION WITH ITS OWN HEADER ROW**, after MATERIALS, re-printed
with `(cont.)` when a page breaks inside it, so every header reads true over its column. The option
not taken was reusing the equipment grid as MATERIALS does, which prints `MANUFACTURER` over a media
name.

**11.218.2 RULED: THE OUTLET MAP LISTS ASSIGNMENTS**, one row per outlet with a cord drawn to it
(outlet, device, inlet), then one line per outlet provider giving how many of its outlets are free and
how many devices are counted as plugged in without a drawn cord (DR-171 §11.170.4). Measured on the
starters, which draw no cords: 16 to 74 outlets across UPSes, sequencers and PDUs, about 38 rows to
an A page. The option not taken was every outlet, which on Whole House is about two pages of dashes.

**11.218.3 RULED: AN ACKNOWLEDGED `RCK-013` STILL PRINTS ITS REAR SUPPORT**, with the
acknowledgement's reason in NOTES. The weight is physical, and an acknowledgement usually records
that support is specified. The option not taken, open findings only, would drop a kit somebody needed
because they quietened the drawer.

**11.218.4 RULED, AS A §8.3 AMENDMENT: CR-030's EAR-KIT ADVISORY IS BUILT, AS `RCK-014`.** CR-030 rules
that a half-rack device placed alone *"files an advisory naming the ear kit"*; no rule did. The ear kit
is one of the two pieces of hardware docs/08 names as implied by rules, so the materials line and the
drawer's advisory come from the same predicate: a rail-mounted device narrower than the rack with
nothing else in any of its U on its face. **The v1 catalogue moves to 8 tier-1 + 6 tier-2 + 16
tier-3**, `RCK-014` an advisory in tier 3, with its AC-051 pair.

**THIS PARAGRAPH FIRST READ "DECIDED WITHOUT A QUESTION", AND THAT WAS WRONG.** It was written before
the catalogue gate was read. `rule_catalogue_test.dart` pins the count as v1's rule scope and says a
rule arriving without a §8.3 amendment fails there, which is roadmap M5's *"just one more obvious
rule"*. CR-030 already ruled the behaviour into v1, so this builds a promise rather than widening the
product, but the gate it moves is the user's, and the question was put. The options not taken were
deriving ear kits from placement with no rule, which leaves the drawer and the sheet two answers to
one question, and listing rear supports only.

**Scope.** **§8.3 amendment for §11.218.4 only**: the v1 rule catalogue gains `RCK-014`, by CR-030's
own wording. §11.218.1 to §11.218.3 change no scope: docs/08 §2.2's `T6.30` and AC-026, made
definite.

### 11.219 DR-220 · T6.20 lists a home run open at either end, in room bands, and says which end

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-02, building M6-E1 (`#332`).** `T6.20` Unused Home Runs has been a
v1 sheet since canon §4.3, `AUTO` iff at least one exists, and the corpus defined it three ways:
§4.3's glossary says *"home-run `Link`s with an unbound rack end"*, docs/07 and docs/08 say *"whose
rack end is an `OpenEndpoint`"*, and docs/01 says *"every home run terminated at the DD with no device
on it"*, which is a different sheet. Nothing said how it is laid out.

**MEASURED FIRST**, on the four starters at `4879aaa5`: Apartment, Home Theatre and Small Office carry
no `Link` at all. Whole House carries 27, every one a home run, 12 with an `OpenEndpoint` rack end and
15 landed on a panel port, and **no patch cord anywhere**.

**11.219.1 RULED: A HOME RUN IS LISTED WHEN EITHER END IS OPEN.** A home run is a `Link` carrying a
`StructureOrigin`. It is listed when its rack end or its field end is an `OpenEndpoint`. The rack end
is the end in a rack when exactly one end is, and otherwise the conductor's `to`, which is where
`AddHomeRunCommand` writes it and where `plan_length.dart` reads it. The options not taken were the
rack end only (recommended; §4.3's wording) and docs/01's *"terminated with no device on it"*, which
on Whole House lists all 27 runs: a job that draws no patch cords, which is most of them, would print
every run it has as unused. The user gave no reason; what the choice adds over the recommended one is
a run dressed and landed at the rack and left as a coil at the room.

**11.219.2 RULED: ANSI A LANDSCAPE, ROOM BANDS, TEN COLUMNS.** The paper is T6.30's and the
Termination Schedule's (docs/08 §6.1, *"Equipment List, details"*). Rows sit in one band per room,
titled with the room and its count, rooms in name order and `NO ROOM RECORDED` last. The columns are
`CABLE ID` (with DR-206's lifecycle suffix), `OPEN`, `RACK LBL`, `FIELD LBL`, `OUTLET`, `FIELD END`,
`MEDIA`, `LEN`, `PATHWAY` and `ROUGH-IN`. Every cell the Schedule view also prints is printed by
`ScheduleEntry.cell`, so the sheet and the screen cannot disagree. Not taken: ANSI A portrait in seven
columns, the Pull Sheet's paper, which drops `FIELD END` and `PATHWAY`; and a column printing the open
end's own note, which on every run today is one of two stock sentences.

**11.219.3 RULED: WHICH END IS OPEN IS ITS OWN COLUMN**, `OPEN`, reading `RACK`, `ROOM` or `BOTH`.
§11.219.1 makes a row open at either end, and the ten columns otherwise state it nowhere; a reader
should not have to infer a fact the sheet holds. Not taken: one section per open end, which repeats a
room up to three times; and `— OPEN —` in `FIELD END`, docs/08 §3.3's convention, which states *rack
open* only by absence.

**11.219.4 RULED: WITHIN A ROOM, ROWS PRINT IN CABLE ID ORDER**, natural (`W4` before `W10`). The `W`
number is on the label at both ends, so it is found from whichever end the reader is standing at. Not
taken: field-label order, the order of the plates.

**11.219.5 DECIDED WITHOUT A QUESTION: POSITION AND NUMBERING**, because each follows from a mechanism
already ruled. `T6.20` sits at docs/08 §2.2's `n+3`: after the elevations (and the interconnect, pull
and termination sheets when they land) and before `T6.30`. Its pages are `T6.20` to `T6.29`, and an
eleventh page onward continues from `T6.60`, ahead of the equipment list's own overflow, which then
follows it: `equipmentListNcsId`'s reasoning, that `T6.4x` and `T6.5x` are reserved, applies to any
schedule. A page that opens inside a room re-prints the column heads and the band `(cont.)`, and a
band keeps with its first row (DR-219 §11.218.1, `#337`).

**What this does not rule.** A rack end recorded as a place (`PlaceEndpoint`) is not open and is not
listed; no command writes one today, since `drop_build.dart` leaves the rack end null and null becomes
an `OpenEndpoint`. A run that is not a home run (no `StructureOrigin`) with an open end is a schedule
row and not this sheet's.

**Scope.** No scope moves between releases. `T6.20` was v1 already; this rules its contents and
layout, and amends §4.3's glossary row (§12.44).

### 11.220 DR-221 · T5.01 prints pinout tables; a receiver jack is ring +12 V; a port records its terminal order

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-02, building M6-E2 (`#333`, `#974` to `#976`).** docs/08 §2.2 puts
`T5.01` Plate, Panel & Pinout Details last in the set, `AUTO` *"iff any non-standard pinout exists:
null-modem RS-232, IR pinout variant, Euroblock role map, or a cable whose wiring standard differs
from the project's"*. None of the four had been defined against the model.

**MEASURED FIRST**, at `4879aaa5`. **IR**: 21 seeded ports carry a `pinoutVariant`, 18
`mono-tip-sleeve` and 3 `xantech-stereo`; every starter places at least one, and **two place a
`xantech-stereo`: Home Theatre six jacks and Whole House five** (IRB-1, the connecting block). **This
line first said only Home Theatre**, and the user was told so when the option was put: the census
script crashed on Whole House before printing, and its silence was read as none. The derivation's
first test run found it (M6-E2b, `#975`). **Wiring standard**: `wiringStandardExceptions` exists, written
for this sheet. **Null-modem**: `Link.crossover` is modelled and read, and **nothing in the UI writes
it**. **Euroblock role map**: four words in docs/08's row and **nothing in the model at all**; no field
says which conductor lands on which terminal.

**11.220.1 RULED: PINOUT TABLES ONLY.** One section per kind, each with its own header row (DR-219
§11.218.1's mechanism): receiver jacks, wiring-standard exceptions with a `T568A`/`T568B` colour key,
null-modem cables, and terminal orders against their standard. Not taken: also drawing each outlet's
strap layout to scale, which DR-007, DR-038 and DR-041 made possible; it is a drawing rather than a
table, priced at three to five days, and §11.7.7 itself says it would make the sheet `ON` far more
often.

**11.220.2 RULED: MONO TIP-SLEEVE IS THE IR STANDARD.** An IR-family port (`kIrFamilies`) on a placed
device whose `pinoutVariant` is set and is not `mono-tip-sleeve` turns the sheet on: on Home Theatre
and Whole House as shipped. Not taken: any
variant on a port a cable lands on (no starter fires), and any placed IR port (every starter fires,
and `AUTO` stops meaning much). **Decided without a question**: a `pinoutVariant` on a port outside
the IR families does not trigger, because the question put was about IR and no other variant has a
declared standard.

**11.220.3 RULED, CORRECTING THE CORPUS: A RECEIVER JACK IS TIP IR, RING +12 V, SLEEVE GND.** The
registry, canon, docs/01, `docs/catalog/seed-devices.md` (four times) and three code comments said
ring GND, sleeve +12 V. The user settled it when the two readings were put side by side. **The mechanism §11.125.1 rests on survives
unchanged**: a two-conductor plug bridges ring to sleeve, which shorts the supply whichever of the
two carries it. What changes is the pin map `T5.01` prints, which is the one place the order is read
by a person holding a screwdriver. Corrected in place by §12.45.

**11.220.4 RULED: NULL-MODEM STAYS IN THE TRIGGER, AND ITS WRITER IS FILED.** A cable with
`crossover == nullModem` turns the sheet on whenever a file carries one; the missing control is
`#973`. Not taken: dropping the clause from v1 until something can set it.

**11.220.5 RULED: THE EUROBLOCK ROLE MAP IS MODELLED NOW**, over the recommended parking to v1.1.
`PortDef` gains an ordered list of terminal roles, pin 1 to n, **absent when nobody has said** (G4,
CR-114). The Device Builder enters it as a typed `TERMINALS` column, roles separated by spaces, with
fill-down and paste. Not taken: a per-pin picker, which cannot be mistyped and cannot be pasted
either. **THIS SENTENCE FIRST PROMISED A COUNT CHECK ON THE CELL, against "the connector's pins", and
no such number exists**: `ConnectorTypeDef` carries no pin count, and none of the 492 terminal-block
ports in the starters' templates sets `conductorCount`. The premise was in the option text Claude
wrote, not in the user's answer. Put to the user with prices, they ruled **no count check**: on the
two families with a standard, a wrong count already differs from it and prints on `T5.01`. Not
taken: a pin count on the four terminal-block connectors (half a day, every starter's bytes
regenerated, older documents never checked), and checking `conductorCount` (which checks nothing
until somebody fills it in). **Standards are
declared for two families only: `ctl.cresnet` on 4 pins, `24 Y Z G`, and `ctl.rs232` on 3 pins, `TX
RX G`.** A port whose recorded order differs turns the sheet on; a family with no declared standard
never does. Not taken: standards for balanced line audio (`+ - G`) and speakers (`+ -`) as well,
which the user judged too variable by manufacturer to call a deviation non-standard. Also not taken:
parking the clause to v1.1, or to a later v1 milestone. **The starters never fire it**, since no
seeded port records an order, and that is correct rather than a gap.

**11.220.6 DECIDED WITHOUT A QUESTION: POSITION AND NUMBERING.** `T5.01` is last in the set, docs/08
§2.2's `n+5`, on ANSI A landscape (§6.1's *"details"*). Pages run `T5.01`, `T5.02` and on; type 5 has
no other sheet and no reserved id.

**Scope.** No scope moves between releases: each clause was v1 already, in docs/08 §2.2's row, and
§11.220.5 builds one rather than deferring it. The format gains one optional key on `PortDef`, absent
by default, so no existing file's bytes move (CR-117).

### 11.221 DR-222 · The schedules number in blocks of five, and print their fixed columns

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-02, opening M6-K (`#977`).** The Pull Sheet and the Termination
Schedule are v1 sheets (docs/08 §2.2 rows `n+1` and `n+2`, both `ON`) that M6's decomposition never
filed: `#693` owed the Termination Schedule's columns and `#574` pointed at the Pull Sheet, and nothing
built either page. The rows exist; M3 built `buildScheduleView` and both presets' column tables.

**11.221.1 RULED: BLOCKS OF FIVE.** The Pull Sheet is `T6.10` to `T6.14`; **the Termination Schedule
moves from `T6.11` to `T6.15`**, and runs `T6.15` to `T6.19`. A page past either block takes the next
id from the shared overflow pool at `T6.60`, which every schedule draws from in set order (Pull Sheet,
Termination Schedule, `T6.20`, `T6.30`), so no id lands on two sheets (DR-220 §11.219.5, generalised).
**THE COLLISION THIS FIXES WAS IN THE CORPUS FROM THE START**: at 42 rows a page, any job over 42 drops
needs a second Pull Sheet page, and `T6.11` was already the Termination Schedule's. Not taken: keeping
`T6.11` and sending every second page to the pool, which prints a 60-drop job's Pull Sheet as `T6.10`,
`T6.60`; and giving the Pull Sheet the whole decade with the Termination Schedule at `T6.70`.

**11.221.2 RULED: FIXED COLUMNS ONLY.** The Pull Sheet prints docs/08 §3.2's ten columns and the
Termination Schedule §3.3's thirteen, with DR-055's `FIELD TERM` and `RACK TERM` (`#693`). §3.4's
optional columns arrive with M6-I's export dialog, where a person chooses them. Not taken: turning each
on when its *"Enabled by"* condition holds, which would let the overflow rule promote sheets to ANSI B
on its own and leave M6-I reconciling automatic choices with manual ones.

**11.221.3 DECIDED WITHOUT A QUESTION**, each following a ruling already made: both sheets are `ON`, so
a project with no cable prints a page that says so (T6.30's precedent); jumpers and power cords are
excluded and counted in words (AC-026), since they roll up on `T6.30`; the Pull Sheet groups by
lifecycle and then room (DR-206 §11.205.2), the Termination Schedule by rack with the lifecycle suffix
on `CABLE ID` (§11.205.3); a band repeats `(cont.)` and keeps with its first row (docs/08 §3.6, DR-219
§11.218.1).

**Scope.** No scope moves between releases. §11.221.1 renumbers a v1 sheet, an amendment recorded in
§12.46.

### 11.222 DR-223 · The compact strip drops its repeats, and PATHWAY asks for designators

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-03, building M6-L (`#982`).** M6-K's render of Whole House showed two
truncations, and both were measured with the real font before they were offered.

**MEASURED FIRST.** The compact strip on the portrait Pull Sheet is 510 pt. Row 3, the field run, needs
536 to 561 pt on the four starters, so it overflows on **every** one, and row 2 needs 520 on Whole House.
Both rows carried a repeat: row 2 ended `· PULL SHEET`, the title row 1 prints, and row 3 ended
`SHEET 7/14`, the number row 2 prints. Without them row 2 needs 368 to 474 and row 3 493 to 519, so only
Whole House's row 3 is still over, by 9 pt. **PATHWAY**: docs/08 §3.2 gives it 36 pt for a
`Pathway.designator`, falling back to the name (DR-026 §11.25.1). No starter pathway has a designator,
and their names need 49 to 86 pt, about 62 across two lines.

**11.222.1 RULED: THE COMPACT STRIP DROPS ITS TWO REPEATS, AND A ROW STILL TOO WIDE STEPS DOWN TO 7 PT.**
Row 2's right side is the sheet's number alone and row 3's field run no longer ends with `SHEET`, on the
compact strip only; the full block keeps its grid. A row whose text still does not fit prints at 7 pt
rather than 7.5. Every starter then fits, portrait and landscape, and nothing is lost that the strip
does not print elsewhere. Not taken: a fourth row on portrait (about one Pull Sheet row a page, with
the repeats kept); dropping the repeats without shrinking (Whole House's file name still cut); leaving
it.

**11.222.2 RULED: PATHWAY KEEPS ITS WIDTH, AND A MISSING DESIGNATOR IS NAMED.** When a schedule prints a
pathway with no designator, the export says so in a notice that names the route to fix it (the `DESIGNATOR`
column of the Structured Wiring tab's Pathways view; first written with `▸`, which the corpus keeps
for a menu path, and refused as such by the copy test), and the four starters get designators so they show the
column as designed. Not taken: widening PATHWAY to 60 pt from FROM and TO, which already truncate; the
notice alone, with the starters still showing the fallback; leaving it.

**Scope.** No scope moves. §11.222.1 refines docs/08 §5.2's strip; §11.222.2 adds a notice and changes
starter data.

### 11.223 DR-224 · An export's notices are read by clicking their count

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-03, opening M6-M (`#983`).** Found while writing M6-L's test route:
**no export notice's text reaches the user anywhere.** `describeExportSuccess` prints `Exported 14
sheets · 214 KB · 6 notices` and drops the sentences, and the diagnostic log records the count alone.
So every notice the exporter writes (a sheet below the preferred text size, an index that omitted
sheets, an elevation not to scale, overflow numbering, DR-223's pathways with no designator) has only
ever reached a person as a number. CR-023 and G3 made them notices so they would never gate the bytes;
nothing made them readable.

**11.223.1 RULED: THE COUNT IS A LINK, AND IT OPENS A LIST.** When the status line ends with an
export's notice count, the count is clickable and keyboard-reachable, and opens an `Export notices`
dialog listing every notice from that export, grouped by the sheet id it names, with Copy and Close.
The notices belong to the status message they were counted in: a later message replaces both. Not
taken: printing them on `T0.02`, where a client deliverable would carry the export's housekeeping;
both; and filing the gap unbuilt.

**Scope.** No scope moves. It makes CR-023's notices readable.

### 11.224 DR-225 · The interconnect sheets: one per domain, its own devices, and a fallback measured at 6 pt

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-03, opening M6-D (`#326`), on the recommended option four times.**
CR-073 and DR-001 §11.1.2 fix what the interconnect sheets are: one per domain partition of the one
schematic `Sheet`, rendered `drawn`. Four things they left open were found reading the Story against
the tree, and each would have been decided by whoever typed the code.

**11.224.1 THE FACTS THAT PRICED IT.** The Story and docs/08 §2.2 name six sheets, *"Video, Audio,
Network, Control, Power, Structure"*, and the registry seeds **eight** domains. `schematic_filter.dart`
reads §11.1.1's trigger as **exactly one** `SignalDomainId`, so a sheet holding two domains is by
DR-001's own table a `netLabels` sheet. The on-screen solo draws every symbol, which on paper is the
all-devices sheet CR-074 deleted. And *"a per-sheet Link count above which it would be illegible"*
carries no number anywhere in the corpus, while `wire_trace.dart` records that it has no link-count
branch on purpose.

**11.224.2 RULED: ONE SHEET PER `SignalDomainId`, AT MOST EIGHT, `T6.01` ON.** In the filter bar's
figure order, docs/05 §11.2: Digital Video, Analog Video and RF, Analog Audio, Digital Audio, Network,
Control, Power, Structure. A domain none of whose links lands on a drawn pin produces no sheet; a link
with no device at either end is `T6.20`'s and has nothing on a schematic to attach to. Eight fit under
`T6.10` with `T6.09` spare. The order is an exporter constant over the eight seeded ids, any other id
following in ascending order; it is not a field on `SignalDomainDef`, and the filter bar's own order is
not changed by it. The option not taken was six grouped sheets, which needed a further ruling that
export overrides §11.1.1's "exactly one".

**11.224.3 RULED: A SHEET DRAWS ITS OWN DEVICES, AND A LOCKED DEVICE KEEPS ITS PLACE.** Only devices
carrying a link of that domain are drawn. A device the user locked (`SheetItem.pinned`, CR-068) stays
at its `SheetItem.position`; the rest are laid out around it by phases 0 to 3, on the subset. So the
paper keeps the arrangement the user made where they made one. Not taken: the same subset laid out
fresh, which can move a deliberately placed device; and every device at its screen position, which is
CR-074's sheet.

**11.224.4 RULED: THE FALLBACK IS THE LEGIBILITY FLOOR, MEASURED ON THE SHEET.** §11.1.2's *"per-sheet
Link count above which it would be illegible"* is read as docs/08 §6.2's trigger: the drawn sheet is
fitted to its paper, and if that fit puts any text below `kMinPrintPt` (6 pt), the sheet prints as net
labels instead. No count is invented. **An implementation clause, stated by the implementer and not
asked:** the fallback is taken only when the net-label sheet itself meets the floor. Both renderings
share one symbol layout and one 8 pt type size, so they differ only in how far the ink reaches, and a
sheet whose symbols alone are too big is too big either way; trading its wires for labels there buys
no legibility and costs the wires. Such a sheet stays `drawn`, at its fit, with §6.2's notice: G3, a
heuristic may never hold a deliverable hostage. Not taken: a fixed
link count, which no source supplies and which is wrong in both directions (sixty short runs fit; thirty
on one 48-port panel do not). This is the export's fallback and only the export's: §12.1's AC-040 row
deletes the on-screen degradation, and it stays deleted.

**11.224.5 RULED: THE FALLBACK SAYS SO IN A NOTE BOX ON THE SHEET**, ruled, in the drawing area's upper
left, naming what the reader is holding: the cables are shown as net labels, and drawn they would print
below 6 pt. The export also raises a notice, which DR-224 made readable. Not taken: a suffix on the
title-block title, which is the part of the sheet that is skimmed; and the export notice alone, which a
forwarded PDF does not carry and which would break §11.1.2's *"prints a note"*.

**11.224.6 TWO CONSEQUENCES, STATED SO THEY ARE NOT DECIDED SILENTLY.** `ExportSpec.wireRender` is not
built here: no surface could set it before M6-I's export dialog, so `auto` is the behaviour that ships
and the field arrives with the dialog. And by DR-208 §11.207.1 the legend's convention key gains the tag
pill and the net-label stub in the same change that first prints them (`#984`).

**11.224.7 RULED THE SAME DAY: A BANK THE SHEET WIRES PRINTS EXPANDED.** Found building the partition.
A collapsed bank (CR-103) draws one vector pin carrying its FIRST port's key, so a cable on any other
member finds no pin and is drawn nowhere: counted in `unlabelledLinkIds`, shown to nobody. On Whole
House that is eleven of `PP-1`'s twelve runs, and the Network sheet would have printed one cable of
twelve. DR-174 §11.173 names a set inside a collapsed bank as not ruled, and docs/05 §3 says only that
members *"remain individually routed in the schedule"*. **Ruled by the user:** on an interconnect sheet,
every bank with at least one cable of that sheet's domain prints expanded, so each cable has its own pin,
wire and pill; a bank with none stays collapsed. The partition reads a schematic with every bank
expanded, so no cable is lost before the sheet is chosen. Not taken: routing the members onto the vector
pin, where the v1 router has no lane to separate them and eleven wires print as one; and expanding every
bank, which prints a 48-port switch whole for two cables. The on-screen half is filed separately; this
clause rules the sheet.

**Scope.** No scope moves. CR-073's partition and DR-001 §11.1.2's rendering, made definite.

### 11.225 DR-226 · Network values are typed in a Devices view in Structured Wiring, and a device's MAC has one home

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-03, opening NET-A (`#681`), on the recommended option three times and
the user's own once.** DR-048 §11.47.6 put the surface in *"the table, via `⚙ Columns`"*, and a census
before decomposing found the table does not exist.

**11.225.1 THE FACTS THAT PRICED IT.** **No surface in the product lists device instances.** The
Device Manager tab browses the template library, the Schedule lists cables, Structured Wiring's views
are runs, the matrix, outlets and pathways, and the only `Columns` control is the Device Builder's port
grid, which edits templates, where DR-048 §11.47.10 says no field is added. The batch bar, `Ctrl+D`
fill-down and the cell editors exist, privately, inside Structured Wiring's table. **And a device's MAC
has two fields**: `DeviceInstance.macAddressPrimary`, beside serial number and firmware, and the
`mac` of the `NetworkConfig` DR-048 hung on the device. Neither has ever been written.

**11.225.2 RULED: A `Devices` VIEW IN STRUCTURED WIRING**, a fifth beside Table, Matrix, Outlets and
Pathways: one row per device, its network values in columns, with the batch bar and fill-down that
table already has. It is §11.47.6's table, given a host. DR-020 §11.19.2(5), the precedent §11.47.6
cites, put the as-built tally on a table the product already built rather than a new screen, and this
keeps a job's close-out in one tab. Not taken: an *In this project* view in the Device Manager, which
its name invites and which first needs the table machinery extracted into a shared widget; and an
editable inspector, which reverses §11.47.6's one-place-a-value-is-written argument.

**11.225.3 RULED BY THE USER: THE DEFAULT COLUMNS ARE HOSTNAME, IP, MAC, VLANS AND VERIFIED ON**;
subnet and gateway sit behind the `Columns` toggle. The recommendation was hostname, IP and verified on;
the user added the other two, in their words: *"MAC addresses are heavily used for WOL/SSDP/SDDP
identification, and VLAN's are important for many video distribution systems."*

**11.225.4 RULED: A DEVICE'S MAC IS `macAddressPrimary`**, the device-level identity field. The MAC
column writes it and `T6.50` prints it. `NetworkConfig.mac` stays for per-port use, a device whose
ports carry their own. One fact, one home, so no later surface can write the other copy. Not taken:
`network.mac`, which leaves `macAddressPrimary` as a second home nobody writes. **`verifiedOn` dates
the row**, the MAC included, though the field lives on the device and the date on its `NetworkConfig`:
a tech confirming a device confirms what the row shows.

**11.225.5 RULED: `verifiedOn` IS AN EDITABLE DATE COLUMN, AND THE BATCH BAR STAMPS TODAY.** Editing an
address never changes the date by itself. Not taken: stamping on edit, which marks a value retyped from
an old spreadsheet as freshly checked, the stale-as-fact failure §11.47.3 exists to prevent; and the
date column alone, which turns stamping a rack into a select-and-type every visit.

**Scope.** No scope moves: DR-048 §11.47.6's surface given a host, and its MAC made single.

### 11.226 DR-227 · A template can say it has Wi-Fi, the Devices view lists what can join a network, and one setting orders the view and T6.50

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-03, building NET-A/2 (`#683`).** A §8.3 amendment: it gives
`TemplateBody` a field DR-048 §11.47.10 said it would not have. Recorded with a correction first.

**11.226.1 A PRICE WAS WRONG, AND THE USER RE-DECIDED ON THE RIGHT ONE.** DR-226 §11.225.2 was chosen
over a Device Manager host partly because Structured Wiring would reuse its table's batch bar and cell
editors *"with no extraction"*. Read rather than assumed, those widgets are typed to cable rows (a link
id, `StructureColumnId`, the signal-family registry), so either host needs a new device table; what is
reused is the pattern and the shared `fillDown` binding. Offered again on the corrected price, the user
kept Structured Wiring, on §11.225.2's other reason. That clause stands; its price did not.

**11.226.2 RULED: THE VIEW LISTS NETWORK-CAPABLE DEVICES, WITH SHOW ALL.** By default, a device whose
template has a port in the Network domain **and is not a passthrough**, or whose template says it has
Wi-Fi (§11.226.3), or that already carries a network value or a MAC. A *Show all devices* toggle adds
the rest. Not taken: every device with ports, which on Whole House lists every amplifier, splitter and
panel; and Network ports alone, which leaves a Wi-Fi-only device no row to be given an address on.

**The passthrough exclusion was ruled the same day, on a measurement.** The port rule as first written
listed patch panels and fibre enclosures, which carry Network ports and never an address. The template's
existing `isPassthrough` separates them exactly on all four starters (Whole House 30 rows to 26, `PP-1`
to `PP-3` and `LIU-1` leaving; Small Office 21 to 18; Home Theatre 14 to 13): a passthrough is copper
or glass between two things that have addresses, and has none of its own. No new field.

**11.226.3 RULED BY THE USER: `TemplateBody` GAINS `wifi`, AND IT IS NOT WHAT DR-048 REFUSED.** A
`bool?` (unset, yes, no), shown in the Device Builder as a *Wi-Fi* toggle; a template that says yes is
network-capable without a jack and without an address yet. In the user's words: *"even though it's a
network 'field', it's still a device property (What the device is capable of)."* DR-048 kept network
**values** off the template because they are facts about an install; whether a model can join a
network at all is a fact about the model. The census behind it is also the user's: Wi-Fi-only devices
are rare in this trade, *"aside from the Move 2, Roam, and Ace Headphones (which are portable anyway)
I've seen zero Sonos devices that are WiFi only."* Editing it never forks a template's identity, and
no seeded template sets it, because CR-061 wants a source for every catalog fact and there is none.

**11.226.4 RULED: ONE SETTING ORDERS THE DEVICES VIEW AND `T6.50`.** `ProjectSettings` gains the network
order, *by designator* or *rack by rack, top unit down, then room by room*, set in `File ▸ Sheet set…`,
defaulting to by designator. The user's reason for the default: it *"mirrors how the firm I work for
handles IP address assignment on a network"*, and for the setting: *"other firms may use a different
method for IP assignment."* The view follows the same setting so the table and the printed schedule
never disagree about order: one derivation, two projections (CR-107). Not taken for the view: a fixed
designator order beside a configurable sheet.

**Scope.** **v1 grows by one field**, `TemplateBody.wifi`, superseding DR-048 §11.47.10's *"does not
give `TemplateBody` a network field"* for this capability alone (§12.47). `ProjectSettings` gains the
order. No milestone moves.

### 11.227 DR-228 · T6.50 prints every network column, one row per device with a value

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building NET-A/3 (`#684`), on the recommended option twice.**
DR-048 §11.47.4 put `T6.50` in v1 as an `AUTO` sheet and said nothing about what it prints.

**11.227.1 RULED: ALL TEN COLUMNS, SUBNET AND GATEWAY INCLUDED.** `DEVICE`, `NAME`, `LOCATION`,
`HOSTNAME`, `IP ADDRESS`, `SUBNET`, `GATEWAY`, `MAC`, `VLANS`, `VERIFIED`, from the one derivation the
Devices view renders (DR-226), so the screen and the sheet are the same strings (CR-107). The tech at a
rack who sets a static address on a laptop needs the subnet and the gateway, and paper has no Columns
menu. Not taken: the view's default columns, which leave out exactly what that tech needs.

**11.227.2 RULED: ONE ROW PER DEVICE THAT CARRIES A VALUE**, an address, a MAC or a VLAN, in the
project's network order (DR-227 §11.226.4). The sheet states facts: a blank row in a client deliverable
reads as an omission, which is why `T6.20` and `T5.01` are `AUTO` too (DR-005). Every row prints its
verified day or `unverified` (DR-048 §11.47.3). The export raises a notice naming how many
network-capable devices have nothing recorded, so the gap is said rather than silent; **only when
`T6.50` prints**, an implementer's clause stated so it is not decided silently, since a project that
records no address has no schedule to have a gap in and a notice on its every export would nag about a
feature nobody is using. Not taken: every
network-capable device, blank rows included, which is a commissioning form and prints empty boxes on
the client's copy.

**11.227.3 THE MECHANICAL PARTS, STATED SO THEY ARE NOT DECIDED SILENTLY.** ANSI A landscape, the
schedules' paper (docs/08 §6.1); `T6.50` to `T6.59`, then the shared overflow pool, taking it after the
equipment list, which precedes it; in the set after `T6.30` and before `T5.01`, which DR-221 keeps last.
`kReservedNcsIds` stops reserving `T6.50` for the v1.1 schedule it no longer is; `T6.40` stays reserved.

**Scope.** No scope moves: DR-048 §11.47.4's sheet, made definite.

### 11.228 DR-229 · Open web page from the inspector and the Devices view, at an editable URL

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building NET-A/4 (`#685`).** DR-048 §11.47.7 ruled that the address
launches a browser behind a confirmation that shows the URL, and said neither where the gesture lives
nor what URL it builds.

**11.228.1 RULED: TWO HOSTS, THE INSPECTOR AND THE DEVICES VIEW**, against the recommendation of the
inspector alone. The inspector's `NETWORK` section carries the button beside the address it opens; the
Devices view carries it per row, because that is the table the addresses are typed into and a tech
working down a rack checks them from there. **The row's form is an implementer's choice, stated so it is
not decided silently**: a narrow trailing column holding one button, on the tick gutter's precedent,
since no table in the product has a right-click menu and building one for a single item would be a menu
nobody else uses. It is a column of the view and not of `NetworkColumnId`: it prints nowhere and is not
in the Columns menu.

**11.228.2 RULED: THE CONFIRMATION'S URL IS EDITABLE, PREFILLED `http://<address>/`**, the address being
the row's IP and its hostname when it has none. HTTPS or a port is typed before it opens; nothing is
written back to the device. The trade's gear splits across both schemes (UniFi, Araknis and Crestron
serve HTTPS, older AV kit HTTP), and a stored per-device URL was offered and **not taken**: it is a
model field DR-048 did not rule in. A device with neither address offers no button rather than a
disabled one that cannot say why.

**11.228.3 THE LAUNCH IS A SEAM OUTSIDE `rackpal_core`** (DR-048 §11.47.7, NET-A/4a): an injected
function the app supplies, so the widget tests never open a browser and the core stays free of platform
code. The confirmation opens only `http` and `https` URLs, so an edited field cannot turn the button
into a launcher for a `file:` path or a program.

**Scope.** No scope moves: DR-048 §11.47.7's gesture, given its hosts and its URL.

### 11.229 DR-230 · Export previews the real PDF, and past 40 sheets it says so without asking

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, opening M6-I (`#351`), on the recommended option twice.** The
roadmap's M6 item reads *"export progress, cancel and preview"*, and CR-100 ruled the preview a screen
rendering because a pdfium preview needed a native dependency.

**11.229.1 RULED: THE PREVIEW IS THE REAL FILE, RENDERED BY THE VENDORED PDFIUM.** Export generates the
PDF once, off the main isolate (CR-099), and opens a preview of **those bytes**: each page rasterised on
demand, paged through, with the export's notices beside it. **Save…** writes the bytes that were
previewed; closing the preview writes nothing. CR-100's reason for a screen preview, *"no native
dependency"*, is gone: DR-153 vendored pdfium for floorplan import, committed rather than downloaded,
which is the very condition CR-100 set. A preview of the bytes is faithful by definition where a screen
rendering is faithful only as far as a parity test reaches, and one generation serves both preview and
save. CR-100's **Verify output** button is therefore the preview itself and does not ship separately.
**Measured** on Whole House: the export takes about 100 ms for sixteen sheets and pdfium renders a page
at 1100 px in about 56 ms with its PNG encode. Not taken: CR-100's screen preview (about twice the
price, and its plan sheets need an image path the screen canvas lacks), and no in-app preview at all.
**A MISSING BINARY NEVER HOLDS THE FILE**: without pdfium the preview says so and Save… still works
(CR-023, G3). The OS print dialog stays v1.1, and **Open in system viewer** still ships, as CR-100 ruled.

**11.229.2 RULED: PAST 40 SHEETS THE COUNT IS SAID, NOT ASKED.** At about 6 ms a sheet, forty sheets is a
quarter of a second, so AC-050 A7.4's warning guards against a broken project rather than a long wait.
The preview's header shows the count, marked past 40 as more than a set usually needs, and the export
raises a notice; no prompt, because a commercial job may legitimately run to sixty and would click
through it on every export. **2000 is refused**, before any page is drawn, saying the count and the
cap. Not taken: a confirmation before generating.

**11.229.3 THE MECHANICAL PARTS, STATED SO THEY ARE NOT DECIDED SILENTLY.** The count is the sheet set's
own dry run, which resolves before a page is emitted. Progress is shown only past 400 ms (docs/08
§8.2), which on the measured rate is a set of about 65 sheets, so most exports never show it. Cancel
kills the isolate and nothing is written.

**Scope.** No scope moves: the roadmap's preview, given its mechanism. CR-100's preview clause is
superseded (§12.48).

### 11.230 DR-231 · A cable's crossover is set on the schematic and in the table, and polarity reversed joins it

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, closing `#973`.** DR-221 §11.220.4 kept null-modem in T5.01's
trigger and filed its writer; `Link.crossover` had been modelled since M0 with no command and no
control. A §8.3 amendment, because the model gains a value.

**11.230.1 RULED: TWO HOSTS, THE SCHEMATIC AND THE STRUCTURED WIRING TABLE.** Selecting a cable on the
schematic shows a bar naming the cable with a **Crossover** dropdown beside it, the first per-cable
control the schematic has; the Structured Wiring table gains a **CROSSOVER** column for home runs, on
the machinery `#712`'s CLASS column used. Not taken: the table alone, which lists only home runs and so
could never mark the usual null-modem case, a serial cable inside the rack; and the schematic alone.

**11.230.2 RULED: EVERY CHOICE ON EVERY CABLE**, against the recommendation to offer only what fits the
cable's family, **on the user's trade reason**: cables are deliberately wired crossed on more families
than the recommendation assumed, a subwoofer run wired out of phase being the user's example. The
choices are `Not set`, `Straight`, `Null-modem`, `Polarity A→B` and `Polarity reversed`, unset meaning
nobody has said (G4).

**11.230.3 RULED: `CrossoverKind` GAINS `polarityReversed`, AND T5.01 PRINTS IT.** The user's example
was a speaker pair wired `+` to `−`, which neither existing value describes: null-modem is an RS-232
transmit-receive swap and A→B is fibre. Marked so, the schedule's notes read `POLARITY REVERSED` and
T5.01 lists the cable in its own section, under a note that the swap is deliberate, so whoever
terminates it does not correct it. Not taken: keeping three values and recording the case in the
cable's notes, where T5.01 never shows it. Additive: an older file has no such value and decodes
unchanged, and the codec writes it by name like the others.

**Scope.** v1 grows by one enum value, `CrossoverKind.polarityReversed`. No milestone moves.

### 11.231 DR-232 · A drawn interconnect sheet reserves its own ink, and islands sit side by side

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building `#998`.** Whole House's `T6.02` Network sheet printed at about
5.3 pt, under docs/08 §6.2's floor, with the notice to say so (docs/12 §4.40 flagged it). **Measured first**:
the sheet is two devices, `PP-1` and `LIU-1`, in one column; their bodies total 344 units and they spanned
604, because the drawn rendering was laid out with the net-label comb reservation it never draws. Height
bound the fit at 0.679. Removing the reservation alone reached about 7.5 pt, and the render showed
`LIU-1`'s pill touching `PP-1` with most of the landscape page still empty.

**11.231.1 RULED: THE DRAWN SHEET IS PLACED BY ITS OWN INK.** Each device's ink is its body and the stubs
and pills its own ends draw, recorded by the wire layer as it draws them; within a column, devices stack
with the schematic's ordinary node gap between their inks. The label rendering keeps the label
reservation it needs. So the two renderings no longer share one layout, and DR-225 §11.224.4's
implementer clause is amended to say so (§12.49): the fallback still compares the two on the sheet.

**11.231.2 RULED: ISLANDS WRAP TO FIT THE PAPER**, the recommended option over the gap fix alone. When
every device a sheet draws is an island, with no wire between two of them (a sheet of home runs), they
are arranged in rows and columns, in the layout's order, choosing the arrangement that prints largest.
Whole House's `PP-1` and `LIU-1` sit side by side. Not taken: the gap fix alone, which clears the floor
and leaves one narrow column with empty paper either side.

**11.231.3 A LOCK STILL HOLDS** (DR-225 §11.224.3). A column holding a locked device keeps its layout,
and islands wrap only when none of them is locked: re-placing around a position the user fixed would
move the devices beside it for a reason the user cannot see.

**Scope.** No scope moves: how a v1 sheet is laid out, made legible.

---

### 11.232 DR-233 · An IEC or NEMA cord is a power cord, wherever its far end lands

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building `#908`.** `LinkClass.powerCord` was documented as
auto-classified and the classifier never returned it: `linkClassOf` answered `jumper` for both ends in
one rack and `fieldCable` otherwise. So a cord from an amplifier's IEC inlet to a PDU outlet in the same
rack was a jumper, one to a wall receptacle or another rack landed on the Pull Sheet as a cable somebody
pulls, and the schedule's *"N power cords hidden"* chip could only count links a person had locked by
hand. DR-008 §11.8.1 left the class open in so many words: *"`powerCord` and `internal` are untouched by
this ruling."*

**11.232.1 RULED: A CORD IS ITS PORTS.** A link is a `powerCord` when every port its ends land on is a
`power.ac_iec` or `power.ac_branch` port with a `PortPowerSpec.role`, and at least one end is such a port.
The two families mix freely, since a NEMA-to-C13 lead from a PDU to a device is the commonest cord there
is. The other end may be a place or open, so a cord to *"the wall receptacle behind the TV"* is a cord.
The test runs **before** the rack test, so DR-008 §11.8.1's *"Nothing else"* now reads *"nothing else,
once a cord is ruled out"* (§12.50). The family is the port's effective one, override included (DR-131's
reason: a correction a person made on an instance must reach every reader of the family).

**11.232.2 THE OTHER POWER FAMILIES KEEP THE RACK TEST**, the user's choice, and the recommended one.
`power.ac_hardwired` is a branch circuit an electrician pulls, `power.dc_low` is as often 18/2 pulled to
a keypad or a camera as it is a wall-wart lead, and `power.bonding` is a conductor cut to length. Each
stays a jumper inside one rack and a field cable otherwise, so a pulled run stays on the sheet the
installer pulls from. Not taken: every `power.*` port with a role, the shape `#908` sketched, which hides
a pulled 24 V run in the hidden-cords count; and IEC, NEMA and low-voltage DC together, right for an
in-rack brick and wrong for every DC run that goes through a wall.

**11.232.3 UNDETERMINED STAYS UNDETERMINED.** An end on a port the document cannot resolve still returns
`null` before either test runs (G4): a cord to a staged device is not a guessed cord.

**11.232.4 A LOCK STILL WINS, AND NOW IT CAN DISAGREE.** DR-008 §11.8.2 is untouched: a class a person
set stands, and a link locked to `jumper` that is now a cord reports the disagreement. Measured at the
ruling: none of the four starters draws a link onto a power port, and none locks a class.

**Scope.** No scope moves: a v1 class that was modelled and never produced now is.

---

### 11.233 DR-234 · A set and a multi-draw ask tier 2 per pair, and a set's chip names the first

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building `#909` and `#999`.** DR-116 §11.115.3 ruled that *"a rule is
a statement about the RESULTING STATE, not about the gesture that produced it"*, for the bind gesture.
Measured: two more gestures never asked tier 2. `_commitSet` runs `planAtomicConnect` (tier 1 per paired
position) and commits, so a stereo pair on two 3-pin blocks dropped on an XLR pair is a cable with no
`CON-001` chip, where the pin gesture springs each half back. `_commitMultiDraw` builds its N connects and
runs them, under an arm-time comment saying *"The commit path checks it per pair"*, which it did not. This
ruling applies DR-116 to both and settles the three things `#909` left open.

**11.233.1 RULED: TIER 2 PER PAIRED POSITION, FIRST CHIP WINS.** Each position with a port at both ends is
asked, in the set's declared order (a multi-draw's plan order), and the first chip springs the gesture
back, as tier 1 already does across positions. An open position has no pair and is not asked. At arm
time a target set, or a multi-draw target bank, whose pairs would raise a chip has its pins offered with
the amber ring (DR-116 §11.115.5).

**11.233.2 RULED: THE CHIP NAMES THE FIRST FAILING PAIR, PLUS A COUNT**, the user's choice. The headline
is the pin gesture's own, naming that pair's jacks, and the explanation adds how many more of the cable's
paired conductors (or the run's cables) would spring back. Not taken: naming the two sets by label,
which reads well for a pair and stops naming a jack a person can find once one position of a larger set
is the problem.

**11.233.3 `[ Connect anyway ]` COMMITS THE WHOLE GESTURE**, the set as one cable or the run as N, exactly
what the gesture would have written (CR-017).

**11.233.4 RULED: ON A SET, ONLY `CON-001`'s ADAPTER**, the user's choice. `Declare an adapter` makes the set
cable and declares one adapter on it, which clears every conductor, since `CON-001` reads adapters per
cable. It is offered only when `CON-001` is the only rule any paired position trips: otherwise the remedy
would clear one rule and commit past another. The remedies that insert a device (`SIG-001`'s receiver,
`SIG-002`'s converter) are withheld on a set chip, because each wires pin-to-pin cables and would split a
one-cable set apart. Not taken: no remedies at all, which costs this: the chip is the only host in the
product that can declare an adapter, so a stereo Euroblock-to-XLR cable could never clear `CON-001`.
Also not taken: remedies acting on one conductor, which makes a single-conductor cable out of a pair.

**11.233.5 A MULTI-DRAW CHIP OFFERS NO RULE-SPECIFIC REMEDY.** This clause is the implementer's default,
stated to the user and not separately ruled: the run is N cables, and a remedy that repairs one of them
while the rest commit has no single meaning.

**11.233.6 WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE: A 16/4 TAPPED AND CONTINUED.** The user raised the trade convention of
running 16/4 to a room, tapping one pair at the first speaker and continuing to the second. That is one
cable reaching two devices, a `Breakout` (CR-014), and it never reaches this chip: an unequal count is
§11.8.3's connect-what-fits-and-warn, and no rule reads an unpaired position. An adapter is the wrong
noun for that junction. `Breakout` has no writer and the hand-authored conductor map defers to v1.1
(AC-053, RJ-016); `#1000` records the gap, and its Saga is the user's §8.3 call.

**Scope.** No scope moves: DR-116, reaching two more gestures.

### 11.234 DR-235 · A declared adapter is named on the cable bar, listed on T6.30, noted on the schedule and marked on the drawing

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, building `#1001`.** After `[ Declare an adapter ]` the product says *"Name
the part in the inspector so it reaches the bill of materials."* Measured: nothing in `rackpal_ui` or the app
reads or edits `Link.inlineAdapters`, and nothing in core or export reads an adapter into a bill of
materials; the only readers are the two tier-2 rules and the codec. So the sentence named a control that does
not exist, and DR-128 §11.127.2's own promise, that *"an adapter with no model reaches the BOM as an
unspecified line"*, had no implementation. docs/05 §12 adds that an adapter is *"rendered as a small lozenge on
the wire"*, which no ruling made and nothing draws.

**11.234.1 RULED: DR-128's PROMISE IS KEPT WHOLE**, the recommended option over the equipment list alone and
over deleting the sentence. Deleting it would have hidden an unkept ruling rather than kept it.

**11.234.2 RULED: THE CABLE BAR NAMES IT.** The schematic's cable bar (DR-231 §11.230.1, the one per-cable
host) lists the selected cable's adapters by their two connectors, each with a **Model** field and
**Remove**, each change one undo step. The remedy's sentence names the cable bar. An empty model is unknown
and stays absent (G4).

**11.234.3 RULED: T6.30 LISTS THEM.** The materials table gains **in-line adapters**, after jumpers and power
cords: one row per connector pair and model, with a quantity. An adapter with no model is a row of its own,
printed as unknown and counted in a note, never merged into a stated one.

**11.234.4 RULED: THE SCHEDULE NOTES SAY SO**, the user's choice, on DR-231 §11.230.3's machinery: each
adapter on a cable is noted on its rows by its two connectors, and its model when stated, because the person
terminating the cable is the one who needs to know there is a part in the middle.

**11.234.5 RULED: A LOZENGE ON BOTH RENDERINGS**, the user's choice, against marking only the drawn wire as
docs/05 describes. A cable carrying an adapter draws a small lozenge on each pennant of its net-label pair
and at the midpoint of a drawn wire, on screen and on the drawn interconnect sheets. Each pennant, because
the model does not record which end the adapter sits at, and whoever reads either end should see it. Not
taken: the drawn wire alone, which DR-001's default rendering would almost never show; and the pennants
alone, which would lose the mark when a domain switches to drawn.

**11.234.6 DECIDED BUILDING IT: A BOWTIE, NOT A LOZENGE.** The shape in §11.234.5 is superseded; its placement
stands. Building the lozenge found four families whose glyph is a hollow diamond (Dante, AES67, AVB and
TOSLINK), drawn inside the pennant a few millimetres from where the lozenge would sit on the leader: two
identical marks meaning two different things on one label, and the same diamond prints in T0.01's cable-types
block. Asked, the user chose a **bowtie**, two triangles tip to tip across the cable (two different ends
meeting), which no family glyph uses, oriented along the cable so the line runs through both tips. Not taken:
keeping the lozenge and relying on its position, which an 8 pt page does not reliably show; and a barrel,
which sits close to the hollow square four other families use. T0.01 keys it as *"Bowtie: an in-line adapter
declared on the cable"*.

**Scope.** No scope moves: a v1 value object that was modelled, written and never shown, shown.

### 11.235 DR-236 · One cable may carry several sets to several devices, added from the cable's own bar

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-04, a §8.3 amendment, for `#1000`.** The trade convention: run 16/4 from the
amplifier to a room, tap one pair at the first speaker and continue to the second. One cable, one pull, two
devices. **Measured before ruling:**

- **The model already allows it, and has since the corpus was reconciled.** CR-014 relaxed I-25 to the
  conductor: *"Each `Conductor` spans exactly two endpoints; a `Link` may reference up to N devices"*, and
  AC-029 accepted that for v1 with the dual-head IR emitter as its example.
- **What AC-053 deferred was the authoring**: *"Hand-authoring an arbitrary conductor map defers to v1.1."*
  The v1 gesture connects one set to one set, so the closest a person could get was a set connect and a
  DR-014 split: two cables on the Pull Sheet where the crew pulls one. Roadmap §2.2's row justified waiting
  with *"`atomicConnect` covers component video, stereo pairs, 16/4"*, which is true of a 16/4 between two
  devices and false of this one.
- **The readers misread the ruling they cite.** `net_label_layer.dart` reads the cable's ends off its first
  conductor on the ground that *"CR-014 fixes each conductor at exactly two ends and every conductor of one
  cable shares the same physical pair"*. CR-014 rules the first half and the opposite of the second. Six
  generic readers take that shortcut: the classifier, the schedule's ends, net labels, the schematic's
  layout, link lookup and the canvas; the other sites that read the first conductor are home-run code, where
  one conductor is the shape.

**11.235.1 RULED: SETS ONTO ONE CABLE COME INTO V1**, the user's choice, and the recommended one. A cable may
carry several atomic sets, each landing on its own device. AC-053's deferral narrows to what it still
covers, hand-mapping individual conductors, which stays v1.1 (§12.51). Not taken: the full conductor map,
which needs a per-conductor editor nobody has designed and which the 16/4 case does not need.

**11.235.2 RULED: ADDED FROM THE CABLE'S OWN BAR**, the user's choice. A selected cable's bar (DR-231 §11.230.1)
offers **Add a set to this cable**, which arms the set gesture from a free set on a device the cable already
reaches; the drop appends that set's conductors to this cable instead of minting a new one, in one undo
step. Tier 1 refuses as it does for any set; tier 2 springs back per pair with DR-234's chip. It is DR-014's
split read the other way. Not taken: dropping onto a cable's pennant, which nothing on screen marks as a
target and which a near miss turns into a new cable; and a modifier drag, undiscoverable and one more bare
key in a keymap that has just grown a text field.

**11.235.3 RULED: ONE ROW, EVERY FAR END NAMED**, the user's choice. The Pull Sheet prints such a cable once,
with one length, its far ends named together (`SPK-1 + SPK-2`): it is one pull, which is RJ-016's whole
argument. The Termination Schedule gives each end its own line under the one cable number, since each end
is terminated by somebody. Not taken: a row per far end, the shape RJ-016 rejected.

**11.235.4 RULED: EVERY READER READS EVERY CONDUCTOR.** The readers above take a cable's ends from all its
conductors, as CR-014 always required, and their comments stop citing CR-014 for the opposite. A cable with
every conductor on one pair of devices, which is every cable drawn before this ruling, reads exactly as
before.

**11.235.5 LEFT FOR ITS CHAPTER.** How a drawn wire that reaches three devices is drawn is decided when that
chapter is built, with the user. Where along the run a tap sits (`Breakout.atLengthFraction`) stays unknown
unless a person states it (G4); nothing here invents one.

**11.235.6 DECIDED BUILDING IT: TRUNK AND BRANCH**, the user's choice for §11.235.5, against a wire per pair
(which reads as two cables, the shape RJ-016 argued against) and against keeping such a cable as labels in
drawn mode. The first conductor's route is the trunk, so every two-device cable draws as it did; a further
pair on a device the trunk joins is drawn into the trunk's own escape point there; a further device is a
branch from a filled junction dot at the trunk's midpoint, with its own tag pill. An adapter's bowtie
moves to the trunk's quarter point when a junction is drawn. T0.01 keys the dot when a printed wire
branches (DR-208).

**11.235.7 MEASURED BUILDING IT: THE READERS WERE NOT THE SIX NAMED ABOVE.** The census §11.235.4 promised
found `link_lookup.dart` already walking every conductor; the ruling named it from the shape of the
problem. Of 29 first-conductor sites, four had to read every conductor (the classifier, net labels, the
schematic layout and the cable bar's sentence), three were sound on the first conductor for a reason
their comments did not give (the first conductor is the cable's first far end, so `roomOfLink`,
`plan_length` and `room_estimate`'s datum walk stand), one is the schedule row's (BRK-A/4), and the rest
are home-run code, one conductor by shape.

**11.235.8 AN IMPLEMENTER'S DEFAULT, STATED TO THE USER:** an appended set must carry the cable's own
family. Both of this ruling's cases are one family, and a cable with two services is AC-021's machinery.

**Scope.** **v1 grows**: the authoring of a cable that carries several sets to several devices, and the
readers that make such a cable print right. A new Epic under the v1 Saga holds it; `#1000` moves there.

### 11.236 DR-237 · Speaker wire is bare wire: a binding post or a 2-pole Euroblock mates with the bare-wire terminations

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-06, for `#1010`.** `CON-001` sprang back on every amplifier-to-in-wall-speaker
run: the seeded `conn.binding_post` mated with `conn.banana` alone, and `CON-001` reads the source side's
`matesWith`. **The user's trade fact:** *bare wire is typical for most speakers*, on spring-loaded terminals;
combination binding-post and banana sockets appear mostly on floorstanding, bookshelf and satellite
speakers, not in-wall or in-ceiling ones.

**Measured:** four connectors carry speaker-level ports in the seed. `conn.binding_post` (A02, A04) mated
with banana only, so it fired even against a bookshelf's own binding post; `conn.euroblock_2` (the
commercial A01, A05) mated with itself only, so it fired the same way; `conn.screw_terminal` (F04, F05,
F14) and `conn.unterminated` (F07, F08, F20) mate with nothing, which `CON-001` reads as unknown and skips
(G4).

**11.236.1 RULED: THE TWO SOURCE-SIDE TERMINATIONS MATE WITH EVERY BARE-WIRE ONE.** `conn.binding_post` mates
with `conn.banana`, `conn.binding_post`, `conn.euroblock_2`, `conn.screw_terminal` and `conn.unterminated`;
`conn.euroblock_2` with itself and the same three, and the bare-wire ones list them back (§11.236.2). A
genuine mismatch, an RCA into a binding post, still fires.

**11.236.2 AND EVERY BARE-WIRE TERMINATION LISTS THEM BACK**, because mating is symmetric.
`conn.screw_terminal` and `conn.unterminated` each mate with `conn.binding_post`, `conn.euroblock_2`,
`conn.screw_terminal` and `conn.unterminated`, so the drag may start at either end of a speaker run, and a
screw terminal or a pigtail dropped on an RCA jack now springs back.

**CORRECTED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT.** This clause first read *"the sink-side ones keep their empty lists"*, an
implementer's default: a list there would switch `CON-001` on wherever one is a source. The gate refused it.
`connector_mating_test` pins that if A lists B then B lists A, or the same joint validates one way from each
end, which means a connector with an empty, unknown list can never be listed by another. The default was
mine and not the user's, so it is corrected here rather than superseded. `conn.unterminated` is also a
fiber splice pigtail (N04); it is spliced and never plugged, so a pigtail on an LC port springing back is
right.

**11.236.3 WIDER THAN THE SENTENCE, AND SAID SO.** The user spoke of binding posts; the 2-pole Euroblock is
included because the census found the identical false positive on the commercial amplifiers. It is the
implementer's reading of the trade fact, recorded as such, and narrows to binding posts alone on the
user's word.

**Scope.** No scope moves: a catalogue correction.

### 11.237 DR-238 · A captive cord is part of its device, and T6.30 does not list it

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-06, for `#1002`:** *"remove captive cords on T6.30"*. T6.30's jumpers-and-power-
cords table and its footage note counted every power cord as a piece to buy, and a captive cord (an
amplifier's own attached lead) is bought by nobody.

**11.237.1 RULED: CAPTIVE CORDS LEAVE T6.30's TABLE AND ITS "BOUGHT BY THE PIECE" COUNT TOGETHER**, which are
one count read twice. They stay power cords: off the Pull Sheet (DR-233), on the outlet map, and in the
Schedule's hidden-cords count.

**11.237.2 HOW ONE IS KNOWN, DERIVED AND NOT AUTHORED**, the implementer's choice from `#1002`'s census and
stated to the user: a cord landing on an INLET-role `power.ac_branch` port is the device's own cord. All 13
captive inlets in the seed are exactly that, on a NEMA plug, and every detachable AC inlet is
`power.ac_iec`; a plug on an inlet is the end of the device's own cord. No template field is added.

**11.237.3 COUNTED, NOT HIDDEN (G4).** The footage note says how many captive cords it set aside, so the two
counts on one sheet still reconcile with the Schedule's.

**Scope.** No scope moves: a v1 table made right.
