### 11.238 DR-239 · A rack's envelope is typed in the rack inspector and printed on its elevation

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-06, for `#923`.** DR-188 §11.187.5 measured that `Rack` already declares
its physical envelope (`overallWidth`, `overallDepth`, `overallHeight`, `ownWeight`, `hasFrontDoor`,
`hasRearDoor`, `frontDoorClearance`, `rearDoorClearance`) and that nothing in the product can set them: the
fourth instance of the `Placement.locked` shape (§11.185.0). The user's reason is in DR-188's own record:
*"a cabinet was too small for a pull-out rack, or a closet was shaved down to make space for a mini bar
and the rack no longer fit."*

**11.238.1 RULED: AN ENCLOSURE SECTION, BELOW FORM FACTOR.** The rack inspector gains a section of its own
holding overall width, depth and height, own weight (editable, where it was a read-only row), and per side a
door checkbox and that door's two clearances. Form factor stays about rails and RU. A clearance is dashed
and disabled while its door is unticked, as Hinge side already is without a swing frame; unticking a door
keeps the values, so ticking it back loses nothing. Every field is one `RackField` row through the one
property command, undoable like the rest.

**11.238.2 RULED: TWO CLEARANCES PER DOOR, IN THE TRADE'S OWN WORDS.** The user: *"There needs to be one
for each; "Front Rail Clearance" is typically used for depth inside the door, while "Door Clearance" is
what's typically used for swing space."* So **rail clearance** is the depth between a rail and its closed
door, which handles, cable and door-mounted fans eat, and **door clearance** is the swing space the door
needs in front of it, which is what a closet or millwork must leave free. The existing
`frontDoorClearance` and `rearDoorClearance` keep their names and mean swing space; `frontRailClearance`
and `rearRailClearance` are added beside them, nullable `Len`, an absent key read as unknown (G4) so every
file on disk still opens. **The rear rail clearance is the implementer's extension**, for symmetry with the
existing door pair, and stated as such.

**11.238.3 RULED: MILLIMETRES AND KILOGRAMS**, matching the inspector's usable depth and weight capacity,
so the panel never mixes units. Entering inches is a separate question for every length field at once.

**11.238.4 RULED: THE ELEVATION PRINTS IT.** One line in the elevation sheet's notes band, the printed
dimension a cabinetmaker or general contractor can be handed before any DXF exists. It carries the
envelope and **that face's own door**: the front elevation the front door, the rear the rear. Printed in the
project's display units, as the sheet's load summary already is (an implementer's choice, stated). An
unknown dimension prints as a dash, never a guess (G4); a rack with no number known prints no line, a
ticked door alone included, since a row of dashes tells a reader nothing the absence does not. Every
starter ticks a door and enters no size; that is the case this sentence was refined for.

**CORRECTED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT: OWN WEIGHT IS NOT ON THE LINE, BY MEASUREMENT.** The note column is half
the band, **327 pt** on ANSI B through the real Jost metrics. A 1200 x 1400 x 2400 mm cabinet at 300 kg with
both clearances measured **331.5 pt**, so the sheet would have cut it with an ellipsis; without the weight
the same case is 299.6 pt metric and 285.4 imperial. Prefixing "RACK" to save the room would sit beside the
load summary's "RACK TOTAL", a different weight. So the line carries the size and that face's door, and own
weight stays in the inspector. `elevation_envelope_fit_test.dart` holds the fit against the real font,
because the core test's fake measurer passes any length.

**What this does not rule.** A fit check of the rack against a room, which DR-188 left open and this makes
possible. Whether rack presets carry the envelope. Whether rack elevations join the DXF export (v1.3).

**Scope.** No scope moves: fields the v1 model already declares, given a writer and a reader.

### 11.239 DR-240 · The ground bar note prints on both elevations, and the note band holds six lines

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-06, for `#1016`.** AC-034/m21 ruled that `Rack.groundBarPresent` feeds a
note on the elevation, and docs/04 §4 draws the checkbox with *"prints a note on the elevation (m21)"*. The
checkbox was built, saved and round-tripped, and nothing read it: the inverse of the `Placement.locked`
shape (§11.185.0), a writer with no reader. Three of the four starters tick it. The note band could not take
the line as it stood: it held five, and a rear sheet already fills five (the rear-detail note, the mirror
chip, the scale note, DR-239's envelope line, and the unlabelled-blocks note on a rack of 58 U or more).

**11.239.1 RULED: BOTH FACES.** The ground bar is a fact about the rack, as its envelope is, and the
envelope already prints on both. The front elevation alone was offered and refused: the person bonding the
bar is at the back of the rack reading `T2.02`. The rear alone costs the same band as both, because the
rear is the face that was already full.

**11.239.2 RULED: THE BAND HOLDS SIX LINES.** `kElevationHeaderBand` grows from 56 pt to 66 pt, still a
constant, so two otherwise identical racks keep printing at one ratio whichever notes apply. **Measured
before it was offered**, on ANSI B through the real Jost metrics, empty racks of 1 U to 60 U and every rack
of every starter: **one rack height changes ratio**, an empty 56 U from 1:8 to 1:10, and no starter moves.
The load summary keeps its own five-line budget; only the note column gains the row.

**11.239.3 RULED: THE WORDS.** `RACK GROUND BAR PRESENT. BOND TO BUILDING GROUND PER LOCAL CODE.`, which
measures 288.5 pt of the 327 pt column. It states the fact and the act m21's liability argument is about,
and names no jurisdiction, code section or conductor gauge: sizing is RJ-010's v1.2 work. A bare
`RACK GROUND BAR PRESENT.`, a TIA-607 `TGB` and an NEC grounding-electrode wording were offered beside it.

**Unticked prints nothing, the implementer's reading, stated.** `false` is the default every rack carries
whether or not anybody looked, so `NO GROUND BAR` would print a default as though it were a finding (G4's
reasoning, applied to a boolean). It is also `#1016`'s own DONE clause. **The line sits after the envelope
and before the unlabelled-blocks note**, so the two rack facts read together and the sheet's notice about
itself stays last; also the implementer's, stated.

**What this does not rule.** The bonding-detail sheet, a busbar entity and conductor sizing (RJ-010, v1.2).
Whether the export summary mentions the bar.

**Scope.** No scope moves: m21's own minimum, given the reader it was always owed.

### 11.240 DR-241 · The elevation sits 8 pt inside its frame, and a summary line too long for its column wraps

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-06, for `#1020`.** Rendering `T2.02` through pdfium for DR-240 showed every
note's first letter fused to the drawing-area frame, the load summary's last glyph touching the right edge,
and the top line touching the frame above. The graphic scale bar was worse: its zero tick is drawn on the
frame line itself, so the start of the one-foot bar a person checks with a tape measure disappears into the
border. Every element of the elevation was anchored at exactly the frame's edge. The legend had the same
defect and fixed it with an 8 pt inset; cover, exceptions, network and pinout use the same 8 pt.

Measuring the fix found a second, older defect. The `NOT DRAWN HERE` line grows with its counts and is
**already cut** with an ellipsis at three digits (331.7 pt against the 327 pt column), and an inset narrows
each column to 319 pt, so lines between those widths that print whole today would start being cut.

**11.240.1 RULED: 8 PT ALL ROUND, THE HOUSE STANDARD.** The elevation's whole body, note band, rack
drawing and scale band, sits 8 pt inside the drawing area on every side. **Measured before it was offered**,
over empty racks of 1 U to 60 U and every starter rack through the real Jost metrics: **one rack height
changes ratio**, an empty 55 U from 1:8 to 1:10; no starter moves and no overrun appears. A text-only inset
with 4 pt at the top and no ratio cost was offered beside it.

**11.240.2 RULED: A SUMMARY LINE TOO LONG FOR ITS COLUMN WRAPS AFTER ITS DASH**, onto the next row, instead
of being cut. The load summary is five lines at most and DR-240 gave the band six rows, so a wrapped line
always fits. **This amends §11.239.2's "the load summary keeps its own five-line budget"** (§12.52): the summary
still holds at most five lines, and may print them on six rows. Narrowing the gutter between the columns
(323 pt each, three-digit counts still cut) and filing the truncation separately were offered beside it.

**The break is after the em dash, the implementer's reading, stated**: the only summary line long enough to
wrap is the omission line, and its dash already separates the count from where the devices are. A line with
no dash that does not fit is still cut with an ellipsis, as today.

**What this does not rule.** The note column does not wrap: its six rows are all spoken for, and its widest
line measures 301.9 pt against 319.

**Scope.** No scope moves: a layout defect and a truncation, fixed on the sheet that already carries them.

### 11.241 DR-242 · The sheets say where the cable and port detail is, instead of saying it is not issued

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-07, for `#1030`.** Demonstrating M6's first clause (`#46`, all four
starters export a complete sheet set) read every page of every starter, and two notes printed in every
export state that the set does not carry what it carries:

- `T6.30`, on every page: *"EQUIPMENT AND RACK MATERIALS. CABLE AND POWER SCHEDULES NOT ISSUED IN THIS SET."*
  The Pull Sheet (`T6.10`) and the Termination Schedule (`T6.15`) are `ON` in every set since M6-K
  (`#977`, DR-222). Only the power schedule is absent, because `T6.40` is v1.1 (docs/08 §2.2).
- `T2.02`: *"REAR FACES SHOWN. PORT AND CONNECTION DETAIL NOT ISSUED IN THIS SET."* The rear elevation still
  draws no port strip, but `T6.15`, sorted rack then panel then port, is that detail and ships in every set.

**Both were true when written**, at M1, when no cable schedule existed, and no ruling dictated either
wording. Each became false the day M6-K shipped, and `starters_export_test.dart` asserted the `T6.30`
sentence on all four starters as intended behaviour. A set that contradicts itself is not a complete one,
so the clause waits on this.

**11.241.1 RULED: POINT TO THE SHEETS.** `T6.30` prints *"EQUIPMENT AND RACK MATERIALS. CABLE SCHEDULES: SEE
T6.10 AND T6.15. POWER SCHEDULE NOT ISSUED IN THIS SET."* `T2.02` prints *"REAR FACES SHOWN. PORT AND
CONNECTION DETAIL: SEE T6.15."* The sheet ids are the identities `rack_load_gutter.dart`'s `SEE T6.30` and
the title block's legend reference already print under both numbering schemes. Narrowing each note to its
true half, and dropping the `T6.30` note to its scope alone, were offered beside it.

**Measured before it was built**, in the bundled Jost: the `T6.30` note is 361.9 pt at 6.5 pt, 454.4 pt
with a three-digit `NOT IN A RACK` suffix, on an 11 in wide sheet; the rear note is 243.7 pt at 8 pt, down
from 294.7, in the 319 pt note column DR-241 measured.

**What this does not rule.** The rear elevation still draws no ports; CR-071 keeps the interactive rear panel
at v1.1 and nothing here schedules a port strip. A preset that drops `T6.10` or `T6.15` would make the
pointer false, and presets do not exist yet (docs/08 §2.4); **whoever builds them owes this note a
condition**.

**Scope.** No scope moves: two printed sentences corrected on the sheets that already carry them.

### 11.242 DR-243 · A cloned family's dash is chosen from one pattern per class, at the weights the palette already uses

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-07, for SFE-A3 (`#824`).** DR-122 §11.121.2 says the author of a clone
*"chooses a dash and a weight"* and names no menu, and the headroom query SFE-A3 builds has to enumerate
SOMETHING to say what is still free. Three menus were offered, each priced against the shipped palette:

| Offered | Size | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **One dash per class**, at every shipped weight | 13 classes × 5 weights | Every swatch reads differently in greyscale |
| Every dash pattern the catalogue ships | 37 patterns × 5 weights | `3,3`, `4,3`, `6,3` and `8,3` appear as four separate options, all class `short`, that a laser print barely separates |
| A typed pattern, checked live | unbounded | The nearest thing to the hand-rolled surface RJ-012 objected to, and a value cannot be previewed until it is valid |

**The user chose the first, which was the recommended option**, and gave no reason of their own; the
reasons in the table are the recommendation's.

**11.242.1 RULED: THE MENU IS THE PALETTE'S OWN CLASSES.** A clone's dash is one of the dash classes the
shipped palette draws (canon §14.2), one pattern each, crossed with the distinct weights the shipped
palette uses. **The menu is DERIVED from the seed rather than listed**, so it cannot drift from the palette
that `registry_parity.py` already holds to `pal1_check.py`. Which pattern stands for a class is the
implementation's choice, not the user's, and is recorded so it is not mistaken for one: **the pattern the
most shipped families use, ties broken by the smallest permille list**, because that is the one an
installer is likeliest to have seen in this product already.

**11.242.2 WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE.** PAL-1 is untouched. The gate still checks whatever dash and weight a
family carries, and the within-domain limb still compares exact patterns, so a menu narrower than the
rule refuses nothing the rule permits to exist: it declines to OFFER it. No shipped family moves;
`audio.mic` keeps `4,3` beside `audio.line_unbal`'s `6,3`.

**11.242.3 THE TICKET'S PREMISE, MEASURED.** SFE-A3 said *"digital video and ctl are the crowded groups"*.
That is true by family count and false by headroom. **What constrains a choice is the cross-domain
luminance band, not the number of siblings**, so the tightest domains are `str`, `ctl` and `net`,
and `video.digital` is among the roomiest. And a clone uses up exactly one combination in its own domain,
so *"none left"* is reached by repetition rather than being an everyday state. The query still reports
it as a state of its own (`isExhausted`), as the ticket asked. **The per-domain figures live in
`pal1_test.dart` and are not copied here**: the ones shown when this was offered were computed under a
provisional choice of pattern per class and differ from the built ones by one in three domains, which
is this corpus's argument against a second copy of a moving number, made again in miniature.

**Scope.** No scope moves: it settles a control DR-122 left open. Consumed by SFE-C2 (`#830`).

### 11.243 DR-244 · A clone may take any catalog connector as its default, and keeps its parent's direction and topology

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-07, for SFE-B1 (`#825`).** DR-122 §11.121.2 says a clone *"inherits
domain, direction, topology, connector and every field a rule reads"*, and the case it offers as proof
of the shape, `ctl.vantage`, is *"clone Cresnet, rename, change the connector to `conn.hardwired`"*. Both
cannot hold, and the clone command cannot be written until one gives.

**11.243.1 WHAT A FAMILY'S DEFAULTS ACTUALLY DO, READ RATHER THAN RECALLED.** §11.121.1 says
`defaultDirection`, `defaultTopology`, `defaultConnector` and `acceptedFamilies` *"are read by `TOP-003`,
`DIR-001`, `SIG-002` and `CON-001`"*. **None of the four reads a family.** Every rule reads the PORT's own
`direction`, `topology` and `connector` (`spring_back_rules.dart`, `connect_rules.dart`), and CON-001
checks the two ports' connectors against the catalog's `matesWith`. A family's three defaults are read in
exactly one place, the builder (`archetypes.dart`, `quick_add.dart`, `port_type_change.dart`), which
COPIES them into a port when one is made. And `acceptedFamilies` is a port field; a family has none.

**So RJ-012's objection survives, but by a different road than §11.121.1 drew.** A wrong default
direction or topology is copied into every port quick-added with that family, and the rules then judge
those ports confidently and wrongly. That is real, and it is why those two stay locked. A default
connector is copied the same way, but **what CON-001 judges is a real connector from the catalog against
the catalog's own mating table**, so a clone's choice of default cannot make any rule wrong. At worst it
pre-fills a port with a connector the person changes.

**11.243.2 THREE OPTIONS WERE OFFERED, EACH PRICED.**

| Offered | What it costs |
|---|---|
| **Any connector type in the registry**, defaulting to the parent's | 49 to choose from today; no free text, so no connector is invented |
| Inherit only | DR-122's text kept literally; the Vantage case becomes a by-hand connector change on every port, forever |
| Only connectors the catalog pairs with the parent | Measured: Cresnet's catalog ports use only `conn.phoenix_4`, so Vantage is unreachable, and 23 of 57 families have no catalog pairing at all |

A recommendation made before this was measured, *"a connector the parent already accepts"*, was offered
first and accepted, and is **withdrawn here because it has no host**: no family carries a list of
connectors it accepts, and the only proxy is the third row. **The user chose the first row**, the
re-made recommendation, and gave no reason of their own.

**11.243.3 RULED.** A clone inherits its parent's **domain, direction and topology, locked**. Its
**default connector** starts as the parent's and may be changed to **any connector type the registry
holds**. Connector types remain catalog-updated: this picks from them and never adds one, so RJ-012's
connector-editor limb and DR-122 §11.121.3 are untouched.

**11.243.4 WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE.** CR-078 (the clone's hue is its domain's). DR-243's dash and weight
menu. `@signal=`'s refusal (§11.121.5). Nothing about an EXISTING port moves: a default is read when a port
is made, never afterwards.

**Scope.** No scope moves; it settles a contradiction inside DR-122. §12.53 records the amendment.
Consumed by SFE-B1 (`#825`) and SFE-C1 (`#829`).

### 11.244 DR-245 · A cloned family travels inside the device library, and arrives without changing what is already drawn

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08, for SFE-C4 (`#832`) and the four chapters it became
(`#1033` to `#1036`).** DR-122 §11.121.6 writes a cloned family *"into `doc.registries.signalFamilies`
**and** onto the user's shelf"*. **The shelf could not hold one**: it is a directory of `.rmda` device
libraries, and the format carried device templates and nothing else.

**11.244.1 FAMILIES TRAVEL INSIDE THE LIBRARY, AND THE USER OVERRODE THE RECOMMENDATION TO SAY SO.** Three
homes were offered: a separate families file on the shelf (recommended, about a day), families inside
`.rmda` libraries, or project-only with the shelf half parked. **The user chose the library**: *"the blast
radius sucks but file portability FAR outweighs it."* A family stored apart from the device that uses it
is how a library arrives on another machine with half its ports unresolved; carried inside, a library is
self-contained the way DR-122 §11.121.6's RollerCoaster Tycoon precedent asks a project to be.

`.rmda` and `.rmdx` gain an optional `signalFamilies` list, one shared encoding with the document's. **A
library is written at schema v4 only when it carries a family; one that carries none stays v3.** That is
the implementation's choice, made on `documentMinReaderVersion`'s precedent: the decoder ignores unknown
keys, so an older build reading a v3-shaped library WITH families would drop them in silence and place
devices whose ports name nothing. At v4 the same build refuses with `NewerRmdaSchemaError`, *"so the loss
becomes a refusal somebody notices instead of a deletion nobody does."* An export carries every family
not in the shipped catalogue that its templates' ports name. DR-123 §11.122.6's *"does not touch `.rmdx`
or `.rmda`"* described DR-123's own scope and is not a bar on this; §12.54 records the reading.

**11.244.2 THE PERSONAL LIBRARY IS `My library`, CHOSEN BY THE USER.** A clone is written to
`My library.rpda` in the library directory, created on first use. This is **the first shelf write in the
product**: DR-123's authored devices (`#817`) are unbuilt and will write to the same file. DR-123
§11.122.4 governs it unchanged: **not a `Command`**, so undoing the clone does not remove it from the
library, and **a failure is a notice, never a refusal**, since the project write has already happened.

**11.244.3 ARRIVAL CHANGES NOTHING ALREADY DRAWN.** Placing a library device whose ports name a family the
project lacks brings that family with it (copy-on-place, AC-041, DR-103). Three cases, decided with no
prompt, on DR-103 §11.102.3's rule for templates, which the user chose to apply here:

| The project holds that id | Result |
|---|---|
| Nothing | The family is added as it arrives |
| An identical family | Nothing is added; the ports resolve to it |
| A **different** family | The newcomer gets a fresh id (`ctl.vantage_3`) and, if its name is taken in the domain, a numbered name; the arriving device's ports point to it |

**A newcomer that collides under PAL-1 is placed, and said.** The user chose this over refusing placement
and over placing silently: a notice names the collision in the clone refusal's own words, and Signal
families marks the family until its line is changed.

**11.244.4 A CLONE'S LINE CAN BE CHANGED, AND A SHIPPED FAMILY'S CANNOT.** The notice above was first
offered with *"fix its line"* attached, and **nothing could restyle a family**: SFE-B's census allows no
construction site but the clone. That was caught after the choice and re-asked with prices. The user chose
**Change line on clones**: the same greyscale grid, PAL-1-checked against the project, restyling every
cable of that family. **A shipped family's line stays as the CI gate certified it.**

**11.244.5 WHAT IS THE IMPLEMENTATION'S, NOT THE USER'S.** With families inside libraries, a clone no device
uses still needs a road into the next project, so Signal families lists the families the shelf's libraries
hold that the project does not, each with *Add to this project*, under §11.244.3's rules. Its place inside
the section the user chose for SFE-C1 is the implementation's choice.

**11.244.6 WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE.** CR-078 (a clone's hue is its domain's). DR-243's menu. DR-244's
locks. RJ-012's two remaining limbs. The `.rppj` document format, beyond SFE-C3's additive `clonedFrom` (`892cc8bd`).

**Scope.** No scope moves: it settles how DR-122 §11.121.6's shelf half is built. `#1033` to `#1036`.

### 11.245 DR-246 · A device can say which wireless networks it is on, and it ships with centralized lighting in a band of its own

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-09, from `#1038`** (*"Feasibility of adding wireless network support"*).
The need, in the user's words: *"some houses my firm has done may have two, three, or maybe even six
ZigBee networks depending on size/number of devices/design constraints."* And the trade facts the
protocols rest on, also theirs: *"Lutron's ClearConnectA and ClearConnectX protocols have similar
constraints to Z-Wave and ZigBee, respectively; Vantage I believe also uses the 900MhZ frequency band,
but in yet another proprietary standard with similar constraints to Z-Wave."* The Vantage band is the
user's belief and is recorded as one; CR-061 wants a source before any catalog or rule states it.

**11.245.1 TWO CORRECTIONS FIRST, BOTH TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED.** The ticket said Wi-Fi *"was rejected
at some point"*. **It was not.** DR-048 §11.47.10 kept network *values* off the template, and DR-227
§11.226.3 gave the template `wifi` on 2026-10-03, on the user's own ruling. What no ruling has ever
covered is **which** wireless network a device joins, and that gap is the same for Wi-Fi, ZigBee,
Z-Wave, ClearConnect and Vantage. Second, the ticket files this *"alongside the Lutron support that's
planned after v1"*. **Centralized lighting appeared in no band of roadmap §2**, which §8.3 makes the one
scope list. It is created below rather than assumed.

**11.245.2 PROPOSED, NOT OBJECTED TO: MEMBERSHIP, NOT LINKS.** A project-level list of wireless networks,
each with a name, a protocol, an optional coordinator or bridge device, and for Wi-Fi an SSID; a device
lists the networks it is on, **several where it has several radios** (a Control4 controller on ZigBee and
Wi-Fi, an RA3 processor on ClearConnect A and X). **Nothing is drawn on the schematic**: a mesh routes
itself, so a ZigBee link drawn between two dimmers would record a path no installer designed. This shape
was the feasibility's recommendation and the user answered every later question on top of it, but it
was not put as a question of its own, so field names and the protocol list are **re-opened at
decomposition**, not settled here.

**11.245.3 RULED BY THE USER, OVER THE RECOMMENDATION: IT SHIPS WITH CENTRALIZED LIGHTING.** Recommended
was v1.2 on its own, since membership is useful on any AV or security job without a lighting feature and
§2.3's own criterion (a format addition) places it there. The user bundled it with lighting, whose
keypads are where the six-network houses come from.

**11.245.4 RULED BY THE USER, OVER THE RECOMMENDATION: CENTRALIZED LIGHTING IS A BAND OF ITS OWN, v1.4.**
Recommended was v2, on roadmap §2.6's test that v2 *"changes what the product is"*; the user's own description
was that the product has *"gone from a simple diagramming tool to a light CAD package"*. Also offered:
v1.2, which would have promised a model that does not exist (there is no load, zone or circuit-to-load
model today). **The user created v1.4**, on DR-188 §11.187.3's precedent for v1.3. Its lighting row is a
**stub**: a title and the facts the user has given, with scope to be ruled.

**The panel facts given so far, in the user's words.** *"Lutron has a DIN-rail based system; Vantage uses
a 1x4 module panel, with a slot in the bottom for the controller; Control4 has its own panel with a
network switch enclosure & space for various amounts of modules depending on the panel size."* **None
of these fits `Rack`**, which counts RU and nothing else.

**11.245.5 RULED BY THE USER, ON G5: THE DATA SHAPE SHIPS IN v1 WITH NO UI.** A v1 build drops a
device-level key it does not model when it saves. The project's list of wireless networks and each
device's membership therefore load and save in v1, on `TemplateBody.submittedBy`'s precedent, so a v1
machine edits a v1.4 file and loses nothing. **The user first chose the other option**, stamping such a
file with a reader version a v1 build will not overwrite (`documentMinReaderVersion`'s precedent), and
**reversed it on being shown roadmap §1.1's filter 2**: *"Does omitting it cost a format migration, a
command-stack rewrite, or a reconstruct-and-confirm pass over user data? If yes the **model** ships in v1
even when the **UI** does not."* The feasibility should have cited G5 the first time and did not;
recorded because an answer given without the governing rule in view is not the same answer.

**THE PROTOCOL IS A REGISTRY ROW, NOT AN ENUM, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE RESERVATION WORK.**
`json_codec.dart` decodes every enum strictly, and *"a newer build that adds a value is expected to raise
`minReaderVersion`"*. A protocol enum frozen in v1 would therefore bring back the read-only lockout this
clause declines the first time v1.4 adds a protocol. A registry carried in the document, as signal
families are, lets a newer file bring its own rows. Which rows are seeded is not ruled here.

**11.245.6 RULED BY THE USER, ON G5: A TEMPLATE SAYS WHICH RADIOS IT HAS, AND THE CHANGE IS MADE IN v1.**
DR-227's `wifi` is replaced **before release**, while no user file holds a value and no seeded template
sets one, so it is a rename with no migration ever; a check can then flag a device put on a network its
model cannot join. **Reversed on the same filter**: the user first chose to wait for v1.4, which would have
cost a migration of every saved `wifi: true` and, because a template body keeps no unknown keys (roadmap
§2.2, the `submittedBy` row), a v1 build saving a template from a newer file would have dropped its radios.

**THE SHAPE KEEPS UNKNOWN PER RADIO, AND A SET WOULD NOT.** A plain set of radios turns every radio not
ticked into a stated *no*: a template marked Wi-Fi would claim to have no ZigBee, a fabricated fact under
G4. Each radio is therefore yes, no or unknown, and an absent radio is unknown (CR-114: an absent key).
The Device Builder's *Wi-Fi* toggle keeps working as the Wi-Fi member, DR-227 §11.226.2's Devices view
keeps listing a device whose Wi-Fi is yes, and no other radio has a surface until v1.4.

**11.245.7 RULED: NO RANGE CHECK.** Plan positions know nothing of walls, floors or materials, so a
distance verdict would be an estimate printed as a fact, which G4 forbids. **A count per network
against a cited limit is checkable** and is the candidate rule; it ships, if at all, with its source
(CR-061) and its fixture pair (AC-051).

**11.245.8 A STRUCTURED MEDIA ENCLOSURE IS NOT A LIGHTING PANEL, AND THE USER'S EVIDENCE SAYS SO.** The
feasibility proposed that one non-RU host might serve lighting panels and structured media enclosures,
since docs/01 describes the latter as *"module bays rather than RUs"*. **The user refuted it with two
photographs of installed cans**: *"Structured media enclosures are a bit trickier, as those are usually
a lot more free-form in nature."* What they show: a perforated back plate with a splitter and a
switch enclosure fixed wherever its holes allowed, cable dressed freely around them; and a hinged
door that itself carries a device, an access point. That is free placement on a hole grid, on more
than one surface, not a row of bays. **docs/01's "module bays" is the derived sentence that misled the
proposal.** The photographs are not committed: they are of an installed home.

**Scope.** **A scope change**, per §8.3, carried in its own commit. Creates roadmap §2.5 for v1.4 with
two rows (centralized lighting, a stub; wireless network membership, its surfaces) and renumbers the old
§2.5 to §2.7 as §2.6 to §2.8. **v1 grows by two data shapes and no surface**: the wireless network
registry and membership (§11.245.5), and the per-radio capability replacing `TemplateBody.wifi`
(§11.245.6, §12.55). `#1038`.

**What this does not rule.** The lighting band's contents: loads, zones, circuits, keypad engraving,
processor link limits. **How a lighting panel is modelled**: three vendors' panels described in a
sentence each is not a model, and it wants a census of real panels (slot counts, rail lengths, module
widths, where the controller and the switch sit) before anybody designs one. **How a structured media
enclosure is modelled**, if ever, after §11.245.8. Whether a Wi-Fi network records its passphrase (the
recommendation will be never, since a project file is emailed to clients and trades). Which protocols
are seeded and how each is named.

### 11.246 DR-247 · Wireless distance is checked as advisory with its source shown, and lighting delivers a load schedule and an engraving schedule

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-09**, answering the five questions of LIGHT-0's census
(`docs/research/research-domain-lighting.md` §9, `#1041`). One answer amends DR-246; one adds scope to
roadmap §2.5's lighting stub; three are trade facts recorded in the user's words.

**11.246.1 RULED BY THE USER: DR-246 §11.245.7 IS AMENDED, AND WIRELESS DISTANCE IS CHECKED AS ADVISORY.**
§11.245.7 refused a range check because plan positions know no walls, so a distance verdict *"would be an
estimate printed as a fact"*. **The census refuted the premise**: Lutron's own design rules are
straight-line distances (*"within 30 ft (9.1m) of the RadioRA 3 processor or Repeater"*, *"within 75ft
(22.9m) of the processor"*), so checking them checks Lutron's rule rather than estimating propagation.
**The user then gave Control4's**, in their words: *"ZigBee does have a rule of thumb that Control4
operates on (the bulk of ZigBee installations currently, AFAIK) of 15-20 feet max between devices, and
no more than 300 feet from the ZAP (ZigBee Access Point)."* Offered with G4's own text (roadmap §1.1
filter 4: a heuristic that has not earned authority *"is cut or demoted"*) and CR-061, the user chose
the recommendation:

- a distance check is **advisory**, and every finding says **straight line** and names its threshold's
  **source and grade**: a manufacturer's published rule is not a firm's rule of thumb, and the finding
  says which it is;
- each threshold is **editable per protocol**, because a rule of thumb is a firm's to set;
- **a device on a different plan sheet from what it is measured against is counted as unchecked, never
  passed.** A plan is two-dimensional per sheet and the model carries no floor heights, so a keypad
  upstairs and a ZAP downstairs have no computable distance (G4: report the unknown count).

Not taken: Lutron's published rules only, which is stricter under G4 and skips the protocol most of
the user's installs use; and §11.245.7 kept as ruled. **Not ruled here**: the rule's ID (assigned at
decomposition, with its fixture pair under AC-051), and the default for a range the user gave as
*"15-20 feet"*. The option offered showed 20 ft.

**11.246.2 LEFT UNRULED BY THE USER: LUTRON'S 6 FT SEPARATION.** Lutron 3691055f says *"Mount the panel
so that line-voltage wiring will be at least 6 ft (1.8 m) from audio or electronic equipment and
wiring."* The user: *"Let's leave that one unruled for now; make a note of it for the start of the
epic."* Noted on Epic `#1040`'s description, where the epic's decomposition will read it.

**11.246.3 TRADE FACT: WHERE A LIGHTING PROCESSOR LIVES DEPENDS ON THE JOB.** In the user's words: *"It
depends entirely on the job, but Lutron/Control4/Vantage panels are designed to hold their respective
lighting controllers. Most of the time, we aim to have them in an enclosure if we are using centralized
lighting, but for setups that are based around the wireless systems (RadioRA3 & some HomeWorks products
like Sunnata) the processor will live on a rack/in a low voltage enclosure. Caseta devices do not have a
dedicated panel, so those exclusively live on racks or in enclosures, or oftentimes mounted to the
outside of one."* **What it means for a model**, stated as a constraint and not as a design: a panel's
control compartment is one place a processor can be, never the place it is; the same processor model
sits in a panel on one job and on a rack on the next, and a Caséta bridge is sometimes mounted on the
outside of an enclosure, which no host in RackPal describes today.

**11.246.4 RULED BY THE USER: v1.4's LIGHTING DELIVERS A LOAD SCHEDULE AND A KEYPAD ENGRAVING SCHEDULE.**
Asked what the firm hands over: *"Both ideally, neither typically (partially a documentation issue,
partially a culture issue. I'd want to have both be deliverables though)."* Both join roadmap §2.5's
lighting row. **What each prints is not ruled**; the census lists what Lutron's own load-schedule tool
records (circuit, feed and zone name per load), at summary grade.

**11.246.5 TRADE FACT, RESOLVING A CONFLICT IN VANTAGE'S OWN SHEET: SEVEN ENCLOSURES PER CONTROLLER.**
The IMPE/ISPE sheet says both *"Up to six Secondary Enclosures"* and *"up to 5 additional enclosures per
controller"*. The user: *"It's actually 7 panels (One main + six secondary) for a total of 28 modules for
one controller."* Six secondaries, four modules in each of seven enclosures.

**Scope.** **A scope change**, per §8.3, carried in its own commit. Roadmap §2.5: the lighting row gains
the two schedules; the wireless row's *"No range check"* becomes the advisory check of §11.246.1.
§12.56. No v1 change.

### 11.247 DR-248 · Nothing is adopted until it is fourteen days old, Flutter moves to 3.47.5, and the lint set moves to 11

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-11, for `#1046`**, on the request *"Let's go ahead and update all of
our dependencies, if possible; many of them show entire version releases available."*

**11.247.1 WHAT "ALL OF THEM" MEANT, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS OFFERED.** `flutter pub outdated` on
`b2482999` split the list three ways: fourteen packages that move inside their existing constraints
(`archive`, `image`, `pdf`, `vm_service` and ten transitive ones), one that needs a constraint edit
(`very_good_analysis`), and the rest held where they are **by the Flutter SDK itself** (`meta`,
`vector_math`, `test`, `analyzer`, `xml` and others are pinned by Flutter 3.44.4). Updating everything
therefore means moving the Flutter pin, which docs/11 §7 calls *"load-bearing"* and `ensure_flutter.ps1`
says must move as *"a deliberate, reviewed step"*. Both texts were quoted in the question.

**11.247.2 RULED BY THE USER, A STANDING RULE: NO RELEASE IS ADOPTED UNTIL IT IS FOURTEEN DAYS OLD.** It
applies to every pub package, direct or transitive, and to the Flutter SDK, measured from the
publication date on pub.dev or the release date in Flutter's release feed, against the day the
upgrade is made. **An exception needs a named reason in the commit that takes it**, and a security
fix is the reason anticipated. The evidence the question carried: `archive` published 4.4.0 and 4.5.0
on 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11, and `image` four releases across the same two days. That is most likely
a maintainer at work and is also the shape a hijacked publish takes, and waiting costs nothing.

**11.247.3 RULED BY THE USER: FLUTTER MOVES FROM 3.44.4 TO 3.47.5.** The newest stable at least
fourteen days old on 2026-10-11 (released 2026-09-18, Dart 3.13.4). Not taken: 3.47.7, three days old;
and 3.44.9, the same minor line, which would leave most of the outdated list where it is.
`screen_retriever` 0.3.0 (2026-10-08, needing Flutter 3.47 or later) waits for the rule, not for the
SDK.

**A REJECTION'S PREMISE CHANGES, AND THE REJECTION DOES NOT.** DR-138 declined `pdfrx` partly because
2.x *"needs Flutter 3.47 / Dart 3.13"* against the 3.44.4 pin. That limb no longer holds. DR-153 built
the vendored pdfium binding since, so nothing is reopened; recorded so nobody reads DR-138's version
argument as current.

**11.247.4 RULED BY THE USER: `very_good_analysis` MOVES FROM 9.0.0 TO 11.0.0, AND THE INFO PIN RISES ONLY
BY WHAT CANNOT BE FIXED CHEAPLY.** docs/11 §8 pins the lint set *"exactly"* and says the info ratchet
*"only moves down"*. A stricter lint set raises the count on code nobody touched, so the new infos that
are mechanical are fixed in the same work and the pin rises only by the remainder, with the reason
written in `analyze_info_baseline.txt` as earlier moves were. The pin rises because the rules got
stricter, not because the code got worse. Not taken: raising the pin by everything, and staying on 9.0.0.

**11.247.5 RULED BY THE USER: `pubspec.lock` IS COMMITTED.** docs/03 §10.2 had flagged it as *"a project
decision, not a CI one"*: the lockfile was gitignored, so CI resolved the newest allowed version of every
package on each run, and *"the Flutter SDK is pinned exactly and the package graph is not."* §11.247.2
makes that gap decisive rather than tolerable. **A cooldown that the lockfile does not record holds on
the machine that ran the upgrade and nowhere else**: a clean clone would have resolved `archive` 4.5.0,
published the morning of the ruling. So the lockfile is committed, CI builds the graph the local gates
ran, the pub cache is keyed on it, and every dependency change is a visible diff. Dart's own guidance
is to commit the lockfile of an application, which RackPal is. Not taken: keeping it ignored, which
leaves the cooldown as advice for local upgrades only.

**Scope.** No product scope moves. A process rule (§11.247.2), two pins, and a committed lockfile (§11.247.5). `#1046`.

**What this does not rule.** A gate that enforces the cooldown; today it is a rule the person
upgrading follows, and a gate needs the network in CI. The global Flutter SDK on any developer's
machine, which is theirs to switch.

### 11.248 DR-249 · CR-080 is amended to the faces that ship: Jost for text, Space Mono for `RackMono`, and `RackCond` is retired

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-17, for `#1061`**, a finding of that day's sync audit of the
documents, the OKF bundle and the board.

**11.248.1 THE FACT, AND WHY A COMMENT WAS NOT ENOUGH.** CR-080 (§1.8) rules `RackBody` = IBM Plex
Sans, `RackCond` = IBM Plex Sans Condensed, `RackMono` = IBM Plex Mono, fallback Noto Sans Symbols 2.
`apps/rackpal/assets/fonts/` holds **Jost** Regular and Medium and **Space Mono** Regular and Bold,
and no Plex and no Noto. The swap landed at `0545090`; M8-H3 to M8-H5 (`#771`, `#772`, `#773`,
`#1029`) extended it. `apps/rackpal/pubspec.yaml` says *"This supersedes CR-080's font pick"*, and
§11.6 consequence 9 noted the drift and declined to rule on it. A pubspec comment is not an
amendment (roadmap §8.3), so CR-080 stayed binding over a bundle that contradicted it, and every
derived document that names the face followed the ruling rather than the tree.

**11.248.2 RULED BY THE USER: THE FACES ARE THE BUNDLE AS BUILT.** The text face (`RackBody`'s role)
is **Jost**, Regular 400 and Medium 500, in the modified build `tools/build_jost_glyphs.py` produces
and `tools/glyph_coverage_check.py` holds. `RackMono` is **Space Mono**, Regular and Bold. **CR-080's
other rulings stand**: each face is bundled twice (fonts and assets), only SIL OFL 1.1 faces ship, and
no system font is ever reached for. Not taken: reverting to Plex, offered with its cost (undoing
M8-H3 to H5, rebuilding the added glyphs for another face, retargeting every `FontRef('Jost')`
fixture and the coverage gate, and re-baselining PDF metrics).

**CR-080's three arguments, re-checked against the files rather than carried over.** Measured on
2026-10-17 by reading each TTF's `glyf` contours:

- **Disambiguation holds in the mono face only, and the mono face is not printed.** Space Mono's `0`
  has three contours against `O`'s two, a marked zero. Jost's `0` and `O` both have two and differ
  only in width. So the argument CR-080 made for identifiers transcribed onto physical labels would be
  met where an identifier is set in `RackMono`, and is **not** met in Jost. **The PDF embeds one face,
  Jost Regular** (`kExportFont` in `apps/rackpal/lib/src/session/export_controller.dart`; Medium and
  `RackMono` serve the Flutter widgets only), so **every printed identifier, `CABLE ID` included, is in
  Jost and carries no marked zero.** Space Mono's zero reaches the screen, not the paper. *(This bullet
  said on its first commit that docs/08 §10.1's `RackMono` `CABLE ID` column met the argument on paper.
  docs/08 states the design, not the exporter; the DOCS-2i pass found the gap the same day, before the
  ruling merged.)* Whether the PDF should embed Space Mono for identifier columns is a product question
  this ruling does not answer; it is `#1099`, answered by DR-252 (§11.251): the PDF embeds Space Mono for
  identifier columns.
- **The condensed cut** is §11.248.3.
- **Greek coverage holds, by different codepoints.** Jost carries `U+03A9` and `U+00B5`; Space Mono
  carries `U+2126` (the ohm sign) and `U+00B5`, and not `U+03A9`. A string that names one ohm
  codepoint in a mono column and the other in text finds a gap in one of them. The coverage gate sees
  string literals only, so this is recorded rather than assumed covered.

**11.248.3 RULED BY THE USER: `RackCond` IS RETIRED.** Jost has no condensed cut and none ships;
schedules are set in Jost, as they print today, and the role leaves docs/08 §10.1. **The option as
offered overstated its evidence, and the correction belongs here**: it said M6's sheets already pass
their legibility checks without a condensed face. M6's machine clauses (1, 2 and 4) are
`DEMONSTRATED` without one; **the physical print clauses (AC-054, `#48`, `#49`) are unperformed**, and
a schedule column too tight for Jost at its printed size is exactly what they would show. If they do,
that is new evidence and a new ruling, not a reading of this one. Not taken: keeping the role as owed
debt with a second family chosen later.

**11.248.4 CARRIED IN THE CHOSEN OPTION: NO FALLBACK FACE SHIPS.** The Noto Sans Symbols 2 fallback
was never bundled. The option the user chose named the glyph-coverage gate as what stands in for it,
so that is the ruling: the face's own build carries the codepoints the product emits, and
`tools/glyph_coverage_check.py` reads the binary to hold them. Its blind spot is in its own header and
is restated here: runtime-composed strings and user data are not literals, and a codepoint neither
face carries draws as nothing.

**Scope.** No product scope moves; this ratifies what ships. §12.57. The derived-document edits are
owed and listed on `#1073`.

**What this does not rule.** `RackMono` Italic, which docs/08 §10.1 wants for a derived `LEN` and
`FontRef` cannot express (no slant field); it stays where docs/12 §4.6 left it. The wordmark, which is
DR-089's and is outlines rather than text. Whether a future face change needs this much ceremony: it
does, for the same reason this one did.

### 11.249 DR-250 · The beta gate is M9's judgement, over a floor of five projects and no open bug that loses data or prints a wrong fact

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-17, for `#1062`.** It answers §10.11, which was **deferred on
2026-08-03 with a trigger**: held until M5 landed, and owed before the M6-J5 recruiting ask (`#362`),
because three people cannot be asked to commit real jobs without being told what will be judged. M5
closed on 2026-09-07 (DR-135); the trigger had fired five weeks before anybody noticed, which the
2026-10-17 sync audit found.

**11.249.1 RULED BY THE USER: THE JUDGEMENT GOVERNS, AND A FLOOR STOPS IT PASSING ON FRIENDLY USERS.**
§10.11's own recommendation, option (a) with (b) as a floor. **M9's exit criterion governs exactly as
roadmap §4 writes it**: three integrators have each produced a sheet set they were willing to send to
a client or a job site, and none of the three needed to leave the app to fix something. **The floor**,
both limbs read at the moment the gate is read, never averaged over the beta:

1. **The five real projects** of M9's checklist have each been run end to end.
2. **No open bug loses data or prints a wrong fact.** A wrong fact is a printed value that disagrees
   with the document it came from; an unknown printed as `—` is not one (G4, CR-114).

The floor cannot pass the beta on its own; it can only stop it. Not taken: the judgement alone, which
§10.11 calls gameable by three people who like the author; and a metric alone (N projects, N cables,
no P1 for N weeks), which measures whatever is easiest to count. **A date, §10.11's option (c), was not
offered**, because nothing in the record supplies the external pressure §10.11 names as the only
thing that would make one happen regardless.

**11.249.2 WHAT THIS LEAVES TO M9'S DECOMPOSITION, STATED SO IT IS NOT READ AS RULED.** How a bug is
marked as losing data or printing a wrong fact on the board (a tag, at M9-D's decomposition, `#442`).
**Who the three integrators are**: DR-006 made them three internal users, and DR-036 then made the
project public without saying whether that changed RISK-08's population back. That is the question
`#362` exists to start, and it is the user's.

**Scope.** No scope moves. §10.11 is answered; §13's row says so. `#362` is no longer waiting on a
definition.

### 11.250 DR-251 · DR-096's record exclusion covers the bundle's decisions and its log, and not its live reference pages

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-17, for `#1063`**, a finding of that day's sync audit.

**11.250.1 THE FACT.** DR-096 §11.95.2 ruled *"rename the PRODUCT, never the RECORD"* and listed *"the
`.okf` decision bundle (191, of which 95 are the decision files)"* as record, so the sweep left the
whole bundle alone. About 150 old package paths remain (`rackmate_core`, `rackmate_ui`,
`apps/rackmate` and their kin): roughly half in `decisions/`, and the rest in `practices/`,
`invariants/`, `gates/` and `log.md`. **The pages that are not history are the problem.** A gate or
invariant page tells a reader where the test that enforces it lives, and
`gates/byte-exactness-sweep.md` carries `resource: apps/rackmate/test/gitattributes_byte_exactness_test.dart`,
a file that no longer exists. An agent following a gate page to its test lands nowhere.

**11.250.2 RULED BY THE USER: THE BUNDLE SPLITS INTO RECORD AND LIVE REFERENCE.**

- **Record**, kept in the words of their day: `.okf/decisions/` and `.okf/log.md`. A decision page
  says what was ruled under the name and paths of its time, as a canon blockquote does.
- **Live**, taking current paths and the RackPal name: `.okf/gates/`, `.okf/invariants/`,
  `.okf/practices/`, `.okf/getting-started.md` and `.okf/index.md`. A path inside a quotation on a
  live page stays quoted, with the current path in live prose beside it (§11.95.2's own practice).

Not taken: the whole bundle staying record, which keeps a dead `resource:` pointer and every gate page
pointing at paths that do not exist; and the whole bundle going live, which rewrites decision pages
and the log, the thing §11.95.2 exists to forbid.

**Scope.** No product scope moves. It narrows §11.95.2's reach (§12.58). The substitution is owed on
`#1087`, and the orientation pages' name on `#1081`.

### 11.251 DR-252 · The PDF embeds Space Mono, and identifier columns print in it

**Settled by the user on 2026-10-17, for `#1099`**, the question DR-249 §11.248.2 left open.

**11.251.1 THE FACT.** The PDF embeds one face, Jost Regular: `kExportFont` in
`apps/rackpal/lib/src/session/export_controller.dart` registers `FontRef('Jost')` alone, and
`sheet_frame.dart`'s `kSheetFont` resolves to it. Space Mono, whose zero is marked (three contours
against `O`'s two), reaches the screen and never the paper, so every printed cable ID, designator and
port label is in the face where `0` and `O` differ only by width. CR-080's first argument for a mono
face, that identifiers are transcribed onto physical labels, is not met on any sheet the product prints.

**11.251.2 RULED BY THE USER: THE EXPORT EMBEDS SPACE MONO, AND THE IDENTIFIER COLUMNS USE IT.** Where
docs/08 §10.1 sets a column in `RackMono`, the printed sheet sets it in Space Mono. The question carried
its price: the `pdf` package subsets each embedded font (`TtfWriter`), so the file grows by the glyphs
used and not by the 99 KB face, an amount measured at build rather than assumed; `ExportRequest`'s font
map already takes several faces; about 63 font-choice sites across 24 sheet builders read `kSheetFont`
today, and measured widths change, so truncation, fit and dry-run tests re-baseline. Not taken: keeping
one face and recording the risk; and embedding Jost Medium as well.

**Scope.** Not new scope: it builds what docs/08 §10.1 already specifies and DR-249 ratified as the mono
face. Built as `MONO-A`, `#1104`, under M6. AC-054's print clauses read the result.

**What this does not rule.** Which columns are identifiers beyond docs/08 §10.1's table, which `MONO-A`'s
decomposition reads. Whether Space Mono Bold is embedded, which follows from whether a column docs/08
sets bold is in scope. Jost Medium in print, which was offered and not taken.

## 12. Superseded rulings

Every ruling in Parts 1–3 that DR-001…DR-036 change or void, plus the small set of internal
contradictions the amendment sweep exposed and which are ruled here so the record does not
contradict itself. **A ruling not listed below stands exactly as written in Parts 1–3.**

Each entry gives the ID, what it said, and what now governs.

### 12.1 Superseded by DR-001 (net labels by default)

| Ruling | What it said | What now governs |
|---|---|---|
| **CR-013** | "Sugiyama layering + interval-graph channel routing, full deterministic recompute", with phase 5 (crossing sweep, hop arcs) moved to paint time. | **Superseded in part.** v1 builds **Sugiyama phases 0–3 only** (cycle-break, layer, barycentre sweep, coordinate assignment) which place symbols. Phase 4 (interval-graph channel routing) moves to **v1.2**, gated on evidence that filtered density warrants it. Phase 5 (crossing sweep + hops) is **not built**. `drawn` mode uses a deterministic layer-ordered orthogonal staircase per Link with no channel allocation. Everything CR-013 *deleted* stays deleted: `ObstacleField`, `RouteCache` and "obstacle-aware" remain banned names, the v1 router is not obstacle-aware either, it is simpler still. The interval-graph insight remains the right answer *if* #4 is ever built; it is not wrong, it is not yet needed. |
| **AC-016 #17** | Dash phase diverges across hop arcs; document it in the visual language; suppress hops on control and structure. | **Moot in v1.** No arcs are drawn, so no arc dash-phase divergence exists and there are no hops to suppress. The finding is retained as a v1.2 note attached to CR-013 phase 4. **The other half survives:** `dashPath` is still on the hot path for straight dashed segments and is still explicitly profiled in the perf harness rather than assumed cheap. |
| **AC-016 #20** | "sub-millisecond at N=300" ignores that crossings are unbounded by N; move the Bentley–Ottmann sweep and hop generation to paint time, viewport-scoped; cap hops to `gap` above a threshold; measure X on a real 300-connection fixture. | **Moot in v1.** No sweep, no hops, no cap, no X. **The 300-connection fixture survives** and changes purpose: it is now the layout-determinism and **label-density** fixture, and the thing measured on it is text-run count and commit time for the label layer, not crossings. |
| **AC-040**, density-table half | Kept `design-ux-schematic.md §1.5`'s automatic degradation to net labels above a per-sheet threshold. | **Inverted.** There is no degradation and no threshold, because labels are the base state. The **rule-catalogue half of AC-040 is untouched** and still governs, see §12.6 for its arithmetic. |
| **§7.2.3**, wiring scope table | "Domain filter bar, **auto net-label degradation**, symbol collapse to vector pins, `Alt`-hover transient focus". | The domain filter bar, symbol collapse and `Alt`-hover **stay and are load-bearing**. "Auto net-label degradation" is replaced by **"net labels as the default render; drawn wires on domain filter, hover or focus (DR-001 §11.1.1)"**. |

Phase 4 (interval-graph channel routing) is **v1.2**, gated on evidence. Phase 5 (crossing sweep, hop arcs) is **not built**. Nothing runs at paint time. The Part 3 preamble's "Part 3 governs the release bucket" rule does not apply here, because Part 3 contradicts *itself* (§7.2.7 vs §7.3) and CR-071 is the only source that is internally consistent. |

### 12.9 Superseded by DR-006 (internal tool, self-signed distribution)

**A numbering note, stated so nobody renumbers.** This subsection is §12.9 and not §12.6, even
though it breaks the DR-order of §12.1…§12.5, because **§12.6(a)–(d) are cited by those exact
sub-letters** across this record and the authored documents (§12.6(b) sets the 27-rule count,
§12.6(c) is PAL-1's ruling, §12.6(d) is the zone grid). Renumbering to keep the DR-order tidy would
silently break every one of those citations, which is a worse outcome than an out-of-order heading.

| Ruling | What it said | What now governs |
|---|---|---|
| **AC-058 (D10)**, procurement half | "Windows OV/EV certificate procurement **starts two milestones before release** because reputation-building takes weeks." | **Superseded in part.** No OV/EV certificate is procured, at M6 or anywhere. Signing is **self-signed** (`New-SelfSignedCertificate`, `Set-AuthenticodeSignature` **with a timestamp server**, public `.cer` to `LocalMachine\Root` and `\TrustedPublisher`, ideally by GPO) with **Microsoft Trusted Signing as the named fallback**, adoptable at M8. The lead time D10 was defending against is specific to OV/EV identity verification, the SmartScreen reputation ramp and hardware-token logistics; §11.6.1 shows none of the three attaches to either path DR-006 names. **The rest of D10 stands**: macOS notarisation and stapling, vendored pdfium (CR-100), release pipeline with symbol archival. |
| **§9.7 (M6)** exit criterion, last sentence | "Windows OV/EV certificate procurement starts here, two milestones before release." | **Deleted.** M6 has no distribution obligation of any kind. Every other clause of M6's exit criterion, the complete sheet set on all four starters, the deuteranopia/protanopia and greyscale verification, the ANSI B / ANSI D / photocopy sign-off (AC-058 D13), requirement 7, is **unchanged**. |
| **§9.9 (M8)** exit criterion, first clause | "A signed installer runs on a clean Windows 11 machine **with no SmartScreen warning**." | **Split: §11.6.2.** No build-side property can deliver "no SmartScreen warning": SmartScreen evaluates **Mark-of-the-Web**, which is a property of how a file arrived, not of the binary. The **build-side gate** is: signed, timestamped, valid publisher in file properties, **and the signature still validates after the signing certificate has expired**. The **distribution-side requirement** is documented and not gated: Local Intranet UNC or Intune/GPO, and the ZIP trap stated explicitly. M8's other three clauses (cold start within budget, an induced crash producing a report with no project content, documented limits behaving as documented) are **unchanged**. |
| **§7.2.8**, code-signing row | "Windows code signing with certificate procurement started **two milestones early**; vendored pdfium; release pipeline with symbol archival." | **The procurement clause is superseded**; read the row as self-signed with a timestamp, no early procurement, Trusted Signing as the named fallback. **Vendored pdfium and the release pipeline are unaffected.** |
| **`RISK-07`** (roadmap §7) | "Code-signing certificate lead time blocks a finished build … prefer EV to avoid the SmartScreen reputation ramp." | **Retired in this form.** Replaced by a smaller, wholly internal risk: the public `.cer` is not deployed to the target machine's stores. Likelihood low, impact minor, early warning "a clean test machine shows *Unknown publisher*", mitigation a GPO. |
| **`RISK-08`** (roadmap §7) | "Beta integrators cannot be recruited in time for M9." | **Population changes; the risk does not disappear.** Three integrators become three internal users on three real jobs. **M9's exit criterion is unchanged** and is still a judgement, not a metric. |
| **RJ-014**, certificate sentence | "The part that genuinely cannot wait (the code-signing certificate, whose OV/EV validation and reputation build take weeks) is accepted and scheduled two milestones ahead of release (AC-058/D10)." | **Superseded in that sentence only.** Nothing needs scheduling ahead. RJ-014's ruling (**no in-app auto-update in v1**, a signed installer plus a "Check for updates" item and a version string) is **reaffirmed**, and the `.rmdev` user-library migration half (AC-050/A8.2) is untouched. |
| **§10.3** | Pricing and licensing model; recommendation (c), a free tier with a watermarked PDF. | **Moot while DR-006 stands**: there is nothing to price. Retained in full as the record of the argument. **If DR-006 is reversed, §10.3 reopens exactly as written**, watermark hazard included. Indexed at §13. |

### 12.10 DR-007 supersedes nothing (keystone strap geometry into M3)

**No entry, and the absence is the record.** DR-007 is the first ruling in Part 4 that voids no
Part 1–3 ruling. It is an **addition** to v1 scope made under roadmap §8.3, not a reversal, so a
reader looking for its supersession list is not missing one.

It **extends** two rulings without changing either. `Outlet` remains "ONE WALL PLATE / ONE CEILING
LOCATION" (**CR-016**) and gains an ordered gang list, the alternative, one `Outlet` per gang,
was rejected precisely because it would have redefined CR-016 rather than extended it.
**CR-121**'s keystone rule is consumed as written: the keystone follows `jacketColorId`, never
`jacketColorPulledId`. **CR-047** (the arbitrary-depth location tree), **CR-108** (outlet
templates) and **CR-112** (the project-level Locations panel) are untouched and already carry M3
checklist items.

What DR-007 does change is a **cost**, and §12.7's re-costing should be read with it: M3 stays
`M` but at the upper end, because its exit criterion, a 60-drop rough-in producing a Pull Sheet,
does not itself require strap geometry. The ruling accepts that growth deliberately, on the ground
that building the `Outlet` editor twice is worse work than building it once with the grid designed
in. See §11.7.

### 12.18 Superseded by DR-044 (the shipped templates carry terminations)

**One clause, and it is the shortest-lived entry in this section: hours.** DR-043 was ruled on
2026-08-11 and DR-044 superseded a clause of it the same day, before any of it was built.

| Ruling | What it said | What now governs |
|---|---|---|
| **DR-043 §11.42.5** | The six shipped `OutletTemplate`s are **not** seeded with terminations and stay null, because *"a shop authoring its own template says what it terminates in"*, on DR-024 §11.23.2's precedent. | **Superseded.** **All nine shipped templates are seeded** (§11.43.3). The clause failed on a fact rather than on a judgement: **nothing in this product can author an `OutletTemplate`**, so the sentence describes a capability that does not exist, and the field would have been null everywhere for ever. The DR-024 precedent was also mis-cited: that ruling refused a **standards citation**, and a termination is a recipe fact of the same kind as the cable count already in the recipe. |
| **DR-043 §11.42.2**, the template is the load-bearing path | **Restored rather than superseded.** The argument was sound and its premise was false; §11.43 supplies the premise. **Its cap survives**: a shop still cannot author its own recipe, and §11.43.5 records that as live rather than discharged. |

**Nothing else in DR-043 moves.** The default stays Unspecified (§11.42.1), the colon grammar
(§11.42.3), the vocabulary rule (§11.42.4) and the batch machinery (§11.42.6) are untouched.

**Why this is a §12 entry and DR-042 was not.** DR-042 replaced a figure that had been deliberately
recorded as a **stated choice** precisely so it could be replaced silently, so there was nothing to
withdraw. This voids a **clause of a ruling**, which is the thing §12 exists to index. The contrast
is the whole practical argument for §11.40.4's discipline: one of these needed an entry here and the
other did not.

### 12.19 Corrected by DR-047 (a gang can be fitted with a pass-through)

**A premise rather than a judgement, and it is listed because §12's preamble makes an unlisted
sentence read as still binding.** DR-045 filed the pass-through plate honestly and did not model it;
what it also did was describe the obstacle, and the description stopped being true the moment the
obstacle was removed.

| Ruling | What it said | What now governs |
|---|---|---|
| **DR-045 §11.44.6** | A pass-through plate is *"a plate with no strap behind it, which `PlateFill.coverPlateGangs` structurally cannot express, because that getter returns `gangs.length` and a plateless outlet has zero gangs by construction."* | **Premise changed, conclusion withdrawn.** True only while a brush opening had no gang. Under §11.46.2 the opening **is** a gang, fitted with a `PassThrough` rather than a `Strap`, so the plate's gang count falls out of `gangs.length` as it always did and **`coverPlateGangs` is unchanged**. The sentence's *other* half stands and is reaffirmed: a pass-through plate is a **third object** after the strap and the cover plate, and §11.7.8 change 1's separation is what made room for it. |
| **DR-045 §11.44.6**, the open question | *"It needs its own ruling on whether the plate is a property of the **outlet** or of the **drop**."* | **Answered as neither**, §11.46.1. Both readings were live and both are refused: the drop buys nothing (`outletId` is non-nullable) and costs a de-duplication rule; the outlet cannot express a mixed plate and duplicates a fact the gangs carry. **A question with two named options is not a closed set**, and this is the second time in three rulings that censusing the code before pricing the task produced the answer neither option contained (see DR-043 §11.42, where five drop-entry surfaces corrected a task that had asked for a modifier). |

**Nothing else in DR-045 moves.** `TerminationType.rj45Plug` and its zero cells (§11.44.2), the AP
template (§11.44.3), the three states of an outlet (§11.44.4) and the derived-never-stored rule
(§11.44.5) are all untouched, and §11.46.5 restates the last of them rather than amending it.

## 14. PAL-1, restated: the greyscale rule over rendered values

Ruled under §12.6(c). This section supersedes the statement of PAL-1 in §6.2.2 and the domain-level
verdict table beneath it. It does **not** change any hue, and it does not change requirement 4's
resolution (hue = domain; dash + weight + glyph + tag = type).

### 14.1 The restated rule

> **PAL-1 (rendered-value form).** Every shipped `SignalFamilyDef` renders as the triple
> *(L, dashClass, weight)*, where **L** is the WCAG relative luminance of its **effective** hue,
> **dashClass** is the class of its effective dash pattern per the mechanical definition below, and
> **weight** is its effective line-weight multiplier — *effective* meaning **after** any
> `colorOverride`, `dashOverride` or weight override declared in the signal-family registry, not
> the domain base value.
>
> For **every pair of families belonging to different `SignalDomainDef`s** whose luminances satisfy
> **|L₁ − L₂| < 0.10**, at least one of the following must hold: **(a)** their dash classes differ,
> **or** **(b)** their weight multipliers differ by a factor **≥ 1.4**.
>
> Families **within one domain** are exempt from (a)/(b) — they share a hue by construction, the
> legend prints them adjacently, and the tag pill disambiguates them — but any two families in one
> domain must still differ in **dash pattern, weight, or glyph**.

Two things changed and both matter. It is now stated over **rendered family values**, not domain
base values, which is what is actually drawn. And it is **disjunctive**: the old conjunctive
reading ("no two may share a dash class, *and* weights must differ by ≥ 1.4") is unsatisfiable by
the shipped palette and was never the intent; the domain-level verdict table quoted the maximum
spread across a band rather than checking pairs, which is how the collision survived.

### 14.2 Dash class, defined mechanically so a test can compute it

A dash pattern is a repeating sequence of alternating **marks** and **gaps** in points. Classify
each mark: **dot** < 2.5 pt · **short** 2.5–8.9 pt · **long** ≥ 9 pt. The **dash class** is the
sequence of mark classes over one period, compared **up to rotation**. `solid` is its own class.

Worked: `2,3` → `(dot)` · `1.5,3` → `(dot)` · `6,3` → `(short)` ·
`6,3,3,3` → `(short,short)` · `12,4` → `(long)` · `6,3,1,3` → `(short,dot)` ·
`1.5,3,4,3` → `(dot,short)` = `(short,dot)` by rotation · `1.5,3,1.5,9` → `(dot,dot)` ·
`8,3,1.5,3,1.5,3` → `(short,dot,dot)`.

### 14.3 The collisions, and their fixes

**Eight families moved in total: the three below, plus the five in "The further five" beneath the
table.** The authority for every effective value is `tools/pal1_check.py`.

The first three collisions found, these fixes stand and are reproduced in the check file:

| Pair | Before | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio.spdif_optical` (TOSLINK, L 0.2215) vs `ctl.ir_emitter` (IR, L 0.2930) | `2,3` @ 1.00× vs `1.5,3` @ 0.75×. ΔL 0.0715; both `(dot)`; ratio **1.33**. | **FAILS.** Two of requirement 4's ten named types render as near-identical fine dots in greyscale. | **`audio.spdif_optical` weight 1.00× → `1.25×`.** Dash stays `2,3`. Ratio becomes **1.67 ≥ 1.4** ✓ |
| `structure.pathway` (L 0.3185) vs `ctl.ir_emitter` (L 0.2930) | `2,6` @ 0.75× vs `1.5,3` @ 0.75×. ΔL 0.0255; both `(dot)`; ratio **1.00**. | **FAILS.** | **`structure.pathway` dash `2,6` → `1.5,3,1.5,9`**, class `(dot,dot)` ✓, period 15 pt. Weight stays 0.75×. A double-dot reads correctly as "a route, not a conductor". |
| `structure.undetermined` (L 0.3185) vs **five** families: `audio.line_unbal` `6,3` @ 1.00×, `audio.mic` `4,3` @ 1.00×, `audio.headphone` `3,3` @ 0.75×, `ctl.rs485` `6,3` @ 1.00×, `ctl.trigger12v` `4,3` @ 0.75× | `4,4` @ 0.75×, inherited from the `str` domain base. ΔL 0.0977 / 0.0977 / 0.0977 / 0.0255 / 0.0255; **all six are `(short)`**; ratios 1.33, 1.33, **1.00**, 1.33, **1.00**. | **FAILS all five.** Against `audio.headphone` and `ctl.trigger12v` the dash class *and* the weight are identical, in greyscale they are the same line, separated by hue alone. | **The `str` domain base dash `4,4` → `6,3,3,3`**, class `(short,short)` ✓, period 15 pt, permille `[6000, 3000, 3000, 3000]`. Weight stays 0.75×. `structure.undetermined` carries no `dashOverride` and inherits it, so the legend's `str` swatch and the drawn line move together. `structure.undetermined` is the correct family to move: it is a placeholder, it is not one of requirement 4's ten named types, and moving it is one edit against five. |

`ctl.ir_emitter` is deliberately **not** touched: it is a requirement-4 named type and its `1.5,3`
was itself the correction that brought the control domain up to the dash-period floor.

**The "What was verified, and how" paragraph that stood here is retracted.** It claimed all three
fixes "were checked by enumerating every shipped `SignalFamilyDef` (55 families across the eight
domains) … and comparing it against every family in a different domain whose luminance is within
0.10", and it published per-family in-band tallies and pass counts. **No such enumeration was
performed.** Its own figures give it away: TOSLINK's in-band set is **27** families across four
domains, not the 26 it reported. That made three successive assertions that PAL-1 was "verified
clear", each one made by reading a table of eight domain rows rather than enumerating the family
pairs actually drawn, and each one false. The palette those assertions certified carried
**fourteen** collisions, six of them involving types requirement 4 names by hand: S/PDIF against
RS-232, DMX512, DALI, KNX, contact closure and IR receive.

**A rule checked by inspection is not checked, and the remedy is to stop making the claim in
prose.** No part of this record may assert that a manual PAL-1 sweep was performed, or enumerate
which families were checked against which. The authority is a committed, executable check:

> **`tools/pal1_check.py` is the authority.** It enumerates all **55** shipped families, computes
> each rendered triple *(L, dashClass, weight)*, and tests all **385** in-band cross-domain pairs
> against §14.1 plus the within-domain and dash-period limbs. It exits 0 on the corrected palette
> and reproduces all fourteen violations if the corrections are reverted. **Where this document
> and that file disagree, the file wins and the document is wrong.** It is ported to
> `pal1_conformance_test.dart` in `rackmate_core` at M0 and is the authority thereafter (§14.5).

**The further five.** Enumerating the pairs rather than the eight domain rows found five more
families that had to move. All five preserve their domain's base weight semantics, and **no hue
changed**: the Okabe–Ito domain palette is untouched.

| Family | Before | After | Class change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `video.hdmi.1_4` | solid @ 1.00× | **solid @ 0.75×** | stays `solid` | It was byte-identical to `video.hdmi.2_0`, violating the within-domain limb. The three HDMI generations now read as a bandwidth progression **0.75× / 1.00× / 1.25×** and all stay solid, solid being the native digital-video carrier. |
| `video.composite` | `12,4` @ 1.00× | **`1.5,3` @ 1.00×** | `long` → `dot` | Weight is untouched; the analog-video base weight semantics are preserved. |
| `audio.line_bal` | `10,3` @ 1.00× | **solid @ 1.00×** | `long` → `solid` | It collided with **four** `video.analog` families at once (`video.composite`, `video.svideo`, `rf.ota` and `rf.modulated`) all at ΔL 0.0112. |
| `audio.spdif_coax` | `6,3,1,3` @ 1.00× | **`12,4,3,4` @ 1.00×** | `(dot,short)` → `(long,short)` | Requirement 4's S/PDIF. Cleared all six `ctl` collisions: RS-232, DMX512, DALI, KNX, contact closure and IR receive. |
| `audio.aes3` | `10,3,1,3` @ 1.00× | **`12,4,10,4` @ 1.00×** | `(dot,long)` → `(long,long)` | Cleared `ctl.cresnet` and `video.avoip`. |

Effective values for all eight moved families live in `tools/pal1_check.py`'s `FAMILIES` table,
which is the row-for-row source the §6.4 registry rows must match.

### 14.4 The dash-period floor

**≥ 4.5 pt (1.5875 mm).** The competing figure of 4.25 pt is wrong: 4.25 pt = 1.4992 mm, which is
*below* the 1.5 mm physical floor the rule is derived from, and 4.5 pt is the figure that
generated the shipped correction of the control domain's `1,3` (4.0 pt period) to `1.5,3` (4.5 pt).
Every occurrence of "≥ 4.25 pt" becomes **"≥ 4.5 pt"**. Every corrected pattern clears it:
`2,3` = 5 pt, `1.5,3,1.5,9` = 15 pt, `6,3,3,3` = 15 pt, `1.5,3` = 4.5 pt, `12,4,3,4` = 23 pt,
`12,4,10,4` = 30 pt (the remaining two corrections are `solid`, which has no period). The floor is
a limb of `tools/pal1_check.py`, so this list is checked rather than asserted.

### 14.5 The test that makes this real

A unit test enumerates every shipped `SignalFamilyDef`, computes its rendered triple, and checks
**every cross-domain pair** against §14.1. It exists today as **`tools/pal1_check.py`**, runnable
before any Dart exists (`python tools/pal1_check.py`, exit 0 clean, 1 on any violation), and is
ported to `pal1_conformance_test.dart` in `rackpal_core` at M0, remaining the authority
thereafter. It is a named acceptance criterion of the registry (§6.7) and of M2's exit. The
within-domain exemption is expressed in the test as a domain-equality check, **not** as an
allowlist of pairs, an allowlist is how a real collision gets waived.

---

**End of Part 4.** DR-001…DR-036 are the user's decisions and are binding. §12 is the complete
index of what they supersede, §12.1…§12.5, §12.9, §12.11, §12.12 and §12.13 by ruling, §12.6 by
internal correction, and §12.8 the list of Parts 1–3 sites carrying a pointer. **Two entries
supersede another DR**: §12.12 (DR-018's reasoning as well as its ruling) and §12.13, which also
corrects §12.6(b)'s rule count from 27 to 28. Anything not listed there stands as written
in Parts 1–3.

**§11.30 supersedes nothing and DISCHARGES something**, which is a third relationship and is why it
has no §12 entry. DR-020 §11.19.4 is a *"what it does not rule"* clause with a date on it; answering
it leaves DR-020 entirely intact and simply makes one of its open questions closed. A reader of
§11.19.4 should follow the pointer there rather than infer that DR-020 was amended.
